Experience with spatial data formats and coordinate systems
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to work independently,manage multiple tasks, and show attention to detail

UVM Experience

who excels at translating advanced geospatial and remote sensing technologies into compelling both client-facing and internal documentation for stakeholders. Your background combines hands-on experience in geospatial technologies, strong industry and market insight, and proven project management skills—enabling you to craft clear, differentiated content that positions NV5 to win in a highly competitive landscape.

Work Location: NV5 Geospatial Offices or Remote
Domestic travel up to 10% of the time

Salary Range:
$60,000 - $95,000 per year ($28.85 - $45.67/hour). Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, skills, and location, in addition to market and business considerations.

Exercise independent judgment to coordinate and oversee client-facing documentation development activities.
Lead the coordination of marketing material (but not limited to presentation slides, brochures, documentation, proposals, and bids) from initiation to completion, managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
Develop marketing content that highlights strategy and NV5’s value propositions, differentiators, win themes by analyzing client and internal stakeholder requirements.

Interview subject matter experts to gather critical information necessary for technical content development.
Oversee the entire document production process, including compiling and formatting materials for creation and submission.
Apply advanced project management, writing, and strategic thinking skills in proposal development.
Utilize advanced software tools such as Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, Google Earth Pro, MS Word, and PowerPoint to enhance content quality and presentation.
Ensure the marketing and documentation strategy and quality meet company standards, directly impacting the likelihood of securing new business.
Demonstrate a strong ability to interpret and understand client and internal technical specifications, ensuring meticulous attention to detail so that all technical requirements are accurately reflected and conveyed in the technical proposal.
Utilize AI technology to develop efficiencies in writing, content development, and content management processes.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Excellent customer service and organizational skills.
Experience in a technical marketing or proposal specialist role, positioning technology services and/or software products in a B2B selling environment.
Meticulous attention to detail, with ability to maintain changes and updates throughout documentation process and future work.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
5+years of experience in a similar role or demonstrated understanding of geospatial.
A strategic thinker with the ability to work independently.
Technical writing experience and the ability to adapt to new technological trends and translate them into solutions that address client needs.
Excellent communicator with good presentation and listening skills, adept at building relationships across multiple teams.
Ability to manage and prioritize activities.
Ability to handle complex file and information management.
Experience in submitting winning bids to RFPs/RFQs.

Desired Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in writing, marketing, engineering or a geospatial field (e.g., remote sensing, GIS).
Ability to develop consistent, branded content for client-facing and internal stakeholders.
Domain experience in Energy and/or Electric Utilities and Oil and Gas markets.
Demonstrated experience with technical geospatial value propositions and ROI positioning within a competitive landscape.
Ability to understand remote sensing data acquisition technologies, enterprise-level GIS platforms, geospatial applications development, integrated geospatial solutions, and how they relate to Private clients including Electric Utilities, Oil and Gas, and others.
Proven ability to develop proposal and content management processes.

Employee Assistance Program
Company paid Life & AD&D

jobs.title: Field Application Expert - Navigation & Drones/UAV (H/F)
jobs.description:
Et si votre prochain défi consistait à savoir précisément où l’on se trouve… là où le GPS ne suffit plus ?

SBG Systems conçoit et fabrique en France des technologies de navigation inertielle de haute précision, utilisées partout dans le monde.

Nos systèmes combinent capteurs MEMS de pointe, GNSS et algorithmes avancés de fusion de données pour permettre à des équipements autonomes de se localiser, de s’orienter et de naviguer avec une extrême précision. Drones, robots terrestres, navires océanographiques, aéronautique, spatial ou défense : nos technologies opèrent là où les environnements sont hostiles et où la précision ne tolère aucune approximation.

Entreprise française indépendante, nous faisons le choix fort de maîtriser nos produits de bout en bout : de la recherche fondamentale et la R&D logicielle/matérielle jusqu'à la production industrielle sur notre site. Présents aujourd'hui dans plus de 70 pays, nous équipons les acteurs technologiques et industriels les plus exigeants de la planète.

Aujourd’hui en hypercroissance, SBG Systems change d’échelle avec un défi majeur : grandir vite sans jamais transiger sur l’excellence technologique, l'agilité et l'esprit d'équipe qui font notre différence.

Ce passage à l'échelle se joue au plus près du terrain : pour notre équipe Field Application, cela implique d'accompagner des programmes d’intégration de plus en plus critiques et de bâtir l'expertise de pointe nécessaire pour sécuriser les missions de nos clients.

C’est au cœur de cette dynamique que nous renforçons notre pôle d'expertise technique dédié aux applications Défense et Systèmes Autonomes (UAV).

Votre rôle : L'expertise technique au service du terrain et du produit

Intégré(e) Au Sein D’une Équipe De 10 Personnes Rattachée à Christophe, Directeur Support Client, Vous Rejoignez Le Pôle D'excellence Niveau 3 Aux Côtés D'un Autre Expert Senior Chevronné. Vous Devenez Le Référent Applicatif Dédié Aux Intégrations Complexes Sur Vecteurs Aériens Et Systèmes Militaires Non Habités

Expertise client & Intégration avancée (N3) : Conseiller et auditer les grands intégrateurs et constructeurs de drones de défense dans le choix, l’interfaçage et l’optimisation de leurs architectures de navigation.
Intégration Autopilote & Navigation : Résoudre les problématiques complexes de couplage GNSS/Inertiel avec les couches logicielles de pilotage automatique (PX4, ArduPilot ou équivalents).
Interventions opérationnelles & Essais en vol : Participer aux bancs d'essais, campagnes de vol et recettes techniques sur site client.

(Déplacements ponctuels et ciblés : 5 à 6 missions courtes par an, à l’international).

Pont avec la R&D & Qualification : Élaborer et piloter les campagnes d'évaluation de nos nouvelles centrales face à des scénarios sévères (brouillage/leurrage GNSS, environnements contestés) et exprimer les besoins d'évolution produit.

jobs.title: Environmental Impact Assessment Graduate - Dublin - Start between Nov 26 - Jan 27
jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our

services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of nearly 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

Our Impact Assessment Practice team are currently recruiting a graduate within our Dublin office to start between Nov 26 - Jan 27.

About our Team

Impact Assessment is part of the Environment business, which comprises around 730 professionals across the UK and Republic of Ireland. The team delivers environment and sustainability solutions to both public and private sector clients and plays a leading role in addressing the climate and biodiversity emergencies.

It comprises the following practice areas: Acoustics; Air Quality; Ecology; Geospatial & Data Services; Heritage; Landscape; Water Environment; Impact Assessment; Planning; Climate Change, Sustainability & Resilience; Stakeholder Engagement; and ESIA & ESDD (international environment and sustainability work). Our IAPA work includes:
Coordinating multidisciplinary environmental inputs across a wide range of infrastructure development projects, helping them to gain development consent
Working with clients and design teams to identify environmental constraints, avoid impacts and develop solutions, as well as delivering benefits where possible
Coordinating the preparation of environmental assessment reports
Post-planning consent support to projects (including during project construction and operation)

Projects

AECOM are at the forefront of delivering Environmental Impact Assessments for the nationally significant infrastructure projects that are providing for our future. Key projects include sustainable energy generation and transmission and water distribution.

Here's what you'll do:

We need people with inquiring minds who can ask the questions to understand and then shape projects to achieve environmentally beneficial outcomes. The ability to work with people with different perspectives is essential to understand what Clients really need, what the design means and how it matters to stakeholders. So, communication – verbal and written – to interact with others and seek understanding, is important, but we accept that it is a skill that develops over time. We like people with an appetite to learn and develop – taking personal responsibility, but understanding how to confirm that we are getting to a good outcome.

Enjoy the Perks

At AECOM, you'll enjoy a range of core and personalised benefits designed to support your future and well-being, customised to fit your lifestyle. Take advantage of career development opportunities, our flexible hybrid working model to ensure a work-life balance that suits your lifestyle, technical practice networks, AECOM University, and volunteering days.

Here is what you will get from us!

On the job support and learning

When a graduate starts at AECOM, we pair them with a senior member of the team who will guide and mentor them through their initial period working on live projects and business development tasks, to support with any technical queries.

Graduate Development Programme

Our 2 year graduate ADVANCE programme is designed to help you build your career in AECOM. You will attend a number of instructor-led training sessions where you will meet and hear from people across the business and take part in a series of interactive activities to equip you with the knowledge and skills you need to succeed in your role. Alongside the instructor-led elements of the ADVANCE programme, you will also engage with an online curriculum via AECOM University and have the opportunity to join the ADVANCE webinar series. We will provide you with all the support and tools you need to achieve your professional development ambitions, which may include Chartership with the relevant international professional institution eg Institute for Sustainability and Environmental Professionals (ISEP), Institute of Environmental Science (IES).

We have more than 750 graduates on our programmes across the UK and Ireland from more than 40 different disciplines, each making a tangible difference to the environment in which we live and work.

See our digital early careers e-brochure here

Qualifications

Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?

Here’s what we’re looking for:

Ideally, you will have a relevant first degree and, potentially, a relevant post-graduate degree.

Relevant first or post-graduate degree subjects include: environmental impact assessment,
environmental economics, environmental management, environmental planning, environmental policy, environmental science, geography, housing (sustainable, planning, regeneration and urban management), social science, sustainable development.
A good understanding of the potential for digital solutions to assist in tackling environment and sustainability challenges and be able to help us in delivering our digital transformation agenda
Willingness and ability to travel is essential. A full driving licence or access to reliable transport would be beneficial as the role will involve travel for site surveys and possible transportation of site equipment
Ability to work flexibly under pressure, responding to changing project and programme demands
Good communications skills – verbal and written (fluent in English) – with the confidence to engage with a variety of people (clients, colleagues, stakeholders and sub-contractors alike) and the aptitude to rationally explain, explore and discuss technical issues and capture feedback
Ability to work as a team
Time Management - Work within schedules to coordinate the completion of tasks through to final project completion
Willingness and ability to learn
Strong research and report writing skills (including web-based research) to support team on technical issues influencing project development
Ability to summarise technical information effectively and demonstrate diligent research techniques
Strong skills in Microsoft Office specifically Word, Excel, PowerPoint
Strong numerate skills
Self-starter and enthusiastic, develops and delivers work under own initiative.
Solid attention to detail and thorough approach to work
Strong organisational skills
Commercial awareness for business development, marketing, and proposal preparation.

We celebrate diversity, including neurodiversity, and believe it enriches our team. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and abilities. If you are an applicant with a disability that requires reasonable accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us at ReasonableAccommodations@aecom.com

At AECOM, we value everyone's unique contributions and perspectives. If you meet some of the requirements above or have transferable skills you believe would benefit us, we would be delighted to hear from you!

Additional Information

Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected for an advanced offer start.

Please include a covering letter with your application and provide all predicted and/or obtained academic grades.

You must have permanent right to work in the Republic of Ireland as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.

Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity

You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.

You will help us foster a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

AECOM provides a wide array of compensation, benefits and well-being programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.

Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

We are a Disability Confident Employer and will offer an interview to applicants who have a disability or long-term condition, who meet the minimum/essential criteria for the role. Please let us know using this email address ReasonableAccommodationsUKI@aecom.com if you would like to apply through the Disability Confident Interview Scheme.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Environmental Field Technician
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Project Manager
plans, coordinates, and oversees safe, efficient environmental field work in accordance with Field Work Orders (FWOs), company procedures, client expectations, and regulatory requirements. This role connects Project Management, Field Operations, clients, vendors, contractors, and field personnel; ensures work is properly scheduled, staffed, equipped, documented, and completed; and provides field leadership and support as needed.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Report writing
Lead tasks on more complex projects
Client interaction
Regulatory interaction
Troubleshooting
Budgeting/costing projects
Participate in field activities
Prepare FWOs, schedules, drawings, permits, sampling requirements, site information, and other project documents before field work begins.
Schedule and coordinate qualified personnel, vehicles, equipment, materials, lodging, and vendors;
Perform or lead environmental sampling, monitoring, investigation, remediation, well installation, and related field services in accordance with project and regulatory requirements.
Direct employees, temporary staff, and contractors; assign work, provide training and coaching, monitor performance, and reinforce accountability and professionalism.
Maintain a safety-first work environment, verify required training and PPE, report incidents and unsafe conditions, and stop or delay work when necessary.
Coordinate waste pickups and disposal; prepare, track, and retain manifests and supporting records through final disposition.
Ensure timely submission of FWOs, field notes, sampling records, photographs, manifests, and other required documentation.
Communicate project status, field conditions, deviations, equipment or personnel concerns, and recommended solutions to appropriate stakeholders.

ACCOUNTABILITY & PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Success is measured by safe, well-planned, adequately staffed and equipped field work that meets project requirements, is documented promptly, and is completed with minimal avoidable delays. The role is expected to anticipate needs, resolve issues, maintain an accurate field calendar, and keep project progressing.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Required

High school diploma or GED and relevant environmental, construction, industrial, or field-services experience.
Valid driver’s license
Ability to develop and/or execute FWOs, collect and document field information accurately, and communicate effectively with employees, contractors, clients, and Project Managers.
Ability to work outdoors, operate or learn field equipment safely, manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and work independently or as part of a team.

Preferred

Associate or bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, engineering, construction management, project management, or a related field.
40hr HAZWOPER certification;
OCC Environmental Consultant, AST/UST Remover
ASB/LBP Licenses
Experience with environmental sampling or remediation, field equipment, waste manifests, project coordination, and leading crews or contractors.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

Project coordination, scheduling, organization, prioritization, and problem solving.
Clear written and verbal communication with employees, clients, vendors, contractors, and regulators.
Leadership, coaching, accountability, and collaborative decision-making.
Environmental sampling, field documentation, basic equipment troubleshooting, and recognition of unusual or unsafe conditions.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to learn OES scheduling, project-management, documentation, and communication systems.

WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Work outdoors in varying weather and at construction, industrial, and environmental project sites, including uneven terrain.
Stand, walk, bend, kneel, climb, and lift, carry, push, or pull equipment and materials consistent with job requirements.
Wear required PPE and work around vehicles, machinery, heavy equipment, and environmental sampling equipment.
Travel between offices, project sites, client locations, vendors, and disposal facilities; overnight, extended hours, or weekend work may be required.

Reasonable accommodation may be made for qualified individuals with disabilities consistent with applicable law.

CORE OES COMPETENCIES

• Safety

• Integrity

• Accountability

• Teamwork

• Communication

• Professionalism

• Organization

• Quality

• Reliability & Customer Service

• Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Protect confidential company, employee, client, and project information.
Participate in required meetings, training, and continuous-improvement activities.
Perform other duties as assigned based on business needs.

JOB DESCRIPTION DISCLAIMER

This job description summarizes the general nature and level of work and is not an exhaustive list of duties, qualifications, or working conditions. OES may modify duties based on business needs. Employment is at will
, meaning either the employee or OES may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice or cause, subject to applicable law.

Extraordinary Teams Building Inspiring Projects

Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place.

Differentiated by the quality of our people and our relentless drive to deliver the most successful outcomes, we align our capabilities to our customers' objectives to create a lasting positive impact. We serve the Infrastructure; Nuclear, Security & Environmental; Energy; Mining & Metals, and the Manufacturing and Technology markets. Our services span from initial planning and investment, through start-up and operations.

Core to Bechtel is our Vision, Values and Commitments. They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our extraordinary teams building inspiring projects in our Impact Report.

Project Overview

Port Arthur LNG, LLC (PALNG) is developing a Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) production and export facility on a site located on the western shoreline of the Port Arthur Canal in Jefferson County, Texas. The project base scope will include two (2) identical LNG trains, two (2) LNG Storage Tanks, one (1) LNG Carrier Berth, and associated utilities/facilities. The Project is to be constructed on a parcel of land located along State Highway 87 south of Port Arthur, Texas, between the inner coastal waterway bridge and Keith Lake. The Infrastructure Global Business Unit (GBU) is executing site civil and marine scopes of work associated with our scopes of work on the Energy GBU LNG projects. As the #1 LNG EPC contractor by installed capacity, Bechtel has the capability to successfully deliver a broad range of LNG projects through our integrated EPC self-perform model, strategic partnerships, and proven experience in LNG project delivery. Partnering with Bechtel means lower cost, shorter delivery schedules, and greater certainty of outcomes for our customers.

Job Summary

In this role, you will integrate environmental requirements into large-scale project planning documents, permit applications, design criteria, construction plans, schedules, and subcontract documents. You will provide input on bid decisions, identify new approaches, conduct inspections, and participate in emergency response. Your work will help reduce adverse environmental impacts of Bechtel projects.

Major Responsibilities

Assists execution of the environmental component of an ESH Program inclusive of technical and administrative aspects.
Assists development and implementation of Environmental Management Plans, associated environmental plans and procedures, and training program.
Provides input to Engineering, Construction, Procurement, Subcontracts, Commissioning, and other groups to assure that environmental requirements are integrated within project planning and execution.
Interprets environmental requirements and provides guidance on risk assessment and program execution.
Researches issues and regulatory requirements and prepares documentation and reports.
Supports environmental permitting, studies, risk assessments, and reviews involving site conditions, natural resources, cultural resources, and communities.
Participates in emergency response and incident investigation and resolution.
Participates in meetings with customers, team members, subcontractors, permitting agencies, and other stakeholders.
Conducts inspections and environmental monitoring and sampling to help identify risks, confirm the effectiveness of mitigation measures, and assess compliance with contract, regulatory, project, and Bechtel requirements.
Provides guidance regarding environmental mitigation, permit conditions, sustainability concepts, and protection of environmentally sensitive areas, species, and communities.

Education And Experience Requirements

Requires a Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) related to environmental sciences, field biology, or natural resources and 2-5 years of relevant experience or 6-9 years of relevant work experience

Required Knowledge And Skills

Specialized knowledge in a field of science (e.g., meteorology, ecology, biology, forestry, wetlands, archeology), engineering (e.g., civil, environmental, mechanical) or related disciplines
Knowledge of environmental laws and regulations and resource agencies’ permitting processes and responsibilities
Knowledge of engineering, construction, and subcontract work processes Skilled in oral and written communication and knowledge of computer applications
Must be willing to work a flexible schedule if required, including, but not limited to extended work weeks, weekends, nightshift or split shift.
This position has a work scope that includes field inspections and the physical ability to conduct field inspections which require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces.
Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress).
Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e., harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.)

Total Rewards/Benefits

For decades, Bechtel has worked to inspire the next generation of employees and beyond! Because our teams face some of the world's toughest challenges, we offer robust benefits to ensure our people thrive. Whether it is advancing careers, delivering programs to enhance our culture, or providing time to recharge, Bechtel has the benefits to build a legacy of sustainable growth. Learn more at Bechtel Total Rewards

Diverse Teams Build The Extraordinary

As a global company, Bechtel has long been home to a vibrant multitude of nationalities, cultures, ethnicities, and life experiences. This diversity has made us a more trusted partner, more effective problem solvers and innovators, and a more attractive destination for leading talent.

We are committed to being a company where every colleague feels that they belong-where colleagues feel part of "One Team," respected and rewarded for what they bring, supported in pursuing their goals, invested in our values and purpose, and treated equitably. Click here to learn more about the people who power our legacy.

jobs.title: Environmental Programs Administrator-EPD
jobs.description:
Overview

At Orange County Government, we are proud to serve the public with integrity, honesty, fairness, and professionalism. We develop innovative policies and services that impact Central Florida and shape the future of our community. We believe in hiring the very best. Our workplace experience sets us apart and makes us a great place to work. Our goal is to create an environment of exceptional organizational values, customer service standards, and employee satisfaction. Orange County Government is committed to providing equal opportunity in employment and services to all individuals.

The Environmental Protection Division (EPD) is seeking several qualified, experienced, and collaborative leaders to serve as an Environmental Programs Administrator. This position provides broad administrative, managerial, and technical leadership across EPD strategic priorities and may be assigned responsibility for multiple environmental programs, teams, initiatives, or regulatory areas based on organizational needs and the selected candidates' experience. The successful candidates will demonstrate the ability to lead environmental professionals, manage complex regulatory and operational matters, exercise sound independent judgment, communicate effectively with diverse audiences, and support the Division's mission and priorities.

Job Description

General Functions:

The Environmental Programs Administrator is responsible for supervising two or more environmental programs or teams and for developing performance goals aligned with the Planning, Environmental and Development Services (PEDS) Strategic Management Plan coordinating work priorities, and ensuring effective delivery of environmental services. Work is performed under the general supervision of the EPD Division Manager and Assistant Manager. Incumbent must be able to exercise independent judgment in the oversight and supervision of assigned responsibilities.

Representative Duties/Assignments:

Advises EPD Division leadership and, as appropriate, senior County management, the Board of County Commissioners, and the Environmental Protection Commission or other County Advisory Boards on environmental, regulatory, permitting, compliance, and policy matters.
Coordinates the preparation of Board agenda items, public hearing materials, briefings, reports, correspondence, and other technical or executive-level work products.
Represents EPD in interactions with citizens, applicants, consultants, regulated entities, public interest groups, County departments, municipalities, and local, state, and federal regulatory agencies.
Provides leadership, direction, and oversight for assigned environmental programs, teams, regulatory functions, and special initiatives.
Supervises environmental professionals and/or program supervisors; establishes expectations, develops staff, supports hiring and succession planning, and promotes accountability for results.
Monitors, analyzes, and facilitates operations and activities associated with environmental permitting, compliance & enforcement, development review, pollution prevention, water-quality, and stormwater-related programs, waste-management permitting, natural resources management, and other environmental functions as assigned.
Provides direction on complex or sensitive environmental permitting, compliance, enforcement, development, and regulatory matters and assists with resolution of internal and external concerns or complaints.
Supports the development, interpretation, implementation, and update of environmental codes, ordinances, policies, procedures, and program requirements.
Assists with development and monitoring of budgets, contracts, grants, performance goals, workload measures, and other resources necessary for effective program delivery.
Directs or participates in studies, surveys, technical evaluations, and specialized research related to environmental matters.
Promotes consistent application of County, Department, and Division objectives, policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements while maintaining a high level of public service.
May serve in a higher-level leadership capacity during the absence of Division management.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor's degree in environmental or civil engineering, environmental law or natural sciences or a related field, and seven years of environmental protection experience, to include three years in a supervisory role. An equivalent combination of relevant education or experience may be substituted on a year for year basis.

Preferences:

Preference may be given to candidates whose experience demonstrates a combination of environmental program management, regulatory oversight, public/stakeholder engagement, leadership, and technical expertise relevant to EPD operations.

Desired experience may include:

Public Relations, communication, GIS, technical analysis, environmental field methods, or other specialized environmental tools and practices applicable to assigned responsibilities.
Relevant professional certifications or licenses - Professional Wetlands Scientist, Certified Environmental Professional, Certified Hazardous Materials Manager, examples include working knowledge of Florida habitats, wetland delineation and use of the Uniform Mitigation Assessment Method (UMAM).

jobs.description:

Essential Job Duties

The
Sheth plant evolutionary ecology lab
in the
Department of Plant and Microbial Biology
at
North Carolina State University
(Raleigh, NC) is currently seeking field technician to participate in an NSF -funded study (
https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2220928&HistoricalAwards=false
) under the direction of Dr. Seema Sheth and in collaboration with Drs. Susana Wadgymar (Davidson College), Jill Anderson (University of Georgia), Megan DeMarche (University of Georgia), and Emily Josephs (Michigan State University).

The project combines approaches from evolutionary biology, field ecology, and population genomics in a broadly distributed native plant species (
Chamaecrista fasciculata
, Fabaceae) to forecast population dynamics range-wide under climate change. The technician will be part of a dynamic, dedicated, and engaged research group as well as a member of a multidisciplinary and multi-institution collaborative group that includes Botanic Garden and conservation professionals.

The successful candidate will contribute to a collaborative study of eco-evolutionary responses to climate in the partridge pea,
Chamaecrista fasciculata
, an annual legume that grows in disturbed habitats in central and eastern North America. The technician’s primary responsibilities involve collaborating with the PIs and other researchers to establish and maintain a large common garden experiment and to collect data from ~6,000 transplanted seeds at Mason Farm Biological Reserve in Chapel Hill, NC. This work includes preparing seeds for planting, planting seeds, setting up the garden infrastructure, building open-top chambers, collecting data on traits and fitness, entering data, maintenance tasks in the garden (e.g., weeding), processing samples in the lab, and communicating with Dr. Sheth and other team members. The technician will also have opportunities to train and mentor undergraduate students and work with graduate students.

jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 300069

Relocation Authorized: National/International - Family
Telework Type: Full-Time Office/Project
Work Location: Cameron, LA

Extraordinary Teams Building Inspiring Projects

Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place.

Differentiated by the quality of our people and our relentless drive to deliver the most successful outcomes, we align our capabilities to our customers' objectives to create a lasting positive impact. We serve the Infrastructure; Nuclear, Security & Environmental; Energy; Mining & Metals, and the Manufacturing and Technology markets. Our services span from initial planning and investment, through start-up and operations.

Core to Bechtel is our Vision, Values and Commitments. They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our extraordinary teams building inspiring projects in our Impact Report.

Project Overview

The Cheniere Sabine Pass Liquefaction (SPL) Project is a Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) export facility located along the Sabine River estuary on the southeastern coast of Cameron Parish, Louisiana. Bulk early work for Stage 1 began at the 1,000+ acre facility in August 2012 and by December 2022, Bechtel had successfully and safely turned over the final phase of Stage 4 to Cheniere. The SPL campus now consists of six operating Trains with an LNG production capacity of approximately 27 million tons per year (MTPA), 3 Jetty superstructures that can accommodate the world’s largest vessels, and dozens of associated buildings and utilities.

Sabine Pass Liquefaction Stage 5 Expansion Project (SPL5) is the newest phase at the SPL facility. It will consist of one liquefaction process train with a production capacity of approximately 5 MTPA; one boil-off gas reliquefaction unit; tie-ins to existing storage tanks, ship-loading facilities, and flare systems; and associated utility support infrastructure. SPL5 will perform this work predominantly on a direct hire basis with support from only a few specialty and service subcontractors.

Job Summary

The Project Environmental Manager is the primary contact for environmental permits, planning, performance, and compliance. This includes technical support and guidance on regulatory requirements and field activities to mitigate risk or harm to environmentally sensitive areas, resources, and communities. The position includes communication, training, interface with regulatory agencies, and data and document management. The overarching responsibility is the development and implementation of an environmental management and compliance program for a large-scale project.

Major Responsibilities

Supervises the Project’s environmental program, in compliance with Bechtel’s ESH Management System, and contract and regulatory requirements.
Ensures that environmental requirements are integrated in planning documents, design criteria, work plans, schedules, training programs, and subcontract documents. Works with other project-level functional leads (e.g., engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning) to integrate environmental aspects in their work activities.
Communicates with internal and external stakeholders on environmental requirements and actions, inclusive of project personnel, subcontractors, and regulatory agencies. Identifies and oversees preparation and submittal of environmental permit applications, reviews and negotiates permit conditions with regulatory agencies, and tracks permit compliance and closeout.
Prepares a project-specific Environmental Management Plan and mitigation plans (e.g., Stormwater Pollution Prevention; Spill Prevention and Control, Waste Management, etc.) Prepares and submits notifications and routine reports to regulatory agencies including reportable releases, chemical inventory reports, and waste reports. Emphasizes and uses risk assessment, data analysis, and Bechtel’s ESH Management System to aid environmental performance, corrective actions, and technical guidance.
Participates in ESH emergency preparedness planning, and investigates and helps resolve environmental incidents.
Prepares and maintains required documentation and conducts inspections, monitoring, and sampling to assess site conditions and compliance with contractual commitments, laws and regulations, environmental permits, and Bechtel requirements.
Delivers training and awareness campaigns on environmental, sustainability, and regulatory compliance to the project’s workforce through various forums. Supervises and guides assigned environmental personnel, and participates in safety and health components of the ESH program.

Education And Experience Requirements

Requires a Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) related to environmental sciences, field biology, or natural resources and 8 -10 years of relevant experience or 12-14 years of relevant work experience

Required Knowledge And Skills

Prior experience with environmental regulatory requirements, impact assessment, and mitigation practices for large-scale projects. Technical skills, work experience, and knowledge of various environmental sciences applicable to the engineering and construction industry.
Knowledge and experience with ISO 14001 Management System standards. Knowledge and experience with environmental mitigation practices (e.g., habitat protection, waste management, stormwater and erosion control, cultural resources).
Knowledge and experience in environmental permitting and regulatory approvals.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including technical writing and data management.
Able to traverse and work outdoors under various weather and site conditions. Experience managing environmental subcontractors or consultants.
This position has a work scope that includes field inspections and the physical ability to conduct field inspections which require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces.
Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress).
Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e., harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.)

Total Rewards/Benefits

For decades, Bechtel has worked to inspire the next generation of employees and beyond! Because our teams face some of the world's toughest challenges, we offer robust benefits to ensure our people thrive. Whether it is advancing careers, delivering programs to enhance our culture, or providing time to recharge, Bechtel has the benefits to build a legacy of sustainable growth. SUMMARY OF POSITION

Under general supervision, performs technical tasks in the operation, maintenance and repair of the water and wastewater utility concrete repairs. Employees in this job series perform technical, manual work. Water Utilities Concrete Restoration Technicians are responsible for repairing water utility cuts and operate and maintain moderate to complex equipment. They perform related work as required.

Essential Functions/Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

GENERAL EXPECTATIONS FOR ALL EMPLOYEES

Learn and demonstrate an understanding of how team, department, and City goals are interconnected.

Contribute to the development of others and/or the working unit or overall organization.

Ability to continuously learn and develop through a mix of internal and external training opportunities, and if applicable, encourage subordinates to do the same.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Performs preventative maintenance on equipment and tools by cleaning and servicing regularly.

Assists preparing work areas and securing job sites by setting up cones, barricades, and other traffic control devices with supervision.

Works efficiently with iPads while entering work orders within CityWorks.

OTHER JOB FUNCTIONS:

Perform other duties as assigned or directed.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES, AND BEHAVIORS

Ability to embrace and embody the City’s core values of Respect, Integrity, Service, and Excellence (R.I.S.E.).
Ability to communicate effectively with peers, supervisors, subordinates, and people to whom service is provided.
Ability to produce desired work outcomes, including quality, quantity, and timeliness.
Ability to plan and organize work, time, and resources, and if applicable, that of subordinates.
Demonstrates City's core values of respect, integrity, service, and excellence, with the ability to implement the City's vision in delivery of services.
Shows leadership in daily activities and through actions, setting an example for others to follow.
Ability to review, classify, categorize, prioritize, and/or analyze data and/or information. This includes exercising discretion in determining data classification, and in referencing such analysis to establish standards for the purpose of recognizing actual or probable interactive effects and relationships.
Ability to provide guidance, assistance, and/or interpretation to others on how to apply procedures and standards to specific situations.
Ability to operate, maneuver, and/or control the actions of equipment, machinery, tools, and/or materials used in performing essential functions.
Ability to utilize a wide variety of descriptive data and information and equipment operator manuals..
Ability to perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division; ability to calculate decimals and percentages; ability to utilize principles of fractions; ability to interpret graphs.
Ability to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagrammatic form, which involves semi-routine, standardized work with some latitude for independent judgment concerning choices of action.
Ability to exercise the judgment required in situations characterized by repetitive or short cycle operations covered by set procedures or sequences.
Ability to perform coordinated movements, which involve placing and turning motions, such as operating a backhoe, dump truck and trailer, front-end loader, air compressor, gas and electrical pumps, and various hand tools.
Ability to work in a team environment while contributing as a team member and treating co-workers, subordinates, and customers with respect; Ability to build professional relationships with internal staff and customers.
Ability to offer flexibility and adaptability, especially during times of change.
Ability to find, locate and follow McKinney Public Works Standard Operating Procedures
Skill in communicating effectively both orally and in writing.

Required Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any work related experience resulting in acceptable proficiency levels in the below Minimum Qualifications may be an acceptable substitute.

Highschool diploma or GED equivalent supplemented by previous experience and/or training involving concrete construction, maintenance and repair type work, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Must possess a valid Class A commercial driver's license or the ability to obtain within twelve (12) months of employment.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Some experience with hand tools and power tools
Some experience with outside elements and manual labor.

During storms or natural disasters, staff will be divided into two 12-hour shifts. During storms or natural disasters, staff may be called in while on vacation.

DEMANDS

Tasks involve the ability to exert heavy physical effort in heavy work, with greater emphasis on climbing and balancing, but typically also involving some combination of stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling, and the lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling of moderately heavy objects and materials (20-50 pounds); may occasionally involve heavier objects and materials (up to 150 pounds). Some tasks require visual and odor perception and discrimination.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

There is limited exposure to environmental conditions. Tasks may require exposure to strong odors and/or smoke, traffic hazards, extreme heat/cold or extreme weather conditions.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking a Environmental Technician to support environmental remediation for an industrial client. You will work alongside experienced technicians and field crews to execute field tasks safely and efficiently, maintain high-quality documentation, and support operations, maintenance, and sampling activities. The site is located in Niagara Falls, NY.

This role emphasizes hands-on fieldwork and adherence to safety and quality protocols, with growth opportunities into advanced field responsibilities. The successful candidate will ideally have some experience in general operations, environmental remediation/sampling, and hands-on mechanical experience.

Field Operations & Site Support

Oversee pump-and-treat system operations, including monitoring, troubleshooting, maintenance, and performance optimization.
Sampling groundwater Influent and Effluent from groundwater treatment systems primarily for volatile organic compounds. Preparing chains-of-custody and sample cooler loading in preparation for transport to contracted analytical laboratories.
Gathering and maintaining specified records of scientific data for the technical lead/supervisor, including environmental sampling, operations and maintenance, and inspections at client sites
Assisting with calculations, setting up, and operating equipment (sampling devices and pumps), inspecting equipment and installations for compliance with specifications and maintaining proper project documentation.
Driving AECOM-leased site vehicles.
Mechanical aptitude to make basic repairs to treatment equipment.
Overseeing and working in collaboration with client mechanical, electrical, and industrial contractors.

Health & Safety Participation

Follow AECOM safety policies and Site-Specific Health and Safety Plans (SSHPs); participate in JHAs/tailgates and stop work if unsafe conditions arise.
Use required PPE correctly, report incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions immediately.
Maintain compliance with OSHA and applicable state requirements during all phases of work.

Documentation & QA/QC

Maintain complete and accurate field logs, daily reports, equipment logs, photo documentation, and chain-of-custody records.
Perform basic data entry and QA/QC checks for measurements and sampling results.

Coordination & Communication

Coordinate day-to-day needs with the site supervisor, project manager, subcontractors, and client representatives as directed.
Communicate field status, issues, and material/equipment needs promptly and professionally.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Must possess a High School Diploma (or GED).
U.S. citizenship (due to project requirements)
In order to receive a security badge at the client worksite for which you are being hired to perform services, you will be required to pass the client's background, medical and drug screening requirements, which will be done after you have commenced employment and is a condition of your continued employment.
Ability to travel to various client sites locations using a AECOM provided Vehicle to conduct fieldwork, including but not limited to environmental sampling, operations and maintenance and inspections.
Must possess a valid driver’s license and clean driving record.
Position requires frequent (more than 50% of workday) standing/walking; often (25-50% of workday) performing power gripping/squeezing (hand tools, levers, etc.), operation of vehicles, performing repetitive or fine hand movements, and lifting of less than 25 pounds; occasionally (10-25% of workday) performing work with arms above shoulder level, repetitive bending & stooping, working at heights, climbing stairs, using portable ladders, work in an environment of heavy, moving, dangerous equipment, work in confined spaces, keyboard/mouse operations, work alone in isolated/remote areas, and lifting of 25-50 pounds; rarely (less than 10% of workday) wearing fall protection, and lifting of 50-75 pounds.
Position will include wearing associated personal protective equipment, including but not limited to gloves, safety glasses/goggles, face shield, safety shoes/boots, hard hat, hearing, and respiratory protection.
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER (current) or ability to obtain within 60 days of hire (training provided).

Preferred Qualifications

1+ years of environmental remediation, construction, utilities, or industrial fieldwork experience.
Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER with recent refresher; OSHA 10 or 30 Construction and CPR/First Aid certifications.
Experience with basic sampling, meter use (e.g., PID, multi-parameter), and remediation system O&M tasks.
Some experience or aptitude with flow meters, pH meters, and level probes would be beneficial but not required.
Proficiency with field documentation (daily reports, chain-of-custody, photo logs); basic Excel/Word skills.
Previous knowledge or experience with process control systems
Familiarity or previous experience with environmental regulatory compliance.
Mechanical aptitude and hands-on skills to operate groundwater treatment equipment.
Associate degree or college course education in engineering, chemistry, or other sciences.

Additional Information

Qualified applicants who are offered a position must pass a pre-employment substance abuse test.
In order to receive a security badge at the client worksite for which you are being hired to perform services, you will be required to pass the client's background, medical and drug screening requirements, which will be done after you have commenced employment and is a condition of your continued employment.
This position does not include sponsorship for United States work authorization.
This position does not include relocation benefits.

Description

We are currently seeking an Environmental Compliance Coordinator
to manage the environmental portion of a Distribution Transformer Inspection Program. The program inspects up to 40,000 underground transformers per year. This role combines office-based program management with field support and coordination of environmental compliance activities.

The ideal candidate is organized, self-motivated, and an excellent communicator who can manage databases, coordinate with contractors and internal stakeholders, and support timely environmental remediation and regulatory reporting.

WHAT WE OFFER:

Industry competitive pay.
Company vehicle with a fuel card for work purposes.
Medical/Dental/Vision/VOYA/Vacation Accrual/Paid Holidays/EAP, 401K, life insurance, short and long-term disability, Paid Maternity Leave.
Paid Sick Time.
Weekly Pay Cycle.
Participation in Referral Bonus Program.
Ongoing training and assistance with obtaining industry certifications.
A standard 5-day, 40-hour work week, with opportunities for overtime when needed and approved.
A hybrid schedule consisting of approximately 60% office work and 40% field work.
Three days per week working from an office is required; remote work from home two days per week is optional.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Program & Data Management

Manage the environmental portion of the Distribution Transformer Inspection Program.
Manage and maintain spreadsheets and databases used to track transformer replacement and repair status when oil contamination or leaks are present.
Coordinate with the Asset Management Team to support successful program rollouts across all 32 districts.
Track spend rates and manage budgets.

Spill Response & Environmental Compliance

Communicate with inspection contractors and internal stakeholders to ensure timely remediation of oil spills.
Report oil spills internally and, when required, externally to VADEQ.
Approve or deny environmental containment while inspectors are in the field.
Dispatch spill response vendors to remediate oil contamination.
Document spill response measures and perform QA/QC of cleanup efforts when necessary.
Make proper PCB/non-PCB determinations and manage PCBs in accordance with TSCA regulations when discovered.

Training & Team Support

Attend in-person meetings and provide training and guidance when necessary.
Assist with environmental tasks such as SPCC/SWPPP inspections, management of universal and hazardous waste, and support of the collective team during storm events.

WHAT YOU NEED TO HAVE:

Approximately 2-8 years of experience in a combination of environmental management, SWPPP/CGP inspections, waste management, spill response/remediation, SPCC/tank inspections, state/federal agency reporting, wetland delineations, PCB management, or NPDES/VPDES work.
Excellent communication skills.
Strong organization skills and the ability to be a self-starter and stay motivated.
Database management skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel.
Ability to travel up to approximately 2.5-3.5 hours to locations within the assigned region, occurring up to one day per week.
Ability to travel overnight approximately 1-3 nights per month.

WHAT WOULD BE AMAZING TO HAVE:

A degree in Environmental Science, Construction Management, Forestry, or a related field. A degree is preferred but not required.
Energy utility experience.

Working Environment

This position is approximately 60% office-based and 40% field-based. Working from an office three days per week is required, with the option to work remotely from home two days per week. The preferred candidate will live within one hour of Richmond. Regional travel and occasional overnight travel are required as described above.

Company Overview

ArborMetrics (AMS) is a leading provider of vegetation and asset management consulting services to the utility industry. Successful professionals at AMS have come from a variety of backgrounds, including forestry, arboriculture, natural resource management, biology, landscape maintenance, horticulture, nursery management, environmental sciences, geology, agriculture, parks & recreation management, urban forestry, geography, and more.

jobs.title: Director Of Environmental Health & Safety
jobs.description:
Manage the EHS Department staff and student employees. Oversee the College’s radiation, laser, biosafety, chemical safety, fire safety, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and Campus Policies, and hazardous waste disposal programs. Ensure organizational compliance with local, state, and federal safety and environmental regulations, complete required periodic regulatory reports, and coordinate regulatory inspections.

Director of Environmental Health & Safety (EHS)

Pay Status and Classification:
Exempt, Regular Full-time. This position is not eligible for relocation assistance or visa sponsorship.

Work Location:
This position is an onsite role and is not eligible for a hybrid work schedule.

Supervisor:
Vice President for Human Resources and Chief of Staff.

This position also collaborates closely and strategically with the Director of Campus Safety and the Director of Facilities as key institutional partners to align safety compliance with daily operations.

Position Purpose:
Manage the EHS Department staff and students employees. Oversee the College’s radiation, laser, biosafety, chemical safety, fire safety, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and Campus Policies, and hazardous waste disposal programs. Ensure organizational compliance with local, state, and federal safety and environmental regulations, complete required periodic regulatory reports, and coordinate regulatory inspections.

Essential Responsibilities and Duties:

Strategic Leadership, Governance & Program Management (30%)

Develop and execute long- and short-range plans, policies, and operating procedures for the EHS department to build a proactive and collaborative culture of safety across campus.
Hire, supervise, mentor, and evaluate EHS department staff.
Partner with Union Finance to manage the EHS budget and forecast annual costs for services, supplies, etc.
Chair the Academic Affairs Safety Committee and partner with faculty, staff, and administration to evaluate and continuously improve safety initiatives.
Collaborate and partner with Facilities Services on code compliance and occupational health & safety within the departments including both large and small projects.
Designs and delivers EHS safety training programs for students and employees.
Stay current on EHS trends, innovations, and higher education safety benchmarks, introducing modern practices and systems.
Work with Human Resources to recommend preventative safety measures and controls and investigate employee injury incidents.

Regulatory Compliance, Audits & Agency Liaison (25%)

Direct Union College’s compliance with local, state, and federal health, safety, and environmental regulations (OSHA, EPA, NYSDEC, NYSDOH, NYS Office of Fire Prevention & Control, etc.).
Monitor changing health, safety and environmental legislation, update institutional policies and practices accordingly.
Lead the strategy, administration, and instructional delivery of institutional compliance and safety training programs (e.g., OSHA, Radiation Safety).
Oversee mandatory compliance reporting and serve as the primary institutional liaison during official agency inspections and audits (NYS Cooling Tower Registries, Asbestos and lead safety reporting, and other facilities related reports).

Academic, Laboratory & Specialized Safety Operations (20%)

Responsible for oversight of Union’s chemical inventory program (CEMS), safety training for authorized entry to the ISEC chemical stockroom and serves as the Chemical Hygiene Officer (CHO) for the College.
Serve as the designated Biosafety Officer (BSO), Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) and Laser Safety Officer (LSO). Maintain compliance with Union’s Radioactive Materials License conditions, and biosafety and laser safety standards, and inventory controls.
Direct safety inspections, hazard assessments, and chemical hygiene programs in Science & Engineering research and teaching laboratories.

Environmental Protection, Hazardous Materials & Bulk Storage (15%)

Oversee environmental stewardship programs, including the Petroleum Bulk Storage (PBS) program and hazardous chemical/waste management.
Direct hazmat spill response readiness, ensuring proper containment protocols, reporting, and maintenance of emergency spill equipment.
Manage electronic and universal waste recycling programs.

Fire Safety, Life Safety & Emergency Response (10%)

Manage fire safety and life safety inspection and training schedules across academic, administrative, and residential physical environments.
Serve as a campus community liaison and share relevant health and safety information.
Respond to campus EHS emergencies, serving as the technical advisor during hazardous materials incidents or severe laboratory events.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree (in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, Chemistry, or a related field) required.
6+ years of directly related experience in environmental health and safety leadership, preferably in higher education.
Safety certifications preferred such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Chemical Hygiene Officer (CCHO), Certified Hazardous Material Manager (CHMM), OSHA 10 or 30 hour general industry certification.
Ability to lift 30 lbs. required.
Thorough working knowledge of EPA, OSHA, NYSDEC, NYSDOL, NYSDOH, and NYS Office of Fire Prevention & Control regulations.
Strong safety consciousness, communication, organizational, and time-management skills.
Demonstrated capability to lead diverse teams, and ability to foster inclusive safety practices across campus.
Able to anticipate, deliver on, and exceed the expectations of students, faculty, alumni, supervisees, and fellow staff colleagues, etc.
Ability to respond to on-campus emergencies, inspect lab/workspace facilities, handle spill response equipment, and navigate campus buildings.

Compensation:

The annual salary range for this position is $95,000 - $110,000.
Except for roles with a set rate of pay, the wage/salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to departmental budgets, qualifications, experience, education, licenses, specialty, and training. The stated hiring rate/range represents the College’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the rate/range of possible compensation at the time of posting.

Schenectady, NY

Free On-Campus Fitness Facility Access and Discounts for On-Campus Wellness Programs

Tuition Exchange

jobs.title: R&D Professional AI for Earth Observation
jobs.description:
VITO develops technology to facilitate the transition to a more sustainable society and economy. One of the key technologies applied in this context is Remote Sensing. The Remote Sensing Unit of VITO celebrated last year its 25th anniversary but Remote Sensing has never been more fascinating than today. With the increasing number of satellites, drones, processing facilities and technologies like artificial intelligence, the opportunities with remote sensing are larger than ever.
Meet the team:

The Applied GeoAI and Embedded Solutions (AGES) team develops robust AI-driven solutions that power remote sensing, environmental monitoring, and security applications worldwide.
The AI Engineer will work on a variety of applications in the fields of environmental monitoring and security, utilizing the latest AI technologies to develop solutions that address the unique challenges and opportunities of each domain.
We offer a challenging and dynamic work environment, with opportunities for personal and professional development. If you are passionate about AI and want to make a difference in the field of Earth Observation, please apply for this position.
What’s the job about?

Develop and implement AI algorithms and techniques for Earth Observation applications, ranging from prototypes to pre-operational workflows.

Work in a multidisciplinary team with experts in EO, GIS, computer science, and engineering to design, develop, and test AI solutions.

Collaborate with international R&D and industrial partners and customers from the European Space Agency, European Commission, federal and regional governments and companies.

Keep up to date with the latest advances in AI, computer vision, machine learning, and deep learning techniques and apply them in innovative ways to solve EO problems

Develop and apply multi-modal learning techniques to integrate data from various sources such as optical, SAR, hyperspectral and thermal data, IOT and textual information.

Contribute to the coordination and management of R&D projects, including planning activities, following up on progress and deliverables, and coordinating with project partners and customers.

Communicate results and progress to team members, partners, and customers in a clear and concise manner

Requirements:

We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled AI Engineer to work in an applied research context in the field of Earth Observation. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in engineering, mathematics, or science, and will be passionate about keeping up to date with the latest state-of-the-art in AI, such as foundation models, multi-modal learning, generative and agentic AI.
MSc. degree in engineering, mathematics, computer science, or a related field

Strong programming skills in Python

Hands-on experience with AI/ML frameworks such as PyTorch and with state-of-the-art AI models, including foundation models and multi-modal architectures

Ability to learn new concepts and technologies quickly and apply them in innovative ways to solve problems

Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team and collaborate with partners from different cultural and technical backgrounds

Experience in EO or GIS domain is a plus

Experience in project management or coordinating collaborative R&D projects with multiple partners is a plus

Strong communication skills in English, both written and verbal

Offer

We work 'activity-based', our activities bring us to our location. Our headquarter is in Mol. Part-time working from home or a satellite office in Antwerp-Berchem, Genk, Leuven or Ostend is possible.

A competitive salary with a range of benefits, including allowances, insurance and a modular package of holidays.

Innovation is our asset, so it goes without saying that we give our employees the opportunity to take additional training courses and stay up-to-date in their field. You will always have the opportunity to broaden your knowledge and discover new technologies.

You will have the opportunity to be part of an organization with an international reputation, known for its cutting-edge technological research and scientific consultancy.

With us, you will contribute directly to sustainable developments at local, national and global level through your innovative applications. You provide answers to contemporary societal challenges.

Moreover, we highly value a good work-life balance at VITO! This is achieved by adopting a flexible attitude depending on your specific needs.

A NATO security clearance is required for this position and will be part of the onboarding process.

jobs.description:
Gawaya Baya Wind Farm | FIFO from Queensland | 2/1 Roster | Symal Infrastructure

Lead environmental performance on a landmark renewable energy project
.

Symal Infrastructure is delivering the Gawaya Baya Wind Farm, a major renewable energy project in North Queensland, and we’re seeking an experienced Senior Environmental Advisor to join our project HSEQ team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced environmental professional to take a senior role on a $347M major infrastructure project, working alongside an experienced project leadership team and playing a key role in driving environmental compliance, sustainability and performance across the project.

The project comprises approximately 400MW of renewable energy generation, 68 wind turbine generators, 78km of access roads, significant bulk earthworks, concrete works, drainage infrastructure and major bridge construction, with a peak workforce of approximately 300 personnel.

The Opportunity

As Senior Environmental Advisor, you’ll be a key environmental leader on the project, providing specialist advice and practical support to the Project Manager, Environment & Sustainability Manager, construction teams, subcontractors and client representatives.

You’ll have a strong field presence and be responsible for ensuring environmental requirements are embedded into day-to-day construction activities, while proactively identifying risks, driving compliance and supporting the project to achieve its environmental and sustainability objectives.

You’ll be responsible for:

Leading the implementation and ongoing review of the Project Environmental Management Plan, Sustainability Management Plans and associated environmental controls.
Providing senior technical advice to project leadership, construction teams and subcontractors on environmental risks, compliance and best practice.
Driving environmental compliance across construction activities and ensuring legislative, contractual and project requirements are understood and achieved.
Leading environmental inspections, audits, monitoring programs and risk assessments.
Identifying environmental risks and implementing practical mitigation and control measures.
Managing environmental approvals, permits, licences and associated conditions.
Reviewing and providing input into environmental documentation, including EMPs, SEPs, SMPs, SWMS, procedures and construction methodologies.
Maintaining a strong field presence and working directly with supervisors, engineers and subcontractors to ensure environmental controls are effective.
Leading the identification, investigation and close-out of environmental non-conformances and corrective actions.
Supporting and, where required, leading environmental incident investigations and ensuring appropriate preventative actions are implemented.
Supporting regulatory engagement and environmental reporting requirements.
Preparing environmental and sustainability reporting for project leadership, senior management and clients.
Supporting project audits and maintaining compliance with relevant environmental management standards, including ISO 14001.
Working closely with the Client HSEQ team and participating in environmental audits, risk workshops, project meetings and incident investigations.
Delivering environmental training, inductions and toolbox sessions to employees and subcontractors.
Coaching and mentoring junior environmental team members and supporting their professional development.
Identifying opportunities to improve environmental performance through innovation, technology and industry-leading practices.
Contributing to a strong environmental culture across the project and ensuring environmental performance remains a priority throughout delivery.

About You

We’re looking for a hands-on and commercially aware environmental professional who can operate confidently within a major construction project environment.

You’ll ideally have:

A tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management, Earth Sciences, Science, Engineering or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience in a Senior Environmental Advisor or Environmental Advisor role within civil construction, infrastructure, resources, renewable energy or major projects.
Strong knowledge of Australian environmental legislation, approvals, compliance requirements and construction environmental management.
Proven experience implementing Environmental Management Plans and environmental controls across major construction projects.
Strong experience conducting environmental inspections, audits, monitoring and risk assessments.
Experience managing environmental incidents, investigations, corrective actions and regulatory requirements.
The ability to provide confident and practical environmental advice to project managers, engineers, supervisors and subcontractors.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to build effective relationships with clients, regulators and project teams.
Excellent communication, reporting and documentation skills.
A proactive approach with the confidence to challenge poor environmental practices and drive positive outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and support less experienced environmental professionals.
White Card.
Current driver's licence.
Cert II Erosion and Sediment Control / Green Card, or equivalent experience, highly regarded.
ISCA Sustainability Accreditation desirable.

Why Join Symal?

At Symal, We Build Better Together.

We’re a team that rolls up our sleeves, gets involved and takes pride in delivering great outcomes. We value collaboration, different perspectives and people who are prepared to challenge the way things are done.

This is an opportunity to join a growing infrastructure business and work on a high-profile renewable energy project that will make a lasting contribution to Queensland's energy future.

You’ll work alongside experienced construction, project and HSEQ leaders while having the autonomy and support to make a genuine impact on environmental performance.

Career Development

At Symal, we invest in our people and support ongoing professional development across the HSEQ function.

You’ll have access to opportunities including:

Environmental management and compliance training
Environmental Management System auditing
ICAM training
ISCA sustainability development
Mentoring and leadership development
Progression into Environmental & Sustainability Management roles

The Gawaya Baya Project

Gawaya Baya Wind Farm is a major renewable energy development in North Queensland, approximately 2.5 hours from Townsville.

The project includes:

$347M D&C project
400MW renewable energy generation
68 wind turbine generators
78km of project roads
Approximately 1.8 million m³ of earthworks
Approximately 55,000 m³ of concrete
Major drainage and culvert work
60m Michael Creek bridge
Peak workforce of approximately 300 personnel

The Roster

2 weeks on / 1 week off

FIFO/DIDO opportunities are available from Queensland, with accommodation, flights/travel and site amenities provided in line with project arrangements.

Take the Next Step

If you’re an experienced environmental professional looking for the opportunity to take a senior role on a major renewable energy project, we’d love to hear from you.

Join Symal Infrastructure and help build the future of renewable energy in Queensland.

Apply now.

Help
