jobs.description:
Operations Field Manager - Restoration 
Power Dry | Columbus, OH

Who We Are
For over 37 years, Power Dry has been the trusted leader in water damage restoration, founded in the Kansas City metro area and expanding our footprint to Columbus, OH and Des Moines, IA. When water damage disrupts homes and businesses, our team delivers fast, reliable, high-quality service—bringing calm, clarity, and confidence to every situation. We build long-term partnerships by showing up, educating our clients, and doing what we say we will do.

Position Details

Job Type:
Full-time

Compensation:
Competitive base salary plus performance bonuses

Position Overview
The Operations Field Manager 
will be responsible for supervising and guiding a team of technicians in responding to property damage caused by water or mold. This role requires a proven ability to manage operations efficiently, ensure compliance with safety and quality standards, and maintain excellent customer relations. A strong knowledge of construction practices and jobsite safety protocols is essential. The ideal candidate will be proactive, detail-oriented, and highly skilled in both the technical and leadership aspects of mitigation work.

What You'll Do
Key responsibilities include:

Lead, coach, and develop the mitigation team to achieve operational excellence and exceptional customer satisfaction

Oversee mitigation projects from start to finish, ensuring quality workmanship and on-time completion

Conduct on-site inspections and provide hands-on leadership when needed

Direct crews in the field and ensure proper construction and mitigation methods are followed

Develop and improve operational workflows to maximize efficiency and productivity

Monitor project progress, resolve issues quickly, and ensure customer expectations are exceeded

Manage customer complaints and service issues through resolution, working directly with customers to address concerns and ensure a positive overall experience.

Hire, onboard, train, and mentor new team members

Conduct ongoing performance evaluations and provide coaching for continuous improvement

Collaborate with other department leaders to coordinate staffing, equipment, and project resources

Oversee inventory management and ensure equipment is properly maintained and available

Review construction plans, scopes of work, and project documentation

Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety standards, and industry best practices

Provide operational support during emergency situations, including after-hours response when needed

Monitor job costing, resource allocation, and operational performance

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience required

2–5 years of management experience in construction, restoration, or a related industry

Previous mitigation and restoration industry experience preferred

Hands-on construction experience strongly preferred

Strong understanding of financial reporting, job costing, and resource management

Demonstrated leadership experience with the ability to motivate and develop teams

Excellent communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills

Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and jobsite safety practices

Ability to read and interpret construction plans and project documentation

Bilingual (English/Spanish) is a plus

What Makes You Successful

High-energy, positive leadership style

Strong integrity and professionalism

Excellent time management and organizational skills

Customer-first mindset with the ability to remain calm under pressure

Hands-on approach and willingness to work alongside your team in the field

Ability to make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment

Benefits
We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

Competitive base salary plus performance bonuses

Bi-Weekly pay

Choice of medical plans, including select plans with $0 payroll cost for employee coverage

Dental insurance

Vision insurance

Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) for medical and dependent care expenses

Health Savings Account (HSA) available with qualifying high-deductible plans

Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance

Company-paid life insurance

401(k) with company match 

Paid time off

Paid holidays plus one floating holiday

Sick time that carries over year to year

Paid training and certification support

Opportunities for advancement and career growth

Travel reimbursement for work-related travel

Employee referral bonus program

Company-provided uniforms

Bring in the work. Generate and manage technical estimates on company leads and your own referral network, meeting or exceeding the sales and profitability goals Spyder sets.
Win through credibility. Walk potential projects, scope the repair accurately, and turn one solid inspection into a client who calls you directly next time.

Lead the room. Host project kickoffs, internal pre-construction meetings, and OAC meetings. Get the production team aligned on scope, budget, and schedule before work starts.
Step up when it gets hard. Be the escalation point project managers count on, resolve scope disputes and client issues, and help PMs grow.

What You Bring

The way you are wired:
You build trust through follow-through, not flash. People do business with you because you are accurate and dependable, not because you talked them into it.
You genuinely enjoy the hunt. New relationships and new business energize you, and you are comfortable initiating them yourself.
You work independently. You do not need to be managed to deliver, and you take ownership of the outcome either way.
You care about getting it right. Precision in your estimates and your word is what keeps clients coming back.
This role is not a fit if you need a lot of oversight, prefer working from a script, or would rather manage a pipeline than build one yourself. If that is you, this probably is not your seat, and that is fine. It saves everyone time to know now.

Active Colorado Asbestos Supervisor license

Valid Colorado driver's license and a record that meets Spyder requirements

4-year degree, preferably in Construction, Project Management, or a related field

Regular travel between job sites.

Why Spyder

Own the Outcome. Start it, finish it, own it.
Deliver Consistently. Maintain our standard, every time, everywhere.
Forge Real Relationships. Be authentic, earn trust.

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
Company-Paid Life Insurance
401(k) with 4% Company Match

Optional Accident and Critical Illness Insurance
Employee Assistance Program

Job Title: Environmental Program Manager
UCBEnvironmental is a family of companies focused on Sustainable Sustainability™. Through our five distinct divisions: UsedCardboardBoxes.com, UCBPalletSolutions, UCBOrganicWaste, UCBTrading and UCBZeroWaste… we service many of the largest, most trusted brands in the country!

UCBZeroWaste is a comprehensive fully managed waste reduction program. We are not a hauler! Nor do we compete with haulers; We manage them! We partner with the world leading companies to implement our proven methodology to reduce waste by focusing on the origin of waste (inside the building) as well as the processing of waste (outside the building). Our comprehensive programs include waste reduction, recycling, reuse, resale as well as de-packaging, digesting, composting and/or waste-to energy (WTE). UCBZeroWaste offers a (no-cost) comprehensive waste audit in order to quantify the financial and environmental opportunity.

Why work at UCB:
• Competitive Salary
• Longevity Bonus
• A Player Bonus
• Year-End Profit-Sharing Bonus
• Your work helps reduce environmental impact.
• Supportive and accessible leadership team
• Work with a passionate and collaborative team of people
• Career growth opportunities
• Work with the biggest most well-known companies.

Work Hours and Schedule: Night Shift - U.S. Business Hours (Monday to Friday)
Work Duration: Full-time (40 hours per week)

Summary:
The Program Manager/Environmental Program Manager is responsible for overseeing and managing the UCBZeroWaste implementation projects to ensure they are completed in a timely fashion and profitably. The Project Manager is in charge of setting short- and long-term milestones together with the National Implementation Managers (the clients’ account managers) to ensure UCBZeroWaste is delivering to the contracted clients what was promised on our proposals and agreements, including the six-step proven process. The Project Manager is in control of properly documenting the implementation milestones on UCB’s tracking systems, monitoring progress, and keeping internal stakeholders informed the entire way.

Responsibilities:
• Create long- and short-term plans, including setting targets for milestones and adhering to deadlines
• Predict resources needed to reach objectives and manage resources in an effective and efficient manner
• Create and document detailed "Implementation Process Steps" for new clients or expansion of existing clients to clarify client deliverables and expectations
• Make effective decisions when presented with multiple options for how to progress with the project

and related experience

• Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tasks efficiently

• Excellent communication skills (verbal and written)

jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is hosting an exclusive, invitation-only hiring event in Boston on October 21-22.
This is a great opportunity to learn and connect with AECOM for career opportunities starting Spring/Summer 2027.

The event kicks off on Wednesday evening with a networking mixer
, where you can hear from AECOM staff about various projects, career paths, and the company itself. You’ll also have the chance to meet other students, recent graduates, and AECOM professionals from across our business lines.

On Thursday, interviews will take place at our Boston office
. This is a fantastic opportunity to learn about and connect with AECOM for early career opportunities

AECOM
is seeking an Entry-Level Environmental Engineer to be based in our Rocky Hill, CT office. This position will support our Remediation team within our Environment business line.

This position is expected to begin June 2027, but that date is flexible.

Job Overview:

The Entry-Level Environmental Engineer will serve as a team member in the office and the field, assisting project and program management with site investigation, design and implementation of soil, groundwater, sediment and surface water remediation programs, data analysis, remediation construction and program management, and report preparation. This role is approximately 60% field and 40% office.

Our teams work on complex remediation projects, accessing the right resources from across the company to support project needs. By joining our team, you will have the opportunity to work on diverse projects that will challenge you technically while giving you the opportunity to work with experienced colleagues and subject matter specialists in a variety of areas. Together, these opportunities will aid in your growth in this industry.

The job responsibilities of this position may include, but are not limited to:
Project field and office support for site assessment and remediation projects.
Site visits at industrial, federal, commercial, and municipal client facilities
Data collection and analysis for environmental compliance and sustainability. Compares findings to relevant studies and local, state and federal regulations to ensure compliance.
Environmental sampling (e.g., soil, sediment, groundwater, stormwater, wastewater, air, and hazardous waste)
Development of technical memoranda and reports
Building analytic and engineering design skills under the supervision of an experienced engineer
Use of computer software (e.g. CAD, GIS, data analysis tools) as a tool for solving basic engineering problems
Performing work in accordance with agreed upon budget and schedule under supervision
Local travel is likely and U.S travel possible and project dependent.
Field work in locations as appropriate (approximately 60%).

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:
BA/BS in Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering or related field + 0 years of related experience and/or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
Valid US Driver’s License and as a condition of employment must pass the AECOM Motor Vehicle screening
Due to the nature of work, U.S. Citizenship is required
Position requires frequent traveling to field locations in personal vehicle. Locations and distances vary and could include occasional overnight travel and operation of rental vehicle. Frequently lifting, carrying, and loading equipment such as sample coolers, without assistance up to 50lbs.

Preferred Qualifications:
General knowledge of basic engineering, chemistry, and environmental sciences
Experience and/or demonstrated interest in environmental remediation
Proficiency in standard Microsoft Office suite software applications
Ability to demonstrate professional demeanor in written and verbal communications with clients, regulatory officials, and fellow employees
Ability to write and to convey complex thoughts and ideas in a clear, concise manner
Ability to learn through on-the-job experience
Tolerance for work in outdoor environments in a range of weather conditions
Ability to work independently, both in an office environment and in the field
OSHA 40 Hour HAZWOPER Certification
Ability to travel locally, including occasional extended travel
Previous experience operating a full-size pickup truck or large sport utility vehicle
Mechanical aptitude is strongly desired
Passing Engineering-in-Training (FE) test is strongly recommended

Additional Information

Relocation is not available for this position
Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $65000 to $75000.

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Staff Environmental Engineer I
jobs.description:
Position Overview

This position will assist the project team and Project Manager in providing field support, and technical assistance on environmental investigation and remediation projects.

Position Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in relevant technical field.
Typically requires 0-2 years of experience.
Ability to safely perform various routine field activities including but not limited to applying proper sampling techniques for all environmental media and overseeing and directing subcontractors.
Exhibits strong work ethic, positive attitude, and general enthusiasm for the work.
Entry level data evaluation and analytical skills.

Essential Duties

Field Activities:
Assists other technical staff in calibration of sampling/monitoring equipment, soil sampling, well installation, development and purging, groundwater sampling, vapor/indoor air sampling, remediation monitoring, and oversight.

Project Assistance:
Assists project team in preparation and review of data tables, soil boring logs, and figures and other components of technical reports.

Physical Demands/Work Environment Conditions

This position works predominantly in the field working independently or as part of a larger team at exterior project sites (i.e., industrial/brownfield facilities, monitoring wells, treatment systems, construction projects) to perform sample collection, recording of operational/meter parameters, and oversight of subcontractors (e.g., drillers, heavy equipment operators, truckers). These field activities require the ability to drive to different project sites and physically move around outdoors in various terrains, in adverse weather conditions and occasionally for extended or irregular hours. Conducting work involves the use of hand-held monitoring instruments and tools, as well as water sampling equipment, which requires the ability to routinely lift and carry objects, stand, walk, reach, bend, squat, kneel and twist. Office work is primarily stationary/sedentary using a computer and keyboard/mouse requiring repetitive hand movements.

Base Salary Range: $65,000 - $75,000. This salary range is based on what Roux in good faith believes it might pay at the time of posting for this position and for this geographic location. Actual compensation may vary based on job-related factors such as relevant work experience, market conditions, education/training, certifications, skill sets, and internal equity. In addition, this position is eligible for performance bonuses based on individual job performance and the profitability of the firm.

Roux offers a comprehensive benefits package for this position including:

Medical, dental, and vision care coverage for employees and eligible dependents
401(k) profit sharing plan with employer match
Flexible Spending Accounts
Company paid life insurance and disability insurance
Supplemental life, long-term care, accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance
Employee Assistance Program

Paid Parental Leave

jobs.title: Director/Senior Attorney, Land Conservation
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Land Conservation Director/Senior Attorney will lead a team of experienced land conservation advocates who focus on safeguarding our priceless public lands to preserve critical ecological and cultural values. This includes working defensively against the onslaught of attempts to sell off public lands, protecting bedrock conservation laws, elevating targeted campaigns in priority landscapes, and promoting durable, conservation focused solutions to meeting energy demands. The Director will play an important leadership role in NRDC’s lands work - joining the Lands Division Leadership team, collaborating with teams and leadership across NRDC, and engaging on external campaigns and coalitions. In addition to serving as a Senior Attorney and thought leader for Land Conservation advocacy, the Director will oversee the team’s day-to-day work, engage in fundraising, guide communications efforts, and help lead priority state and federal legislative and administrative advocacy campaigns.

This role will operate in a hybrid remote capacity in any of our US NRDC Offices (
Chicago, Santa Monica, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C.)

Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the following essential functions:
Manage the land conservation team, which consists of lawyers, scientists and policy advocates advancing critical land conservation efforts, including public lands defense and conservation focused solutions to meeting energy demands.
Develop and lead Land Conservation team strategies and goals, ensuring alignment with fundraising, institutional priorities, team members expertise and capacity, and key partnerships.
Represent NRDC and the Land Conservation team as an authoritative source both internally as well as externally in public forums, including administrative proceedings, legislative committee hearings, and media outlets.
Build and maintain relationships with partners, coalitions, decisionmakers, and other stakeholders to guide strategy, influence policy outcomes, and identify advocacy needs.
Oversee staff performance and provide mentoring, guidance, and on-going feedback to ensure that staff develop and reach performance goals that support division priorities, institutional DEI, professional development, and management needs.
Provide legal expertise and guidance to Nature Leadership and staff, including other NRDC departments, on priority strategies and related legal, technical and/or policy issues; and help develop and oversee litigation on priority public lands issues, in collaboration with NRDC’s Litigation Team.

The above list of duties is not comprehensive but generally demonstrates the types of matters under this position’s responsibility. Other duties may be assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Education & Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience required, with authoritative knowledge concerning land conservation. Law degree required.; litigation experience preferred.
7+ years of experience of legal and/or policy advocacy, including 3 years of management experience. Experience leading state or federal campaigns, litigating and advocating for public lands preferred.
Experience successfully building and navigating diverse teams and/or coalitions, including developing consensus on policy issues and driving toward equitable, positive outcomes.

Skills, Abilities, Competencies

An ability to foster and cultivate a positive, inclusive and equitable working environment with colleagues, leadership and external stakeholders.
Advanced interpersonal skills and the ability to provide leadership, guidance, feedback, and coaching in the context of employee engagement, team/coalition building, and project and people management.
Excellent organizational and project management skills.
An ability to effectively communicate and deploy written and verbal skills to advance complex concepts.
Excellent strategic judgment, integrity, professional discretion, and ability to handle sensitive/confidential matters.
Ability to travel to NRDC U.S. based offices, approximately 20% annually
Commitment to NRDC’s mission, values, and DEI principles

-------------------------------------
NRDC (the Natural Resources Defense Council) works to safeguard the Earth, its people, its plants and animals, and the natural systems on which all life depends. NRDC combines the power of more than 3 million members and online activists with the expertise of some 800 policy advocates, lawyers, scientists, and communication experts to confront the climate crisis, protect nature, ensure the rights of all people to clean air, clean water, and healthy communities. As an international nonprofit environmental organization, NRDC is working to address the world’s most urgent environmental challenges, and advance innovative, science-based, and enforceable solutions.

Since our founding in 1970, NRDC has helped craft and deliver many of America’s foundational environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act. Today, we continue to lead in advancing and defending strong environmental protections at the local, state, federal and international levels, as well as through the marketplace. Our team works across the United States and around the world, from offices in Chicago, Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C., as well as in Beijing, and New Delhi (a subsidiary of NRDC India Pvt. jobs.title: Geospatial Surveyor
jobs.description:
Join a team delivering complex, high-impact projects that shape infrastructure, utilities and the built environment across the UK. At Tetra Tech, you’ll combine advanced geospatial expertise with real project ownership, working on technically challenging surveys that support major programmes across water, defence, nuclear and infrastructure sectors.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As a Geospatial Surveyor, you will deliver surveying and geospatial projects from initial planning through to final delivery, supporting a diverse range of technically demanding projects across the UK. Working within a collaborative national team, you’ll combine field-based surveying with office-based data processing and analysis to produce high-quality outputs for clients across multiple sectors.

This role offers genuine variety, autonomy and client exposure, giving you the opportunity to take ownership of projects while developing your technical and professional capabilities in a supportive environment focused on innovation, collaboration and continuous development.

Your Impact in this Position

You’ll play a key role in delivering accurate geospatial information that supports critical engineering, infrastructure and asset management decisions. Your expertise in surveying, data capture and interpretation will help clients manage complex projects safely, efficiently and effectively.

By building strong client relationships and delivering reliable technical outputs, you’ll contribute directly to successful project outcomes while strengthening the reputation of Tetra Tech’s Geospatial team across the UK and beyond.

Core Capabilities
Geospatial Survey Delivery

Deliver geospatial surveying projects from inception through to completion
Carry out topographical, setting-out, measured building, levelling and laser scanning surveys

Data Capture & Technical Analysis

Capture, process and interpret high-quality survey data using industry-leading technologies
Produce accurate outputs using AutoCAD, Leica Infinity and related software tools

Survey Technology Expertise

Operate Total Station and GNSS equipment confidently across varied project environments
Apply modern surveying techniques to support technically complex projects

Client & Project Collaboration

Build strong working relationships with clients and multidisciplinary project teams
Balance site-based and office-based responsibilities while managing competing priorities effectively

Professionalism & Adaptability

Work independently with a proactive, solutions-focused approach
Adapt to different sectors, project locations and operational requirements

Training, Qualifications & Experience

Experience in topographical surveying, survey software and GNSS/Total Station equipment is essential, alongside strong communication and client-facing skills. Experience with laser scanning, levelling, measured building surveys or terrain modelling would be advantageous, as would a relevant technical qualification. A full UK driving licence is required.

Working Environment

This role offers a balance of site, office and hybrid working, with flexibility available where practical to support work/life balance. Projects are located across the UK, with occasional international opportunities and travel depending on project requirements. You’ll join a collaborative and supportive team environment with opportunities for professional development and chartership support.

Tetra Tech is a leading provider of consulting and engineering services working across the full project lifecycle worldwide. We have a wide range of expertise across our teams, providing a global support network with a personalised approach to client relationships to better understand where we can add value. We provide a collaborative environment that supports individual performance, innovation, and creativity.

We support public and private sector clients on local, national, and international projects to deliver sustainable and resilient solutions. Our operations in the UK, Ireland, and the Netherlands include more than 6,000 employees who are Leading with Science® to solve our clients’ most complex problems.

jobs.title: Graduate Environmental Planning Consultant
jobs.description:
Location: London, Birmingham or Leicester

Start Date: September 2027

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

Tetra Tech Europe is an industry-leading multi-national, multi-disciplinary consultancy. Our Environmental Planning Team supports the continued growth of the UK Environment, Sustainability & Planning (ESP) team and wider business, delivering environmental co-ordination, EIA and related assessment and management work across renewables/energy, water/utilities, residential, defence, infrastructure, waste and minerals. You’ll join a team with an established workload, a strong reputation, ISEP EIA Quality Mark membership and active involvement in industry working groups, presentations and conferences.

Your Impact in this position

Working with support from senior colleagues, you’ll contribute to environmental planning, optioneering and impact assessment across a varied project portfolio. You’ll help deliver work to programme, budget and quality standards, build your skills in project management, business development and technical assessment, and produce technically robust outputs that inform responsible project decisions.

5 Core Capabilities

Project Co-ordination Support – Support project managers across multiple projects, working with teams, stakeholders and subcontractors, and helping programme site surveys.
Environmental Impact Assessment – Assist with screening, scoping, data collection, impact assessment and reporting, with working knowledge of EIA Regulations and the EIA process.
Report Writing and Communication – Prepare clear reports such as EIAs and CEMPs, present findings where needed, and review deliverables for accuracy and compliance.
Collaboration Across Disciplines – Work with colleagues in air quality, biodiversity, land use, transport and other teams to assess impacts and mitigation.
Technical Specialism Development – Build expertise in climate change, socio-economics, human health, natural capital or construction phase environmental management.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

A Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Management or a related field, plus academic and/or practical EIA experience. Knowledge of environmental laws, regulations, guidelines and the UK planning/consenting process is essential, alongside strong communication, coordination, time management, problem-solving, attention to detail and analytical skills.

Working Environment

This is a graduate role based in a supportive consultancy environment, with hybrid working available in line with team and project needs. As you develop in the role, there will be an expectation to spend more time in the office initially to support learning, collaboration and onboarding. The role may also involve occasional travel to site or other offices as required.

About The Role

Introduction Do you possess strong analytical skills and are you open to a unique mental and physical challenge in a varied work environment? Do you hold a WO (university) degree in fields such as Geology, Geography, Technology, Biometrics, or Nuclear Technology? The Dutch Land Forces are seeking a Geospatial Analyst Officer (Intelligence & Security – I&V GSA). Your workplace will be at the barracks, but also during exercises and deployments. Note: Attendance at the info day on 13 May is mandatory to participate in the application process. If selected, you will be appointed by the Ministry of Defence as an ‘Officier Inlichtingen & Veiligheid (I&V) Geospatial Analist (GSA)’. What You’ll Do As an I&V GSA, you’ll work in a multidisciplinary team of analysts, supporting missions, projects, deployments, and exercises—lasting from a few weeks up to 4–6 months. Your core responsibility is to describe and analyze the spatial and temporal aspects of the physical environment and events occurring within it. Your analyses may include: Suitability analyses Terrain analyses Geostatistics Remote sensing analyses Your geospatial insights will be integrated with analyses from other disciplines to build operational situational awareness and produce intelligence products that support military planning and decision-making. Key Benefits Salary: Gross base salary of €4,052–€4,463 per month, with allowances, favorable travel expense reimbursement, and comprehensive pension and health insurance—resulting in a net income that’s pleasantly surprising. Work Environment: You’ll become part of an exceptionally close-knit team—unmatched anywhere else. Career Development: Defensie is not only an employer but also a major training institution, offering opportunities for personal and professional growth. After attending the info day, you may join the selection process, which lasts ~6–9 months and includes multiple stages (see details at the bottom of the page). Where You’ll Work You’ll be stationed at the Joint ISTAR Commando (JISTARC) in ’t Harde. ISTAR stands for Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition, and Reconnaissance. JISTARC collects and analyzes information to provide military commanders with the most complete and up-to-date operational picture possible. As a GSA, you’ll be both a geospatial specialist and a military officer. While your primary workplace is the barracks in ’t Harde, you’ll also participate in domestic and international exercises and deployments (e.g., missions in Mali, Lithuania, and others). You’ll collaborate closely with international partners of the Dutch Armed Forces—and may support police investigations under Defensie’s third core task. Training Pathway Before starting your role, you’ll complete: Defensiebrede Korte Officiersopleiding (DKOO) – a 1-year officer training at the Royal Military Academy (KMA) in Breda. Vaktechnische Opleiding (VTO) Intelligence & Security (I&V) – a 7-month specialized training at the Intelligence & Security Academy (ISA). Upon successful completion, you’ll begin your career as an I&V Geospatial Analyst Officer in the Land Forces—and receive additional geo-specific training during your first year on the job. Contact & Logistics Location: ’t Harde Salary Range: €4,200 – €5,600 (gross, including allowances) Annual Leave: 23–30 days Free Driver’s License: Obtained at no cost Questions? Email: JISTARC.106INLCIE.SOLLICITATIES@mindef.nl The Royal Netherlands Army considers your preferred location, but may adjust placement for organizational reasons. You’ll be informed of your final posting during the VTO. We Believe in Your Potential Maybe you’re unsure—we’re not. We don’t just see who you are today—we see who you can become. What you can’t do today, you’ll learn tomorrow. With top-tier training, coaching, and a supportive team behind you, we’ll help you grow. If challenges arise, we’ll find the right fit together. jobs.description:
About The Job

We have a vacancy for a researcher at the Department of Psychology in the research group for Citizens, Environment and Safety for 2 years.

The Position Combines Work In Three Externally Funded Projects

The HARMONI project aims to develop a comprehensive knowledge toolbox for hybrid products that combine the benefits of cultivated and plant-based meat alternatives, enabling the creation of appealing new food concepts and expanding future food choices. To achieve this, HARMONI brings together a consortium of Cellular Agriculture and Bioprocess Engineering (Technical University of Munich), Meat Science, Cultivated Muscle Cells and Nutrition (Aarhus University), Material Science and Microbial Systems (Katholieke Universiteit Leuven), Sustainable Food Systems (University of Helsinki), and Environmental and Consumer Psychology (NTNU), complemented by leading industrial partners. The part of NTNU is to study consumer perceptions of such products with focus group interviews, experiments and surveys. Data is likely collected in Norway, Germany, Belgium, and Finnland.
The cells4energy project is a real-world laboratory for 100% renewable energy systems. At its core lies the systemic energy cell approach, where locally generated renewable energy is intelligently stored, utilized, and interconnected with other cells. Through digital technologies and innovative business models, we test in real-world environments how a flexible, resilient, and scalable energy supply can be achieved for the future. The task for NTNU in this project is to implement and analyse the results from an automatized internet-based intervention platform to motivate energy saving. Data will be collected in Austria.
The SaferClay project is a research project focusing on developing methods to assess changes in quick clay landslide risk with time. SAFERCLAY will provide a new approach for adapted and sustainable risk management for living and building in quick clay areas, including recommendations to ensure both public and environmental safety. NTNUs task in this project is analysing perceptions of quick clay and its effects on behaviour in different stakeholder groups. A survey has been designed and is currently implemented in Norway.

What binds the work in all three projects together is the focus on collecting citizen / stakeholder perceptions on novel products, risk factors, and behaviour interventions. In all three projects, these will primarily be studied with quantitative methods, thus excellent knowledge of quantitative analysis methods, data curation and handling, as well as designing research and surveys is essential.

Your immediate leader is the head of department.

Duties of the position

Designing surveys, experiments and qualitative interviews with the respective project groups
Implementation of data collections (in cells4energy coordinated with an external technology provider for the internet platform)
Data cleaning and curation
Data analyses (mainly quantitative, but also qualitatitve)
Preparation of research papers based on the analyses
Feedback and coordination with the research partners

Required Selection Criteria

A finished degree or PhD in psychology with a specialization in environmental psychology, social psychology, behavioural psychology or closely related fields
Excellent skills in data management, curation and complex statistical analysis (e.g. structural equation modelling)
Experience in empirical work in the field
Good written and oral English skills

Preferred Selection Criteria

Experience with work in interdisciplinary fields
Experience with project management
Ability to communicate in at least one of the languages data in the different projects will be collected in (Norwegian, German, Finnish, Flemish, French) in addition to English
Experience with qualitative work

Personal characteristics

Flexibility
Ability to structure your work and handle three projects at the same time
Openness for collaboration with other disciplines and practice partners

We offer

exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment
an open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues
favourable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
employee benefits

Salary and conditions

As a researcher (code 1109) you are normally paid from gross NOK 633 400 per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The position is subject to external funding.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU.

After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

About The Application

Your application and supporting documentation must be in English.

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note:
the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your Application Must Include

CV, diplomas, and certificates
A motivation letter (max 2 pages) outlining your motivation and fit for the position
Academic works – published or unpublished – that you wish to be considered during assessment of your application (up to 5 items)
A description of the scientific/artistic works you consider most relevant, which you particularly wish to be factored into the assessment
A complete publication list
Details of projects for which you have served as project manager or had a significant position in, including information on financing, duration, and scope
Names and contact information for three relevant referees

It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for documentation of your competence.

Joint work will also be considered. If it is difficult to identify your specific input to a joint project, you must include evidence of your contributions.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

NTNU is obliged by the evaluation criteria for research quality in accordance with The San Fransisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and The obligations in the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment ( CoARA) on responsible assessment of research and recognition of a wider range of academic contributions to science and society. This means that we will pay particular attention to the quality and academic range demonstrated by your scientific work to date. We will also pay attention to research leadership and participation in research projects. Your scientific work from the last five years will be given the most weight.

Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview.

General information

Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Christian Klöckner, e-mail Christian.klockner@ntnu.no

If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact Ina Grønbech Halvorsen, e-mail Ina.G.Halvorsen@ntnu.no

About Us

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview

We are seeking a Project Manager to join our Planning, Permitting and Licensing practice in Houston, TX.

Responsibilities

The main focus of this role is to support a growing energy (oil and gas, data centers, renewables) practice as a Project Manager. Responsible for managing environmental reports and complex field and desktop assessments, and environmental permitting.
Have a significant role in maintaining quality and profitability on TRC’s projects.
Budget, scope, and schedule development, monitoring and adherence for tasks and projects managed.
Lead solicitation requests working with technical teams, operations, and market directors.
Successfully manage medium to large-scale, often multi-disciplinary projects and maintain productive working relationships with clients.
Lead FERC Environmental Reporting efforts.
Lead applicant prepared and/or third-party environmental planning pertaining to NEPA to meet requirements/regulations to facilitate advancement of the design or construction of projects including preparation of Environmental Assessments and Environmental Impact Statements.
Lead permitting efforts with the USACE wetland/stream delineations, CWA Section 404 permitting and ESA threatened and endangered species habitat assessments.
Lead state and local permitting efforts.
Mentor and coach staff on technical delivery, quality, and project financials.
This individual will be responsible for selling environmental planning and permitting services for energy clients. When feasible, this individual should look to sell all of TRC’s Sector Services, e.g., Environmental, Power, Infrastructure, and Field Services (known as “OneTRC”).
An average of 25% of work time could account for out-of-town traveling.

Qualifications

Bachelor of Science/Arts degree in biology or a related field (i.e., ecology, wildlife biology, aquatic biology, botany, zoology, environmental science, natural resources management).
10 to 15 years of experience performing and managing the environmental planning, permitting, and licensing projects with a focus on energy projects.
Possess strong verbal, written, presentation and excellent client management skills; demonstrated ability leading and managing complex projects; as well as being goal oriented, quality focused, and have demonstrated success with creating and fostering a team environment.
Local regulatory experience in the Southeast with USACE, USFWS, State Wildlife and Natural Resource Agencies, and Local Governments.
NEPA experience completing Environmental Assessments and/or Environmental Impact Statements.
The successful candidate must provide demonstrated experience being a primary author on natural resources reports for a variety of agencies and project types/sizes.
Proven track record with business development, business management and oversight of regional businesses.
Experience managing cross disciplinary scientific and engineering teams and front-end project development projects.
Strong business acumen and attributes, coupled with a commitment to TRC Values: Safety, Quality, Integrity, Creativity, Accountability, Teamwork and Passion.

Medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance.
401k package that includes both traditional and Roth IRA options and Company match.

All full-time employees enjoy a minimum of 8 Paid Holidays per year.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TvscsQSYIM

About Cdphe

At the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, we are charged with protecting Colorado’s health and

environment – a responsibility that affects every person and every community in the state. CDPHE is distinctive because we bring public health and environmental protection together under one agency, recognizing that healthy people depend on healthy places. Our teams prevent diseases and injury, respond to emergencies ranging from E.coli outbreaks to global pandemics, reduce air pollution, protect water quality, regulate health facilities, manage environmental hazards, perform advanced laboratory testing, provide birth and death records, and implement health promoting programs. We turn science and data into action, set statewide standards, and work alongside local public health agencies and community partners to meet Colorado’s most pressing health and environmental challenges. Working at CDPHE means applying your expertise to complex, consequential work that can improve lives across the state.

Our mission captures this broad portfolio of work: to advance Colorado’s health and protect the places we live, learn, work, and play. Our vision is a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations can thrive. Achieving the mission and vision takes bold action, talented people, broad partnerships, and a commitment to serving every Coloradan.

Important Information

This position will have hybrid workplace options available but will still be required to report to the listed address at the discretion of the supervisor and based on business needs.
The referral list generated by this position announcement may be used to fill multiple position vacancies and may be extended.

CDPHE offers:

CDPHE offers a comprehensive benefits package and the opportunity to build a meaningful career in public service. Benefits include:

Medical and dental plans.
Colorado PERA retirement options, including defined benefit plan or defined contribution plan.
Optional 401(K) and 457 retirement plans.
Employer-paid life insurance.
Short- and long-term disability coverage.
Potential flexible working arrangements
11 paid holidays per year and generous paid time off.
Free parking and access to RTD bus lines.
Tuition assistance.
Employee wellness programs.
Professional development opportunities.
Career opportunities throughout Colorado state government.
Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program .

Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program. For more information, go to: https://studentloans.gov/myDirectLoan/pslfFlow.action#!/pslf/launch

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Toxicology and Risk Assessment (TARA) Program is under the direction of the Division of Environmental Health and Sustainability Deputy Director and exists to provide epidemiologic research, surveillance data, toxicology and health risk assessment assistance, and consultation to CDPHE management, divisions and programmatic units; federal and local public health and environmental agencies and officials; and businesses and the public. Our programs span the topics of exposure to toxic substances (e.g., lead, mercury, carbon monoxide, and pesticides), cancer clusters, oil and

gas health impacts, and more.

TARA responds to community concerns about environmental exposures and disease clusters. Staff members provide expertise and oversight for state and community-based environmental health research, health surveillance, and biomonitoring.

The Regulatory Toxicology Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. The Regulatory Toxicology Workgroup conducts health risk investigations and evaluates environmental exposures, hazards and health status of communities. The purpose of this workgroup is to (1) provide statewide consultation to the department's environmental programs other state agencies federal agencies (US EPA, ATSDR) local public health departments, and the general public and (2) conduct public health assessment to identify potential impacts from environmental chemical exposures. The work unit is responsible for reviewing, interpreting and presenting on the toxicological properties of chemicals as it relates to evaluating the public health risks from environmental chemical exposures.

The Emerging Issues Work Group is a work group within the Environmental Contaminants Health and Outreach Unit within TARA. The purpose of this work group is to: (1) be a resource on the relationship between PFAS/emerging issues exposure and public health for stakeholders including: TARA, DEHS, other CDPHE divisions, other state agencies, federal agencies, and the general public; (2) increase transparency and understanding of PFAS/emerging issue data and what it means for public health;

What You Will Do

The purpose of this position is to support science communication needs for the ECHO unit. This includes translating

complex technical information into understandable information for a variety of stakeholders through appropriate

methods. In addition, this position is responsible for evaluating the effectiveness of communications to different

stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Based on guidance and support from senior TARA staff, provides risk consultation and communication expertise on environmental health problems to local public health agencies, and other stakeholders as needed.
With support of senior outreach staff, educate communities, local public health partners, and local policymakers about environmental health risks and protective measures.
With the guidance and support of other TARA staff, conduct data analysis, visualization, and interpretation to assist in data-driven decision making on environmental contaminants.
With the guidance and support of other TARA staff, conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis on the effectiveness of communication and outreach methods for different stakeholders.
Participate in responding to technical inquiries from the public (i.e., Toxcall, PFAS TAP).
Assists with public workshops, seminars and other meetings.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions Of Employment & Appeal Rights

Residency Requirement
This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

Class Code & Classification Description

I3B2T* Physical Science Researcher/Scientist I

NOTE: An applicant may meet the minimum qualifications for this job in one of two ways: They may qualify through their work experience alone or through a combination of education and work experience.

Experience Only

Five (5) years experience in a related field such as toxicology, environmental science, environmental public health, human health risk assessment, education, and community engagement and outreach.

OR

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in biology, chemistry, toxicology, environmental science, public health, education, communication, journalism, or closely related field AND
one (1) year experience synthesizing toxicology, risk assessment, or data analysis information into clear communications on scientific issues or closely related work experience.

You must substantiate that you meet the minimum qualifications when filling out the Work Experience section of the application. Failure to do so will result in the application not moving forward in the hiring process. “See resume” will not be accepted. Resumes are considered supplemental information and are not considered in the initial evaluation. In addition, part-time work will be prorated when determining whether minimum qualifications are met.* *

Preferred Qualifications

In addition to the minimum requirements, the successful candidate in this position will have the following highly desirable experience and competencies:

Demonstrated experience serving as a resource for explaining the complexities of environmental exposures in public health.
Previous experience in developing health education materials (verbal and written) that educate affected communities about the relationship between hazards and risks associated with contaminants.
Excellent critical thinking and problem solving skills.
Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.
Excellent writing skills.
Ability to interpret and analyze data.
Ability to work well independently and within a team.
Masters or other advanced degree in public environmental health, toxicology, or closely related field.

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by delivering innovative solutions that create a more connected, sustainable world. As an Environmental Planner 
based in  Atlanta, Georgia
, you'll support federal, state, and local infrastructure projects across our  Environmental Planning & Permitting team
, including transportation programs that help shape the future of communities throughout the Southeast.

In this role, you'll contribute to the successful delivery of environmental planning and compliance services for complex infrastructure projects. In the immediate term, this role is designated to provide environmental planning support on a large multi-phased P3 transportation project. Working alongside planners, scientists, engineers, and communications professionals, you'll help guide projects through the environmental review process, develop high-quality NEPA documentation, coordinate with agencies and stakeholders, and support project teams in achieving regulatory compliance while advancing client objectives.

What You'll Do

Assist with the management and preparation of NEPA documentation, including Categorical Exclusions (CEs), Environmental Assessments (EAs), and Environmental Impact Statements (EISs), and Re-Evaluations for Design-Bid-Build and Design-Build projects
Coordinate with engineering teams to evaluate alternatives and develop avoidance and minimization measures for environmental and community impacts
Support public involvement, stakeholder engagement, and agency coordination activities
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to prepare technical studies and environmental compliance documentation
Assist with the development and review of scopes of work, project schedules, cost estimates, and technical proposals
Assist with the management of multiple projects and deliverables simultaneously while maintaining quality and schedule commitments
Maintain environmental permitting schedules and project records
Support planning, engineering, and construction projects for transportation and other public-sector clients.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Planning, Environmental Science, or a related field.
2+ years of experience as a NEPA Analyst supporting transportation infrastructure projects.
Understanding of the NEPA process and relevant state DOT environmental procedures
Strong working knowledge of NEPA and applicable environmental regulations, including Section 4(f), Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, and other relevant environmental requirements
Familiarity with the development and management of project scopes, schedules, and budgets
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and ability to work collaboratively

Ideally, you'll also have

Master's degree in Planning, Environmental Science, or a related field.
Experience with state and federal environmental permitting requirements
Experience with ArcGIS.
Experience with developing and implementing public and stakeholder engagement strategies.

Key Skills & Attributes

Strong program-level thinking and ability to manage complex, multidisciplinary efforts
Ability to manage multiple simultaneous workflows
Strong cross-discipline integration capabilities
Ability to identify and resolve schedule risks
Effective communication with clients, agencies, and program leadership

The ideal start date for this role is within the following timeframe September 21, 2026 – October 30, 2026.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $75,300.00 to $117,600.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on September 02, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
GIS Analyst

Rock Energy Cooperative

South Beloit, Illinois

Job Summary:

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated GIS Analyst to join our team. The successful candidate will play a key role in managing and analyzing geographic data to support our organization's day-to-day operations and long-term objectives. The candidate must work with operations staff and field staff to identify ways to optimize established workflows, data capture processes, and reporting systems.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

GIS Database Management
Design, implement and maintain GIS databases to store and retrieve spatial data
Ensure data integrity and accuracy through regular quality checks and updates

Mapping and Spatial Analysis
Conduct spatial analysis to support decision-making processes
Generate insightful reports and visualizations based on spatial data analysis
Create and export custom map images to communicate information to technical and non-technical audiences

Data Collection and Integration
Collect and integrate geographic data from various sources, including satellite imagery, GPS, and field surveys
Collaborate with other departments to incorporate non-spatial data into GIS databases

Workflow Automation
Incorporate programming and scripting languages to automate regular and or frequent ETL processes
Utilize built-in GIS data relationships to reduce manual data entry and ensure accurate data capture quality

Software and Technology
Stay abreast of the latest GIS technologies and software
Provide training and support to staff on GIS tools and applications

Documentation
Document GIS procedures, data sources, and workflows for future reference
Ensure that all GIS activities comply with organizational and industry standards

Other tasks and duties as assigned

Competencies:

Problem-solving and process-driven thinking
Attention to detail
Ability to multitask
Strong work ethic
Work independently and in a team-focused environment
Strong communication skills, particularly in conveying technical knowledge and processes to non-technical staff

Preferred Skills and Qualifications:

Education

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Computer Science, Geography, Surveying, Engineering, or related field

Experience

2 years of experience in a GIS-focused role, including the following:
Experience in the utility industry, with natural gas distribution and/or electric distribution
Experience with SQL Database Management
Experience with editing and managing spatial data within the utility industry

Technology

Familiarity interacting with ArcGIS Utility Network
Familiarity with web-based GIS services in an ArcGIS Enterprise environment
Proficiency in GIS software including ArcMap, ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Survey123, and ArcGIS Field Maps
Familiarity with programming and scripting languages for the purpose of developing extract, transfer, and load processes including Python, SQL, JavaScript, and ArcGIS Arcade
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, SQL Server Management Studio, AutoCAD
Familiarity with PHP/HTML is beneficial but not required

Qualifications:

Must have and maintain a valid driver’s license
Must have reliable transportation to and from work
Reside within one hour driving distance of work location
Ability to sit, stand, push, pull, walk, stoop, bend, reach above the shoulders, and occasionally lift up to 25 lbs.
Pre-employment drug testing and physical required

Work Location:
South Beloit, IL

Schedule:

This is an in-person position
Monday through Friday (excluding some holidays)
7:30 am – 4:00 pm

Salary:

$60 - $70,000 per year

Benefits:

Medical, prescription and dental benefits at an 85%/15% employee split
401K with 4% employer contribution
Employer funded pension plan

Full Time

jobs.title: Consulting Senior Associate, Environmental Engineer, Geologist, or Scientist
jobs.description:
Launch Your Environmental Consulting Career and Help Shape More Sustainable Outcomes

ERM
is seeking a Consulting Senior Associate, Environmental Engineer, Geologist, or Scientist,
based in Indianapolis
. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to meaningful environmental projects involving site investigation, remediation, compliance, and hazardous waste management. You'll gain exposure to cutting-edge technologies, collaborate with experienced practitioners, and build the technical foundation needed to advance your professional career and pursue professional registration.

Why This Role Matters

Environmental challenges are becoming increasingly complex, and organizations need innovative solutions that protect people, communities, and the environment. In this role, you'll help deliver critical environmental services that support regulatory compliance, property transactions, site remediation, and sustainable business operations. Your field and technical contributions will directly support project success while providing invaluable real-world consulting experience across a diverse portfolio of projects.

What Your Impact Is

As a Consulting Senior Associate, you will play a key role in collecting environmental data, supporting investigations, evaluating site conditions, and assisting with compliance and remediation efforts. Working closely with project managers and technical specialists, you'll help deliver high-quality environmental solutions while developing skills across multiple environmental disciplines. This position also offers opportunities for travel throughout the United States and, on occasion, globally.

Required

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, environmental science, or related environmental discipline. Minimum 3.0 GPA, or equivalent experience.
1-2 years of experience.
Willingness and interest in field assignments; ability to perform field work standing or walking for full field days.
Strong commitment to safety, including following established Health and Safety protocols.
Effective written and verbal communication skills along with strong organizational and analytical abilities.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Detail-oriented with a solutions-focused, results-oriented approach and strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
Ability to multi-task, maintain flexibility, travel, and work independently with minimal supervision.
Ability to lift at least 40 pounds.
Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area.
This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Preferred

Master's degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, environmental science, or related environmental discipline.
Experience recording and writing detailed technical data and reports.
40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification.
GIT or EIT certification.
Local candidates preferred.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct field work, including data collection; soil, sediment, groundwater, surface water, soil vapor, and indoor air sampling; aquifer testing; drilling oversight and soil logging; soil boring and monitoring well installation; well development, purging and sampling; remedial and wastewater treatment pilot tests; remedial system operation and maintenance; and in-plant support.
Assist in groundwater and wastewater system performance monitoring.
Perform Phase I and II environmental assessments to support property transfer transactions.
Compile and evaluate data and assist in report preparation.
Prepare environmental compliance work plans, permits, and reports for air quality, hazardous waste, spill prevention, storm water, and wastewater.
Assist in ensuring compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations.
Work within quality, budget, schedule expectations, and scope-specific assignments.
Communicate with subcontractors, regulatory agents, tenants, and clients during field activities.

Who We Are:

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!
