jobs.description:
Overview

The Department of Environmental Conservation, Water Investment Division, Dam Safety Program (DSP) is seeking a highly motivated individual with regulatory policy experience to join the regulatory and emergency action planning group within our team. Experience or interest in dam safety engineering, regulation, Emergency Action Planning, and hydrologic and hydraulic modeling for dams is preferred. Candidates with the intent to pursue Professional Engineer licensure in the future are desired.

An ideal applicant will have the ability to multi-task and work in a fast-paced work environment where public safety is vital, and the goal is to reduce risks to life, property, and the environment from dam incidents and failure through effective communication, education, and regulation. Candidates should have strong technical skills, written and verbal communication skills, organizational skills, and the ability to identify and implement process improvements.

The DSP acts as both a regulator and dam owner, regulating nearly 1,000 non-power, non-federal dams statewide and acts as the State's owner representative at 14 dams, including the three Winooski River Flood Control dams. The DSP is a growing team that includes staff engineers, analysts, technicians, and professional engineers with many years of Dam Safety experience. Major duties include dam safety rule compliance and program buildout, permit review, issuance, and oversight; development, maintenance, and review of Emergency Action Plans (EAPs); development of EAP policy and training; assistance with dam emergencies, dam inspections; dam operation and maintenance support including flood control dam oversight and operations.

As of July 12, 2026, the step 1 rate for pay grade 25 will be $31.54 per hour and the step 15 rate will be $49.45 per hour.

Who May Apply

This position, Environmental Engineer VI - Dam Safety Program Regulatory and Emergency Action Plan Services (Job Requisition #53919)
, is open to all State employees and external applicants.

Please Note: This position is being recruited at multiple levels. If you would like to be considered for more than one level, you MUST apply to the specific Job Requisition.

Level V: 53918

Level VI: 53919

If you would like more information about this position, please contact Steven.Hannah@vermont.gov

Resumes will not be accepted via e-mail. You must apply online to be considered.

Please note that multiple positions in the same work location may be filled from this job posting.

Environmental Factors

Duties are largely performed in an office setting; however, some field travel may be necessary for which private means of transportation must be available. Fieldwork may involve exposure to chemicals, gases, hazardous liquid and solid waste, and construction sites during all weather conditions; and may involve traversing rough terrain and bodies of water. Some work outside of regular working hours, including attendance at public meetings, may be required. Strong differences of opinion may be encountered on a regular basis.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or higher in environmental, sanitary, chemical, water resources, civil or mechanical engineering or a related field AND three (3) or more years of experience in in a related engineering field

OR

One (1) year or more of experience as an Environmental Engineer V or two (2) years or more as an Environmental Engineer IV.

Total Compensation

State Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FMLI)
Two ways to save for your retirement: A State defined benefit pension plan and a deferred compensation 457(b) plan

Qualified Employer for Public Service Student Loan Forgiveness Program

jobs.description:
Dallas is Growing. Grow With Us.

Looking for more than just a job? The City of Dallas offers careers with purpose. With competitive benefits, growth opportunities, and a vibrant work culture,

we’re committed to helping you thrive while you help our city flourish. Be part of a team that’s committed to service, innovation, and community.

Job Summary

Under minimum supervision, develops and manages environmental programs for the City of Dallas, ensuring compliance with laws. Coordinates public engagement, builds community partnerships, and communicates environmental initiatives through events and presentations.

Overview

Job Description

The Environmental Coordinator II serves as an experienced resource on environmental regulations and compliance, environmental due diligence, environmental sustainability, and environmental outreach for the City of Dallas. Serves as a key resource on environmental compliance, sustainability, and outreach. Plans and delivers training for city staff, businesses, and the public, while coordinating with internal and external partners to communicate environmental initiatives.

Essential Functions

1 Performs environmental audits, annual inspections, and develops corrective/preventive action plans, including implementation of Environmental, Quality, and Safety Management Systems requirements. Reviews Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments, screenings, and risk assessments.

2 Supports inspection programs to ensure compliance with environmental regulations and ISO 14001. Conducts facility and storage tank inspections, ensures timely reporting, and assists with audit responses and corrective actions.

3 Writes inspection reports, conducts follow-up inspections to achieve closure, and archives documentation.

4 Ensures compliance of contractors, including construction crews, tenants, and service providers, conducts encroachment inspections when necessary.

5 Develops and promotes outreach programs on stormwater, waste, sustainability, and air quality to educate the public and target communities. Delivers presentations, supports program development, and tracks citywide environmental training outcomes.

6 Participates and often handles inspection and calibration of safety or sampling equipment to maintain regulatory compliance.

7 Responds to spills, ensures cleanup follows city protocols, and updates the Spill Response Bulletin. Maintains documentation and adjusts programs, procedures, and systems to stay compliant with evolving regulations.

8 Drafts and monitors the relevant wording and disbursement of informational materials, promoting the city's environmental initiatives. Creates online and social media content for the benefit of environmental programs.

9 Reviews and submits corrections to regulatory agencies, performing compliance calculations, quality control checks and maintaining department regulatory compliance.

10 Analyzes and addresses areas of change and makes recommendations to improve operations; monitors program success through evaluations.

11 Coordinates continuous improvement projects and initiatives as part of the city’s Environmental Management System, including planning, implementing, and tracking.

12 Performs other work as needed or assigned.

Knowledge and Skills

1 Advanced knowledge of Stormwater, Zero Waste, Environmental Due Diligence, Sustainability Conservation Concepts, and EMS.

2 Knowledge of Federal and State rules, regulations, and standards and ability to provide guidance on environmental management standards for various industries.

3 Knowledge of project management, permitting specifications, and project schedules.

4 Ability to manage projects, volunteers, citizen education, and events.

5 Ability to interact with TCEQ and other external agencies, City of Dallas executives, consultants, and contractors.

6 Ability to develop, evaluate, and coordinate strong website and social media presence.

7 Ability to conduct inspections, collect data and draft reports.

8 Skill in MS Office and data management.

9 Skill in public outreach, establishing and cultivating public relationships, and maintaining interaction through various communication methods.

10 Skill in communicating effectively both verbally and in writing, often via social media outlets.

11 Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships.

Education

Bachelor's degree (or higher) in an architectural, engineering, geoscience, environmental, or natural science field.

Experience

Three (3) years of experience in coordinating with state and federal environmental agencies, working on pollution prevention/environmental programs addressing potential environmental liabilities, managing environmental projects or programs, conducting internal or external environmental audits and/or researching and developing standards in environmental regulatory field at a large municipality in a geographically diverse area.

Licenses and Certifications

Valid driver's license with good driving record.

For Water Quality divisions, Class D Water license from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) is required.

For Water Reservoir, Stormwater Neighborhood and Water Quality divisions, a Boater Certificate is required. HAZWOPER certification must be obtained within the probationary period for all spill response divisions. For Stormwater Neighborhood, Certified Environmental Storm Water Compliance Professional (CESCP) certification must be obtained within the probationary period.

Preferred

ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems certified programs
HAZWOPER Certification
OSHA Safety Certification
CHMM (Certified Hazardous Materials Manager) Certification
Investigation, remediation, mitigation (water/soil/air/climate)
Water quality (drinking/source) sampling and field analysis
Emission inventory and compliance reporting
Sustainability and pollution programs
Geo-spatial information system (GIS) data analyses
Permit preparation, reporting and training
Public outreach and community relations in environmental sustainability or pollution prevention

Associate degree in the specified fields and five (5) years of the required experience will meet the education and experience requirements.

jobs.description:
The BEC Research Group develops and applies state-of-the-art ecological knowledge, methods, and tools to understand ecosystem functioning, ecological responses, and feedback within coupled social-economic-ecological systems. The Group applies this knowledge to investigate management options that support sustainability goals with ecological implications.

The BEC Group leads research supporting EU Member States and other countries worldwide in identifying priority areas for habitat conservation, restoration, and sustainable use, in order to achieve national and international area-based conservation targets.

These positions are linked to two Horizon Europe projects:

SafeNet, co-develop management and policy solutions with key stakeholders to provide integrated knowledge and guidance supporting the conservation, restoration, and management of the EU's forests.
NatureRestoreR, supporting competent authorities across EU Member States in designing, implementing, and revising restoration plans for terrestrial ecosystems, through the development of the flexible, coherent, and user-friendly NatureRestoreR modelling platform and accompanying baseline data for estimating the effectiveness of proposed restoration measures for species, habitats, and ecosystems.

The Positions:

The selected candidates will work in close collaboration with Dr. Martin Jung, Dr. Lauren Talluto, and Dr. Piero Visconti.

Position 1 - Spatial Prioritization for Land-Use Planning

This researcher will apply spatial prioritization methods for integrated land-use planning at national and continental scale. Candidates with strong literacy in spatial multi-criteria optimization methods, reinforcement learning, or other state-of-the-art spatial planning approaches are of particular interest.

Position 2 - Ecological Modeling of Population Dynamics

This researcher will develop statistical and process-based ecological models simulating spatially dynamic, time-dependent population responses to colonization and population dynamics, as a function of land management (including restoration and conservation actions), species interactions, and other abiotic effects such as climate.

While both researchers will contribute primarily to existing projects and outputs, candidates are encouraged to develop their own research profile within applied ecological and conservation research, in alignment with BEC's research objectives.

, Main Duties And Responsibilities,

Develop workflows for integrated conservation planning using optimization frameworks - (Position 1).
Prepare large (spatial) datasets for spatial planning and assess protected area effectiveness - (Position 1).
Apply and develop ecological modeling approaches to estimate the impact of land-use, climate, restoration, and conservation actions - (Position 2).

For both positions:

Lead the dissemination of project results via high-quality journal publications and conference presentations.
Contribute to the organization of project-related workshops and/or webinars.
Support project partners and other group members in drafting reports and grant proposals.
Develop other scientific outputs as needed.

,

SKILLS, QUALIFICATIONS AND Experience

Electrify your career and help build a brighter tomorrow.

Every generation has a challenge that defines them. At OPG, we are calling on all innovators, disruptors, thought leaders and change-makers. Join us as we work to electrify life in one generation and build a sustainable future powered by our electricity, our ideas, and our people. Join OPG and make history.

Whether you work in the skilled trades or are a business professional, a career at OPG is an opportunity to electrify your life on -- and off -- the job.

Ontario Power Generation (OPG) is looking for a dynamic, strategic and results-driven professional to join our team in the role of Environmental Advisor
.

Job Overview

Develop, maintain, implement, monitor, and improve performance of the OPG Environmental Management System by developing, coordinating, supporting, and providing oversight on OPG environmental managed systems and programs. Provide expertise and support to the Generating Units and Functions in managing OPG's environmental management programs and environmental performance; including interpretation and advice on legislation and policies, identifying and correcting environmental performance issues, assessing and reporting on environmental compliance and performance, establishing effective relationships with external and regulatory environmental agencies, and obtaining EA approvals and other approvals and permits.

Key Accountabilities

Develop, implement, monitor, and improve environmental management systems and programs across areas such as waste, spills, contaminated lands, biodiversity, emissions, approvals, fish, endangered species, and ozone-depleting substances.
Maintain and review environmental governance, documentation, compliance programs, and EMS performance across Generating Units and Functions.
Provide environmental expertise, legislative interpretation, policy advise, and support to resolve performance issues and improve compliance.
Liaise and negotiate with regulatory agencies to obtain, influence, and manage permits, approvals, regulations, and licenses.
Prepare, analyze, and coordinate environmental compliance reports, performance reports, executive communications, and public-facing environmental information.
Monitor environmental performance using compliance data, metrics, audits, self-assessments, reviews, and non-conformance reporting to identify issues and improvement opportunities.
Conduct and coordinate environmental studies, project support, training requirements, budgets, business plans, and advice to senior management and stakeholders.

Qualifications

4 Year University degree in an appropriate field of Engineering or Science
Requires experience related to environmental planning and approvals processes, particularly within an environmental management system, programs, and strategies.
Requires related experience in environmental management performance, including identifying and resolving environmental issues and recommending improvements as appropriate.
Requires experience coordinating Generating Units and Functions to establish metrics, develop targets, respond to current and emerging environmental issues, and champion environmental performance improvement opportunities.
Requires demonstrated experience scoping, establishing, managing, and executing environmental systems and environmental study programs.
Requires demonstrated communication and interpersonal skills, including team committee effectiveness, with over 2 years of related work experience.
Requires experience supporting the development and implementation of corporate biodiversity initiatives, including environmental management systems, regulatory processes, and climate change adaptation and mitigation initiatives.
Requires the ability to travel to remote project sites, conduct analytical reviews, research, reporting, compliance monitoring, ISO 14001 procedure development, biodiversity certification support, site visits, and EHS regulation review coordination.

The successful candidate will exhibit uncompromising integrity and commitment to upholding corporate values, and the OPG Code of Business Conduct.

OPG is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and accessible environment. If you require accommodation during the selection process, please contact AODA@opg.com.

What makes a career at OPG different?

With operations across Ontario, OPG is one of the most diverse power producers in North America. As the largest generator in Ontario, we meet approximately 50% of the province’s electricity needs, largely from low-carbon sources like nuclear and hydro.

As we work to achieve our vision of Electrifying life in one generation, OPG and our family of companies are also helping advance the development of new low-carbon technologies such as Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), refurbishment projects, and electrification initiatives to help power the growing demands of a growing economy. Join OPG and make history.

The Darlington New Nuclear Project is leading the way in the advancement of Small Modular Reactor (SMR) technology in Canada – the future of nuclear power generation! Using new and innovative technologies such as small modular reactors, hydrogen and battery storage, while expanding our hydroelectric and nuclear portfolios, we are changing the electricity landscape in Ontario.

Important Information

The base salary range considers many factors including, but not limited to experience, education, and training, including any collective agreement requirements for union represented positions. It is not typical for the salary to be offered near the top of the range, and salary is dependent on numerous factors. For management roles, the base salary range does not represent the total compensation package. The total compensation package for regular full-time management roles includes pay-for-performance programs for annual and medium time periods. Maintaining a high-performance culture and excellence is a core expectation of every member of our leadership team and is rewarded through the established compensation framework.

OPG is committed to employment equity. As such, we encourage applicants from equity-seeking communities (Indigenous Peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, and women). We strongly believe that alleviating the under-representation of equity-seeking individuals will create a stronger OPG team and allow us to better serve the needs of our diverse communities.

In order to fulfill the above-mentioned purpose, priority in hiring may be given to qualified persons who self-identify as a member of equity-seeking groups as identified in the application process. This initiative constitutes a special program under the Human Rights Code/Canadian Human Rights Act.

All job postings at OPG are to fill existing vacancies within our organization.

OPG may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools as part of the applicant screening process. However, applications will also be reviewed by a member of our Recruitment team to ensure a fair and thorough assessment.

Company Description
I’Arte Rinasce is a specialist fine art conservation and restoration studio working across two continents. The studio delivers museum-standard services to private collectors, galleries, museums, auction houses, government institutions, heritage trusts, corporate collections, universities, and cultural organizations in Auckland and India. Knowledge of conservation ethics, preventive conservation, and best practices for storage, transport, framing, and environmental control.

jobs.title: Drone Operator – Commercial Property & Thermal Inspections
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

ScaleCapture is seeking **FAA Part 107 certified drone operators** to perform aerial data collection for commercial property inspection projects.

Operators will travel to assigned commercial properties and capture standardized **RGB and thermal aerial data** according to mission\-specific collection requirements provided by ScaleCapture.

Typical assignments may involve mapping commercial properties, documenting roofs and building façades, capturing parking areas and surrounding site conditions, collecting aerial video, and performing thermal data collection.

ScaleCapture provides the mission requirements, collection specifications, and operational coordination. Operators are responsible for safely and legally completing assigned flight operations, **reviewing applicable FAA airspace requirements, obtaining or submitting required flight authorizations or waivers when necessary**, completing the required field collection, and uploading complete, organized data.

This is a **project\-based independent contractor opportunity**. Assignment availability is based on location, client demand, equipment, qualifications, and operator availability.

Responsibilities

Depending on the assignment, operators may be responsible for:

* Conducting automated RGB mapping flights
* Capturing high\-resolution aerial imagery of commercial properties
* Documenting roofs, façades, parking areas, and surrounding property features
* Capturing systematic roof and façade imagery
* Capturing aerial overview and orbit video
* Performing thermal data collection of roofs and building façades
* Following provided Mission Briefs, shot lists, flight requirements, and collection procedures
* Reviewing the mission location and confirming applicable **FAA airspace requirements before flight**
* Obtaining or submitting necessary **FAA airspace authorizations, LAANC authorizations, waivers, or other required approvals**, as applicable to the operation
* Providing applicable authorization or waiver information/documentation to ScaleCapture when required
* Operating within all applicable FAA regulations, airspace restrictions, authorization conditions, and approved altitude limitations
* Verifying required data coverage before leaving the property
* Organizing and uploading raw imagery, video, mapping data, and thermal files
* Communicating mission progress, airspace concerns, authorization issues, or field issues to ScaleCapture Operations

Operators are responsible for **data collection only**. Operators are not expected to analyze thermal imagery, diagnose building conditions, identify defects, provide engineering opinions, or make compliance or property\-condition determinations.

Example Commercial Property Assignment

A typical commercial property inspection assignment may require both **RGB and thermal aerial collection**.

During the RGB portion of the mission, an operator may complete an automated mapping flight and capture detailed imagery of the roof, building façades, parking areas, and surrounding property. Additional aerial video or orbit footage may also be required.

The thermal portion may require systematic thermal imagery of the roof and building façades using a qualifying thermal aircraft.

Because RGB and thermal imagery can require different environmental or lighting conditions, collection may occur during specific time windows outlined in the Mission Brief.

Before conducting the flight, the operator is responsible for **reviewing the location's airspace and confirming that the operation can be legally conducted**. If FAA authorization or a waiver is required, the operator must complete the applicable authorization process and provide required information to ScaleCapture before conducting the mission.

Exact mission requirements are provided before the assignment is accepted and may vary by project.

Required Qualifications

Applicants must have:

* Current **FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate**
* Strong working knowledge of FAA Part 107 regulations
* Ability to evaluate airspace and identify applicable flight restrictions
* Experience using **LAANC and/or applicable FAA authorization processes**
* Ability to obtain or submit required FAA authorizations or waivers when necessary for an assigned operation
* Experience safely conducting commercial drone operations
* Ability to conduct structured aerial imagery collection
* Ability to safely conduct automated mapping flights when required
* Reliable transportation to assigned properties
* Smartphone with reliable cellular/data access
* Ability to follow detailed Mission Briefs and capture procedures
* Ability to upload large image and video datasets
* Strong attention to detail
* Professional communication and reliability
* Ability to independently complete field assignments according to defined requirements and schedules

Commercial data collection, mapping, inspection, construction, real estate, thermal, or similar drone experience is preferred.

Recommended Equipment for Commercial Property Assignments

Some commercial property missions require **enterprise\-grade RGB/RTK and thermal capabilities**.

RGB / Mapping Equipment

Recommended aircraft include:

* DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise (M3E)
* DJI Matrice 4 Enterprise (M4E)
* DJI Phantom 4 RTK (P4 RTK)
* Comparable professional aircraft meeting the mission requirements

For certain commercial property assignments, the RGB aircraft may need:

* 20MP or greater camera
* Mechanical shutter
* RTK capability
* Automated mapping/flight planning capability
* Ability to capture high\-resolution still imagery and video

Thermal Equipment

Recommended thermal aircraft include:

* DJI Mavic 3 Thermal (M3T)
* DJI Matrice 4 Thermal (M4T)
* Comparable professional thermal aircraft meeting the mission requirements

Certain thermal assignments may require:

* Thermal resolution of at least **640 × 512**
* High\-quality still thermal imagery
* Radiometric thermal data when specified by the project
* Abilit

jobs.title: Regional Environmental Engineer, AWS Environmental Team
jobs.description:
Description

Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental professionals who play a leading role in environmental permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. The work of our Regional Environmental Engineers is critical to enabling AWS's growth in the US and around the world.

The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE), you will be responsible for environmental compliance at operating AWS data centers in Louisiana (SHV). You will develop standards and policies to support regulatory compliance, complete environmental performance analysis, establish and monitor metrics, and guide the teams in implementation of Amazon environmental standards. You will provide guidance and build effective relationships with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, design, construction, operations and other key stakeholders.

This position is based in Shreveport, Louisiana and will require travel throughout the state and the US.

Key job responsibilities

Manage and oversee compliance with environmental regulations and Amazon policy;
Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization;
Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards;
Develop environmental metrics to measure, monitor and forecast performance;
Conduct thorough and accurate environmental audits for continuous improvement;
Prioritize and manage multiple technically complex assignments concurrently;
Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company;
Build collaborative relationships with various stakeholders to ensure risks are identified early and managed appropriately;
Assist in time-critical compliance report submission to various governmental agencies;
Complete thorough and accurate environmental incident investigations and associated regulatory reports and develop appropriate corrective action.

About The Team

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Why AWS?

AWS is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering
Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance programs including regulated waste, water, and air regulations in accordance with applicable laws
7+ years of experience in environmental compliance

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a data center or other critical environment
Experience with increasing responsibilities in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

Company Overview

Mountainview Biological Consulting, LLC is a growing environmental consulting firm providing biological consulting services throughout California. Our team of experienced wildlife biologists, botanists, environmental planners, and project managers is dedicated to delivering high-quality biological surveys, environmental compliance monitoring, and natural resource management solutions for public and private sector clients.

We are seeking motivated professionals who are passionate about conservation and enjoy working in the field while contributing to meaningful environmental projects.

Position Summary

Mountainview Biological Consulting is seeking a Part-Time Wildlife Biologist based in the San Diego, California area. This field-based position supports a variety of biological monitoring and survey projects throughout Southern California. Work schedules vary based on project needs and may include early mornings, weekends, and occasional overnight travel.

This is an excellent opportunity for biologists looking for flexible, part-time field work with opportunities for professional growth.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct biological field surveys for wildlife, vegetation, and sensitive natural resources.
Perform special-status species surveys in accordance with agency protocols.
Conduct nesting bird surveys and construction compliance monitoring.
Assist with habitat assessments and biological resource inventories.
Complete detailed field notes and collect field data using Survey123, ArcGIS Field Maps, GPS units, and other mobile applications.
Prepare daily monitoring reports and communicate findings to project managers.
Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Represent Mountainview professionally while interacting with clients, contractors, and agency personnel.
Work safely in remote field conditions under varying weather and terrain.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Wildlife Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, Biology, or a related field.
One (1) or more years of biological field experience preferred.
Knowledge of Southern California wildlife species, vegetation communities, and habitats.
Experience conducting biological field surveys and environmental compliance monitoring.
Familiarity with the California Endangered Species Act (CESA), Federal Endangered Species Act (FESA), Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA), and other environmental regulations.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Excellent organizational, time management, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and collaboratively as part of a team.
Valid California driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Ability to hike up to 10 miles per day over rugged and uneven terrain while carrying field equipment.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions, including heat and rough terrain.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience conducting special-status wildlife surveys.
Experience with nesting bird surveys and construction compliance monitoring.
Proficiency with Survey123, ArcGIS Field Maps, GPS equipment, and Microsoft Excel.
Experience with ArcGIS Pro or other GIS software.
Familiarity with San Diego County habitats and local wildlife species.
Wetland delineation experience or certification.
USFWS and/or CDFW survey permits are highly desirable.

Competitive hourly compensation based on years of experience, qualifications, certifications, and demonstrated field expertise.
Flexible, part-time scheduling based on project needs.
Opportunities to work on diverse environmental and conservation projects throughout Southern California.
Mentorship and professional development with experienced environmental professionals.
Potential for increased hours and advancement as project workload grows.

jobs.description:
Environmental Engineering – AI Data Trainer

About The Role

We're partnering with the world's leading AI research labs to build smarter, more technically rigorous AI models — and we need environmental engineers to make it happen. As an AI Data Trainer, your domain expertise will directly shape how AI understands and reasons through complex environmental engineering problems, from contaminant transport to regulatory compliance.

This is a rare opportunity to sit at the intersection of environmental science and cutting-edge artificial intelligence — no prior AI experience required.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Hourly Contract
Location: Remote
Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

What You'll Do

Design Advanced Technical Problems — Craft challenging, real-world environmental engineering scenarios across domains including contaminant transport, mass balance in treatment plants, hydrology, and Life Cycle Assessments (LCA)
Author Ground-Truth Solutions — Develop rigorous, step-by-step reference solutions — including chemical dosage calculations, hydraulic flow models, and pollutant dispersion simulations — that serve as the gold standard for AI responses
Audit AI Outputs — Critically evaluate AI-generated remediation plans, environmental impact statements, and mathematical proofs for technical accuracy, safety, and adherence to regulatory standards (EPA, ISO 14001, and others)
Refine AI Reasoning — Identify logical errors in AI responses — such as incorrect stoichiometry in biological treatment processes or failure to account for secondary environmental impacts — and provide structured feedback to improve model performance
Work Independently — Complete task-based assignments on a flexible, asynchronous schedule that fits your life

Who You Are

Pursuing or holding a Master's or PhD in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering (environmental focus), or a closely related field
Strong foundational knowledge in one or more core areas: aquatic chemistry, wastewater process design, air quality engineering, or hazardous waste remediation
Able to communicate complex technical and ecological concepts clearly and precisely in writing
Detail-oriented — confident checking unit conversions (mg/L to ppm), balancing chemical equations, and verifying regulatory compliance logic
Self-motivated and comfortable working independently on analytical tasks
No prior AI experience required

Nice to Have

Experience with data annotation, data quality review, or evaluation workflows
Familiarity with environmental modeling software (e.g., AERMOD, SWMM, EPANET)
Background in EHS compliance, environmental permitting, or regulatory frameworks

Why Join Us

Work on cutting-edge AI projects with top research labs and organizations at the forefront of AI development
Fully remote and flexible — work on your own schedule, from anywhere
Freelance perks: autonomy, variety, and global collaboration
Apply your environmental engineering expertise in a meaningful new context
Potential for ongoing work and contract extension

jobs.description:
Job Title:
Environmental Programs Manager

Location:
San Jose, CA or El Monte, CA – (National scope; field-based with regular travel)

Position Type:
Full-time – Exempt

Salary:
$85,000- $118,000 + 15% Bonus Incentive and Full Benefit Package Day One

Who We Are

Flexcar is completely reimagining car ownership. We offer the world's first month-to-month car lease, with insurance and maintenance included. By combining operational expertise with technology, data, and AI, we are transforming every aspect of the customer journey and providing a smarter, more flexible alternative to traditional ownership. We're scaling fast — and we're building the next generation of leaders to scale with us.

Job Summary

We are seeking an Environmental Programs Manager to build and own environmental compliance across Flexcar's national network of vehicle hubs. Our operations generate regulated waste streams at every site, including used motor oil, coolant, brake fluid, detailing chemicals, waste tires, and 12V lead-acid batteries, along with stormwater, wash water, and chemical storage obligations that vary by state. You will own the environmental program end to end: setting the standards, holding the permits and registrations, managing waste vendors, serving as the company contact during agency inspections, and equipping our regional EHS Specialists to execute site-level environmental tasks day to day. This is a build role: the program does not exist yet in mature form, and you will be the person who creates it.

What You Will Do

National Environmental Program Ownership

Build and maintain Flexcar's environmental compliance program across all operating states, including written standards, site playbooks, and inspection checklists that regional EHS Specialists execute at their sites.
Own the national compliance calendar covering permits, registrations, renewals, inspections, sampling windows, and reporting deadlines, tracking corrective actions to verified closure.
Own environmental regulatory relationships nationally, serving as the company contact for agency inspections, information requests, and correspondence.
Conduct periodic environmental audits at sites across the network, and report environmental performance and open risks to Operations leadership.
Monitor state and federal regulatory changes affecting our operations and translate them into program updates before they become findings.

Hazardous, Universal, and Regulated Waste

Own generator classification and EPA identification across all sites, under federal RCRA and state programs, including California's Title 22 requirements, which regulate several of our streams more stringently.
Manage waste streams end to end at every site: used motor oil, coolant, brake fluid, detailing and cleaning chemicals, waste tires, and 12V lead-acid batteries, including characterization, accumulation and storage practices, container management and secondary containment, manifesting, and disposal.
Manage universal waste programs for 12V lead-acid batteries, aerosol cans, lamps, and electronics, including accumulation limits, labeling, and storage time rules under each state's program.
Maintain waste tire compliance state by state, including registered haulers, trip logs, and storage thresholds, covering CalRecycle requirements in California.
Apply used oil rules by state, including California's presumption that used oil is hazardous.
Qualify and manage waste haulers, disposal vendors, and environmental consultants nationally, including contracts, cost, and performance.

Water, Storage, and Site Conditions

Determine stormwater applicability at each site and maintain the resulting obligations, including industrial permit coverage or No Exposure Certification, SWPPPs and BMPs, sampling, annual evaluations, and state portal submittals.
Set standards for detailing and wash water handling across the network, including discharge authorization, clarifiers and interceptors, drain control, and dry cleanup practices.
Maintain aboveground storage tank compliance and SPCC plans where oil storage triggers applicability, including tank inspections, secondary containment, integrity and monitoring requirements under state programs, and spill containment readiness.
Manage EPCRA Tier II chemical inventory reporting where storage thresholds are met.
Maintain chemical inventory and SDS standards nationally, including approved-chemical controls.

California-Specific Programs

Maintain Hazardous Materials Business Plans, CERS reporting, and CUPA relationships for California sites, and serve as the site contact for CUPA inspections.
Maintain Prop 65 warning and exposure obligations.

Air Quality and Coating Operations (Planned Facility)

Lead air district permitting for the planned coating operation, including permit to construct, permit to operate, permit conditions, modifications, and renewals with the applicable district.

jobs.description:
At Optum, we are driven to transform health care not just for our own good, but for the greater good. Here, innovation isn't about another gadget, it's about transforming the health care industry. And, with your geospatial technology expertise, you can join us on our mission to help make the health care system work better for everyone.

As part of Optum Technology, you will thrive as you help deliver solutions for Optum and UHG with world class enterprise geospatial technology as a member of the Enterprise Geospatial Analytics team. As a Geospatial Analyst
, you will be a primary contributor in defining the patterns and practices for applying geospatial technology within healthcare. This position will design geospatial solutions to solve healthcare business problems, assist with platform operations and enhancements, and complete geospatial analytics projects and deliverables in partnership with business units. This role requires someone who is a product-minded technologist, proactive, innovative, and collaborative.

Location
: Remote

You'll enjoy the flexibility to work remotely* from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges. For all hires in the Minneapolis or Washington, D.C. area, you will be required to work in the office for a minimum of four days per week.

Innovate at the intersection of geospatial technology, artificial intelligence (AI/GeoAI) and business market intelligence in support of the development of company products, tools, platforms, and services.
Complete geospatial analytics projects, build deliverables, create marketing collateral, and contribute to knowledge sharing with a geospatial user community.
Apply advanced geospatial analysis techniques to provide insights into healthcare related business problems.
Assist with defining, designing, and building geospatial technology solutions (patterns and practices) to make non-geospatial experts successful with the technology in their day-to-day work.
Assist with building and maintaining geographic data assets from disparate sources through ETL and automation.
Contribute to GIS platform enhancements and assist with automation, operations, and maintenance needs.
Engage with existing and prospective customers (internal), gather business needs, and communicate the value of Enterprise Geospatial Analytics internal product offerings.

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Experience with geospatial platform scripting, automation tools and/or web development (Ex: ArcGIS Python API + Jupyter, ArcGIS JavaScript API) including use of AI coding assistants such as copilot, codex or similar
Experience or interest in Data Science, Machine Learning computing and/or the R Statistical package is a plus
Experience with ArcGIS GeoAnalyics Engine, Databricks and/or Snowflake
Experience applying geospatial analytics in the private sector to solve commercial business problems
Excellent presentation, interpersonal, and listening skills
Healthcare industry experience

to support the development of a 25-Year Real Property Master Plan
for the Virgin Islands National Guard.

GIS Database Development

Build and organize an installation GIS database from available source information.
Compile, clean, organize, and manage spatial and non-spatial data.
Develop GIS layers for facilities, land use, infrastructure, transportation, environmental constraints, and other relevant planning factors.
Maintain data quality, accuracy, organization, and metadata.

GIS Analysis & Mapping

Map land-use opportunities and constraints supporting long-range installation planning.
Conduct spatial analysis to support land-use and development recommendations.
Analyze existing conditions and spatial relationships among facilities, infrastructure, environmental resources, and development areas.
Integrate GIS information with planning, facility, environmental, and infrastructure data.

Planning Support

Support installation site assessments and field data collection.
Assist the Senior Master Planner with planning analyses and development recommendations.
Support preparation of Area Development Plans and other planning exhibits.
Provide GIS analysis and mapping support for master planning activities.

Maps & Graphics

Produce professional maps, exhibits, graphics, and figures for master plan deliverables.
Prepare maps for stakeholder presentations, planning workshops, and technical reports.
Develop clear and accurate graphics suitable for inclusion in formal planning documents.
Coordinate GIS information with other technical disciplines and project team members.

Documentation & Quality Control

Support documentation and quality control of GIS-related information included in the final master plan.
Verify spatial data and map products for accuracy and consistency.
Assist with preparation of supporting technical documentation and planning materials.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Geography, GIS, Urban Planning, Environmental Science, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of professional experience in GIS, planning, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining GIS databases.
Experience mapping land-use and environmental constraints.
Experience producing maps and graphics for planning, engineering, environmental, or similar technical documents.
Proficiency with ArcGIS Pro.
Working knowledge of AutoCAD.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
Strong analytical and organizational skills.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently in a primarily remote environment.

Experience with DoD GIS data standards.
Experience supporting military installations, National Guard facilities, federal facilities, or military bases.
Installation master planning experience.
Environmental planning or environmental constraints analysis experience.
Experience integrating GIS with land-use, facility, infrastructure, or real property planning.
Federal or DoD project experience.
Experience in the U.S. Virgin Islands, Caribbean, or similar island environments.

This position is primarily remote and part-time
. The selected candidate must be comfortable working independently and coordinating remotely with the Senior Master Planner and project team.

Approximately one trip to St. Croix and/or St. Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step into Your New Role

Kleinfelder is seeking a Project Level Environmental Professional Engineer or Professional Geologist to work in our Sacramento, CA or Concord, CA office. Candidates must have a minimum of 6 years of environmental experience.

The ideal candidate will participate in and contribute to a diverse range of professional tasks, in the field and office, in our team-oriented environment. The candidate would be able to take a project from the proposal phase through report preparation on the most challenging remediation projects.

Responsibilities:

Perform task management duties on site investigation, remedy selection, and remediation projects across Northern California
Coordinate with and mentor junior-level staff on small to large project and tasks
Lead conversations with private and municipal clients, as well as relevant regulatory agencies
Prepare and peer review project deliverables as needed, including work plans, reports, remedy selection documents, and internal, client, or agency-facing presentations
Guide team members in meeting Kleinfelder’s safety and quality standards
Prepare proposals for small to medium sized projects (<$50,000 to $250,000) with support from senior staff Review RFPs and RFQs, and participate in go/no-go evaluations of identified opportunities.
Manage small to medium sized projects ( Work independently and perform routine, well-defined field and office tasks and analysis under direct supervision by senior team members
Communicate effectively with field/construction contractors
As needed, oversee subsurface drilling investigations to determine the presence and extent of impacts in soil, soil vapor and groundwater
Confirm the quality procedures used by team members when collecting multimedia samples for field and laboratory testing
Assists in performance of hydraulic tests to support hydrogeologic analysis of water resource projects and environmental remediation system design (including groundwater recovery and treatment, de-watering, and hydraulic containment) (as needed)
Prepare designs, reports, and calculations for simple to moderately complex environmental site assessments and remediation type projects (commercial, industrial, and educational facilities, levees, dams, pipelines, electrical facilities, etc.)
Supervise and direct surface and subsurface investigations that employ soil borings, test pits, well installations, well destructions, soil, groundwater, and vapor sampling, aquifer testing, and surface geophysical surveys

Requirements:

6-10 years of related environmental experience – 8+ years highly preferred
BS in Civil or Environmental Engineering or a BS in Geology or other related discipline (e.g., Geophysics, Hydrogeology, Geochemistry, Environmental Geology, etc.)

Environmental Compliance & Operations

Environmental Management Systems

Support EMS implementation, audits, report-outs, and the internal auditor program; complete required auditor training within six months of entering the role.

Incident Response & Corrective Action

Provide first-line response to spills, releases, accidents, and other environmental incidents, including required notifications to management and regulatory agencies.
Ensure investigations and incident analyses are completed and corrective actions are implemented.
Maintain emergency response and applicable operation and maintenance plans.
Help operations proactively identify and address potential environmental risks.

Environmental Projects & Remediation

Support environmental investigations, remediation, due diligence, acquisitions, property sales, and other environmental projects across multiple media and regulatory jurisdictions.
Develop scopes of work; evaluate and manage consultants and contractors; and oversee project budgets, schedules, deliverables, and coordination with operations and legal counsel.

Leadership & Collaboration

Maintain effective relationships with regulatory agencies, consultants, contractors, legal counsel, trade associations, vendors, and other external partners.
Represent the company as needed in technical forums, regulatory hearings, legal matters, and other public or private discussions.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree, preferably in Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemistry, Geology, Biology, or a related science discipline.
4 to 7 years of experience with environmental regulations and sampling or testing involving air, water, soil, hazardous waste, or other regulated materials.
Knowledge of applicable local, state, and federal environmental programs, regulations, and approved sampling techniques.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, and documentation skills, with the ability to communicate environmental requirements and recommendations to operational and technical audiences.
Ability to read and understand engineering plans and specifications.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, environmental management systems, and environmental testing or analytical equipment.

Lift and carry up to 20 pounds frequently and up to 50 pounds occasionally.

jobs.description:
Nature and Variety of Work

Come join our team!

Prince George’s County Government provides a dynamic and inclusive workplace where employees can thrive, learn, and grow across its 30 diverse agencies, all dedicated to serving the County's residents with essential resources and services. Nestled just minutes away from Washington, DC, Prince George's County combines urban vibrancy with serene surroundings, offering an ideal setting to live, work, and enjoy life.

The Prince George’s County Department of The Environment
is currently seeking qualified applicants to fill an Environmental Planner III
, (Planner 3A)
grade A27
position, in the Sustainable Waste Management Division
.

About The Position

This is a full-performance level environmental planning position in the Sustainable Waste Management Division. The incumbent is responsible for assisting in the fulfillment of the Department/Section responsibilities with emphasis on developing environmental plans and programs for solid waste management. This position is essential to the County’s ongoing solid waste management and recycling efforts. The incumbent develops and implements programs that address specific solid waste management needs and expands recycling and composting opportunities across schools, multifamily properties, nonprofits, businesses, and special events. The position also maintains critical reports related to the County’s waste diversion efforts, facility licensing, collection vehicle permits and Source Reduction activities, ensuring the County can monitor program performance and meet operational and reporting requirements.

About The Agency

The Department of the Environment works for a healthy, beautiful and sustainable County through programs that provide clean water, flood control, recycling and waste management, litter prevention, sustainable animal management and pet adoption in partnership with residents and other stakeholders. Some of our core services include providing clean water services (Stormwater Management Division); flooding prevention for buildings and structures (Sustainability Division and Stormwater Management Division); collecting, processing and diverting waste from the County-operated landfill, commercial facilities and householders (Resource Recovery Division); providing sustainability services to reduce greenhouse gas and emission (Sustainability Division); and facilitating pet adoptions, managing an animal holding facility, issuing pet licenses, investigating cruelty complaints and conducting humane outreach and education events (Animal Services Division).

Examples of Work

Participates in the development of policies and procedures for enhancing the County’s Recycling, Composting, and Source Reduction Programs.
Maintains reports on recycling, composting and waste diversion efforts.
Assists with developing educational and informational materials on recycling and composting and provides technical assistance to the commercial sector in establishing and improving recycling and composting programs.
Engages with business/commercial properties to ensure compliance with Recycling Legislation Council Bill CB-87-2012 and provides recycling or technical assistance to the businesses in development of recycling or composting programs.
Represents the Division at meetings with the public and/or with other governmental entities to advance County policies and initiatives on solid waste recycling and composting pertaining to residential/commercial sectors.
Performs research and prepares studies and devises plans with cost analysis for introduction of new waste diversion opportunities within the County.
Researches appropriate funding sources for grant application to advance recycling and promote source and waste reduction strategies.
Plans Special Events, designed to promote and increase recycling rates, including scheduling of location, date, time, resources needed, advertisement and outreach materials to notify the public.
Assists in contract management of recycling, compost and waste diversion contracts, including municipal recycling agreements.
Reviews and process contracts and amend documents from the contractor and various County agencies.
Reviews and process invoices for payment in accordance with contract documents.
Willingly and cooperatively performs a variety of duties and responsibilities which may not be stated herein but are within the scope of tasks typically associated with the employee's class of work
Complies with all motor vehicle laws and Departmental regulations.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in urban and regional planning, public administration, economics, business administration, political science, environmental science, public health or other closely related fields.
A minimum of two (2) years of professional planning/program development experience in environmental planning.
Possession of a valid state issued driver's license.

Any equivalent combination of relevant training, education and experience may also be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated knowledge and experience of methods and requirements for best management practices (BMPs) and programs aligned with recycling, source reduction, solid waste management, and environmental sustainability.
Ability to address inquiries in a responsive and thorough manner, with a willingness to ensure that all necessary information has been obtained and to ask any follow-up questions that may be necessary.
Ability to foster and approach tasks with a team-focused mentality and the ability to successfully and fruitfully engage with coworkers with a wide variety of work styles and skill sets.
Strong attention-to-detail and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to be flexible and adaptable to change.
Advanced experience with Microsoft 365 Office applications, including proven strength in the use of spreadsheets, database and presentation applications, including Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook and PowerPoint and One Drive and SharePoint.

Job Summary

GeoSpatial Analyst MAP will analyze complex geospatial data sets using Splunk Admin capabilities to deliver actionable insights that enhance operational efficiency and strategic planning across the enterprise. The role involves hybrid work in a day shift schedule and focuses on building robust monitoring solutions that improve resilience transparency and data driven decision making for business and society.

Responsibilities

Analyze diverse geospatial data sources using Splunk configurations to generate clear operational and strategic insights that help internal teams make timely and informed decisions across regions and functions.
Develop and maintain Splunk dashboards tailored to geospatial metrics that allow stakeholders to monitor performance trends identify anomalies and track key indicators that support long term organizational objectives.
Configure Splunk data ingestion pipelines for geospatial feeds to ensure reliable collection indexing and search performance that supports high quality analytics and minimizes downtime across critical business workflows.
Collaborate with cross functional teams to translate complex geospatial and operational requirements into efficient Splunk search queries and visualizations that address real business problems and improve service outcomes.
Optimize Splunk search performance for large scale geospatial datasets by tuning queries indexes and resource usage to deliver fast accurate results that enable timely responses to emerging risks and opportunities.
Implement data quality checks and validation routines for geospatial inputs within Splunk to ensure that downstream analyses reports and alerts remain trustworthy and support responsible decision making.
Support hybrid work collaboration by documenting Splunk configurations dashboards and geo analytics processes in an accessible manner that allows distributed teams to operate smoothly and maintain continuity.
Integrate relevant external geospatial data sources with internal Splunk environments to expand analytical coverage enrich context for patterns and help the organization understand regional impacts on operations and communities.
Provide clear analytical summaries and recommendations based on Splunk geospatial outputs that guide business teams toward actions which reduce risk improve resource allocation and strengthen societal impact.
Coordinate with cybersecurity and infrastructure specialists to maintain secure and stable Splunk environments for geospatial analysis ensuring compliance with organizational standards and protecting sensitive information.
Design alerting mechanisms in Splunk based on geospatial thresholds and trends so that operational teams can respond quickly to incidents service disruptions or emerging demand patterns in specific locations.
Document repeatable analytic workflows for geospatial investigations in Splunk to support continuous improvement knowledge sharing and scalability of analytical capabilities across the enterprise.
Participate in periodic reviews of geospatial analytics use cases to refine Splunk configurations and reporting structures ensuring that solutions remain aligned with evolving business strategies and societal expectations.

jobs.title: Staff Geospatial Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Location:
London | Hybrid

We're partnering with one of Europe's fastest-growing technology businesses to hire a Staff Geospatial Data Scientist
into its Data team.

The company operates a rapidly scaling, technology-led logistics network, moving millions of parcels through an increasingly complex last-mile operation.

Geography sits at the heart of that network. Where demand occurs, how territories are designed, where capacity is positioned, how couriers move through cities and how the physical characteristics of an area affect delivery performance all have a direct impact on cost, speed and customer experience.

The Role

You'll work at the intersection of Geospatial Data Science, Machine Learning and real-world operations, using large-scale spatial datasets to understand and improve how the network operates.

This is a senior individual contributor position with significant technical ownership. You'll work closely with Data Scientists, Operational Research Scientists, Engineers, Analysts and operational teams to turn complex geographic problems into production solutions.

What You'll Do

Develop geospatial models that improve how a large-scale last-mile network is designed and operated.
Analyse millions of spatial and operational data points across parcels, couriers, routes, locations and delivery outcomes.
Build models around travel time, accessibility, demand density, network coverage and geographic performance.
Develop sophisticated spatial features and datasets that can be used across optimisation and machine-learning systems.
Apply techniques such as spatial statistics, clustering, graph/network analysis and geospatial machine learning.
Identify geographic patterns and constraints that influence delivery cost, capacity and service performance.
Build scalable geospatial pipelines and tooling rather than relying on one-off analysis.
Work closely with Operational Research and Engineering teams to integrate geospatial intelligence into production decision systems.
Define technical standards and best practices for geospatial Data Science across the organisation.
Mentor other Data Scientists and provide technical leadership on complex spatial problems.

What We're Looking For

Significant professional experience in Geospatial Data Science, Spatial Data Science or a closely related quantitative discipline.
Expert-level Python and strong SQL.
Deep understanding of geospatial concepts including coordinate systems, spatial joins, distance calculations, spatial indexing and geographic data structures.
Strong experience with Python geospatial tooling such as GeoPandas, Shapely, PyProj, Rasterio, H3 or similar.
Experience working with large-scale spatial datasets in a production technology environment.
Strong understanding of spatial statistics, clustering, network/graph analysis or geospatial machine learning.
Experience building production-quality Data Science systems rather than purely conducting research or GIS analysis.
Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience collaborating closely with engineering teams.
Ability to take ambiguous real-world problems, define the analytical approach and own solutions through to production.
Comfortable operating as a senior technical IC and influencing technical direction across multiple teams.

Particularly Relevant Backgrounds

Experience within logistics, mobility, transportation, mapping, marketplaces, delivery networks or location intelligence would be highly relevant, although we're open to exceptional Geospatial Data Scientists from other technology environments.

Experience with areas such as road networks, routing, travel-time modelling, geocoding, catchment analysis, territory design or spatial optimisation would also be particularly valuable.

jobs.title: Consulting Associate, Environmental Scientist (Assistant Wetland Delineator)
jobs.description:
Launch Your Environmental Consulting Career While Making a Real Difference

Join ERM
as a Consulting Associate, Environmental Scientist (Assistant Wetland Delineator)
in Houston, Texas
or New Orleans, Louisiana
, and gain hands-on experience supporting impactful infrastructure, energy, and development projects. This is an exciting opportunity for an early-career environmental professional to work alongside experienced consultants, develop technical field skills, and contribute to projects that help clients make informed decisions while protecting natural resources. If you're passionate about wetlands, environmental stewardship, and building a career in consulting, this role offers a strong foundation for long-term growth and development.

Why This Role Matters

As a Consulting Associate, Environmental Scientist (Assistant Wetland Delineator), you'll play a critical role in helping clients understand and responsibly manage environmental impacts. Your work supports informed decision-making for infrastructure, energy, and development projects, balancing progress with environmental stewardship.

What Your Impact Is

You’ll provide high-quality analytical and field support as part of ERM’s Impact Assessment team, contributing to wetland delineations, habitat assessments, and permit support across a wide range of projects. Working alongside experienced professionals, you'll help deliver technically sound, fit-for-purpose solutions while building valuable expertise in environmental consulting. Your contributions will support project success, regulatory compliance, and responsible environmental management for clients across multiple industries.

Required

What You'll Bring

BA/BS or Master’s degree in a natural science discipline, or the equivalency of 8+ years related experience in lieu of education
0+ years of professional experience
Coursework or training in wetland delineation using the 1987 Corps of Engineers Wetlands Delineation Manual and applicable Regional Supplements
Familiarity with Army Corps of Engineers Regional Supplements (Arid West and/or Great Plains)
Ability and willingness to conduct fieldwork up to 75% of the time, outdoors and in variable conditions
Working knowledge of GPS technologies and map interpretation (e.g., NWI, USGS, aerial imagery)
Strong commitment to health, safety, and fieldwork best practices
Effective written and verbal communication skills, with attention to detail
Ability to prioritize tasks, adapt to changing needs, and work independently with minimal supervision
Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area
This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Preferred

Previous internship, field course, or hands-on experience with wetland delineation or habitat assessments
Experience collecting, reviewing, or managing environmental field data
Local or regional familiarity with the Houston area and surrounding environments
Local candidates preferred

Key Responsibilities

Conduct wetland delineations in accordance with the 1987 Corps of Engineers Wetlands Delineation Manual and Regional Supplements
Document ordinary high-water marks (OHWM) and geophysical characteristics of waterbodies
Perform habitat and environmental assessments
Complete data collection, GPS data management, and quality review
Support desktop environmental constraints analysis and permitting processes
Assist with survey report preparation and permit applications
Participate in fieldwork safely and in alignment with ERM and client safety standards
Collaborate with multidisciplinary team members and subject matter experts
Communicate effectively with clients and internal stakeholders on environmental science matters
Deliver work in accordance with scope, schedule, budget, and ERM quality standards
Support the growth and delivery of ERM’s environmental and impact assessment services

Who We Are:

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!

Permit Application Preparation : Prepare environmental permit applications and supporting documents.
Impact Analysis : Analyze how proposed actions affect the natural environment (e.g., natural resources, wildlife) and the built environment (e.g., infrastructure, communities, economics).
Coordination with Design Teams : Interface with design engineers and technical specialists to align planning efforts and design efforts to obtain and incorporate information into environmental planning and permitting documents.
Client Interaction : Participate in meetings with clients as needed to support preparation of environmental planning and permitting documents.
Agency Coordination : Coordinate with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies and entities to secure environmental permits and approvals for proposed actions.

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

The ideal candidate will need the following as a foundation for success in this role:

BA/BS in Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Biology, Environmental Planning, or related field.
Minimum 4+ years of directly related professional experience.
Experience preparing environmental planning documents for National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA) compliance for capital projects.
Experience preparing permit applications for Clean Water Act Section 404 and 401 permits for capital projects.
Knowledge of Endangered Species Act (ESA) and Migratory Bird Treaty Act and experience supporting ESA Section 7 consultation for capital projects.
Expertise in a relevant technical discipline (e.g., ecology, wetlands, fisheries, environmental sciences). Wetlands expertise will be prioritized.

Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

Working knowledge of CERCLA (Superfund) regulations, environmental cleanup actions, and application of environmental regulations in that context.
Experience with Applicable or Relevant and Appropriate Requirements (ARARs) analysis and documentation for CERCLA remediation planning and design.
Experience with mitigation planning and implementation for impacts to Waters of the United States (WOTUS).
Experience performing field reconnaissance and field data collection.
HAZWOPER 40-hour training/8-hour refresher.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Ability to see details at close range
Ability to see details at a distance

Complex problem solving and decision making

Leading a team or coordinating multiple priorities
