Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities

Must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
Office and remote work environment

10%

We are seeking an Associate Attorney to join our land use and municipal practice group to advise clients on zoning, land development, and local government matters in Pennsylvania. The successful candidate will conduct legal research and analysis, represent clients in administrative hearings and court, draft agreements and ordinances, and work closely with planners, engineers, and municipal officials to secure approvals and resolve land use disputes. A strong working knowledge of the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, municipal law, and civil litigation is essential.

Key Responsibilities

Counsel municipalities, developers, property owners, and boards on zoning, land development, subdivision, conditional use, variances, and other land use matters.
Represent clients at zoning hearing board meetings, planning commission hearings, municipal council meetings, and in administrative appeals and litigation in Commonwealth and trial courts.
Prepare and file land development submissions, zoning applications, subdivision plans, and permit appeals; draft legal memoranda, motions, briefs, and administrative comments.
Draft and review land use agreements, development agreements, easements, covenants, municipal ordinances, resolutions, and conditions of approval.
Advise on compliance with the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, local ordinances, and applicable state and federal statutes and regulations.
Conduct factual and legal research, prepare closing binders, hearing exhibits, pre-hearing statements, and legal opinions for clients and boards.
Negotiate settlements, conditions of approval, and development terms with opposing counsel, developers, municipal staff, and third parties.
Coordinate with planners, engineers, surveyors, and other consultants to evaluate technical reports and integrate legal strategy with project requirements.
Manage a caseload, maintain client communications, meet deadlines, and supervise/paralegal staff as needed.
Support business development efforts by preparing pitch materials, participating in client meetings, and contributing to practice-group marketing initiatives.

Qualifications

Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school and admission to the Pennsylvania bar (or eligibility to waive and obtain admission shortly after hire).
2+ years of experience practicing municipal law, land use, zoning, and/or local government law; experience representing clients in zoning hearings and land development matters strongly preferred.
Demonstrated familiarity with the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code and experience applying it to real-world land use and development projects.
Proven civil litigation skills, including drafting briefs, motions, and pleadings, and experience in administrative appeals and court proceedings.
Experience with real estate development matters, including drafting and negotiating development agreements, easements, covenants, and related documents.
Strong written and oral communication skills; ability to prepare clear legal analysis, persuasive hearing presentations, and client-facing memoranda.
Comfortable working with municipal officials, planning commissions, zoning hearing boards, engineers, and planners; ability to translate technical information for legal strategy.
Excellent project management skills, attention to detail, ability to manage multiple matters and meet deadlines, and a collaborative team approach.
Proficiency with legal research tools (e.g., Westlaw, Lexis) and common office software; familiarity with municipal permitting and project-tracking systems a plus.

jobs.title: Civil/Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
At MacKay, we believe great people are the foundation of our growth and success.

We are in an exciting phase of expansion, creating new opportunities for our employees to take on meaningful work, collaborate across disciplines, and build long-term careers. Whether your role is technical or part of our support services team, you play an important role in delivering high-quality work and helping our projects succeed.

Pioneer Technical Services has built a reputation for delivering innovative engineering and environmental solutions while earning the trust of clients and communities throughout the Intermountain West.

Now, as Pioneer Technical Services, A Part of MacKay, we’re building on that foundation as part of a growing national infrastructure and environmental services firm. Joining MacKay expands opportunities for our employees through multidisciplinary collaboration, broader technical expertise, and the resources of a larger organization, while preserving the collaborative culture, local leadership, and commitment to practical, client-focused solutions that have always defined Pioneer.

We are seeking a Civil/Environmental Engineer
specializing in environmental remediation and heavy-civil earthwork design to join our team at our Kellogg, Idaho
office. The position requires experience across multiple phases of environmental and civil engineering consulting, including preparing technical plans and specifications, managing client and design teams, preparing bidding documents, and overseeing field inspections. The engineer will be required to travel for 10-30% of their time.

Sign-On bonuses available for well-qualified candidates.

Key Responsibilities

Independently perform environmental and civil engineering tasks, including remedial designs for projects within the Silver Valley of Idaho and Western Montana. These designs include conducting alternatives analyses, preparing sampling plans, preparing construction drawings and specifications, preparing bidding documents, and managing construction projects.
Work collaboratively with other engineering disciplines within MacKay, including structural, geotechnical, and water resources engineers.
Conduct technical review and project management for engineering deliverables, schedule, and invoicing.
Manage and mentor junior engineering staff.
Prepare and review technical reports.
Develop scopes of work and budget estimates for conducting engineering projects.
Manage junior staff performing construction observation.
Assist with business development and proposal writing efforts, when warranted.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering or a related discipline
Montana or Idaho P.E. license
5-10 years of experience in Federal and State environmental regulations or related design experience in heavy civil or earth-moving projects.
Proficient in MS Office and AutoCAD Civil 3D
Ability to communicate effectively across all levels and cross-functionally
Ability to collaboratively solve complex technical problems
Experience with proposal development, cost estimating, and determining specifications.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Why Join Pioneer Technical Services – A Part of MacKay?

Pioneer Technical Services is now part of MacKay, a growing national infrastructure and environmental services firm with more than 50 years of experience serving clients across the United States.

While our name will transition to MacKay in January 2027, our people, leadership, and commitment to delivering innovative, practical solutions remain the same. Together, we’re combining Pioneer’s trusted expertise with the expanded resources, multidisciplinary capabilities, and career opportunities of a growing national organization.

At Pioneer, you’ll have the opportunity to work alongside talented professionals on meaningful projects that strengthen communities and the environment. We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, professional development opportunities, and a collaborative culture where employees are empowered to grow and make an impact.

Our Values

At MacKay, our values guide how we work, collaborate, and support one another.

Honesty. We build trust through transparency, integrity, and accountability.
Dedication. We are committed to the success of our team members, clients, and communities.
Relationships. We foster lasting connections that strengthen our work and the teams around us.

Who We Are

MacKay is an infrastructure and environmental services firm built on more than 50 years of experience and a growing collective of expertise.

We are in an exciting phase of growth, expanding our reach, strengthening our capabilities, and bringing together talented teams across the country. That growth is creating new opportunities for our employees to take on meaningful work, collaborate across disciplines, and build long-term careers.

Every role at MacKay contributes to the success of our projects and the clients we serve. Whether your work is technical or operational, you are part of a team that delivers quality, builds relationships, and moves projects forward.

We’re looking for dedicated, talented individuals who deliver excellence, thrive in collaborative environments, and value both meaningful work and work-life balance. If this sounds like you, we’d like to hear from you.

Experience supporting large-scale water and wastewater capital improvement projects.

jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Senior Analyst is responsible for supporting environmental data management, analytics, and regulatory compliance activities. This role supports the collection, validation, and reporting of environmental data across energy, waste, and environmental compliance programs; ensuring accuracy and consistency across systems and reporting processes. The Senior Analyst also supports renewable energy tracking and analysis, including maintaining program data, preparing reporting, and assisting with performance monitoring.

A Day In The Life

Sustainability Data Analytics:

Review Scope 1 and Scope 2 environmental datasets, including data validation, reconciliation, and discrepancy resolution.
Update and maintain energy and waste data tracking models to support ongoing performance monitoring and reporting.
Analyze data trends and anomalies in energy and waste performance and prepare summaries to support internal reporting and decision-making.
Collaborate with Internal Audit and cross-functional teams to enhance environmental data controls and processes.
Support the development and maintenance of forecasting models for energy and waste data, including updating inputs and assisting with output analysis.
Coordinate with Energy Engineering and internal teams to develop and implement project planning based on environmental analytics findings, including opportunity identification, resolution tracking progress, and resulting savings models and validation.

Renewable Energy Analytics & Program Execution:

Maintain renewable energy tracking tools and monitor progress toward renewable energy goals.
Compile and track renewable energy credits (RECs) from multiple sources.
Monitors and manage active solar arrays to ensure optimal performance. This includes energy production trending, and initiating repairs and maintenance for owned solar.
Support improvements to renewable energy data tracking and reporting processes.
Coordinate with internal teams, landlords, and vendors to support renewable energy projects and initiatives.
Monitor renewable project performance and coordinate issue resolution with internal stakeholders and vendors.
Support internal partners on landlord owned and operated onsite solar, including re-roofs, RTU replacements, and solar system repairs needed.

Environmental Compliance Support:

Maintain sustainability documentation and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to support compliance with environmental regulations.
Support audit readiness activities, including documentation, data validation, and record organization.
Coordinate data and documentation required for sustainability disclosures.
Assist Sustainability team in preparation of data sets and reporting for various federal, state and local environmental compliance programs.
Assist in identifying and addressing gaps in data controls and compliance processes.

You'll Come With

Bachelor’s degree; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
3–5 years of experience in sustainability, environmental analytics, or related field.
Experience manipulating large data sets, collaboration with team members to provide suggestions on data management, provide data validation and auditing, reviewing current state of data-driven processes, development of KPI/dashboard, and work both independently and as part of team environment.
Advanced proficiency in data analytics tools such as: Excel, MS Access, Power BI or equivalent technologies.
Experience using reporting, visualizations, and analytical tools to build insights, communicate findings, and deliver actionable business solutions to stakeholders.
Able to connect various requirements into one synchronized process and work with various stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communications skills that reflect an ability to clarify complex issues.
Ability to work independently, collaboratively, and manage multiple competing projects to timely completion.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist - Water
jobs.description:
Environmental & Water Treatment Engineer
Houston Texas

First Point Group is urgently looking for a Senior Environmental & Water Treatment Engineer to lead environmental compliance and industrial water-treatment design for Manufacturing & Technology projects. This role owns engineering deliverables from basis of design through procurement, construction support, commissioning, and startup.

Key Responsibilities:
Develop and review environmental basis documents, permit-support packages, compliance matrices, discharge limits, wastewater criteria, and environmental design inputs.
Lead industrial water and wastewater treatment design, including water balances, PFDs/P&IDs, process design criteria, equipment specifications, datasheets, requisitions, and technical bid evaluations.
Define source-water quality requirements, pretreatment systems, clarification, multimedia filtration, activated carbon, softening, ion exchange, ultrafiltration, reverse osmosis, demineralization, and wastewater treatment solutions.
Evaluate RO feedwater quality, scaling/fouling risk, recovery targets, membrane protection, chemical dosing, CIP requirements, concentrate/reject-stream routing, and reuse options.
Coordinate design interfaces with process, mechanical, civil, electrical, I&C, procurement, suppliers, construction, commissioning, and client teams.
Review vendor submittals, calculations, equipment selection, hydraulic profiles, control philosophies, utility requirements, and package interfaces.
Resolve environmental and water-treatment risks involving discharge compliance, waste classification, treatment performance, operability, constructability, and startup readiness.
Support HAZOPs, design reviews, vendor meetings, field troubleshooting, commissioning, and performance testing.

Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Chemical, Environmental, Mechanical, or related Engineering discipline.
8+ years of relevant engineering experience with a degree, or 12+ years of relevant industry experience.
5+ years of environmental, industrial water-treatment, wastewater-treatment, RO, or process-water engineering experience.

jobs.title: Software Engineer – Flight Automation & Drone Integrations
jobs.description:
At Airpelago, we are pioneering the inspection of power grids with drones. We combine modern drone technology, proprietary software, and expertise in drone regulations to help grid owners inspect and get insights about their assets, which our society is dependent on. As we continue to scale, we are looking for a Software Engineer to develop the flight automation software that makes our inspections autonomous, and to bring new drone platforms and payloads into our system.

Your mission

You will build and improve the software that plans, executes and monitors autonomous inspection flights. You will also develop integrations with new drone platforms and payloads, from evaluating an SDK to having the aircraft fly a full mission with our software in the field. You will work close to the hardware, close to the data, and close to the people who operate the system in production.

Responsibilities

Develop and maintain our flight automation software, from mission planning to in-flight execution.
Integrate new drone platforms, flight controllers, and payloads (cameras, LiDAR, sensors) into our system.
Work with manufacturer SDKs and APIs, and evaluate new hardware for technical fit.
Build the tooling and abstractions that let us support several drone platforms without duplicating work.
Test and validate your work in the field, together with our operations and testing engineers.
Debug issues that cross the software/hardware boundary: logs, telemetry, radio links, and sensors.
Contribute to technical decisions on architecture, safety and reliability of autonomous flight.
Take ownership of your domain end to end, from idea to production.

What We're Looking For

At least 3 years of software development experience.
Experience integrating hardware and software - drones, cameras, sensors, embedded systems or robotics is a strong advantage.
Comfort working with SDKs, APIs and vendor documentation of varying quality.
Interest in getting out of the office: this role includes field testing with real aircraft.
Structured approach to testing and safety in systems where failures have physical consequences.
Ability to work autonomously and take ownership of a technical domain.
Full proficiency in Swedish and English, both written and verbal.
A valid B driver’s license, with comfort working outdoors and travelling for field testing.
Experience with camera geometry is a strong plus: projection models, calibration (intrinsics/extrinsics), and coordinate transformations.

Experience with MAVLink and DJI SDKs is beneficial but not a requirement. Curiosity and the ability to learn a new platform quickly matter more to us!

Why join Airpelago?

You will play a central role in transforming an industry with automated aerial data. We are currently on an exciting growth journey, and you will become part of a driven, passionate, and highly skilled team. We believe in achieving great things while having fun along the way - including an annual winter office abroad and recurring company gatherings. We offer a dynamic, high-trust environment where our technical innovations directly impact real-world operations and commercial success.

He angitūtanga: The opportunity

Auckland Council's Environmental Services department has an opportunity for a Senior Bio Information Analyst to join our Bio Information Team.

This role focuses on the management, analysis and continuous improvement of ecological information that supports biodiversity protection, environmental planning and Significant Natural Area (SNA) programmes across Tāmaki Makaurau.

Working alongside ecologists, planners and technical specialists, you'll help ensure environmental data is robust, accessible and fit for purpose. You'll take a leading role in maintaining key ecological datasets, providing specialist spatial analysis and developing innovative approaches to environmental data capture, classification and reporting.

This is an opportunity to influence how ecological evidence is used to inform environmental policy, planning decisions and long-term biodiversity outcomes for Auckland.

Please note:
The official title for this position is Senior Bio Information Analyst. We've included Ecological Data & Significant Natural Areas in the advertised title to reflect the primary focus areas of this vacancy.

Day-to-day you could expect to:

Lead the management and maintenance of SNA, ecosystem and ecological datasets.
Undertake spatial data reviews and quality assurance to support environmental decision-making.
Develop and improve ecological data capture, classification and analysis methodologies.
Apply remote sensing and image analysis techniques to support ecological assessment and monitoring.
Deliver specialist GIS, mapping and reporting services for environmental programmes and projects.
Mentor others in spatial data methodologies

He kōrero mōu: About you

You'll bring a strong understanding of environmental information management and enjoy turning complex ecological data into meaningful insights that support real-world environmental outcomes.

You are naturally curious, analytical and collaborative, with the confidence to provide expert technical advice while helping others build their capability.

Our must-haves:

A relevant Bachelor’s degree in an environmental discipline, natural sciences or computer science, together with 7+ years’ relevant professional experience.
Strong knowledge of natural sciences, ideally New Zealand ecology, and experience working with environmental information.
Proven experience developing and implementing information, database, geospatial or data-support solutions.
Advanced capability in ESRI ArcGIS/spatial mapping and/or database design and management, with strong Microsoft Office skills and experience using relevant ecological analysis software.
A full NZ driver’s licence, along with the communication, initiative, relationship-building and resilience to operate confidently in a complex, collaborative environment.

Nice to haves:

A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
Experience with ecological surveys and assessing the significance of natural areas.
Knowledge of SQL database design and functionality in an environmental management context.
Experience specifically across biodiversity, biosecurity or geological information.
Experience mentoring other analysts or leading technical work, projects or information initiatives.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is passionate about the role environmental information plays in protecting and managing Auckland's natural environment. You’ll ideally have experience working with SNA and ecosystem datasets, regional or local plan mapping, remote sensing and image analysis, and an understanding of the RMA and planning system transformation will be highly valued.

We are expanding our team for an exciting Large-scale Mixed‑Use Development project in the North Coast of Egypt
and are looking to engage a highly skilled professional for the role of Sustainability & Environmental Manager.

The Sustainability & Environmental Manager will be responsible for leading and overseeing all sustainability and environmental management activities across the project. The role will ensure compliance with environmental regulations, sustainability targets, and project-specific environmental requirements while integrating sustainability principles throughout design, construction, and operational phases. The successful candidate will act as the primary environmental and sustainability advisor within the PMC team, driving environmental performance, reporting, stakeholder engagement, and alignment with international best practices.

Key Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and monitor sustainability and environmental management strategies, plans, and initiatives across the project.
Ensure compliance with all applicable environmental regulations, permits, standards, and project requirements.
Lead environmental monitoring activities and track sustainability and environmental KPIs.
Coordinate with design consultants and construction teams to integrate sustainability and environmental requirements into project delivery.
Review and assess environmental impact studies, audits, environmental management plans, and sustainability reports.
Manage environmental compliance audits, inspections, and corrective action programs.
Support the implementation of sustainability frameworks such as LEED and other relevant green building initiatives.
Liaise with government authorities, regulatory bodies, stakeholders, and external agencies on environmental matters.
Identify environmental risks and establish mitigation measures to ensure project compliance and sustainability objectives are achieved.
Prepare and present environmental and sustainability performance reports to project leadership and stakeholders.
Promote sustainable construction practices and continuous improvement initiatives throughout the project lifecycle.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to project teams regarding environmental management and sustainability requirements.

Requirements

Education

Bachelor's Degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Engineering, or related discipline.
Master's Degree in Sustainability, Environmental Management, or related field is preferred.

Professional Certifications

LEED Accredited Professional (LEED AP).
ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems certification preferred.
PMP Certification is considered an advantage.
Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) training or certification preferred.

Experience

Minimum 12-15 years of professional experience in sustainability and environmental management.
Proven experience working within a Project Management Consultancy (PMC) or engineering consultancy environment.
Demonstrated experience on large-scale infrastructure, mixed-use developments, or mega projects.
Strong experience implementing sustainability frameworks, including LEED certification requirements.
Extensive knowledge of environmental compliance, audits, inspections, and reporting requirements.
Hands-on experience preparing and reviewing Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA), environmental management plans, and sustainability reports.
Experience integrating environmental and sustainability requirements throughout design and construction phases.
Strong stakeholder management experience with regulatory authorities, consultants, contractors, and project teams.

Technical Competencies

Sustainability Frameworks (LEED and related standards)
Environmental Compliance & Auditing
Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)
Sustainability Reporting
Environmental Performance Monitoring & KPI Management
Environmental Management Systems (ISO 14001)
Regulatory Compliance
Sustainable Design & Construction Practices
Risk Assessment & Mitigation

Key Skills

Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent report writing and presentation skills.
Strong leadership and coordination capabilities.
Effective stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities within complex project environments.
Collaborative approach when working with design teams, construction teams, and external stakeholders.

Preferred Project Experience

Major infrastructure developments.
Mega-projects and large-scale urban development programs.
Projects pursuing sustainability certification targets (LEED or equivalent).
Multi-disciplinary design and construction environments.

jobs.description:

Contents Restoration Project Manager

PuroClean of Burlington

Burlington, Wisconsin

Full-Time | $65,000–$75,000 Base Salary + Performance Opportunity

Build and Lead a Growing Contents Restoration Division

PuroClean of Burlington is looking for an experienced Contents Restoration Project Manager
to take ownership of our contents restoration operation.

This is not simply a cleaning supervisor position.

We are looking for someone who can manage contents restoration projects from the initial inspection and pack-out through inventory, cleaning, storage, insurance documentation and final pack-back.

The right person will combine restoration experience, project management, customer service, organization and leadership
. You will work directly with property owners, insurance professionals, technicians, vendors and company leadership while helping us continue to build and expand our Contents Division.

For the right candidate, this position offers the opportunity to grow beyond individual project management and into broader Contents Division leadership
as the department expands.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

Project Management

Manage residential and commercial contents restoration projects from initial assignment through completion.
Perform or participate in initial contents inspections and project planning.
Establish the pack-out, cleaning, storage and pack-back strategy for each project.
Develop project scopes, schedules, labor requirements and production plans.
Coordinate multiple active projects while maintaining clear priorities and deadlines.
Identify project changes, additional services and potential scope issues before they become problems.
Maintain consistent communication with customers throughout the restoration process.

Pack-Outs, Inventory & Documentation

Oversee professional pack-outs and pack-backs of customer belongings.
Ensure contents are photographed, inventoried, labeled and tracked accurately.
Maintain chain of custody and accountability for customer property from pickup through final return.
Separate and document cleanable, questionable and non-salvageable contents.
Work with customers and insurance representatives regarding cleaning decisions, replacement considerations and non-salvageable items.
Ensure photographs, inventories, work authorizations, job notes and supporting documentation are complete and accurate.
Maintain organized digital project files and documentation.

Contents Cleaning & Restoration

Oversee The Proper Processing Of Items Including

Furniture
Hard contents
Clothing and textiles
Electronics
Appliances
Artwork and decorative items
Household goods
Specialty and high-value contents

Coordinate Appropriate Cleaning Methods Including

Hand cleaning
Ultrasonic cleaning
Deodorization
HEPA cleaning
Smoke and soot removal
Textile restoration
Specialty vendor restoration

Determine when specialty vendors or outside restoration resources should be used.

Customer & Insurance Communication

Serve as a primary point of contact for customers during the contents restoration process.
Explain the contents restoration process, expectations and timelines clearly.
Communicate professionally with insurance adjusters, agents and other claim stakeholders.
Provide documentation necessary to support the services performed.
Assist with estimating, supplements and scope discussions when necessary.
Help resolve customer or insurance questions before they delay the project.

Estimating & Financial Performance

Prepare or assist in preparing contents restoration estimates using industry-standard estimating practices and software.
Review project scope against actual work performed.
Identify missed billable services and legitimate supplemental items.
Monitor labor, materials, subcontractors, storage and project costs.
Help ensure projects are properly documented, invoiced and financially closed.
Maintain awareness of project gross margin and department profitability.
Help management identify opportunities to improve productivity and profitability.

Team Leadership

Lead, schedule and coordinate Contents Technicians.
Establish daily production priorities.
Train employees in proper packing, inventory, cleaning, handling and documentation procedures.
Maintain high standards for productivity, workmanship and professionalism.
Perform quality-control inspections throughout each project.
Hold team members accountable for documentation, organization and customer service.
Assist with recruiting, onboarding and developing additional contents personnel as the division grows.

Warehouse & Storage Management

Maintain an organized contents processing and storage operation.
Ensure customer belongings remain properly labeled and separated.
Maintain organized vaulting, shelving and storage systems.
Coordinate incoming pack-outs and outgoing pack-backs.
Maintain appropriate cleaning equipment, materials and supplies.
Help improve warehouse workflows as contents volume increases.

What We’re Looking For

The strongest candidate will have previous experience in property restoration, contents restoration or insurance-related property claims.

We are particularly interested in candidates with experience managing contents following:

Fire and smoke losses
Water damage
Sewage or contaminated losses
Mold remediation
Large residential losses
Commercial property losses

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of restoration or contents restoration experience.
Previous project management, crew leadership or supervisory experience.
Experience with insurance restoration claims.
Strong understanding of pack-out, inventory, cleaning, storage and pack-back procedures.
Comfortable communicating with homeowners and insurance professionals.
Strong organizational and documentation skills.
Ability to manage several projects simultaneously.
Experience with Xactimate or similar estimating software is strongly preferred.
Comfortable learning and working with digital inventory, photography and project-management systems.
Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.
IICRC certifications are preferred but not required.

Restoration experience is more important to us than a college degree.

The Person Who Will Succeed Here

You should be someone who:

Takes ownership without needing constant direction.
Notices problems before someone else has to point them out.
Can organize a complicated loss and turn it into a workable plan.
Understands that customers’ belongings require both careful handling and accurate documentation.
Can lead technicians while still being willing to step into the field when necessary.
Communicates confidently with homeowners, adjusters and insurance professionals.
Understands that good production and good documentation are equally important.
Pays attention to revenue, costs and profitability instead of treating every project as simply another work order.
Wants responsibility and the opportunity to build something.

This Is a Management Role, But It Is Still Restoration

This position involves both office/project-management responsibilities and field involvement.

You will visit loss sites, inspect contents, oversee crews, interact with customers, work inside damaged properties and periodically assist with contents handling when circumstances require it.

Candidates should be comfortable working around properties affected by fire, smoke, water, mold and other property damage.

The position may occasionally require lifting or assisting with items weighing approximately 50–75 pounds.

Emergency restoration does not always operate between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM. Some schedule flexibility may occasionally be required based on customer and project needs.

Compensation

Base Salary: $65,000–$75,000 annually
, depending on restoration experience and demonstrated ability.

Additional performance-based compensation may be available based on individual and division performance.

Additional benefits and employment details will be discussed during the interview process.

Career Growth

Our goal is not simply to hire someone to manage today’s contents projects.

We are building a larger restoration company and expanding our contents capabilities.

A successful person in this position can grow with the operation as project volume, staffing and revenue increase, with the potential to advance into a broader Contents Division Manager
leadership position.

If you have experience in contents restoration and are ready to take greater ownership of projects, people and results, we want to hear from you.

Apply today to learn more about the Contents Restoration Project Manager opportunity with PuroClean of Burlington.

Compensation: $65,000.00 - $75,000.00 per year

jobs.description:
Restoration Technician – Water, Fire & Mold | Middlesex, NJ

When a pipe bursts at 2 a.m. or a family comes home to a flooded basement, we're the team that shows up. PuroClean Disaster Response is hiring a full-time Restoration Technician to perform water damage restoration, mold remediation, and fire and smoke cleanup in homes and businesses across Central New Jersey. No restoration experience required — we provide paid, hands-on training and pay for your IICRC industry certifications.

Pay & Schedule

$18–$25/hour depending on experience, with overtime opportunities
Full-time, year-round work — this industry doesn't slow down in winter
Rotating on-call schedule for emergency response (extra earning opportunity)
Based in Middlesex, NJ, serving Middlesex, Somerset, and Mercer counties

What You'll Do

Respond to water damage emergencies: water extraction, flood cleanup, and sewage cleanup in residential and commercial properties
Set up and monitor professional drying equipment — dehumidifiers, air movers, air scrubbers — and take daily moisture readings
Perform mold remediation, including containment setup and HEPA cleaning
Assist with fire and smoke damage restoration, deodorization, and contents cleaning
Perform controlled demolition (removing wet drywall, flooring, and insulation)
Document job conditions with photos and notes using our mobile apps
Load, maintain, and organize company vehicles and equipment
Communicate professionally with customers on some of the hardest days of their lives

What We're Looking For

Valid driver's license and insurable driving record
Able to lift 50 lbs, work on your feet, and wear PPE including a respirator
Reliable, coachable, and able to follow written procedures and checklists
Available for a rotating on-call schedule

Experience That Transfers Well (Not Required)

Many of our best technicians came from construction, general labor, carpentry, plumbing, HVAC, landscaping, moving, janitorial, or warehouse work. If you've done physical work with your hands and take pride in doing it right, we'll teach you the restoration trade. IICRC certifications (WRT, ASD, AMRT) are a plus — and if you don't have them, we pay for you to earn them.

Benefits & Perks

Paid training and company-paid IICRC certification courses
Defined career path: Technician → Lead Technician → Crew Chief → Project Manager — we promote from within and can show you the exact skills required for each step
Paid time off and paid holidays
Uniforms, safety equipment, and all tools provided
Steady year-round work — no seasonal layoffs

Compensation: $18.00 - $25.00 per hour

PuroClean Disaster Response is an established, locally owned property damage restoration company backed by the PuroClean national network of over 500 locations. We handle water damage restoration, fire and smoke damage, mold remediation, and biohazard cleanup for homeowners, businesses, and insurance carriers across Central New Jersey, including Middlesex, Somerset, Mercer, Hunterdon, and Monmouth counties. Our values are rooted in community, accountability, respect, excellence, and service with a heart. You'd be joining a team that shows up for people on their worst day — and a sales role where the service you're selling genuinely matters.

jobs.title: Manager of Environmental Programs & Services
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We're powering a cleaner, brighter future.

Exelon is leading the energy transformation, and we're calling all problem solvers, innovators, community builders and change makers. Work with us to deliver solutions that make our diverse cities and communities stronger, healthier and more resilient.

We're powered by purpose-driven people like you who believe in being inclusive and creative, and value safety, innovation, integrity and community service. We are a Fortune 200 company, 20,000 colleagues strong serving more than 10.7 million customers at six energy companies -- Atlantic City Electric (ACE), Baltimore Gas and Electric (BGE), Commonwealth Edison (ComEd), Delmarva Power & Light (DPL), PECO Energy Company (PECO), and Potomac Electric Power Company (Pepco).

We're committed to creating an environment where every person can thrive. Our employee experience is grounded in four tenets that guide how we support our people: purposeful careers, growth opportunities, community impact, and support to thrive.

In our relentless pursuit of excellence, we elevate diverse voices, fresh perspectives and bold thinking. And since we know transforming the future of energy is hard work, we provide competitive compensation, incentives, excellent benefits and the opportunity to build a rewarding career.

Are you in?

Primary Purpose

PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION

Manage personnel, budget and activities of the environmental program to support development and implementation of cost-effective compliance with applicable environmental laws, and regulations associated with all company operations. Oversee program plans for environmental compliance, site remediation, MGP projects and superfund activities including program objectives, budget, procurement plans, and shared project goals. Develop and maintain relationships with internal departments and external organizations, including regulatory agencies, & government officials to facilitate and leverage acceptance, approval, and funding of projects, regulatory engineering and environmental leadership positions. Position may be required to work extended hours for coverage during storms or other energy delivery emergencies.

Primary Duties

PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES

Develop & direct complex MGP/superfund site remediation program including risk-based program objectives, budget, schedule and contractor management. Support negotiation of new contracts or changes to existing contracts that support business and regulatory objectives. Identify and implement business and technical best practices.
Ensure world-class performance of the company's Environmental Management System. Work collaboratively with Operations and Support Services to address environmental risks and the development of liability reduction programs. Ensure all environmental permitting, waste handling and tracking, spill prevention, pollution prevention, recycling, greenhouse gas reduction, leaking equipment and PCB reduction programs are effectively implemented and tracked.
Manage Department budget, establish and monitor business plans, objectives and goals. The EHS Staff will master legal regulations related to safety, Health, Environment, Chemicals, and Energy, and ensure compliance through training, guidance, and implementing improvement activities.

Responsibilities

Master legal regulations regarding Safety, Health, Environment, Chemicals, and Energy.
Periodically update new regulations, evaluate their impacts, and provide training and guidance on implementing improvement activities to ensure legal compliance.
Prepare and submit periodic and ad-hoc records and reports on Safety, Health, Environment, and Chemicals to the competent state authorities.
Implement EHS targets and indicators, as well as action and improvement programs to achieve set goals.
Develop rules, procedures, and measures to ensure Safety, Health, Environment, Chemicals, and Energy.
Participate in developing and implementing risk assessments, plans, risk prevention measures, and response plans for environmental and chemical incidents.
Inspect, monitor, and resolve outstanding issues related to Safety, Health, Environment, Chemicals, and Energy to ensure compliance with the law and corporate EHS regulations at the factories.
Measure, inspect, and evaluate hazardous and harmful factors affecting employees' working conditions (such as temperature, dust, noise, toxic gases, etc.), and synthesize solutions for improvement to ensure proper conditions for workers.
Organize investigations and report on occupational accidents, traffic accidents, and safety incidents. Compile statistics on outstanding issues and monitor the implementation of corrective and preventive solutions until completion.
Organize and implement safety inspections, risk assessments, and machinery/equipment safety evaluations.
Conduct safety evaluations prior to performing non-routine work, and inspect/evaluate safety impacts when launching new projects.
Update and monitor records and inspection deadlines, and organize annual periodic inspections for equipment with strict safety requirements.
Organize and deploy annual EHS programs and activities (such as monthly EHS meetings, 5S/HHK activities, KYT, stop-cards, etc.).
Monitor, inspect, and supervise the distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) to employees. Check inventory, synthesize data, and plan PPE orders to ensure adequate distribution to all workers.
Implement periodic environmental and occupational environment monitoring programs. Evaluate the results and propose improvement solutions if they fail to meet legal requirements or company targets.
Synthesize and control waste data; evaluate, process payments, classify, and retain monthly records. Coordinate with relevant departments to propose appropriate solutions to minimize, reuse, and recycle waste.
Inspect and evaluate waste classification, waste storage, chemical storage, wastewater treatment stations, and exhaust gas systems, proposing improvements if they do not meet legal requirements.
Participate in developing and organizing training courses on Safety, Environment, and Chemicals for employees.
Perform other tasks as assigned by supervisors.

Qualifications

University graduate majoring in Occupational Health and Safety or Environmental Management.
Professional knowledge of ISO 14000-2015 and ISO 45001 systems.
Proficient in using computers, office equipment, and software (Google Sheets, Docs, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
Proficient in English for communication, reading comprehension, and preparing related reports for the region.
At least 1-3 years of working experience in Safety, Environment, and Chemicals at manufacturing plants.
Ability to work independently and in a team (proactively executing assigned tasks with the factory, from planning to implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and measurement).
Agile, enthusiastic, responsible, and fully compliant with internal company regulations and the law.

Required Skills

Strong knowledge of EHS regulations and standards.
Excellent communication and training skills.
Ability to analyze and synthesize data for reporting.

Preferred Skills

Experience in a multicultural work environment.
Familiarity with advanced EHS software tools.

jobs.title: Senior Bio Information Analyst - UAV & Environmental Tech
jobs.description:
Lead Auckland Council's environmental UAV programme and support best-practice aerial data collection
Combine ecology, geospatial analysis and emerging technologies to drive better environmental outcomes
Mentor pilots, champion innovation and shape the future of environmental data capability

He angitūtanga: The opportunity

Auckland Council's Environmental Services department has an opportunity for a Senior Bio Information Analyst to join Bio Information Team.

With a passion and understanding of ecosystem services, to take on both spatial analysis and Senior Remote Pilot duties, including those delegated from our Chief Pilot, this role sits at the intersection of ecology, geospatial technology, UAV operations and environmental innovation.

You'll play a key role in how environmental information is captured, analysed and transformed into insights that support biodiversity protection, ecological monitoring and environmental decision-making across Tāmaki Makaurau.

We are CAA certified and maintain a high standard of UAV best practice in our ecological survey, including thermal night flights; you’ll be comfortable leading by example, and helping maintain the high standards expected within our CAA-certified programme

As a senior member of the team, you'll also contribute to our Enabling Tools programme, identifying opportunities to use emerging technologies, automation and digital solutions to improve environmental outcomes and organisational capability along with mentoring pilots across the department.

Please note:
The official title for this position is S enior Bio Information Analyst
. We've included UAV & Environmental Tech
in the advertised title to reflect the primary focus areas of this vacancy.

Day-to-day you could expect to:

Support and enhance Auckland Council's Environmental Services UAV programme, including delegated Senior Remote Pilot responsibilities.
Deliver expert GIS, spatial analysis and environmental information management advice across a range of environmental initiatives.
Undertake and support UAV-based ecological surveys, mapping and environmental monitoring activities.
Mentor and support UAV pilots, contributing to capability development and best-practice operations across the department.
Identify and implement innovative digital, imagery and data solutions that improve environmental outcomes and organisational capability.

He kōrero mōu: About you

This role requires significant experience in environmental information, spatial analysis, GIS or a related natural science field, alongside the confidence to provide technical leadership and specialist advice.

We're looking for someone who enjoys working where ecology and technology come together, someone who can go beyond simply managing data. You'll be naturally curious, solutions-focused and motivated by finding new ways to collect, analyse and apply environmental information.

Ideally, you'll have experience operating UAVs to best-practice standards and be certified to 102, along with experience in IoT and image processing.

Our must-haves:

A relevant Bachelor’s degree in an environmental discipline, natural sciences or computer science, together with 7+ years’ relevant professional experience.
Strong knowledge of natural sciences, ideally New Zealand ecology, and experience working with environmental information.
Proven experience developing and implementing information, database, geospatial or data-support solutions.
Advanced capability in ESRI ArcGIS/spatial mapping and/or database design and management, with strong Microsoft Office skills and experience using relevant ecological analysis software.
A full NZ driver’s licence, along with the communication, initiative, relationship-building and resilience to operate confidently in a complex, collaborative environment.

Nice to haves:

A Master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
Experience with ecological surveys and assessing the significance of natural areas.
Knowledge of SQL database design and functionality in an environmental management context.
Experience specifically across biodiversity, biosecurity or geological information.
Experience mentoring other analysts or leading technical work, projects or information initiatives.

Most importantly, we’re looking for someone with the drive to make environmental information useful. You’ll need to be comfortable taking ownership, solving problems where there isn’t always an obvious answer, influencing others and confidently providing advice to both technical and non-technical audiences.

You’ll also bring an appreciation of Te Ao Māori and tikanga, and a willingness to continue developing your confidence and capability in te reo Māori and our Treaty responsiveness journey.

Ngā āhuatanga kei a mātou: What we offer

Auckland Council is the largest local government council across Oceania, serving over 1.7 million people and contributing towards making Tāmaki Makaurau a world-class city.

We offer a range of employee benefits and proudly support flexible working options where possible.

You’ll have access to a range of fantastic Auckland Council benefits, EAP services, an Oranga Day and discounted Leisure Centre membership and a range of other partnership discounts! View a snapshot of some of our employee benefits here :

We are a diverse organisation – we value diversity in our thinking, and we can only achieve that with a diverse team!

Introduction

We encourage you to consider an exciting career with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). If you are dedicated to protecting and preserving Maryland's air, water, land resources, and safeguarding the health of all its citizens, we invite you to apply and become a part of our team.

MDE is committed to a mission of protecting and restoring the environment for the health and well-being of all Marylanders, with a vision of healthy, vibrant, and sustainable communities and ecosystems throughout the state.

As part of our continuous efforts to optimize performance and drive success the Natural Resource Planner II is eligible for an annual promotion. The incumbent may advance to a higher grade within the classification series, based on satisfactory work performance. Progressive grade levels include: Natural Resource Planner III – Grade 16 $67,309.00 -$106,155.00 Yearly.

PLEASE FILL OUT THE APPLICATION COMPLETELY.

To learn more about MDE Click Here .

GRADE

STD0015

LOCATION OF POSITION

MDE - Water and Science Administration

Stormwater Program Review Division

1800 Washington Boulevard

Baltimore, MD 21230

Main Purpose of Job

The NRP II core responsibilities and key functions consist of the following:

Program Review & Permit Development
: Evaluate local erosion and sediment control, stormwater management, and federal stormwater permitting programs by applying principles of natural resources, hydrology, and climate change science. Maintain up-to-date scientific knowledge to inform and develop permit language.

Field Inspections & Programmatic Evaluation
: Travel throughout Maryland to inspect urban pollution control practices, assess the local implementation of state laws and regulations, evaluate local codes and enforcement policies, and observe programmatic procedures in practice.

Reporting & Recommendations
: Analyze collected data and field observations to evaluate local program effectiveness. Develop reports and recommendations regarding program delegation and enforcement to help improve the quality of local compliance efforts and protect Maryland's streams, rivers, and the Chesapeake Bay.

Stakeholder Engagement & Outreach
: Build strong relationships with internal staff and external stakeholders, respond to technical inquiries, and act as a statewide resource to promote consistency across local programs. Effectively communicate policies regarding climate change and environmental justice.

The incumbent in this position will be required to drive a State vehicle.

Driver’s License
:
A valid driver’s license with no more than five points is required to operate a State vehicle.

Out-of-State Licenses
:
If you hold an out-of-state license, you must provide a certified copy of your driving record from the appropriate Motor Vehicle Administration at the time of appointment.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in an environmental science or natural resources planning, management or development.

Experience:
One year of experience in natural resources planning or applied environmental science.

Notes

Candidates may substitute the possession of a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in urban or regional planning, engineering, physical geography, or the physical, chemical, biological sciences and one year of experience in natural resources planning or applied environmental science for the required education.
Candidates may substitute the possession of a Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in natural resources planning, management, administration, development, environmental, urban or regional planning; resources economics or development; environmental system management; water or land resources planning and management; environmental landscape architecture; or the physical, biological, chemical or environmental sciences for the required experience.
Candidates may substitute U.S. Armed Forces military service experience as a commissioned officer in the general natural resources management and biological sciences classifications or general natural resources management and biological sciences specialty codes in the general natural resources management and biological sciences field of work on a year-for-year basis for the required experience and education.

Desired Or Preferred Qualifications

It is preferred that the selected candidate has the following:

Familiar with NPDES municipal separate storm sewer system permits;
Background in the implementation of best practices for stormwater management and soil erosion and sediment control;
Ability to evaluate plans and write reports;
Experience working with databases and GIS mapping.

LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS

NOT APPLICABLE.

SELECTION PROCESS

Please make sure that you provide sufficient information on your application to show that you meet the qualifications for this recruitment. All information concerning your qualifications must be submitted by the closing date. We will not consider the information submitted after this date. Successful candidates will be ranked as Best Qualified and placed on the eligible (employment) list for at least one year.

The Maryland Department of the Environment has determined that this position requires a background investigation to verify suitability for employment. About Indiana Department Of Environmental Management (IDEM)

Our mission is to implement federal and state regulations to protect human health and the environment while allowing the environmentally sound operations of industrial, agricultural, commercial, and governmental activities vital to a prosperous economy. We issue air, water, and solid and hazardous waste permits that restrict discharges to environmentally safe levels. Staff members inspect and monitor regulated entities; provide compliance and technical assistance; monitor and assess air, land, and water quality; use enforcement actions as necessary to ensure compliance; and respond to incidents involving spills to soil or waters of the state.

Role Overview

This position exists within the Office of Water Quality and will be stationed in the Indianapolis Office of the Indiana Department of Environmental Management. However, based on the candidate selected alternate locations may be considered.

The position is responsible for administering stormwater regulations in an efficient and consistent manner. The primary function of this position is to administer the stormwater program, which includes a multidisciplinary approach to stormwater management, erosion and sediment control, and pollution prevention. Responsibilities include permitting industrial and construction sites and contributing to program development. Responsibilities also include but are not limited reviewing stormwater pollution prevention plans and conducting regulatory inspections for construction sites and industrial facilities and audits of local Municipal Separate Storm Sewer Systems (MS4s).

This position requires a valid IN driver's license.

to view the total compensation package.

A Day In The Life

Serves as an environmental expert and provides guidance to regulated communities, government officials, attorneys and staff responsible for a variety of programs and program elements.
Project Management: Performs project management duties to ensure effective and timely management of program area needs, attends meetings, and responds to telephone calls, e-mails, etc., as required. Acts as a technical point-of-contact for assigned programs administering environmental programs which may include, but not limited to, environmental media sampling, data analysis, technical writing, work plan and report preparation, technical reviews, etc.
Permits: Researches state and federal guidance, laws, and regulations related to permits. Contacts applicants to request additional information to process applications, when necessary. Responds to comments from applicants, defends permit terms and conditions, and interacts with permittees to resolve permitting issues. The Environmental Graphics Officer is responsible for designing, evaluating, and managing high-quality signages, wayfinding systems, spatial graphic displays, and property enhancement set-ups across the integrated resort. Reporting to the Environmental Graphics leadership, the primary objective of this role is to elevate guest navigation, support brand consistency, and maintain the aesthetic and structural integrity of all environmental graphics through precision design, site assessments, and strict adherence to Service Level Agreements (SLAs). The position operates within the limits of established brand guidelines, safety standards, material and fabrication budgets, and departmental project management protocols, requiring technical accuracy, creative initiative, and flexibility to meet project deadlines.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Environmental Graphic & Spatial Design

Design comprehensive property signages, wayfinding systems, and graphic artwork in alignment with the resort’s brand identity and team scope.
Develop conceptual and production designs for temporary and permanent spatial installations, including promotional booths, VIP lounges, stage set-ups, construction hoardings/board-ups, and property improvement elements.
Produce precise layout specifications, scale drawings, and detailed plans reflecting accurate dimensions for all proposed signage and graphic installations.

Site Inspection & Technical Assessment

Conduct initial site ocular inspections for proposed projects to assess physical space dimensions, structural requirements, and material suitability.
Perform daily site ocular inspections for ongoing and installed projects to monitor the physical condition, functionality, and visual appeal of signages under the team's accountability.
Apply technical understanding of floor plans, elevations, section plans, and architectural terminology to ensure seamless integration of designs with existing resort structures.

Fabrication & Material Coordination

Evaluate and select appropriate building and construction materials suitable for various environmental conditions across the property.
Oversee and guide signage fabrication processes, ensuring technical standards are met for components such as backlit displays, LED adboxes, lightboxes, and architectural signage.

Project & Workflow Management

Manage incoming project job orders to ensure strict adherence to agreed Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and project timelines.
Evaluate workflow processes, organize project task lists, and prioritize design deliverables to optimize team efficiency.
Report real-time project status, operational risks, and design bottlenecks to superiors, ensuring timely escalation and necessary approvals.

Stakeholder Engagement & Administrative Support

Participate in and present design concepts, technical proposals, and project deliberations during stakeholder meetings.
Draft professional email communications, design briefs, and presentation materials for internal and external project collaborators.
Provide ongoing technical and administrative support to team leadership to streamline overall department operations and daily workflows.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Civil/Structural Engineering, Fine Arts, Graphic Design, or an equivalent field of study.
Work Experience:
Minimum of 2–3 years of hands-on experience in environmental graphics, signage design, wayfinding, or spatial/exhibition set-up design, ideally within large-scale commercial, hospitality, or resort properties.

Advanced proficiency in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software and graphic layout programs, including Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, CorelDraw, and relevant 2D/3D drafting tools.
Strong ability to read, interpret, and generate technical layout plans, floor plans, structural elevations, and section diagrams.
Fabrication & Material Knowledge:

Solid understanding of architectural/building materials, visual display components, and fabrication techniques for lighted signs, LED adboxes, lightboxes, and structural installations.
Communication & Soft Skills:

Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with proven confidence in delivering technical presentations, writing project briefs, and collaborating across teams.
Strong aesthetic judgment, creative imagination, and attention to detail.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Associate
jobs.description:
This position is based on a hybrid work schedule and will require in-office work 3 days per week.

As a member of Sargent & Lundy’s Environmental and Permitting team, you will utilize your academic background and experience to review, evaluate, and implement federal, state and local environmental regulatory requirements as they apply to a variety of electric power, nuclear power and industrial projects. You will be asked to use your knowledge of environmental regulations and engineering principals to meet project team and client needs for defining, evaluating, and implementing environmental mitigation, compliance, and permitting projects.
The position will offer you the opportunity to expand your knowledge of federal, state and local environmental regulations as they apply to major industrial projects, and to work with multi-disciplined project teams to:
Review and implement federal, state, and local regulatory requirements as they apply to specific projects and develop strategies to implement cost-effective mitigation compliance plans.
Prepare site-specific environmental impact studies to evaluate the suitability of a site for a proposed fossil fuel power plant, nuclear power facility, wind energy farm, solar generating station, electric substation, or transmission line.
Work with project engineers to ensure projects are designed and developed using criteria that recognize all relevant environmental requirements.
Prepare permit matrices and permit applications and interface with federal, state, and local permitting agencies.

Prepare complex technical reports including site selection studies, environmental and social impact assessments, compliance audits, and regulatory reviews. You will have the opportunity to develop your environmental career via peer-learning and knowledge sharing with other engineers and environmental professionals and participating in Sargent & Lundy’s System of Processes and our associated “Communities of Practice.”
The position offers the opportunity to travel to client offices and project site locations for project reviews. Some international travel may be required.

Qualifications

We do not sponsor employees for work authorization in the U.S. for this position.

Essential Sk Ills And Experience

A BS in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or related field, MS preferred.
Five or more years of experience in environmental compliance, environmental impact assessment, and/or permitting for complex industrial projects.
Familiarity with environmental laws and regulations that apply to large industrial facilities, including the National Environmental Policy Act, Threatened & Endangered Species Act, Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act.
Environmental impact assessment/permitting experience, including specific experience in one or more of the following fields:
Environmental Impact Assessments.
Phase 1 and 2 Environmental Site Assessments
Subsequent License Renewals and associated Environmental Reports.
Preparation of Title V Permit Application
NPDES wastewater and construction stormwater discharge permitting.
Army Corp (wetlands) permitting.
Preparation of SWPPP/SPCC plans
Major source air permitting including preparation of air permit applications, emissions calculations, New Source Review and PSD permitting.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to interact and multitask with project team members, clients, and regulatory agencies
Ability to work on multiple projects at the same time and coordinate various inputs between the internal engineering team, client and regulatory agency.
Ability to provide guidance to associate staff members.
Experience with all Microsoft applications including proficiency specifically in Excel and Word.

Valued But Not Required Skills And Experience

Proficiency in ArcGIS mapping and experience in developing interactive maps showing critical environmental resources such as wetlands, critical habitats, and other sensitive receptors.
Certification or coursework in GIS is a plus

Proficiency in AERMOD and experience in preparation of inputs to the software.

Technology & Innovation

Sargent & Lundy values the appropriate use of technology to improve how work gets done and deliver high-quality outcomes for our clients. Depending on the role, employees may use data, automation, artificial intelligence, and other digital tools to support research, analysis, engineering and design activities, workflow improvement, or other aspects of their work.

We value candidates who demonstrate an interest in learning and effectively using emerging technologies where relevant to their role. Employees remain accountable for their work and are expected to apply appropriate professional judgment and review when using technology-assisted tools.

Experience with AI, automation, programming, or similar technologies is valued where relevant but is not required unless specifically identified elsewhere in the job description.

About Sargent & Lundy

At Sargent & Lundy, we care about the health and well-being of our employees. Our commitment extends beyond the workplace, offering comprehensive healthcare plans and generous paid time off to support our team members in every aspect of their lives. We understand the importance of work-life balance, which is why we are proud to provide competitive, award-winning benefits. Our dedication to employee satisfaction has earned us the prestigious Top Workplaces Culture Excellence Award for compensation and benefits in 2022, 2023, and 2024.

Individuals may also be eligible to participate in our yearly discretionary bonus.

About This Business Unit

The Energy & Industrial Group (EIG) specializes in delivering advanced engineering solutions across various sectors, including power generation, environmental compliance, oil & gas, and industrial projects, from new plant design to plant betterment and upgrade services for operating facilities. We have designed nearly 900 conventional power plants, yielding over 100,000 megawatts (MW) of generation capacity. Our expertise includes numerous recent and ongoing combined cycle projects that leverage the latest advanced machinery, including combustion turbines, steam turbines, and heat recovery steam generators from all leading suppliers. EIG is recognized for its commitment to decarbonization through innovative technologies in renewable energy, carbon capture, and hydrogen power. We excel in detailed engineering services for photovoltaic (PV) solar projects and energy storage integration, and lead the industry in carbon capture technologies, managing projects from conceptual studies, pilot demonstrations and through commercial scale implementation for utilities and industrial plants.

jobs.description:
Build a brilliant career. Shape a sustainable tomorrow.

Do you want to build your career with a globally connected, welcoming team? Where you'll be trusted with real responsibility, empowered to contribute to projects that create a more sustainable future - and given the support to develop both professionally and personally?

Take the driver's seat in your career on the AtkinsRéalis Graduate Development Programme, guided by inspiring, supportive managers. And say yes to brilliant opportunities that spark your interest, knowing you'll have training and the support you need to maintain a healthy work‑life balance.

We believe reaching your full potential means being able to bring your whole self to work and feeling like you belong. Find out more about our global programme Different Makes a Difference.

We are AtkinsRéalis, a world‑class engineering services and nuclear organization. Here you’ll help create world‑class sustainable solutions that connect people, data and technology. We're transforming infrastructure and energy systems, growing partnerships with our clients, and bringing the most complex projects across the globe to life.

Our global team of 40,000+ employees speak over 70 languages and represent some 130 nationalities across six continents. Our work covers a variety of sectors, including power, transportation, infrastructure, environment, water, nuclear, technology, defence and aerospace.

Where you could work

You'll have the opportunity to work on a diverse range of projects, develop new skills and gain valuable experience while making a positive impact on people, communities and the environment.

Depending on your interests and location preferences, you could join one of our teams working within the Buildings and Places and Water sectors, helping to deliver some of the world's most complex and rewarding projects.

Want to learn more? Follow the links above to explore each sector, the teams and types of projects you could work on.

What you can bring

A curious mindset and enthusiasm for solving real-world challenges
A desire to champion a culture where everyone belongs
A collaborative working style and confidence building positive relationships
Enthusiasm and drive to develop your skillset and seek out development opportunities within a supportive team
Motivation to achieve professional accreditation (where applicable)
Comfortable embracing agile ways of working and learning new technologies
A commitment to spend a minimum of three days a week in the office or on client site (project dependent). Being together in person helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more effectively, and accelerate your learning and development.

How do I apply?

Click " Apply
" to start your application - you'll be taken to our vacancies platform, where you can explore specific graduate roles that match your interests. On the platform use the search and filter options to narrow down roles by location, sector and other preferences, select the role you'd like to apply for and submit your application.

Please note - you can only make one application
per recruitment campaign.

For tips and advice on applying - and to message your questions directly to one of our graduate mentors - check out our Early Careers TalentConnector platform.

As a Disability Confident Employer we can make adjustments to support you to perform at your best during the recruitment process. To find out how we can support you please contact us confidentially at graduates@atkinsrealis.com

Our deadline for applications is 3 December 2026. However, as our Graduate Development Programmes are incredibly popular, apply early as some roles may close sooner.

More about us

AtkinsRéalis is a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We design and deliver major projects on the built and natural environments all around the world. We believe that digitally enabled engineering has the power to radically improve the way we are all housed, connected, powered, and protected and can change our relationship with our communities and our planet for the better. We are committed to building a culture where everyone belongs - a place where you can all be yourself, thrive and reach your full potential. Join us and engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

Learn more

Training and development

Our Graduate Development Programme is designed to give you an insight into many areas of work and the chance to explore where your own skills and interests lie. It features a series of training events and modules, professional development, mentoring, and on-the-job experience as well as practical skills development.

From day one, you'll work on real projects that offer scale and variety, collaborating with colleagues and creating meaningful impact on the world around us. You'll work towards your professional accreditation (where applicable) - whichever path you take, your future starts here.

Meeting your needs

We’ll reward and support you in many ways, including offering:

a settling-in payment of £2,500 when you join and a further payment of £2,500 when you achieve chartered status or reach an equivalent stage in your professional development
33 days’ annual leave, including bank holidays, with the option to buy an additional 15 days or sell up to 5 days
two paid annual volunteer days
a brilliant range of rewards and benefits
opportunities to join talented graduates in skill-building, social events, charity challenges, Young Professional Awards, social clubs and exciting secondments
access to employee networks for social interaction, peer support and personal development
opportunities to develop yourself by applying to various company-wide development programmes
access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP), providing you with immediate and confidential help for any work, health or life matters and a wealth of other wellbeing resources
an enhanced maternity scheme and family-friendly policies.

Our graduate salaries are between £32,000 - £34,500 depending on role and location.

Additional information

This role may require a security clearance, and offers of employment will be dependent on obtaining the relevant level of clearance. If this is necessary, it will be discussed with you at the interview. The vetting process is delivered by United Kingdom Security Vetting (UKSV) and may require candidates to provide proof of residency in the UK of 5 years or longer. If applying to this role, please do not make reference to (in conversation) or include in your application details of any current or previously held security clearance.

Due to current Government immigration salary thresholds, AtkinsRéalis do not sponsor any skilled worker visas for our early careers programme as the Home Office's eligibility criteria would not be met. Given the length of our early careers programme AtkinsRéalis requires applicants to have the right to work in the UK (without sponsorship by AtkinsRéalis) for the duration of the programme. Applicants should ensure they can meet this requirement prior to making an application. For more information, please visit our International Students page.
