Position Description

JOB DESCRIPTION

Nevada Gold Mines is looking for an Environmental Specialist to join our Environmental Team at the Phoenix Mine. The successful candidate will play a key role in maintaining and improving the site’s environmental management systems, with a primary focus on ISO 14001, Cority, environmental document control, and GIS.

The successful candidate will work closely with Environmental, Operations, Engineering, and other site departments to ensure environmental information is accurate, accessible, properly documented, and maintained in accordance with regulatory and company requirements.

This is an excellent opportunity for an individual who enjoys working with environmental data and systems while also having the opportunity to support field activities and continuous improvement initiatives.

Responsibilities

Support the ongoing implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the site’s ISO 14001 Environmental Management System.
Maintain ISO 14001 documentation, records, procedures, forms, and associated environmental management system information.
Support internal and external ISO 14001 audits, including preparation of documentation and evidence.
Track audit findings, corrective actions, opportunities for improvement, and associated action plans.
Assist with maintaining environmental objectives, targets, programs, and performance metrics.
Support environmental aspect and impact assessments and evaluation of compliance processes.
Assist with Management of Change (MOC) processes from an environmental perspective.
Track environmental management system action items and ensure documentation is completed and maintained.
Support employee awareness and training related to ISO 14001 and environmental management system requirements.
Serve as a key user and administrator/support resource for the site's Cority environmental management system.
Maintain the Environmental Department's document control system.
Ensure environmental procedures, plans, work instructions, forms, permits, reports, and records are properly controlled and current.
Maintain and update environmental GIS databases, maps, and spatial data.
Develop maps and figures to support environmental permitting, compliance, reclamation, monitoring, and reporting activities.
Manage environmental spatial data, including sampling locations, monitoring points, reclamation areas, disturbance areas, infrastructure, permits, and other environmental features.
Support users with data entry, system questions, and troubleshooting.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Manages budgets, including the budget for external ISO audits.
Coordinates with supply chain personnel to procure contractor and consultant services, as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree preferred
Experience with compliance systems and ISO 14001 preferred
Experience with PowerPoint, Publisher, Word, and Excel required
Three to five years in a mining industry setting preferred
Experience in Environmental compliance programs preferred
Excellent verbal, written, presentation and interpersonal skills required
Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously required

About Us

Our mission is to be the world’s most valued gold and copper mining business. We are committed to partnering with our host countries and communities to transform their natural resources into tangible benefits and mutual prosperity.

Barrick is a leading global mining, exploration and development company. With one of the largest portfolios of world-class and life-long gold and copper assets in the industry - including six of the world's Tier One gold mines - Barrick's operations an projects span 18 countries and five continents. Barrick is also the largest gold producer in the United States. We create real, long-term value for all stakeholders through responsible mining, strong partnerships, and a disciplined approach to growth. Barrick shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "B" and on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol "ABX".

About The Team

Nevada Gold Mines (NGM) is a joint venture between Barrick (61.5%) and Newmont (38.5%) that combined our significant assets across Nevada in 2019 to create the single largest gold-producing complex in the world. NGM produces approximately 3.5 million ounces of gold a year. The massive mining operation comprises eight mines along with their associated infrastructure and processing facilities and hosts three of Barrick’s Tier One assets: Carlin, Cortez, and Turquoise Ridge. At NGM, our mission is to be the world’s most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and owning the best assets, with the best people, to deliver sustainable returns for our owners and partners.

This Opportunity

WSP has an exciting career opportunity for an Environmental Remediation Project Manager/Office Manager
to join our Rifle, CO
team. Scope of this role includes remedial design, field investigations, contaminated site management, data analysis and team oversight. This role will work closely with contaminated site portfolio leads and ensure the correct delivery of projects within the oil and gas industry, as well as overseeing the Rifle office on a day-to-day basis, overseeing staff and assisting with monitoring progress on contractor submittals, requests for Information, information bulletins, change/field Orders. This role would report to the North Mountain Site Investigation and Remediation (SIR) Service Line lead and be able to draw on expertise and resources in the SIR team throughout Colorado and the West.

Will have the opportunity to be involved in projects with our Earth & Environment Team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our client’s objectives and solves their challenges.

Are you looking for an exciting career opportunity where you can put your skills and talents to work with an established engineering consulting firm that values its employees’ enthusiasm and technical contributions? Do you enjoy managing projects and bringing in new projects? We encourage you to apply for this opportunity. We provide the atmosphere to allow individuals to grow their career. We’d love you to join our team of friendly, hard-working, dedicated and collaborative professionals. Our ideal candidate is seeking challenging work and is committed to quality.

Rifle, Colorado is a small town located on the beautiful Western Slope of Colorado, and centrally located 30 minutes west of Glenwood Springs; 1 hour northeast of Grand Junction, CO; 90 minutes northwest of Aspen, CO; 2 hours west of Breckenridge, CO and 3 hours west of Denver, CO.

Located directly on the Colorado River and near some of Colorado’s most popular tourist destinations, Rifle is the ideal location for adventure seekers. Residents enjoy skiing, fly fishing, hiking, camping, rafting, kayaking, and mountain biking all located right out your backdoor. Rifle Mountain Park (popular with rock climbers) is located 16 miles north of Rifle and Rifle Falls, Rifle Gap and Harvey Gap state parks are close by. There is access to BLM areas Hubbard Mesa Open Area, Rifle Arch and the Roan Plateau. The Rifle Creek Golf Course is 6 miles north of the center of Rifle.

Your Impact

Assist Senior Project Managers with their duties as necessary.
Coordinate weekly scheduling meetings.
Assist project Teams with multiple projects as requested.
Provide support to other staff on processes and requirements, monitor contract compliance, participate in the development of contracts.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Manage/oversee projects under the client’s Terms and Conditions which have been negotiated prior.
Support field staff collecting soil, groundwater and air samples for field and/or laboratory analyses.
Assisting and reviewing in the creation of detailed maps, lithologic logs and cross sections gathering, tabulating and analyzing data.
Preparing and reviewing proposals, cost estimates and technical reports for regulatory agencies submittal.
Oversee the team operating and maintaining field equipment and instrumentation.
Understand federal and state rules and regulations regarding environmental permitting compliance and remediation.
Provide senior-level expertise and technical guidance on complex regulatory projects.
Lead and mentor geologists, engineers and environmental scientists, guiding junior staff.
Prepare technical and Forms reports related for the Energy and Carbon Management Commission, Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission and Utah Department of Oil, Gas and Mining.
Takes projects from original discovery through final remediation.
Oversee various moderately-complex projects without the oversight of a Senior Project Manager and minimal oversight from technical teams.
Responsible for assembling project/task teams and assigning individual responsibilities, identifying appropriate resources needed. Given the complexity of the project, these teams could be larger, multi-disciplinary, and may reside in various states.
Develop the project scope and objectives, as well as clarify the role and function of each team member to effectively coordinate the activities of the team.
Identify, monitor, and mitigate risk on projects where the client may not have a full understanding of the project risks.
Take lead in development of proposals in collaboration with others.
Plan the execution of the project and monitor performance according to the project execution plan and the contract terms and conditions.
Manage project closure aspects ensuring correct project documentation.
Ensure project team (including sub-consultants/contractors) have understood and continually reassess the HSSE requirements of the project.
Develop and ensure adherence to the project schedule.
Supervise change request activities by appropriately addressing anticipated scope changes as they evolve and can advise others on scope change.
Assess and predict the possible impacts of schedule changes and the time management outcomes for future project impacts.
Develop a multi-disciplinary project budget and interact with subcontractors to develop the project budget.
Assign project budgets to task leaders and manage their performance.
Ensure compliance with client invoicing requirements and timely payment.
Will travel to project sites mostly in western Colorado and surrounding states. Approximately 10% overnight travel.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

BS degree in Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or related discipline; PG or PE license preferred.
Minimum of 7 -10+ years of environmental consulting and/or project management experience.
Demonstrated experience with project financial tracking, and change management related to scopes of work.CAD, Civil 3D®, ArcGIS experience a plus
Expertise in project planning, numerical tracking and analysis (e.g., using MS Excel or similar programs).
Highly organized, adaptable, a developing leader and calm under pressure.
Experience in managing multi-discipline teams.
Effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to a scientific and non-scientific audience.
Highly capable self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
Ability to work independently and provide guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
Proficiency with technical writing, office automation and communication software, technology, and tools.
Ability to assertively direct others in the field such as subcontracted drillers, excavation contractors, utility locators, and others to consistently complete tasks safely and efficiently.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek
Ability and willingness to travel to project sites mostly in western Colorado and surrounding states. Approximately 10% overnight travel.
Must pass drug test, background check and must have a satisfactory driving record in accordance with the Company's driving (MVR) policy.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional licensure/certification.
40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120) preferred.

WSP Benefits

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Expected Salary (Colorado only): $105,000 - $175,000

jobs.title: Environmental Project Manager (Environmental Remediation) - Goshen, NY or Woodbridge, NJ
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is seeking an experienced Environmental Project Manager
to join our Environmental Investigation, and Remediation team in the Goshen, New York or Woodbridge, New Jersey area
.

This position is ideal for an environmental professional with a background in engineering, environmental science, geology, or a related technical discipline
who has strong technical and project management capabilities.

The successful candidate will manage environmental projects for private-sector industrial in northern New Jersey. We are particularly interested in candidates with strong technical backgrounds in soil assessment, groundwater fate and transport, non-aqueous phase liquids (NAPL), and environmental chemistry. In addition, candidates should have strong project management skills, including the ability to plan and manage the scope, schedule, and budget of multiple fast-paced environmental assessment and remediation projects.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Tetra Tech is a leader in the environmental industry, providing strategic planning, consulting, engineering, investigation, remediation, and compliance support for private-sector, industrial, and public-sector clients.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to lead projects addressing complex environmental challenges across multiple media, including soil, groundwater, sediment, surface water, and air
. You will work directly with clients, regulatory agencies, technical teams, and subcontractors to develop practical solutions and successfully deliver projects.

Position Summary

Working alongside a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, geologists, designers, and technical specialists, you will manage environmental investigation, remediation, and related projects from initial scoping through completion.

The position will include responsibility for project scope, schedule, budget, technical quality, staffing, client communication, and financial performance
. Depending on the project, responsibilities may include interpreting federal, state, and local environmental regulations; directing site investigations and remediation activities; evaluating technical data and calculations; and overseeing preparation of reports, plans, cost estimates, permit applications, and other deliverables.

Much of the technical work may support the investigation and/or remediation of active and inactive NJDEP Site Remediation Program sites.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Manage environmental investigation, remediation, and related consulting projects.
Manage project planning, scope, schedules, budgets, staffing, subcontractors, deliverables, and financial performance.
Plan, develop, coordinate, and direct multidisciplinary project teams.
Interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Assess environmental conditions, potential impacts, regulatory requirements, and technical challenges.
Scope environmental investigations, remediation programs, compliance activities, and other technical projects.
Review and interpret site-specific technical data, calculations, laboratory results, reports, drawings, cost estimates, environmental permit applications, and permit terms and conditions.
Prepare and/or oversee preparation of technical reports, work plans, permit applications, specifications, cost estimates, and other project deliverables.
Provide technical leadership and sound professional judgment when addressing complex project issues.
Coordinate with regulatory agencies, clients, laboratories, subcontractors, and other project stakeholders.
Direct and review the work of engineers, scientists, geologists, field personnel, and other technical staff.
Maintain project quality through appropriate technical review and quality assurance/quality control procedures.
Collaborate with the senior technical team to develop site closure strategies.
Mentor and support the professional development of junior and mid-level staff.
Manage multiple projects, clients, deadlines, and priorities concurrently.
Prepare proposals, scopes of work, schedules, staffing plans, and cost estimates.
Participate in client meetings, presentations, and interviews.
Identify upcoming client needs and opportunities for additional work.
Conduct periodic field and site visits to support project delivery and maintain familiarity with project conditions.
Assist field team implementing planned projects.
Work at remediation sites, construction sites, and other locations where heavy equipment, contamination, or other environmental or physical hazards may be present.
Travel within northern New Jersey based on project and client needs.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, or a related environmental or technical discipline.
Minimum of 5 years of relevant environmental consulting experience, including experience in one or more of the following:
Environmental investigation and remediation.
Brownfield or contaminated site redevelopment.
Industrial or private-sector environmental consulting.
Demonstrated project management experience, including responsibility for project scope, budgets, schedules, staffing, and deliverables.
Experience communicating directly with clients and managing client expectations.
Working knowledge of applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
Experience managing or coordinating multidisciplinary technical teams.
Strong technical problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.
Self-motivated and disciplined, with the ability to learn new software and work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships with clients, colleagues, regulators, and subcontractors.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to client and project sites as needed.
Possess or able to obtain a Transportation Worker Identification Card (TWIC) by hire date.

Preferred Qualifications

7–10+ years of environmental consulting experience with progressively increasing project and client management responsibility.
Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG), or other applicable professional certification or licensure.
Experience with New Jersey environmental regulations and regulatory programs.
Experience working with NJDEP.
Experience managing investigation and remediation projects involving soil, groundwater, sediment, vapor intrusion, or other environmental media.
Experience working with sites with intermingled contamination.
Experience supporting industrial and private-sector environmental clients.
Experience developing scopes, budgets, and fee estimates and managing project financial performance, including invoicing.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop junior technical staff.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate environmental assessment data and determine the next step in the remediation process.
Experience with Autodesk Civil 3D, GIS, or other relevant environmental or engineering software is a plus.

Physical Requirements

Regularly required to sit and work at a computer for extended periods, with occasional standing and walking within an office environment.
Occasionally required to lift or move up to 10 lbs., with infrequent lifting of up to 25 lbs.
Requires use of hands for typing, handling materials, and operating office and field equipment.
Vision abilities include close vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
May travel to field sites, generally approximately 10–30% of the time, depending on project and client needs.
Field assignments may involve walking on uneven terrain and working around active construction, remediation, landfill, or industrial operations.
When in the field, must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including a respirator when required, and meet applicable medical clearance requirements.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made.

Office-based work typically involves low hazard exposure, though noise levels may vary depending on nearby activities or equipment.
Outdoor project work may involve exposure to heat, cold, precipitation, uneven terrain, heavy equipment, physical hazards, and potential chemical or environmental hazards.
Appropriate PPE, including hearing protection and respiratory protection where applicable, may be required.
Travel between project sites, client locations, and Tetra Tech offices may be required, with employees expected to operate vehicles safely under varying weather, traffic, and environmental conditions.

Additional Information

This position will be based near Tetra Tech’s Goshen, New York or Woodbridge, New Jersey office.
A hybrid work arrangement may be available based on project, client, and team needs, with the expectation that the employee will be available for in-person client meetings, office collaboration, and project site visits as needed.
Regional travel throughout New York, New Jersey, and surrounding areas may be required.
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. Tetra Tech SWE will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa).

Pay:
$75,000 – 125,000 annually, commensurate with skill level, geography region and experience.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 30,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor, and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Job Description

Turner & Townsend Heery
is seeking an experienced Environmental and Solid Waste Project Manager
to provide project management and program support for the Charles County Department of Public Works on a diverse portfolio of environmental, solid waste, water resources, civil infrastructure, and related capital improvement projects.

The Project Manager will support projects throughout the project life cycle, from planning and feasibility through design, permitting, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout. The position will work closely with County staff, engineering consultants, contractors, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders to ensure projects are effectively coordinated and delivered in accordance with established scope, schedule, budget, quality, safety, and regulatory requirements.

The ideal candidate will have experience managing environmental or solid waste infrastructure projects and be comfortable working in both office and field environments.

Facilitate project meetings and maintain clear and timely communication among project stakeholders.
Coordinate project activities across multiple County departments and maintain continuity as projects transition between planning, design, procurement, construction, and closeout.

Perform other project management duties as assigned.

Experience in one or more of the following areas is desirable:

Solid waste management and infrastructure.
Landfill development, expansion, closure, and remediation.
Recycling and materials recovery facilities.
Citizen disposal facilities.
Composting and organics management facilities.
Environmental remediation and restoration.
Dams, flood-control infrastructure, and water resources.
Dredging and sediment management.
Stormwater and drainage infrastructure.
Water and wastewater infrastructure.
Environmental permitting and regulatory compliance.
Public works and municipal capital improvement programs.
Other environmental or infrastructure-related capital projects.

.

, preferably involving environmental, solid waste, civil infrastructure, public works, or construction projects.

Experience coordinating engineering consultants, contractors, government agencies, and other project stakeholders.
Strong understanding of project scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality, and change management.
Ability to review and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, technical reports, cost estimates, schedules, and other project documentation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

.
Experience with municipal, County, State, or other public-sector capital improvement programs.
Experience with environmental permitting and regulatory agencies, particularly in Maryland.
Experience with landfill, solid waste, recycling, environmental, or water resources projects.
Construction management or owner's representative experience.
Experience managing projects involving multiple consultants and contractors.
Familiarity with public procurement, construction contracts, change management, and payment processes.
Experience with project controls, cost estimating, scheduling, and risk management.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on, organized, and collaborative project manager
who can effectively coordinate technical, environmental, construction, regulatory, and administrative requirements.

The successful candidate will be comfortable communicating with engineers, environmental professionals, contractors, regulatory agencies, County leadership, and field personnel. Candidates with strong project management experience in environmental, solid waste, landfill, water resources, civil infrastructure, or related public works projects
are encouraged to apply. Experience in every listed discipline is not required.

The position will involve a combination of office, field, construction site, landfill, and other project locations
throughout Charles County. Regular site visits, project meetings, and coordination with County staff, consultants, contractors, and other stakeholders will be required.

The successful candidate will work as part of the Turner & Townsend Heery team supporting the Charles County Department of Public Works and will be expected to establish effective working relationships with County staff and external project stakeholders.

Description

JSI invites you to join our team as an Archaeologist/Environmental Specialist II
on our Environmentals & Permitting
team in our Lubbock, TX
office where you'll play a critical role in advancing broadband and telecommunications initiatives that expand connectivity and drive digital inclusion—while advancing your career within a mission-driven, growth-focused organization.

Position Overview:

As an Archaeologist/Environmental Specialist II
on the Environmentals & Permitting
team
you will serve as one of the firm's senior decision-makers with expert knowledge of Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA). You will ensure overall compliance with historic preservation legislation for federal infrastructure projects funded through BEAD, USDA RUS ReConnect, and other federal programs.
Our clients are electric cooperatives, telephone companies, and broadband providers deploying fiber across long linear corridors on aggressive federal funding timelines. What they need from us is a defensible finding, delivered when they need it, that survives agency review without a second round.

Responsibilities

Regulatory Practice Leadership:
Serve as a Western Region Senior Technical Authority on NHPA, ensuring Section 106 compliance with all federally funded undertakings in the portfolio.
Determine whether an activity constitutes an undertaking, identify historic properties, define direct and indirect Areas of Potential Effects (APE), and provide all required documentation.
Apply National Register eligibility criteria, provide eligibility recommendations, and make and defend effect findings of no historic properties affected, no adverse effect, and adverse effect, including conditioned no-adverse-effect findings.
Negotiate, draft, and shepherd Memoranda of Agreement and Programmatic Agreements to execution, including multi-state and territory-wide agreements.
Direct resolution of adverse effects through avoidance, minimization, and mitigation strategies, including development of agreement documents.

Consultation – SHPO, THPO, Tribal, and Agency:
Consult with State Historic Preservation Officers across multiple jurisdictions and support federal agency clients in coordination with federally recognized Tribes and Tribal Historic Preservation Officers.
Identify consulting parties, facilitate public involvement under 36 CFR 800.2(c), and ensure sensitive site information is protected under NHPA Section 304 and the Archaeological Resources Protection Act.
Advise federal agencies on Advisory Council on Historic Preservation participation and build consultation relationships that persist across projects.

Practice Management and Growth:
Contribute cultural resources scope, level-of-effort assumptions, and pricing to proposals and statements of work.
Mentor archaeologists and architectural historians, maintain firm qualifications and permit standing, and represent JSI with clients, agencies, trade associations, and technical conferences.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications
Master's degree in Anthropology, Archaeology, Architectural History, Historic Preservation, History, or a closely related field.
Meets the Secretary of the Interior's Professional Qualification Standards (36 CFR Part 61) in Archaeology, Architectural History, or History.
Minimum of 5 years of Section 106 compliance practice, including at least four in a principal, program-lead, or equivalent decision-making role
Demonstrated record of drafting and negotiating Memoranda of Agreement or Programmatic Agreements to execution.
Direct, sustained consultation experience with multiple SHPOs and with THPOs or Tribal representatives.
A portfolio of eligibility and effect determinations that withstood agency review, with the ability to walk through the reasoning on request.
Experience with linear or corridor undertakings, where the APE is long, narrow, and crosses many jurisdictions.
Strong technical writing skills with experience developing MOAs, PAs, and other regulatory documentation.

Preferred Qualifications:
Registered Professional Archaeologist (RPA) credential.
Experience supporting broadband, telecommunications, BEAD, ReConnect, E-Rate, or FCC tower sitting via TCNS and Forms 620 / 621.
Experience with ArcGIS Pro, geospatial analysis, archaeological predictive modeling, or cultural resources GIS applications.

Benefits and Compensation

Competitive salary + performance-based bonuses.
Comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)).
Generous PTO and travel support.
Ongoing professional development and educational opportunities.

In collaboration with other members of the clinical research site teamwork to ensure the entry of clinical visit data in EDC and other clinical data software/systems. Responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

Managing data entry into computer systems for clinical trials, including entering patient data into eDC and other software

Proficiency with computer applications such as Microsoft applications, email, and web applications, and the ability to type proficiently (40+ wpm);
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

jobs.title: Director of Conservation Biotechnologies
jobs.description:
HOW YOU WILL IMPACT OUR MISSION

The Director of Conservation Biotechnologies is responsible for the overall direction, planning, coordination, and implementation of a scientific research program that supports and is aligned with the conservation objectives and strategy of the SDZWA. The Director will oversee an integrated scientific group, encompassing our conservation genetics, reproductive sciences, and biodiversity banking teams. The Conservation Biotechnologies department takes an integrative and innovative approach; applying an array of scientific disciplines to support strategies (e.g., genetic rescue, population assessment and management, assisted reproduction) designed to safeguard and restore biodiversity and to manage wildlife populations in situ and ex situ. Scientific disciplines practiced within the Biotechnologies department include cryogenic biobanking of living cells and gametes (which comprise the SDZWA Frozen Zoo®), advanced population genomics, advanced reproductive technologies, cell biology, endocrinology, stem cell biology, bioinformatics and more. The Director of Conservation Biotechnologies is a subject-matter expert in either conservation genetics/genomics, reproductive sciences, cellular biology, or biodiversity banking, with a high level of fluency in the other disciplines. This position requires a proven track record of innovating, applying, and critically evaluating scientific approaches for biodiversity conservation, as well as a strong record of collaboration across sectors.
As a leadership position in the Conservation Science Wildlife Health (CSWH) department, the Director of Conservation Biotechnologies communicates the SDZWA conservation vision and strategy to their team, identifies and prioritizes projects that strengthen connections with other teams in CSWH, departments within SDZWA, external partners, and has a working knowledge of approaches/tools used by the SDZWA to ensure activities support conservation outcomes (e.g., The Conservation Standards). The Director of Conservation Biotechnologies will develop and steward strategic collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders, including government agencies, NGO's, academic institutions, and local communities. The Director will have a proven track record for successful grant writing and team leadership. Working knowledge of regional, national, and international conservation frameworks and conventions is essential.
The Director is a member of the Conservation Science leadership team, and is responsible for monitoring, reporting, and communicating the Conservation Biotechnology team's conservation and science outcomes. The Director will contribute to organizational conservation strategic planning and fundraising, including securing grant funding through various sources.
Additional responsibilities of the Director of Conservation Biotechnologies include budget development and oversight, internal and external communications, ensuring that the team complies with ethical, safety and other guidelines as defined by SDZWA policies and procedures. The Director drives team cohesion and morale and serves to effectively connect the team to the broader CSWH department and with our strategic conservation objectives. This position will report to the Vice President of Wildlife Conservation Science.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Leads the development of broad-scale scientific research programs for the department that are aligned with the strategic conservation goals of the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance
Ensures relevant scientific innovations are incorporated into research programs and that scientific activities support larger-conservation objectives
Responsible for the productivity, mentorship and morale of department staff, ensuring that staff activities are effectively directed to meet organizationally aligned conservation goals
Oversee operations and budget of multiple field and/or lab research programs
Serves as departmental liaison within the organization and oversees all relevant compliance areas, including animal welfare, legal, financial, human resources, and grant deliverables
Promotes organizational reputation externally through partnership cultivation and professional service, including presentations to diverse audiences and participation in committees, conferences, working groups, and academic institutions

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are seeking a visionary conservation science leader who brings deep scientific expertise, a track record of innovation, and the ability to translate integrative science into transformative conservation outcomes. The ideal candidate will inspire and lead a multidisciplinary team, build strategic partnerships and shape the future of conservation biotechnology through scientific excellence, collaboration, and strategic leadership.

JOB EXPERIENCE

Must have 7 or more years of experience directing and conducting scientific research in genetics/genomics, reproductive sciences, cellular biology, biodiversity banking, or related scientific field required
Must have 5 or more years of experience managing a team required.
Must have a noteworthy publication record in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
Successful track record of grant writing required.

EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS

PhD in genetics/genomics, reproductive sciences, cellular biology, biodiversity banking, or related field required.
Valid California Driver’s License in good standing required.
Valid Passport

SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE

Plan and develop strategic conservation science projects and programs
Working knowledge of multiple scientific disciplines to foster transdisciplinary approaches to conservation
Productive engagement across geography and cultures in the development of collaborative initiatives
Navigate federal and local regulatory agency environments, rules, and compliance
Travel as needed to manage diverse projects and teams
Prepare and review grant applications and administer grants
Develop, administer, and monitor budgets
Manage and create a team dynamic
Communicate effectively, verbally and in writing to scientific and lay audiences
Prepare papers for publication in scientific journals

SOME OF THE REWARDS YOU WILL ENJOY AS A TEAM MEMBER

Free admission to the San Diego Zoo and the San Diego Zoo Safari Park
Family Passes
Complimentary Tickets
Free Parking at the San Diego Zoo & San Diego Zoo Safari Park
Local and In-House Discounts
Employee Assistance Program
Wellness Program

Provide environmental support to on-going civil construction projects.
Monitor construction and ensure compliance with permits and regulations.
Permits include Construction Rock Handling, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plans, Multi-Sector General Permits, Cultural Resources Protection and Monitoring Plans, and Nesting Bird Standard Operating Procedures.

Document compliance with plans, policies, procedures, and permit requirements.
Complete inspections, monitor data sheets, and reporting forms.
Coordinate between the construction manager and the construction teams to facilitate communication and quickly resolve conflicts, issues, and challenges related to environmental concerns that may arise in the field.
This position has no supervisory responsibilities.
Other duties as assigned.

Bachelor's degree in encironmental sciences, engineering, chemistry, natural resource management, or related field.

Practical experience in erosion prevention and sediment control for construction projects, and turbidity monitoring and sampling; AK-CESCL certification/credentials desired.
Knowledge of applicable regulatory, legal, and other requirements.
Working knowledge of arctic wildlife and vegetation management.
Experience working under US and State of Alaska environmental statutes/regulations/permits.
Strong technical skills and the practical ability to solve problems.
Ability to work in a team environment and work effectively across all levels of the business.
Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record for the past three (3) years to be eligible under company vehicle insurance policy.

Competencies

Professional, highly self-motivated, passionate, energetic, creative and strategic thinker.
Dedicated to meeting the expectations and requirements of internal and external customers.
Always acts with customers in mind, knows how to establish and maintain effective relationships with customers/prospects and gains their trust and respect.
Desire to improve personally, increasing ability and skillset.

Weather: Indoors/Outdoors – Frequent exposure to moderate to harsh weather conditions. Requires work to be done both inside and outside.

Noise level: The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Position Summary:

The School Of Engineering & Technology At Central Michigan University Invites Applicants For a Tenure-track Assistant Professor Position To Support The Environmental Engineering Program. The Start Date For This Position Is August 2027. We Seek a Colleague With Expertise In Any Aspect Of Environmental Engineering, But Preference Will Be Given To Candidates With Backgrounds In One Of The Following Areas

Environmental remediation
Solid and hazardous waste engineering
Molecular biology techniques for environmental engineering (e.g., qPCR, metagenomics, etc.)
Air pollution engineering

The selected candidate is expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses and laboratories, develop an externally funded research program, advise students in research and capstone design projects, and contribute service to benefit the program, School, College, University, profession, and surrounding community. The selected candidate will teach required and elective courses in the Environmental Engineering program but may also teach general engineering and engineering technology courses (depending on specific expertise) that support all programs within the School.

Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in Environmental Engineering, Ecological Engineering, Civil Engineering, Chemical Engineering or a related field. Candidates with a Ph.D. in a related, non-engineering field must have an undergraduate engineering degree in one of the disciplines listed above to be considered for this position. Exceptional ABD candidates will be considered if their degree is completed by the start of the appointment.
Potential for outstanding teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels and the ability to teach core and elective courses offered within the School.
Demonstrated record of quality research and ability to develop a rigorous scholarship program that involves students.
Strong commitment to research that attracts external funding and leads to publications in competitive peer-reviewed journals.
Commitment to student success and fostering a supportive environment for every member of our university community.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Ability to perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated record of effective teaching as the lead instructor.
Demonstrated record of securing external funding.
Postdoctoral experience (academic or industry).
Experience integrating high impact teaching practices (e.g., active learning, project-based learning) into the classroom.
Professional engineering licensure, or possibility of obtaining licensure in the near future.
Relevant industrial or government experience.
Background in environmental remediation, solid and hazardous waste engineering, molecular biology techniques for environmental engineering (e.g., qPCR, metagenomics, etc.), or air pollution engineering.

Message To Applicants

You must submit an online application in order to be considered as an applicant for this position.

Please Submit The Following Materials

cover letter (2 page max)
CV
statement of teaching philosophy (2 page max)
statement of research (2 page max)
contact information for 3 professional references

Cover letters may be addressed to the Hiring Committee.

Position is open until filled, although priority consideration will be given to applications completed by October 19, 2026.

About The Department

The School of Engineering and Technology
(SET) is housed in the College of Science and Engineering
(CSE). SET has four undergraduate Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Computer, and Environmental Engineering), three undergraduate Engineering Technology (Industrial, Mechanical, and Product Design Engineering Technology) and a graduate (MS in Engineering) program. All undergraduate programs are accredited by ABET. SET presently has 24 full-time faculty members. Courses are taught in an attractive 70,000 square foot engineering & technology building which houses more than twenty laboratories and support spaces.

Central Michigan University has a more than 125-year legacy of preparing students to become leaders and changemakers in their communities and in their personal and professional lives.

We serve nearly 15,500 students on our Mount Pleasant campus, in satellite locations around the state and throughout the country, and through flexible online programs. Many of our approximately 300 undergraduate, master's, specialist and doctoral programs in the arts, media, business, education, human services, health professions, liberal arts, social sciences, medicine, science and engineering are nationally ranked for excellence.

CMU leads the nation in leadership development programming through our Sarah R. Central is home to 17 men's and women's Division 1 sports including football, basketball, gymnastics, baseball, wrestling and more. CMU is located in Mount Pleasant, a community that blends the best of small-town living with big-city amenities. It's part of the culturally varied and vibrant Great Lakes Bay Region that also includes Saginaw, Bay City, Midland and the state's largest Native American community, centered on the Saginaw Chippewa Isabella Reservation in Mount Pleasant.

Area residents enjoy the mix of outdoor activities, cultural events, shopping and dining options, and family attractions. Other major Michigan destinations and attractions — Lansing, Grand Rapids, Detroit, Traverse City, wineries, beaches, golf and ski resorts, and many more — are within easy reach of the city's central location in Michigan's Lower Peninsula.

CMU employees enjoy access to a nationally recognized wellness program along with health care and benefits that exceed regional, state and national norms.

About The Role

I. PURPOSE OF THE POSITION Provide technical and operational support to WWF-Indonesia in the management, collection, processing, standardization, and updating of spatial data and databases to support the development and operationalization of the Socio-Ecological Spatial Intelligence Systems (SoESIS). This position also supports the development and refinement of the SoESIS WebGIS platform, including data integration, visualization, and web-based data presentation. Additionally, the role involves supporting the inventory and integration of data from various WWF-Indonesia directorates, programs, and landscape/seascape initiatives, ensuring data is structured, accurate, documented, standardized, and easily accessible—enabling optimal use for program planning, monitoring, spatial analysis, and data-driven decision-making. II. ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES A. Project Planning Support planning of spatial data and database requirements for SoESIS development and implementation. Assist in data inventory, prioritization of data collection and management activities, and timeline development. Support coordination and data requirement gathering across WWF-Indonesia directorates, programs, and landscape/seascape teams. Support integration of data into the Ministry of Forestry’s SIGAP platform as project needs arise. B. Implementation Program Collect, inventory, and document spatial and non-spatial data in alignment with SoESIS requirements. Support implementation of standardized methods for spatial data collection, processing, analysis, and presentation. Perform data cleaning, quality control, and standardization to ensure data quality and consistency. Prepare and integrate spatial data to meet SoESIS needs. Regularly update databases and spatial datasets. Support documentation, progress monitoring, and reporting of data management activities. Coordinate with external developers and internal teams for SoESIS development and implementation. Coordinate with the Ministry of Forestry for integration into the SIGAP platform as needed. C. Reporting Support preparation of periodic reports on spatial data management progress and SoESIS implementation. Prepare supporting data and information for internal and external reporting. Document progress, outcomes, and achievements of data management and SoESIS development activities. Document challenges, needs, and follow-up actions arising during data management and implementation. Support development of presentation materials and visual information on data management progress and outcomes. III. AUTHORITY A. Internal Working Relationships Coordinate with the Forest & Wildlife Program Director and program implementation teams to ensure project progress and sustainability. Collaborate closely and regularly with program support teams (e.g., General Services, Grant & Finance, People & Culture, Legal, and others). B. External Working Relationships Coordinate and collaborate with relevant stakeholders—including local governments, private sector, academics, civil society organizations, and local communities—as needed to achieve program goals and ensure sustainability. IV. REQUIREMENTS To successfully fulfill the responsibilities and contribute to organizational goals, the candidate must meet the following criteria: A. Knowledge & Experience Minimum Bachelor’s degree (S1) in Geography, Geomatics, Forestry, Environmental Science, or a related field. Demonstrated knowledge and experience in GIS and spatial data management, including data collection, processing, cleaning, and quality control. Proficiency in ArcGIS/QGIS and foundational understanding of spatial databases, coordinate systems, geodatabases, and metadata. Familiarity with various spatial and tabular data formats: Shapefile (.shp), GeoTIFF (.tif/.tiff), KML/KMZ, CSV, PDF, GeoJSON, and GeoParquet. Experience in database management, data standardization, and documentation; experience in conservation, forestry, biodiversity, or landscape management is an advantage. Ability to learn and apply concepts and technologies in WebGIS development, including spatial data visualization, web mapping, GIS services/APIs, and integration of spatial data into web platforms. B. Technical/Specific Required Knowledge & Skills Proficiency in ArcGIS/QGIS for spatial data processing, analysis, and visualization. Understanding of spatial data management practices: cleaning, quality control, standardization, and metadata. Knowledge of spatial databases and data integration fundamentals: coordinate systems, geodatabases, data structure, and attributes. Ability to systematically conduct data inventory, documentation, and reporting, and ensure data readiness for SoESIS integration. Experience in geospatial work and spatial dashboard development is an advantage. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, and ability to write clear, concise reports. Capacity to work independently and collaboratively, including in remote field locations with minimal supervision. Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Willingness to travel to project sites as required by the organization. At WWF Indonesia, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diversity is valued and equal opportunities are provided to all. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and offer benefits to support a healthy work-life balance. Application deadline: 27 September 2026. We encourage early applications, as this position may be closed before the deadline if a suitable candidate is found.

jobs.title: Senior Consultant, Environmental Permitting Specialist, FERC Generalist
jobs.description:
Ready to make an impact?
Join ERM
and help shape the future of energy infrastructure while advancing your career with a global sustainability leader.

Why This Role Matters

Energy infrastructure is evolving rapidly, and the need for sustainable, compliant solutions has never been greater. As an Environmental Permitting Specialist and FERC Generalist
at ERM, you’ll play a pivotal role in shaping the future of energy projects—from natural gas pipelines to renewable energy developments. This is your opportunity to join a global leader in sustainability consulting and make a tangible impact on projects that power communities and protect the environment. This role can be based anywhere in the United States.

What Your Impact Is

You’ll be the go-to expert for environmental permitting and regulatory compliance, ensuring projects meet federal, state, and local requirements. Your work will directly influence the success of major energy initiatives, helping clients navigate complex regulations while advancing cleaner, more efficient energy solutions.

Required

What You'll Bring

Bachelor’s degree in a natural science or engineering discipline
3+ years of relevant experience in environmental permitting or regulatory compliance
Strong knowledge of MS Office Suite
Ability to conduct desktop research and interpret GIS maps (National Wetland Inventory, USGS, aerial photography)
Field readiness: capable of working in varied weather conditions and navigating with GPS/maps
Excellent technical writing and communication skills for diverse audiences
Valid driver’s license and willingness to travel up to 40%
Proven ability to work independently, multitask, and maintain flexibility

Preferred

Experience with Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) processes
Familiarity with natural resource management and regulatory agencies (e.g., U.S. Army Corps of Engineers)
Consulting or field experience, including active construction sites
Working knowledge of ArcGIS software and field survey techniques

Key Responsibilities

Prepare permit applications for energy and industrial projects in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
Evaluate regulatory requirements and maintain accurate records and survey reports
Develop technical project documents, including data tables, spreadsheets, and engineering calculations
Assist in project planning, scheduling, and progress reporting
Communicate effectively with clients, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders, providing clear recommendations and guidance
Uphold ERM’s commitment to safety and sustainability in all project activities

Who We Are

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

jobs.description:
Position: UAV Design Engineer (CFD & FEA Specialist)

Location:
Manesar, Haryana
Experience:
3-6 years

Role Overview

We are looking for a hands-on Design Engineer to join our core engineering team and drive the design, development, testing, and optimization of next-generation drone and UAV systems.

The ideal candidate is a practical, field-tested engineer with strong expertise in mechanical design, UAV structures, aerodynamics, CFD, materials, and manufacturing
- someone who has independently taken UAV components or complete systems from concept through CAD, analysis, prototyping, manufacturing, testing, and real-world field deployment
, not just theoretical or simulation work.

Key Responsibilities

UAV & Mechanical Design

• Independently design UAV/drone airframes, structural components, and mechanical sub-assemblies.
• Develop production-ready 3D models and 2D engineering drawings (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, AutoCAD, or equivalent).
• Own designs end-to-end — from concept through prototyping, manufacturing, and field deployment.
• Balance weight, strength, stability, durability, and manufacturability in every design decision.
• Partner with electronics, flight-control, and systems teams on integration and weight distribution.
• Reverse engineering capabilities to scan a model and prepare the design with required modification.
Aerodynamics & CFD

• Apply practical aerodynamics and fluid mechanics knowledge to real UAV flight scenarios.
• Run CFD simulations (ANSYS Fluent/CFX or equivalent) to optimize lift, drag, stability, and efficiency.
• Translate simulation results into concrete design changes.
• Diagnose and resolve aerodynamic issues that surface during actual flight testing, not just on paper.
Manufacturing & Materials

• Select materials (carbon-fiber composites, high-strength polymers, lightweight alloys, aerospace-grade materials) based on strength, weight, cost, and durability requirements.
• Apply design-for-manufacturing (DFM) principles to keep designs production-ready and repeatable.
• Coordinate with fabrication teams on CNC machining, 3D printing, and composite molding. Testing & Field Validation

• Validate designs through prototyping, ground testing, and flight testing.
• Use field feedback and test data to drive continuous design iteration.
• Demonstrate a track record of designs that are personally developed and currently operating in the field - not shelved prototypes.
Documentation & Compliance

• Produce detailed engineering drawings, specifications, and BOMs.
• Ensure designs meet applicable engineering, safety, and regulatory standards.
• Maintain configuration control and documentation throughout the product lifecycle.
Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Work closely with flight-control, electronics, manufacturing, and operations teams to resolve design and performance issues.
• Support fast design iteration cycles based on test data and operational needs.

Required Qualifications & Skills

• Education Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Aeronautical, Mechanical, or Mechanical Design Engineering, or a related field.
• Proven, independent ownership of UAV/drone mechanical and structural designs — not just design support.
• Demonstrable experience with UAV components or systems that have been manufactured, tested, and deployed in the field.
• Strong practical grounding in aerodynamics, fluid mechanics, and UAV structural design.
• Proficiency in SolidWorks, Fusion 360, AutoCAD, or equivalent CAD tools.
• Hands-on CFD analysis experience using ANSYS Fluent/CFX or equivalent.
• Working knowledge of composite materials, lightweight structures, CNC machining, and additive manufacturing.
• Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to turn theory into flight ready hardware.

Preferred

• FEA/structural and multi-physics simulation experience.
• Experience with fixed-wing UAVs, multirotors, VTOL, or other autonomous aircraft.
• Direct experience working with manufacturing/fabrication teams and running flight tests.
• Background in aerospace, defence, aviation, drone, or robotics industries.
• Strong technical communication skills.

Ideal Candidate

Someone who can point to a real design lifecycle they've owned: Design → Analysis → Manufacturing → Testing → Field Deployment.

Job Description

Are you an experienced environmental due diligence consultant, skilled in uncovering environmental risks and turning technical findings into clear, actionable advice for decision-makers? Do you enjoy working across EHS and ESG topics to help shape sustainable outcomes for transactions and post-acquisition strategies? Are you a detail-focused communicator who thrives on fast-paced due diligence work, site visits, and collaborative problem-solving?

If this sounds like you, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our CST Due Diligence UK & Ireland team as our new Experienced Senior Consultant Environmental Due Diligence and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

As an Experienced Senior Consultant Environmental Due Diligence, you will be part of our busy UK transactions team supporting fast-paced UK and global M&A transactions. You will assist with the identification of key EHS and ESG risks and opportunities and provide high-quality, targeted advice to clients on both buy-side and sell-side due diligence projects

Our team advises on transactions across a wide range of sectors, typically including industrial, commercial and infrastructure assets and businesses, often for finance sector clients. We work closely with in-house specialists across several EHS and ESG disciplines to provide targeted due diligence advice. Our clients use this advice to support negotiations during the bidding process and o to make informed impactful decisions on sustainability priorities post-acquisition. 

You will play a key role in the team, principally delivering due diligence assessments, while also supporting project management and the development of client proposals. 

Your key responsibilities will be:

Preparation of proposals, including pricing/budgets and timescales. Participation in client discussions and support with developing new client relationships.
Project Management and coordination of medium to large projects including multi-site projects over several geographies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence.
Delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments and Limited Environmental Compliance Review(LECR) assessments for a range of sites, including more complex manufacturing facilities; including participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing focussed client reports. 
Delivery of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) assessments of companies in support of buy-side and sell-side due diligence. This will include desk-based research (review of data rooms and publicly available information), participation in management calls, interpreting available information and preparing client focussed reports.

About You

If you have relevant EHS/ESG knowledge, experience in due diligence and want to advance your career in a collaborative team, we would like to hear from you.What matters most to us:

Relevant degree/qualifications. Ideally in environmental studies/geography or similar.
Sound understanding of UK environmental regulations and an understanding of key environmental and sustainability regulations in Europe.
7 to 12 years of practical work experience in other companies where you have personally been involved in the delivery of Phase I Environmental Site Assessments, LECR assessments, ideally including to ASTM standards, and ideally also ESG assessments. Have the ability to understand information quickly and work efficiently, proactively and autonomously.
Experience in supporting the preparation of proposals.  
Strong communication skills (both written and verbal), and be comfortable engaging with external clients and advisors.
Project Management experience.
A collaborative approach and willingness to travel, typically within the UK and Ireland.

What We Can Offer You

Commitment to your development
Leaders guided by our Leadership Principles
A culture that welcomes you as the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company
Flexible work environment
27 days annual leave plus bank holidays
Matched pension contributions
Private medical cover and life assurance

Ready to join us?

So if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. jobs.title: Chef for droner og counter-drone hos Forsvarsministeriets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse
jobs.description:
Vil du arbejde med en industri, som er under hastig udvikling, og bidrage til at forme fremtidens forsvar? Droner ændrer den moderne kampplads i et tempo, der sjældent er set før. IForretningsområde for Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) og Counter Uncrewed AircraftSystems har vi ansvaret for, at Forsvaret altid råder over de rigtige og mest relevante drone- og counter dronesystemer.

Om os

Forsvarsministeriets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse (FMI) er Danmarks centrale myndighed for forsvarets og beredskabets materiel, IT og cybersikkerhed i fred, krise og krig.

Vi arbejder for at sikre, at det samlede forsvar er udstyret, opdateret og operativt, i en tid, hvor kravene til hastighed og kampkraft aldrig har været større. Det er os, der anskaffer, driver og bortskaffer materiel og IT for Hæren, Søværnet, Flyvevåbnet og resten af Forsvarsministeriets koncern.

Vi er en mangfoldig organisation med ca. 2.500 medarbejdere, civile og militære, fordelt ud over hele Kongeriget.

Vores forretningsområde er inde i en markant udvikling, så vi søger en chef, der er klar til at drive udviklingen af Forsvarets drone- og counter-dronekapaciteter fremad. Du bliver en del af et stærkt fagligt miljø, hvor teknik, operativ forståelse og internationalt samarbejde går hånd i hånd.

Vi har ansvaret for, at Forsvaret altid råder over de rigtige drone- og counter-dronesystemer i en tid, hvor droner ændrer den moderne kampplads i et tempo, der sjældent er set før.

Vi køber, implementerer, opdaterer og drifter systemerne og følger dem hele vejen fra operativt behov til virkende kapacitet.

Det kræver, at teknik, operativ forståelse og kommerciel indsigt spiller sammen, og at vi arbejder tæt sammen med brugerne i alle værn, tekniske fagmiljøer, leverandører, industrien og internationale partnere i blandt andet NATO, Norden og EU.

Om stillingen

Som chef får du det samlede ansvar for udviklingen af forretningsområdet for UAS og Counter UAS. Disse områder er konstant under udvikling og hænger i stigende grad sammen, og skal derfor udvikles i sammenhæng.

Du Vil Lede Gennem Underlagte Chefer Og Har Ansvaret For Både Militære Og Civile Medarbejdere. Dine Opgaver Omfatter Blandt Andet At

Lede drift og udvikling af eksisterende kapaciteter.
Sikre anskaffelse, implementering og løbende opdatering af nye droner og dronebaserede Counter UAS-kapaciteter.
Være projektejer ved materielanskaffelser inden for ansvarsområdet og følge dem fra operativt behov til leveret og virkende kapacitet.
Rådgive divisionschefen i tekniske, operative og kommercielle spørgsmål inden for ansvarsområdet.
Sikre sammenhæng mellem operative behov og tekniske løsninger gennem tæt dialog med brugere i alle værn, tekniske fagmiljøer, leverandører, industrien og internationale partnere.
Have det samlede ansvar for ledelse, koordinering, prioritering, økonomistyring og materielrelateret opgaveløsning på tværs af ansvarsområdet.

Ansvarsområdet forandrer sig i takt med politiske beslutninger og teknologisk udvikling, og du får derfor en central rolle i løbende at udvikle og tilpasse egen organisation, arbejdsprocesser, kompetencer og prioriteringer, så de understøtter opgaverne og kapacitetsudviklingen. Stillingen har et internationalt perspektiv, og rejseaktivitet må påregnes.

Om dig

Vi forventer som udgangspunkt, at du har erfaring med ledelse af ledere, eksempelvis som kontorchef, eller er oberstløjtnant/kommandørkaptajn. Du kan komme fra Forsvaret, industrien, en anden styrelse eller et andet teknologitungt miljø. Det vigtigste er, at du kan bevare overblikket i meget omskiftelige rammer og under et stort politisk pres.

Du prioriterer ledelse, men har lyst til at gå nysgerrigt ind i teknologien, sammen med dine specialister. Du kommunikerer klart på dansk og engelsk og er vant til at sikre et højt niveau af skriftlighed.

Erfaring med organisationsudvikling er en klar fordel, fordi fagområderne er under konstant udvikling, og organisationen løbende skal tilpasses opgaverne.

Teknisk indsigt i luftforsvars- eller dronesystemer er en fordel og ikke et krav.

Du skal kunne opbygge samarbejdsrelationer på tværs af hele koncernen, og som chef skal du gå forrest og skabe følgeskab i en tid, hvor der stilles ekstraordinære høje krav til din organisation.

Er det dig?

Ansættelsesvilkår

Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår forhandles efter rammeaftalen om kontraktansættelse af chefer i staten. Den endelige lønpakke vil afhænge af din baggrund og dine kvalifikationer, men stillingen er indplaceret i løngruppe 1.

Derudover er der mulighed for at forhandle tillæg efter kvalifikationer, ligesom der er mulighed for, at ansættelse kan ske ved konstitution. Der er til stillingen knyttet en arbejdsgiverfinansieret pension.

Hvis du i forvejen er tjenestemand, er der mulighed for, at ansættelsen kan ske som tjenestemand i lønramme 37 efter en konkret vurdering. Ansøgningen skal stiles til Kongen, medmindre du allerede er indplaceret i lønramme 37.

Som ansat under Forsvarsministeriet er du omfattet af nogle særlige vilkår. Det betyder blandt andet, at du skal kunne sikkerhedsgodkendes og opretholde denne i hele din ansættelsesperiode.

Du har som ansat pligt til at forrette tjeneste uden for landets grænser, herunder ved enheder i internationale operationer med henblik på deltagelse i konfliktforebyggende, fredsbevarende, fredsskabende, humanitære og andre lignende operationer.

Såfremt du er M331 og skal udnævnes til stillingen, skal du som udgangspunkt have helbredsvurdering C. Ligeledes bedes du vedlægge dine seneste tre FOKUS-bedømmelser.

Kontakt og ansøgning

Hvis du vil høre mere om stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte OL Lars Stokholm på tlf. 53 76 77 27.

Har du spørgsmål til løn- og ansættelsesvilkår, er du velkommen til at kontakte Personelkommandoen, HR-konsulent K. Anton Nyholm på tlf. 61 40 74 92.

Ansøgningsfristen er d. 11. oktober 2026 og samtaler forventes afholdt i forlængelse heraf.

Stillingen er til besættelse 01. januar 2027.

Du søger stillingen via linket, og vi beder dig vedhæfte ansøgning, CV og kopi af uddannelsesbevis og evt. FOKUS.

Vær opmærksom på, at bilag skal tilføjes i PDF-format.

I Forsvarsministeriets organisation tror vi på, at mangfoldighed optimerer opgaveløsningen. Derfor opfordrer vi alle interesserede uanset baggrund til at søge stillingen.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Geospatial
jobs.description:
Imagine having the power to stress-test an entire power grid against a hurricane or thunderstorm before the clouds even gather. That is the reality we are creating at Neara.

We use advanced machine learning to create engineering-grade, physics enabled digital twins of electricity grids across four continents, this helps asset owners understand their biggest challenges and bring the most viable solutions to life across millions of kilometres of infrastructure.

By simulating extreme weather and structural stress at a network-wide scale, we empower the world’s largest utilities to pinpoint risks, optimise investments and build a more resilient global energy future.

Our team is a collection of brilliant minds who are fanatical about making a tangible difference in the real world, utilising AI and machine learning to accelerate everything from data classification to complex scenario analysis. We have built a special culture where innovation thrives because everyone owns the mission and we need smart, creative people to help us scale this impact to every corner of the globe.

Data Scientist, Geospatial

We're looking for a Data Scientist, Geospatial to join our Houston team, supporting a key regional electric utility. You’ll work directly with their team to build physics-backed models on Neara, leveraging complex datasets like LiDAR, GIS, asset records, and weather data. Your work will directly prevent wildfires by simulating vegetation encroachment, predict grid failures under extreme weather loads, and inform capital investment decisions to harden critical infrastructure.

What You Will Do

Embed and collaborate directly with customer geospatial and GIS teams in a hybrid setting, spending time on-site at their offices to deeply understand their data workflows, integrate systems, and solve complex spatial challenges.
Build predictive risk models on Neara that combine LiDAR, terrain models, and weather data to simulate conductor sag, sway, and vegetation fall-in risks to directly prevent wildfire ignitions.
Translate complex spatial and structural risk metrics into defensible, data-driven insights that inform utility capital investment decisions for grid hardening.
Build and maintain robust spatial data pipelines to ingest, clean, vectorize, and integrate diverse geospatial data formats from our utility partner.
Establish QA/QC benchmarks for spatial accuracy, coordinate reference system (CRS) transformations, and structural alignment across disparate data sources.
Mentor others in best practices for model training, data analytics, and building data-driven products.

Who You Are

5+ years of hands-on experience in data science or machine learning. Geospatial data or power grid domain experience is a plus.
Strong quantitative intuition for data, with excellent communication skills and proven experience presenting complex findings to customers and senior leaders.
Experience working in fast-paced, high-growth scale-up technology environments is a plus.
Self-driven with a bias for action; comfortable taking full ownership of complex projects and adapting quickly to shifting priorities.
Natural collaborator who thrives at the intersection of technical teams (ML, Software) and external customer stakeholders.
Grounded, resourceful approach to problem-solving, with a track record of navigating messy, real-world datasets to deliver clear, business-driven outcomes.

What We Offer

Work with an industry-leading, multi-modal spatial data stack - including airborne LiDAR, high-resolution satellite imagery, and physics-enabled digital twins - to solve real-world engineering challenges at immense scale.
Your spatial modeling will directly mitigate wildfire risks, optimize utility vegetation management, and harden critical infrastructure across millions of kilometers of energy grids.
Shape the spatial architecture of our core product line while collaborating with top-tier ML and software engineers.
Enjoy a highly competitive compensation package with a significant equity component, ensuring you are a true stakeholder in our rapid global scaling.

Compensation Range: $140K - $150K
