Job Summary

The Sr. Technical Analyst/Prog Ent App is responsible for the development, support, and continuous improvement of GIS applications and system integrations within the ArcGIS and ArcFM environment supporting Avangrid electric and gas companies. The role partners with business stakeholders, IT teams, and external vendors with the design, develop, and implement technology solutions, provide solution architecture guidance, and ensure the reliable day-to-day operation of critical GIS systems.
The Sr. Technical Analyst/Prog Ent App position serves as a technical lead in the design, development, integration, and support of enterprise GIS platforms and related business applications. Responsibilities include application development, system integration, software lifecycle management, data management, troubleshooting, cloud and on-premises platform support, and translating business requirements into scalable technology solutions. The position requires strong analytical, programming, and problem-solving skills, combined with expertise in modern GIS technologies, enterprise architectures, automation, and emerging AI-driven capabilities that enhance operational efficiency and business value.
The Sr. Technical Analyst/Prog Ent App role reports to the Sr. Manager – GIS & OSG Applications.

Key Responsibilities

· Operate effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment while managing multiple projects, technical priorities, and production support responsibilities with limited supervision.
· Act as a technical lead for GIS requirements gathering, solution design, and cross-functional consensus building with business units, vendors, and IT teams.
· Develop, configure, enhance, and support enterprise GIS applications, integrations, services, and automation workflows across ArcGIS, ArcFM, and related business systems including SAP and OMS/ADMS.
· Support processes in FME Form & FME Flow including ETL processes, data orchestration, data validation, automation workflows on common DBMS platforms including Oracle, SQL Server, and PostgreSQL.
· Provide technical support for geospatial data, database compliance, platform administration, system performance, cybersecurity requirements, and application reliability.
· Identify, evaluate, and recommend new technologies, services, AI-enabled tools, and modernization opportunities that support the GIS application roadmap.
· Lead technical phases of major projects, establish technical plans, monitor schedules, manage dependencies, validate deliverables, and support successful project execution.
· Create, enforce, and continuously improve technical standards, development practices, documentation, release processes, and operational support procedures.
· Troubleshoot complex production issues, perform root-cause analysis, coordinate vendor support, and implement sustainable corrective actions.
· Manage and provide technical support for the GIS and SAP integrations. This includes working with external vendors & modernizing the current supporting technologies.
· Supporting mission-critical GIS environments with high availability, disaster recovery, and business continuity requirements.
· Provide after-hours support when needed for activities such as IT maintenance, storm support and GIS IT On-Call rotation.

Required Qualifications

· Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Geographic Information System (GIS), Computer Science, or a related field of study and a minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Strong problem solving and analytical skills and ability to multitask.
Must be a proven team player to work, promote and consolidate efficient team working relationships.

GIS & Utility Industry Expertise:

· Strong understanding of enterprise IT GIS concepts, principles, methodologies, standards, and best practices.
· Experience with Esri technologies including ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Utility Network, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Experience Builder, ArcGIS Field Maps, ArcGIS Survey123, ArcGIS Dashboards, ArcGIS Workforce, ArcGIS Velocity, and ArcGIS Developer technologies.
· Experience supporting Schneider Electric ArcFM applications and utility-focused GIS solutions.
· Knowledge of electric and gas utility operations, asset management, outage management, work management, engineering, customer service, and field operations processes.
Application Development & Integration Expertise:

· Experience developing enterprise GIS and business applications & automations using Python is required. Additional benefits for this role include JavaScript, TypeScript, C#/.NET, ASP.NET, REST APIs, SQL, HTML5, and CSS.
· Experience developing and supporting integrations between GIS and enterprise systems such as SAP, EAM, OMS, ADMS, CIS, mobile workforce applications, cloud services, and vendor platforms.
· Experience with service-oriented architecture, event-driven architecture, APIs, microservices, middleware technologies, secure coding practices, and software design patterns.
Cloud, Infrastructure & Application Security Expertise:

· Experience supporting GIS solutions in hybrid and cloud environments, including Microsoft Azure and AWS.
· Strong understanding of modern enterprise application platforms, cloud and infrastructure technologies, cybersecurity principles, networking concepts, system administration, and operational support practices
Artificial Intelligence Expertise:
· Knowledge of AI, Generative AI, and automation technologies, with experience using AI tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Copilot) to reverse engineer application code or scripts, generate code, improve development productivity, and automate business processes
DevOps & Modern Software Delivery Expertise:
· Experience with source control and version management tools including Git, GitHub, JIRA, Azure DevOps, Visual Studio, VS Code.
· Knowledge of Agile, Scrum, DevOps, ITIL, application lifecycle management, and production support processes.
Leadership, Communication & Business Engagement Experience:
· Ability to work directly with business stakeholders to define requirements, refine functional designs, prioritize work, and translate business needs into scalable technology solutions.
· Ability to lead technical evaluations, proofs of concept, product assessments, vendor reviews, and roadmap recommendations.
· Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex GIS & IT technology concepts to non-technical audiences and senior leadership.
· Ability to collaborate, build consensus, influence with and without authority, work independently, and proactively identify improvement opportunities.

Preferred Qualifications

· Master’s degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Geographic Information System (GIS), Computer Science, or a related field of study.
· Graduate-level training or technical certification in GIS, cloud platforms, AI, or enterprise architecture.

jobs.description:

MasTec Professional Services
delivers critical infrastructure construction and engineering services for power delivery, gas, and water customers, specializing in overhead and underground electric distribution for power delivery systems, gas distribution construction for gas systems, and turnkey solutions for a variety of water, sewer, and civil infrastructure projects. jobs.title: Environmental Scientist II
jobs.description:
Overview

Colliers Engineering & Design is seeking an Environmental Staff Scientist with 2-5 years of experience to perform wetland and stream delineations, protected species and habitat characterizations, GPS data collection, Arc-GIS application, preparation of permits and reports in support of federal, state and local permits. Take responsible charge for collecting field data, interpreting data and preparing technical reports. Work with a team of environmental professionals including professional engineers, surveyors, and planners in an interdisciplinary setting. Daily activities may include site reconnaissance, conducting environmental due diligence investigations and assessments, collection of soil and groundwater samples, and laboratory data management. This position will require travel and is expected to have a 30% - 60% balance between field and office work, which will vary based on project needs. The ideal candidate will have a Bachelor of Science degree in biology, ecological science, environmental science, environmental engineering, or related scientific discipline. This position is targeted to be loocated in the Raleigh, North Carolina office; however, depending on the ideal candidates location, other offices such as Charlotte and Wilmington, North Carolina may be considered.

Responsibilities

Perform Wetland Delineations in accordance with the Army Corp of Engineers Wetland Delineation Manual.
Assist in the preparation of applications for wetland verifications and permits to regulatory agencies.
Assist in the preparation and assemblage of natural resource reports and supporting documentation to facilitate site development and redevelopment.
Facilitate permit procurement from jurisdictional agencies.
Assist in the preparation of Threatened and Endangered Species Habitat Evaluations, and correspondence with regulatory agencies and permit management.
Assist in the preparation of environmental impacts and assessments.

Plan, coordinate, execute, and document environmental tests - including vibration, thermal, thermal vacuum, shock, and EMI/EMC testing - for spaceflight components, subsystems, and systems in accordance with applicable standards and customer requirements

jobs.title: Director, Development Permitting & Environmental
jobs.description:
Houston Texas | Asset Development

We are seeking a Director, Development Permitting & Environmental to lead the owner's-side environmental development and permitting capability supporting Talen Energy's power generation, battery storage, and digital infrastructure portfolio. The role owns early environmental screening, site-specific diligence, permitting strategy and schedule, agency engagement, and acquisition of approvals needed to advance projects from site evaluation through Final Investment Decision (FID) and transition to execution. The Director will convert environmental and regulatory complexity into practical recommendations that improve project viability, schedule certainty, and investment readiness.

Reporting to the Chief Asset Development Officer, this leader will support simple-cycle and combined-cycle facilities using aeroderivative and large-frame F- and H-class gas turbines; utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS); and powered-land or data center opportunities. The role will work closely with Corporate Environmental and other internal stakeholders while managing external consultants. Detailed studies and permit applications may be outsourced, but the Director retains accountability for development-stage strategy, schedule, budget, risk, quality, agency relationships, and consultant performance. The scope is development and project-specific permitting, not routine operating-fleet compliance, with disciplined transfer of permit conditions and continuing obligations to Project Delivery, Operations, and other accountable compliance owners.

Key Responsibilities

Build and lead the Environmental Development & Permitting function, including screening standards, permitting playbooks, stage-gate deliverables, consultant governance, regulatory intelligence, document controls, and portfolio reporting.
Partner with Site Origination, Project Development, and assigned Project Owners to screen greenfield, brownfield, and co-located opportunities; identify environmental fatal flaws; define early diligence and kill criteria; and recommend whether to advance, mitigate, pause, or exit before material spend.
Develop and maintain a permitting roadmap for each active project, identifying required approvals, agency and public-engagement pathways, study windows, expected permit review periods, application dependencies, risks and mitigations, budget, schedule, critical dates, and contingency plans.
Coordinate closely with Corporate Environmental, Legal, Project Delivery, Operations, and External Affairs to align development-stage environmental and permitting work with applicable Talen policies, procedures, standards, and environmental management-system requirements. Seek early input and provide advance notice when projects may affect existing permits, compliance programs, operating assets, enterprise positions, or material legal or regulatory risk.
Lead air-permitting strategy for gas-fired generation and other stationary sources. Direct applicability analyses, emissions estimates, dispersion modeling, control-technology evaluations, and applications involving NSR, PSD, nonattainment NSR, Title V, NSPS, emission credits, NESHAP/MACT, BACT, LAER, greenhouse-gas requirements, and state programs.
Direct site-specific diligence and field programs, including Phase I and, when warranted, Phase II Environmental Site Assessments; wetlands and waters delineations; threatened and endangered species reviews; cultural and historic-resource evaluations; floodplain and habitat reviews; noise and visual studies; and legacy-liability assessments.
Lead or coordinate Clean Water Act Sections 401 and 404 approvals, NPDES and stormwater permits, erosion and sediment-control approvals, wastewater and water-supply or withdrawal authorizations, wetlands mitigation, and related environmental permits.
Establish environmental strategies for BESS and powered-land or data center developments, including emergency or on-site generation, water and wastewater, stormwater, hazardous materials, spill prevention, noise, mitigation, and interfaces with local approvals owned by Site Origination.
Select, scope, direct, and hold accountable environmental consultants, air modelers, wetland and ecological specialists, cultural-resource firms, laboratories, and environmental counsel. Manage procurement, quality, interfaces, budget, schedule, and acceptance criteria, and challenge unsupported assumptions.
Serve as the principal development-stage environmental interface with EPA, state agencies, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, State Historic Preservation Offices, Tribal representatives, watershed authorities, and local regulators. Lead consultations, permit negotiations, responses, public notice, and hearings as appropriate.
Integrate environmental requirements into project configuration, engineering, procurement, contracting, and construction planning. Maintain permit and obligation trackers, incorporate mitigation commitments into project documents, and coordinate with Corporate Environmental and Legal to transfer continuing obligations to Project Delivery, Operations, and other accountable compliance owners.
Own environmental workstream plans, budgets, schedules, assumptions, and risk registers. Provide decision-ready status, risk, mitigation, and approval recommendations to Project Owners, Development Controls, Finance, Legal, executives, and investment-governance forums.
Perform environmental diligence for acquisitions, partnerships, and existing-site reuse; monitor regulatory developments; and convert lessons learned and agency feedback into stronger standards, consultant networks, and portfolio strategy.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemical engineering, biology, ecology, natural resources, environmental planning, geology, or a related discipline.
10+ years of progressive experience in environmental permitting, consulting, energy development, or complex infrastructure, including substantial responsibility for development-stage capital projects.
Demonstrated success advancing utility-scale energy or comparable industrial projects from screening and diligence through permit acquisition, FID, notice to proceed, or construction readiness while managing schedule, budget, risk, and cross-functional interfaces.
Direct experience permitting or supporting simple-cycle and combined-cycle gas generation using aeroderivative and large-frame F- and H-class turbines, with working knowledge of emissions, air modeling, control technology, water, noise, site-layout, and operating-profile considerations.
Experience with utility-scale battery energy storage and the environmental requirements relevant to site development, construction, hazardous materials, stormwater, spill prevention, emergency planning, and operations.
Strong working knowledge of the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, NEPA, Endangered Species Act, National Historic Preservation Act, CERCLA, RCRA, and related state siting and environmental-review requirements.
Demonstrated ability to lead agency engagement and permit negotiations, interpret complex technical studies, manage external consultants and counsel, and maintain defensible applications, schedules, budgets, records, and commitments across multiple projects.
Strong project leadership, business judgment, analytical ability, and executive communication skills, including the ability to translate environmental findings into clear project and capital-allocation recommendations. Ability to travel regularly.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree and/or relevant professional credential such as Professional Engineer, Certified Environmental Professional, Professional Wetland Scientist, CHMM, or PMP.
Direct experience in PJM states, including familiarity with state environmental agencies, regional water authorities, federal field offices, and permitting practices affecting generation, storage, transmission, and large-load development.
Experience with powered-land, hyperscale data center, or other large-load development, including air permits for emergency or on-site generation, water and wastewater strategy, and environmental site readiness.
Experience with greenfield and brownfield projects, including retired or operating generation sites, legacy contamination, remediation, acquisitions, repowering, and reuse of industrial infrastructure.
Experience supporting construction-phase compliance, financing or acquisition diligence, public hearings, contested or high-profile matters, and transition of permit obligations to construction and operating organizations.

Leadership Profile

Owner-minded environmental leader who accepts accountability for strategy, decisions, risk, consultant performance, and outcomes rather than merely coordinating studies and applications.
Practical strategist who protects compliance and permit defensibility while recognizing that solutions must also be safe, financeable, constructible, operable, and aligned with project economics and schedules.
Decisive under uncertainty and willing to surface fatal flaws, quantify exposure, challenge optimistic assumptions, and recommend mitigation or exit before momentum overrides evidence.
Credible relationship builder who earns trust with agencies, communities, Project Owners, functional peers, and consultants while creating scalable standards, tools, talent, and institutional knowledge.

Success Measures

Timely, decision-quality environmental screening and permitting roadmaps, with material constraints and fatal flaws identified before significant capital or schedule commitments.
Required permits and approvals obtained on defensible terms within approved schedules and budgets, with clear visibility into agency, public-process, mitigation, and compliance risks.
Few avoidable late-stage surprises, redesigns, consultant rework cycles, or permit-driven delays caused by incomplete diligence, weak applications, missed study windows, or poorly managed interfaces.

jobs.title: Senior Geospatial Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
We are looking for someone who already does production geoprocessing in Python - rasterio, geopandas, numpy - and wants the geospatial layer to be the product rather than a chore buried under someone else's roadmap.

M33 is building iris
. You can ask a spatial question in plain language - "vegetation change along this corridor over the last three years" - and iris composes a real, inspectable pipeline against satellite imagery and open vector data, which you can open, change and re-run. All orchestrated with trusted tools, with transparency and provenance about what’s happening all the way through.

We are a small but growing team. You would be joining as our second engineer, and as another geospatial specialist - so we need someone who can function as a subject-matter expert as much as a developer.

The engagement

Independent contract, not employment. Remote, anywhere you can legally invoice as a business. Up to 40 hours a week at your own schedule, with at least 8 overlapping North American hours.

US$45-55/hour
, depending on depth and location.

What you would own

Our Python processing engine - the catalog of composable geoprocessing tasks iris builds pipelines from.
Making a wrong answer hard to ship quietly. Nodata that survives masking, resampling and band maths. Reprojection that does not silently degrade. Pipelines that don’t run green if they’re returning a plausible but wrong number.
Letting someone bring their own data into a pipeline, validating it, and refusing it loudly when it cannot be trusted.
Cloud-native formats and access: COGs, STAC, GeoParquet, PostGIS, DuckDB spatial, dynamic tile serving.
New data sources and connectors - satellite collections, global vector sources, disaster-event feeds.

What we need to see

Production
experience with rasterio, geopandas and numpy. (This one is non-negotiable - substantial real work, not passing familiarity.)
A spatial problem you took end-to-end into production. Any industry: agriculture, disaster response, urban planning, logistics, environmental monitoring. What matters is that you worked through the geoprocessing and shipped something that ran.
Depth underneath those libraries - GDAL internals, coordinate systems and reprojection, raster and vector operations, STAC.
Python you would be happy for someone else to maintain, and comfort working in Docker.
The independence to set technical direction rather than wait to be told what to build.

Nice to have:
SAR or optical remote sensing, spectral indices, change detection, terrain and hydrology. Performance tuning of large raster reads. Knowing how you would prove a server does what it says it does.

How to apply

Use the link to access our (short!) application form. Tell us who you are, and one spatial problem you took into production. If you look like you might be a good fit for M33, we’ll reach out for an interview.

jobs.title: Master Thesis, 30HP: Finding the UAV in a Haystack of Birds -- Deep Models for Target Classification in Radar Tracking
jobs.description:
Are you a student eager to apply your theoretical knowledge and fresh perspectives to real-world challenges? At Saab, we believe that innovation thrives on new ideas, and your master thesis project could be the spark that ignites our next technological breakthrough.

Your role

We recognize the immense value that students bring to our company. Your academic rigor, combined with your enthusiasm for cutting-edge technology, allows you to approach problems with a unique and insightful lens. At Saab, you'll have the opportunity to collaborate with experienced engineers and specialists, gaining invaluable practical experience while making a tangible contribution to our growth and development.

Background

Achieving an air-situational picture of high quality – a task in which radars play a central role – is essential to ensuring the integrity of the air-space, and in turn, the safety of people and society. A surveillance radar works by emitting energy that is reflected by targets of interest as well as other objects in a surveillance volume, giving rise to unlabeled sets of detections of unknown origin. Through repeated measurement of the surveillance volume and the use of target-tracking algorithms, with a foundation in Bayesian estimation, a situational picture emerges described by an a posteriori probability distribution of targets in the air-space.

In particular, developments in recent years have made it increasingly important to detect and track potentially hostile unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), informally known as drones. These objects commonly fly at similar altitudes and velocities to the thousands of birds that may be present in the sky at any given moment. This creates a needle-in-a-haystack problem, where accurate automatic classification of target type is important to avoid overloading the radar operator with bird tracks of little relevance.

Description Of The Thesis

The project aims to explore Bayesian methods for target classification, focusing on exploiting behavioral differences between birds and UAVs to determine target class. We are in particular interested in the prospects of likelihood-based classification using learned system models. Depending on the class of system models under consideration, this may also involve learning filters to facilitate likelihood evaluation within a modest computational budget.

A ladder of different system models may be considered, ranging from traditional kinematic models parametrized by a few parameters, models in deep latent spaces, and hybrid models combining both prior knowledge about dynamics of the kinematic state and deep states which may encode additional behavioral information. By investigating system identification along this ladder, the intention of the project is to address how to combine prior structure and model expressiveness to maximize object classification capabilities.

Your profile

The project is suitable for one or two students. You are in the end of your technical master's education in Engineering Physics, Engineering Mathematics, Electrical engineering, Automation and Mechatronics or similar, with an interest for advanced mathematics and numerical methods. Advanced courses in mathematics, in particular Bayesian statistics, is meriting, as well as practical experience of deep learning.

We provide the support and guidance you need to translate your theoretical knowledge into practical solutions. Join us and become a driving force behind Saab's technological advancements!

This position requires that you pass a security vetting based on the current regulations around/of security protection. For positions requiring security clearance additional obligations on citizenship may apply.

Kindly observe that this is an ongoing recruitment process and that the position might be filled before the closing date of the advertisement.

What you will be a part of

Explore a wealth of possibilities. Take on challenges, create smart inventions, and grow beyond. This is a place for curious minds, brave pioneers, and everyone in between. Together, we achieve the extraordinary, each bringing our unique perspectives. Your part matters.

Saab is a leading defense and security company with an enduring purpose, to help nations keep their people and society safe. Empowered by its 28,000 talented people, Saab constantly pushes the boundaries of technology to create a safer and more sustainable world.

Saab designs, manufactures and maintains advanced systems in aeronautics, weapons, command and control, sensors and underwater systems. Saab is headquartered in Sweden. It has major operations all over the world and is part of the domestic defense capability of several nations. Read more about us here.

Description

NISC IV is seeking an Environmental Engineer to provide environmental compliance and occupational safety and health expertise at the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC) in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. This position performs technical and field-based environmental activities associated with asbestos management, stormwater, sanitary sewer and pretreatment discharges, air emissions, spill response, and the MMAC Environmental Occupational Safety & Health Management System (EOSHMS).

The Environmental Engineer applies professional knowledge and judgment to evaluate environmental conditions, identify hazards and environmental impacts, assess regulatory compliance, develop appropriate controls, and prepare technical documentation. The position works as part of a multidisciplinary team and coordinates with FAA personnel, laboratories, contractors, building occupants, and local regulatory authorities.

This is an in office position in Oklahoma City, OK.

Must be local or willing to self relocate.

Primary Responsibilities

Perform environmental compliance activities associated with asbestos management, stormwater, sanitary sewer and pretreatment discharges, air emissions, and spill response.
Perform Asbestos Inspector duties, including facility surveys, visual inspections, collection of bulk samples, and preparation of technical surveys, reports, and drawings.
Coordinate asbestos projects with building occupants, abatement contractors, laboratories, and third-party air-monitoring personnel; prepare and submit formal written reports to the FAA Program Manager.
Coordinate pretreatment Outfall 002 cyanide effluent sampling; maintain pollutant and flow batch-log information; and review laboratory analyses for accuracy and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC).
Track metal-finishing shop discharges to the Industrial Wastewater Treatment Plant (IWWTP) and maintain associated environmental compliance data.
Evaluate occupational health hazards, environmental impacts, and safety concerns and develop appropriate controls or mitigation measures.
Research applicable regulatory, scientific, and engineering requirements and translate findings into technical recommendations, procedures, training, and compliance activities.
Participate as a member of multidisciplinary teams analyzing field-level hazard-producing mechanisms and environmental conditions.
Develop and maintain procedures, processes, standards, specifications, and technical documentation associated with environmental, occupational safety, and health programs.
Provide professional technical opinions and training concerning environmental stewardship and occupational safety and health matters.
Perform audit activities associated with the MMAC EOSH Management System and develop written documentation necessary to maintain the program.
Compile and verify combustion and refrigeration equipment information used in the air-emissions inventory.
Coordinate environmental compliance activities with local authorities for sanitary sewer, pretreatment, non-stormwater, and stormwater discharges.
Serve as an alternate responder for spill-cleanup emergencies.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, Occupational Safety and Health, or a closely related technical discipline.
4+ years of relevant professional experience (or a Master’s degree with 2+ years of relevant professional experience).
40-hour Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) training.
Current Oklahoma Asbestos Inspector License.
Experience evaluating environmental conditions, regulatory requirements, hazards, or environmental compliance issues and developing technically sound recommendations or corrective actions.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance programs such as asbestos, stormwater, wastewater/pretreatment, air emissions, spill prevention/response, or related environmental programs.
Experience conducting field inspections, environmental assessments, sampling activities, or other field-based environmental work.
Ability to research and interpret regulatory, scientific, engineering, and technical information and apply findings to environmental compliance activities.
Experience preparing technical reports, procedures, assessments, findings, or other formal environmental documentation.
Ability to analyze laboratory or environmental data for completeness, accuracy, and QA/QC considerations.
Ability to communicate technical findings and professional recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to independently organize and complete assigned technical work while coordinating activities across multiple organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with an Environmental, Occupational Safety and Health Management System or comparable environmental management system.
Knowledge of ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 principles and requirements.
Experience working with federal, state, or local environmental regulations and regulatory authorities.
Experience with environmental compliance in a large campus, industrial, aviation, government, or similarly complex operating environment.
Experience with industrial wastewater/pretreatment, stormwater compliance, air-emissions inventories, asbestos management, or spill response.
Experience conducting or participating in environmental or EOSH management-system audits.

jobs.title: Western Policy & Conservation Manager
jobs.description:
Western Policy & Conservation Manager

Organizational Profile

Backcountry Hunters & Anglers (BHA) is a North American nonprofit organization with chapters throughout Canada and the United States. BHA seeks to ensure North America’s outdoor heritage of hunting and fishing in a natural setting through education and work on behalf of our wild public lands, waters, and wildlife.

BHA is a grassroots-driven organization that believes conservation happens on two fronts: by speaking up for public lands and waters and by showing up to care for them firsthand. Through policy advocacy, grassroots organizing, and boots-on-the-ground habitat stewardship, BHA works to ensure healthy habitats and abundant fish and wildlife populations for generations to come.

Primary Objective:
Enhance BHA’s reputation as the leading sportsmen’s voice on public lands, waters and wildlife issues through grassroots engagement on federal, state and local policy issues by providing cohesive direction and robust support across BHA’s chapter network.

As a BHA Western Policy & Conservation Manager
, you are expected to be consistently executing in the following areas:

ROLE DEVELOPMENT & ORGANIZATIONAL LEADERSHIP

Support the evolution of BHA’s Regional Policy & Conservation priorities in response to organizational needs and the changing policy landscape.
Participate in strategic planning and development.
Ensure communication across BHA channels are accurate, timely, and non-partisan.
Develop long-term relationships and represent BHA at professional conferences, regional policy conferences, and events.

POLICY COORDINATION & INTERNAL COMMUNICATION

Provide organizational policy expertise, including the review and critique of proposed conservation policy positions, memoranda, and communication materials for BHA and its chapters to take effective positions on key conservation issues.
Provide direct support on policy matters in your region as a primary focus, while supporting stewardship projects that influence policy work or larger strategic objectives as a secondary focus.
Keep BHA CEO, directors, coordinators, and chapters informed about state policy issues that are related to our mission, including providing updates for HQ staff through weekly calls.
Continue building and refining the systems that support policy coordination, creating clearer processes for communication, issue tracking, prioritization and collaboration among policy staff, field staff and chapters.
Update and maintain legislative tracking reports using BHA native software platforms.
Maintain and facilitate consistent communication between Field Staff, MarComms and Policy Teams to help produce and leverage accurate, well-rounded content with depth and insight into the multiple layers of BHA’s work.

POLICY CAMPAIGNS & STRATEGIC ENGAGEMENT

Help lead major state and federal policy campaigns focused on public lands, water, and wildlife conservation and access. Support advancing federal legislation and administrative actions in close collaboration with Government Relations staff.
Advise and support coordinators and chapters on state, local and federal policy issues, helping connect regional priorities to broader BHA policy positions and build effective grassroots campaigns from the ground up.
Coordinate policy engagement on cross-jurisdictional issues, including management plans, forest revisions, acquisitions and cross-border matters.
Work to identify and coordinate efforts on broadly relevant and critically important policy issues.
Leverage BHA’s grassroots network to support policy engagement and create an approachable environment for volunteers and supporters from all walks of life to meaningfully contribute and learn about conservation advocacy.

PARTNERSHIPS & STEWARDSHIP

Manage existing grants/partnerships and strategically seek new opportunities to support regional and organizational policy and stewardship goals.
Advance BHA’s relationships with state and federal partners.
Connect with coalition groups and stay in contact with partner organizations to track and coordinate engagement on policy issues.
Deepen and build on relationships with Chapter Policy Leaders and staff from partner organizations that share policy priorities.
Facilitate regular communication with partners and chapter leaders across multiple states by sharing and comparing resources on key policy issues related to the conservation of our public lands, waters, and wildlife.
Build on existing partnerships with state and federal agencies (USFWS, USFS, USACE, BLM, etc.) through HQ-led and Chapter-led stewardship projects that improve or conserve wildlife habitat, expand public hunting and fishing access and opportunity, or advance policy goals. Strategically seek new opportunities at the HQ level, ensuring integration with the Stewardship program.

COMMUNICATIONS & MEDIA

Amplify policy and stewardship investments through communications and media.
Produce action alerts, member-facing content and press responses for BHA’s major access cases.
Work collaboratively to identify opportunities for op-eds, LTEs, videos, blogs, action alerts, social pushes, website pages, co-branded events and other content.
Help chapters write and publish policy content when needed, including LTEs, statements, blogs, action alerts and related materials.
Help generate press materials and social media content to implement communications strategies that increase exposure for BHA’s policy priorities and stewardship program.

FUNDING STREAMS

Ensure the long-term viability of the Western Policy and Conservation Manager
role by understanding and developing revenue streams in the short and long-term.

BHA is headquartered in Missoula, Montana. We offer a stimulating and fun work environment, health insurance and 401K plan match, generous leave package including annual time off for backcountry hunting/fishing, and discounts with BHA corporate partners.

Starting Salary & Term:
Compensation dependent on prior experience and qualifications.

Location:
Remote, with preference for candidates based in the Western United States.

Application:
To apply send cover letter and resume to hiring committee at Careers@backcountryhunters.org with the subject line “Western Conservation & Policy Manager” Please attach your cover letter and resume as one pdf document. The application cover letter should outline both your interest and qualifications for this position. Head of UAV Engineering — AGNIVOX Location:
Kerala, India
Employment Type:
Full-time
Industry:
UAV / Drone Technology / Aerospace Engineering

About AGNIVOX

AGNIVOX is building the next generation of intelligent unmanned aerial systems from Kerala to the world. We are developing advanced UAV technologies for applications including agriculture, fire & rescue, industrial inspection, infrastructure monitoring, and specialised aerial operations
.
We are looking for an experienced and technically strong Head of UAV Engineering
to lead our UAV engineering function and drive the development of next-generation drone platforms.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the complete UAV engineering and product development
lifecycle from concept to deployment.
Design, develop and optimise multirotor and autonomous UAV platforms
.
Lead mechanical, electrical, propulsion, avionics and system-integration engineering.
Develop and integrate flight controllers, sensors, communication systems, payloads and autonomous systems
.
Lead UAV prototyping, testing, troubleshooting and performance optimisation.
Develop systems for autonomous navigation, mission planning, obstacle avoidance and dynamic task allocation
.
Establish engineering standards, testing protocols and documentation.
Work closely with software, AI, electronics and manufacturing teams.
Lead field testing and validation of UAV systems under real-world operating conditions.
Support regulatory, certification and compliance requirements applicable to UAV manufacturing and operations.
Build and mentor a high-performing UAV engineering team.
Evaluate emerging drone technologies and identify opportunities for product innovation.
Work closely with management to convert product concepts into commercially viable UAV solutions.

Required Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Aeronautical, Mechanical, Electronics, Electrical, Robotics, Mechatronics or a related engineering discipline
.
5+ years of relevant experience
in UAV/drone development, aerospace systems, robotics or autonomous systems.
Strong understanding of UAV architecture, propulsion, flight dynamics and avionics.
Hands-on experience with flight controllers, autopilots, telemetry and UAV communication systems
.
Experience with platforms such as PX4, ArduPilot or equivalent
will be an advantage.
Knowledge of CAD, electronics integration, embedded systems and UAV system testing
.
Experience leading engineering teams or complex technical projects.
Strong problem-solving and product-development capabilities.

Preferred Skills

Experience in one or more of the following will be highly valued:
Autonomous UAVs | Computer Vision | AI/ML | ROS/ROS2 | PX4 | ArduPilot | Embedded Systems | LiDAR | RTK-GPS | Thermal Imaging | BVLOS Systems | Swarm/Multiple UAV Systems | Payload Integration

What You Will Lead

You will play a key role in developing AGNIVOX's UAV technology roadmap, including:
Concept → Engineering → Prototype → Testing → Certification → Manufacturing → Deployment

This is a leadership position for someone who wants to build real-world UAV products
, not simply manage an engineering team.

Why Join AGNIVOX?

Lead the development of next-generation UAV technology
.
Work on applications with real-world industrial and emergency-response use cases.
Build products from Kerala to global markets
.
Work across aerospace, robotics, AI and autonomous systems.
Opportunity to shape the company's UAV engineering and R&D strategy.

Apply Now If you are passionate about UAV engineering, autonomous systems and building innovative aerospace technology
, we would like to hear from you.
Send your CV and a brief introduction to:

info@agnivox.org

jobs.description:
Cloudnet Systems LLC, a small business federal IT contractor (GSA Multiple Award Schedule holder), is assembling the delivery team for a US Fish and Wildlife Service web platform support and improvement contract we are actively bidding. We are seeking a part\-time GIS Developer to join the proposed team.

**Compensation:** $60 per hour (1099 or W2 hourly depending on arrangement), paid for hours worked.

**What you will do:**

\- Support geospatial data alignment for a national wildlife refuge platform: hunt\-unit boundary analysis and correction, spatial data QA, and synchronization with an annually published authoritative feature layer.

\- Work with ArcGIS Online feature layers, related tables, and public and authorized REST APIs under a federal agency's ArcGIS organization (collaborator account provided).

\- Integrate spatial data and map views into web modules (Angular front end); support species\-to\-hunt\-unit data relationships feeding an annual federal rulemaking cycle.

\- Provide elevated GIS support during the January\-May rulemaking season, including boundary corrections and spatial layer reliability.

\- Coordinate with the agency's GIS advisory committee and data stewards on authoritative data layers.

**Role\-specific qualifications:** At least 3 years with the Esri platform, ArcGIS Online strongly preferred; feature services and REST APIs; spatial data quality workflows. Experience with federal or state natural\-resource GIS data a plus.

**The engagement:** approximately 240 hours in year one, then approximately 120 hours per year in subsequent option years spread as steady part\-time work, not a single block. Fully remote from anywhere in the United States, during Eastern business hours (9:00 AM to 5:00 PM ET). No on\-call or after\-hours work, including for critical incidents. One annual planning trip to Fort Collins, CO or Falls Church, VA may be requested for lead personnel. A Government laptop is provided.

**Important \- contingent role:** This position is contingent upon contract award, expected in fall 2026\. Selected candidates will be named in our proposal and must provide a one\-page resume and sign a brief letter of commitment by Wednesday, September 23, 2026\. There is no obligation and no work performed unless the contract is awarded. Candidates must be able to complete a federal background investigation and PIV credentialing before system access.

**General requirements:** US\-based and working on US soil; Bachelors degree plus at least 3 years of relevant experience (required by our GSA contract); federal contracting experience a plus.

**To apply:** send your resume with "GIS Developer \- FWS" in the subject line. We are moving quickly; qualified respondents will receive a 15\-minute screening call within one business day.

Pay: $55\.00 \- $60\.00 per hour

Work Location: Remote

jobs.title: GIS Technician
jobs.description:
We are Forestry England.

We live and breathe forests.

Job title – GIS technician

Salary- £30,105 pro rata

Contract type – Fixed Term Appointment until 31 March 2029

Hours – 18.5 hours per week

Vacancy closes - 24th September, 23:58

Join us. We're foresters, professionals and experts. We are a passionate team who love to share our enthusiasm and want to make a positive difference for you and the environment.

Together, we’re using our scale and expertise to grow the nation’s forests for everyone. We’re already adapting our landscapes for tomorrow, and getting stuff done today, like creating amazing places and experiences for you to enjoy. We're providing vital homes for wildlife, making our air cleaner to breathe and producing sustainable timber .

What You’ll Do…

As the GIS Technician, you will help Forestry England achieve its objectives by providing an accurate inventory of the districts assets, from which to base future operational planning, and provide technical support on GIS and data matters to the wider forest district to enable them to fulfil their roles within the Forest District.

The GIS Technician works closely with Forestry England colleagues across the Forest District to ensure data is collected and recorded correctly and integrity in datasets is maintained.

Please see the job description below for more information and details about what we need from you

Where you’ll work…

The postholder will be part of Forestry England North District based out of our Grizedale (LA22 0QJ) or Bellingham (NE48 2HP) offices.

Benefits…

Alongside your salary, Forestry England contributes an average of 28.97% towards your pension. You will become a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension Scheme.

25 days holiday a year, raising by one day every year’s service, up to 30 days (pro-rated for part time employees) plus additional days off such as bank holidays.
STaR is our employee benefits scheme offering discounts on everyday supermarket shopping, as well as other things such as hotel stays clothes, mobile phones, other electrical items, medical and car insurance, holidays, gym discounts, household bills, Headspace wellbeing app.
free parking at Forestry England sites and free entry to our National Arboretums at Westonbirt and Bedgebury.
a commitment to lifelong learning through career development. Forestry England will support your career development in a variety of ways, including continual professional development, support for individual learning plans and sponsored membership of professional bodies.

Read more about the benefits on the Forestry England website.

How To Apply…

We cannot accept applications via email. Please follow the steps outlined below. Any CVs and/or personal statements sent outside the system will not be considered for shortlisting.

You will be asked to write a 200 word statement on your relevant experience and career history, along with a personal statement of no more than 500 words. You will be assessed on both during sifting. More details about how to apply are listed on the application form.

The Behaviours being assessed at interview are –

Seeing the big picture
Delivering at pace
Working together
Making effective decisions

You will also be assessed on technical skill. This will involve a short practical exercise loading and interrogating data, using both the in-house Forestry England GIS and ArcGIS Pro - help will be provided from our current GIS technician. Candidates will not need to prepare anything specific in advance for this exercise.

Successful candidates will undergo a criminal record check and the government baseline personnel security standard check.

If you require any reasonable adjustments, please email fcrecruitmentteam@forestryengland.uk.

If you're planning to use AI to support your application, please ensure you've read our guidelines here first.

Read more about our application process and working with us on the Forestry England website.

Nationality Requirements…

Read more about nationality requirements here.

Working for the Civil Service…

Forestry England is part of the Civil Service. The Civil Service has a Disability Confident Scheme (DCS). This means candidates with disabilities who meet the minimum selection criteria during the application process will be guaranteed an interview. We also offer a Redeployment Interview Scheme to current civil servants who are at risk of redundancy, and who meet the minimum requirements for the role. This role is also part of the Great Place to Work for Veterans and Prison Leaver Recruitment initiative.

Within Part 7 of the Immigration Act 2016, it is essential that applicants should have the ability to provide conversation in accurate spoken English.

Our recruitment process makes appointments based on fair and open competition and merit, as outlined in the Civil Service Commissioners’ Recruitment Principles. If you feel your application has not been treated in in line with/according to these principles and you wish to make a complaint, please email: englandhr.services@forestryengland.uk.

jobs.title: Social and Environmental Safeguards Specialist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Job Description

Tiered Approach

In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations.” The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDF’s vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

Preferred

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

SME Finance
Sub-National Finance
Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

UNCDF’s Social and Environmental Safeguards (SES) support UNDCF’s commitment to integrate social and environmental sustainability into our programs, projects, and investment transactions that promote sustainable development.

The Objectives Of The SES Are To

Strengthen the social and environmental outcomes of programs and projects.
Avoid adverse effects on people and the environment. When avoidance is not feasible, minimize, mitigate, and manage adverse impacts.
Enhance the capacities of UNCDF and partners to manage social and environmental risks.
Ensure comprehensive stakeholder engagement, including a mechanism to address complaints from individuals affected by UNCDF initiatives.

A key mechanism for ensuring the application of the SES is the project-level / transaction-level Social and Environmental Screening Procedure (SESP), which is mandatory for most proposed projects/transactions. The objectives of the SESP are to: (a) integrate the SES Overarching Principles (leave no one behind, human rights, gender equality, sustainability and resilience, and accountability); (b) identify potential social and environmental risks and their significance, along with mitigation strategies and options; (c) determine the project/transaction's SES risk category (Low, Moderate, Substantial, High); and (d) outline the level of social and environmental assessment and management needed to address potential risks and impacts during the implementation phase of UNCDF-supported programs, projects, and investment transactions.

Under the direct supervision of the Chief Risk Manager, the SES Specialist will assist with compliance at the program, project, and investment transaction levels with the UNCDF SES (which fully aligns with UNDP’s SES standards) throughout project design and implementation (from cradle to grave). This support is essential to ensure that selected programs, projects, and investment transactions in development avoid potential social and environmental risks and, when avoidance is not feasible, guarantee that proper assessments are conducted. Management measures are established to effectively manage risks during the implementation phase. It is critical that all UNCDF-supported initiatives adhere to their Environmental and Social Management Plan/Framework (ESMP/ESMF) and fully comply with UNCDF’s SES standards (which align with UNDP’s SES standards) throughout the entire project cycle.

The SES Specialist will be based in Nairobi, Kenya, and may be required to travel. UNCDF adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage connections across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNCDF personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multi-disciplinary settings to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties And Responsibilities

Conduct and coordinate SES screenings and SES assessments:
As part of UNCDF's project/investment transaction cycle process, prepare pre-screening (concept stage) and/or full screening (development stage) documentation related to UNCDF projects/investment transactions.
Oversee the quality of consultants' work to support the preparation of these documents.
Identify potential environmental and social risks that require specialized expertise or other considerations.
Review and maintain quality standards for draft and final deliverables, including, but not limited to, the completed SESP template with all supporting documents/evidence, as appropriate.
Provide quality assurance for baseline data collection and oversee the quality of impact assessments, including Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA), Strategic Environmental and Social Assessments (SESA), targeted assessments, etc., as identified through the SESP screening, in coordination with the IID.
Analyze safeguards, legal frameworks, and provisions in UNCDF initiatives to identify gaps and recommend remedial measures.
Establish and maintain standards for remote and/or on-the-ground data collection for SES standards as needed.
Set standards for stakeholder engagement in the assessment process to ensure the quality of UNCDF’s necessary stakeholder engagements.
Prepare and/or provide quality assurance for draft and final deliverables, including, but not limited to, ESIA, SESA, PEAR, etc., with all supporting documents, technical chapters, and evidence, as appropriate.
Regularly prepare analysis reports, summary reports, and presentations of key issues and conclusions from the technical assessments for UNCDF’s Senior Management.
Advise and coordinate the development of SES management plans and management frameworks:
Advise on or coordinate the preparation of management frameworks/plans (including ESMF, ESMP, Indigenous Peoples Plan, Land Acquisition Plans, Resettlement Plan, Livelihoods Plan, etc.) identified through SESP screening and informed by SES assessments.
Advise on or coordinate the preparation of Stakeholder Engagement Plans, which incorporate the design of project Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
Identify any potential issues that may necessitate additional specialized expertise or other considerations.
Determine procedures and methods for risk avoidance, reduction, and mitigation throughout the project cycle.
Prepare draft and final deliverables, such as ESMP, ESMF, and/or other technical management plans, along with all necessary supporting documents, technical chapters, and evidence.
Conduct quality assurance reviews of plans and frameworks prepared by the UNCDF IID, integrating input from stakeholders, affected communities, project boards, and the project teams
Provide implementation support and advice to UNCDF teams:
Provide technical support to UNCDF’s IID on SES standards to ensure effective implementation and monitor the implementation of SES management plan(s).
Advise on and conduct spot checks on stakeholder engagement plans and processes, strategies, and consultations to identify and/or verify risks and advise on FPIC, disclosure, etc.
Establish and maintain a project-level Grievance Redress Mechanism that is appropriate to the scale of the project’s potential adverse risks and impacts.
Quality-assure and revise screenings, conduct assessments, and develop or update management plans of active projects when necessary.
Quality-assure draft and final SES documentation for projects (e.g., ESIA, ESMP, ESMF, IPP, RAP, SEP, relevant ToRs, etc.) to ensure they meet technical standards and requirements.
Commission and conduct, with senior management approval, environmental and social audits of projects to identify potential compliance issues and prepare environmental and social management action plans when problems are identified, through audits or otherwise.
Facilitate capacity development and knowledge sharing.
Develop capacity by training project teams and partners on SES requirements to which all UNCDF initiatives must adhere.
Document lessons learned, including instances where things did not proceed as planned, along with exemplary models of SES implementation.
In close collaboration with relevant teams at the Regional Hubs and HQ, contribute to creating and delivering modular training packages that enhance capacity in SES areas.
Provide on-the-job, demand-driven capacity development support to staff and personnel in your area of expertise. Analyze data and case evidence to extract relevant lessons on policy implementation and advocate for necessary policy changes with HQ teams.
Integrate regional perspectives into executing policy and strategic initiatives at the regional level within their areas of responsibility, supporting the key results, outcomes, and outputs of the UNCDF Strategic Framework.

Senior Environmental Planner & Project Manager

Hybrid or Remote within California

Help Shape the Future of California's Infrastructure and Communities

At ICF, we don't just navigate environmental challenges, we help our clients solve some of the most complex infrastructure, permitting, and sustainability issues facing California and the nation. We are enthusiastic about doing what is right for our clients, our people, the communities where we live and work, and the environment. We are planners, scientists, engineers, program managers, economists, communicators, and strategists united by a common purpose: delivering solutions that improve communities while protecting the environment.

As our energy, water, transportation, and infrastructure practices continue to grow, we are seeking an exceptional Senior Planner & Project Manager
to join our California team. This is an opportunity for a seasoned environmental leader to drive strategic programs, lead multidisciplinary teams, grow key client relationships, mentor future leaders, and help shape major projects from concept through construction.

If you thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced environment, enjoy developing innovative solutions to complex regulatory challenges, and are passionate about advancing projects that matter, we'd love to talk with you.

What You'll Do

As a Principal Environmental Planner & Project Manager, you will serve as a trusted advisor, project leader, and technical expert for public and private sector clients across California and beyond. You will lead complex environmental planning, permitting, and compliance efforts while helping expand ICF's market presence and mentoring the next generation of environmental professionals.

Leadership & Program Management

Manage large, complex environmental planning and compliance projects across all sectors with a focus on water and infrastructure projects.
Serve as a Senior Project Manager for high-profile projects.
Management of federal, state, and local permitting and compliance for projects in compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act [CEQA] and National Environmental Policy Act [NEPA] and other regulations.
Serve as a point of contact with private, local, state, and federal government clients.
Work with multidisciplinary teams of planners, engineers, scientists, economists, cultural resource specialists, biologists, environmental compliance professionals, and technologists.
Manage project scope, budgets, schedules, quality, and risk while ensuring successful client outcomes.
Foster collaboration across technical disciplines to deliver integrated solutions.

Environmental Planning, NEPA, CEQA & Permitting

Lead preparation and review of complex CEQA and NEPA documentation.
Lead regulatory strategy, agency consultation, mitigation planning, and environmental risk management for complex infrastructure projects, including development of avoidance, minimization, compensatory mitigation, and compliance approaches that support efficient project delivery.
Provide technical expertise related to environmental regulations, permitting pathways, agency consultation, and environmental review processes.
Guide clients through federal, state, and local permitting requirements and environmental compliance obligations.
Review technical studies addressing biological resources, cultural resources, air quality, noise, hydrology, transportation, land use, and related disciplines.

Serve as a point of contact and trusted advisor for public agencies, infrastructure owners, developers, and construction and engineering partners.
Guide multidisciplinary teams through complex and high-visibility environmental review processes, including projects with significant public interest, interagency coordination, technical complexity, and schedule or permitting risk.
Build and strengthen client relationships while identifying opportunities to expand existing contracts and develop new business.
Manage proposal development, including strategy, capture planning, scopes of work, budgets, and pursuit teams.
Help drive growth across California while contributing to national opportunities.

People Leadership

Mentor, coach, and develop junior environmental professionals

Help build and strengthen high-performing teams that deliver exceptional results for clients.
Foster an inclusive, collaborative, and growth-oriented culture.

Master's degree in a related discipline.

Experience with water infrastructure, flood risk management, ecosystem restoration, wastewater, rail, transportation, or other major California public works programs.

At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

MITRE’s Geospatial Intelligence program provides skills and capabilities to enable the creation and exploitation of national, tactical, and commercial Intelligence in support of Geospatial Intelligence users. We support the production of intelligence and situational awareness for national and warfighter security, targeting, command and control, and humanitarian aid. Our capabilities include requirements and mission workflow analysis for sensor platforms and ground systems, specialized computing systems, architecture design and integration of data and artificial intelligence in support of exploitation processes, advanced analytics, and integrated intelligence analysis from seabed to space.

Joining the Geospatial Intelligence Program means contributing to work of national and global importance. Our people help strengthen the digital and physical foundations that enable resilient, effective, and trusted geospatial intelligence. Together, we are advancing mission assurance and empowering national policy makers, warfighters, and partners with the confidence and capabilities needed to succeed in an increasingly dynamic intelligence environment.

Roles & Responsibilities:

MITRE is seeking a technically exceptional Principal Project Leader to lead our Geospatial intelligence Program’s Research and Analysis project team. This is a unique opportunity to help shape the future of geospatial intelligence. A key focus for this role is advancing and shaping current research, developing prototypes, transitioning new technologies and tradecraft into systems to enable GEOINT missions through AI-enabled mission automation and orchestration moving beyond manual, legacy processes toward scalable, intelligent operations. In partnership with staff from across MITRE’s Intelligence Center and MTE, you will help to solve challenges in the areas of Geospatial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML), Data Science, Image Science, Spectral Science, and Systems Engineering. You will also collaborate across MITRE, government, and industry to transform raw orbital data into operational advantage.

The selected candidate will be expected to:

Provide strategic and technical leadership as a trusted advisor to the sponsor and help shape the full scope of work for the projects tasks
Build and sustain strong relationships with Sponsor senior leadership, division leadership, branch chiefs, and government stakeholders across the mission space
Define and execute technical objectives based on sponsor priorities and mission outcomes, with an emphasis on areas where MITRE can deliver the greatest value through its technical depth and cross-cutting capabilities
Translate overall project strategy into clear, actionable outcomes, deliverables, and technical products
Identify and integrate relevant research and innovation efforts from across MITRE, including internal innovation programs, to strengthen project impact and advance sponsor objectives
Ensure the technical quality of products and recommendations by establishing clear team expectations aligned with division quality practices, conducting in-progress reviews, incorporating peer review, implementing effective knowledge management, and participating in regular program execution reviews
Partner with MITRE staff resourcing organizations to develop and execute a mission-focused staffing strategy for the project
Collaborate across MITRE and with sponsors to identify, assess, and inform operational trade space decisions for the NGA mission
Lead project administration activities, including financial tracking, project documentation, meeting coordination, status reporting, facility management, task tracking, and contributor expectation setting
Oversee staff management activities, including onboarding and access coordination for required systems, networks, collaboration environments, and classified facilities.
Collaborate across our work program with other PLs to ensure cohesive, well-aligned delivery

Basic Qualifications:

Typically requires a minimum of 12 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 10 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 7 years’ experience; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.
Degree in physics, applied mathematics, aerospace, software development for engineering/physical systems, acquisition, artificial intelligence, data science, imaging, cloud architecture or related disciplines and work experience with a strong technical background
Track record in achieving significant work program, sponsor, or organizational outcomes
Team builder with ability to work across MITRE bringing required staffing resources to bear
Identify, propose, and pursue partnerships with MITRE internally funded efforts (innovation program, PD/SI’s, strategic outcomes, etc.), as applicable to pursue groundbreaking capability advancements and delivery
Proficiency in DoD and IC space sponsors and their role in the development, acquisition, and operational lifecycle and the ability to work across to achieve higher level strategic objectives.
Experience with understanding & presenting technical studies to senior decision-makers to drive action and outcomes
Must have an active Top Secret/SCI U.S Government issued Security Clearance with the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI w/Poly U.S. Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.
This position requires a minimum of 5 days a week on-site

Preferred Qualifications:

Active TS/SCI clearance with a polygraph
Master’s or PhD with research experience in one of the above specified degree programs 
Domian knowledge of emerging and current sponsor related technology fields: Geospatial intelligence, AI / ML, Data Science, Image Processing / Computer Vision, various GIS data (SAR, HSI, Trajectories, etc.)
Knowledge of intelligence operations, the intelligence lifecycle, TCPED, and intelligence systems
Ability to mentor early-career staff, new task leaders, and encourage staff skill development
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex project components simultaneously
Experience advising the federal government on acquisition lifecycle activities (emphasizing software acquisitions), including SOW/SOO development, market research, acquisition planning, technical evaluations, source selection support, or adoption of innovative acquisition approaches
Understanding of space-related physics and engineering concepts, for example, orbital mechanics, satellite propagation, space-based ISR, satellite communications, space domain awareness, etc.
