, we are revolutionizing the consumer drone and gadget market in India. Our mission is to provide premium features without the premium price tag, empowering users to turn everyday moments into extraordinary adventures. We are a team of trailblazers looking for energetic individuals to help us soar to new horizons.

Website:
https://www.izicart.com/

What Are We Looking For?

We are looking for a System Engineer – UAV
with 2–5 years of hands-on experience in UAV/drone systems, system integration, testing, and troubleshooting
.
The candidate will be responsible for integrating and validating different UAV subsystems, including flight controllers, motors, ESCs, batteries, sensors, communication systems, payloads, and embedded electronics
. The ideal candidate should have a good understanding of UAV architecture and the ability to troubleshoot system-level technical issues.

Key Responsibilities

1. UAV System Integration
Support the integration of complete UAV systems and subsystems.
Integrate flight controllers, motors, ESCs, batteries, sensors, GPS, communication modules, payloads, and other electronic components
.
Ensure proper communication and interoperability between hardware and software components.
Perform system-level configuration and integration of UAV platforms.
Assist in identifying and resolving integration issues.

2. System Testing & Validation
Conduct functional, system-level, and field testing
of UAV platforms.
Prepare and execute system test plans and test cases.
Perform pre-flight and post-flight system checks.
Collect and analyze flight and system performance data.
Identify system-level failures and support corrective actions.
Validate UAV performance against defined technical requirements.

3. Flight Controller & UAV Configuration
Configure and calibrate flight controllers and related UAV systems.
Support PID tuning and flight parameter optimization
.
Configure sensors, GPS, telemetry, communication systems, and other peripherals.
Troubleshoot flight-control and system configuration issues.
Support flight testing and performance optimization.

4. Troubleshooting & Issue Resolution
Diagnose hardware, software, electrical, and communication-related issues at the system level.
Troubleshoot issues related to motors, ESCs, batteries, flight controllers, sensors, GPS, telemetry, and communication interfaces
.
Perform root-cause analysis of recurring system failures.
Work with Electronics, Embedded, Mechanical, and Software teams to resolve technical issues.
Maintain records of identified issues, troubleshooting activities, and resolutions.

5. System Requirements & Documentation
Support preparation and maintenance of system-level requirements and technical specifications.
Prepare system integration, test, and validation documentation.
Maintain test reports, issue logs, configuration records, and technical documentation.
Support preparation of system architecture and interface documentation.
Ensure proper documentation of system changes and configurations.

6. Cross-Functional Collaboration
Work closely with Mechanical, Electronics, Embedded, RF, Software, Manufacturing, and Quality teams
.
Coordinate with engineering teams during prototype development and system integration.
Provide technical inputs during design reviews and product development activities.
Support production teams during product testing and troubleshooting.
Communicate technical issues and progress to relevant stakeholders.

7. Field Testing & Product Support
Participate in UAV field trials and flight testing.
Support testing under different operating conditions and environments.
Monitor UAV performance during field operations.
Identify and report system-level issues observed during testing.
Support engineering teams in implementing improvements based on field-test results.

Required Skills

UAV/Drone System Architecture
UAV System Integration
Flight Controller Configuration
UAV Testing & Validation
Basic PID Tuning and Flight Optimization
Electronics & Electrical Fundamentals
Motors, ESCs, Batteries & Power Systems
Sensors & GPS Integration
RF/Telemetry & Communication Systems
Embedded Systems Fundamentals
Hardware & Software Integration
System Troubleshooting
Root Cause Analysis
Technical Documentation
Test Planning & Reporting
Basic Requirements Management

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electronics, Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics
, or a related field.
2–5 years of hands-on experience
in UAVs, drones, robotics, aerospace, embedded systems, or similar hardware products.
Practical experience in UAV assembly, integration, testing, and troubleshooting.
Experience working with flight controllers such as Pixhawk, Cube, or similar platforms
will be an advantage.
Familiarity with UAV communication protocols, telemetry systems, sensors, and GPS.
Experience with autonomous or semi-autonomous UAV systems will be an added advantage.
Experience in defense or industrial UAV applications will be an advantage.

jobs.description:
Description

This position is part of the Timberlands Science & Technology (S&T) organization and reports to the Remote Sensing Manager, part of the Advanced Forestry Systems platform.

The LiDAR/UAV Scientist at Weyerhaeuser is a member of the Remote Sensing team and partly responsible for the acquisition, processing, and analysis of airborne and close-range remote sensing data to support Timberlands business decisions. Supporting the acquisition of aerial LiDAR data for internal inventory programs is a core responsibility for the role. This role requires expertise in LiDAR, UAV operations, and digital photogrammetry, along with proficiency in remote sensing and geospatial technologies.

This is a hybrid in-office position (work in the office Tuesday-Thursday). The preferred location for this role is Centralia, WA. Will also consider candidates to work from Hot Springs (AR), New Bern (NC), Springfield (OR), Vancouver (WA).

Essential Job Functions:

Participate in acquisition and management of LiDAR, aerial imagery, and UAS data in collaboration with Technology and Timberlands teams.
Generate, process, and maintain remote sensing datasets and LiDAR-derived products with rigorous quality control.
Design and enhance decision support tools integrating multi-temporal and multi-spectral remotely sensed data (from active and passive sensors).
Apply remote sensing principles and develop analytical techniques to solve operational problems and improve data applications.
Develop advanced image and signal processing code for feature extraction, classification, and machine learning algorithms.
Support training, and expert input on UAS systems, LiDAR data, and remote sensing strategies.
Prepare and review technical reports, present findings, and support strategic planning with the RS unit manager and stakeholders.
Conduct scientific analyses by correlating remote sensing data with ground truth and modeled results, supporting company objectives through modeling and documentation.
Participate in the development of strategies related to LiDAR, UAV and Terrestrial sensor technology and data collection.
Field work and business travel are required. Driving safety vehicles in forest roads is considered.

Qualifications

Education and Experience Requirements:

MSc or PhD degree with 1+ years of experience in applied sciences such as forestry, Geomatics, natural resources, with a strong emphasis in GIS or Remote Sensing.
Experience in traditional machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision.
UAV experience in data collection is a plus.
Part 107 UAV license available or willing to obtain.
Knowledge and experience in the application of the principles of remote sensors, field checking and image processing, and interpretation of forest or natural resource management.
Experience in programming (Python, R), directly through a computer science degree program or from ancillary coursework to support another degree or professional activity.
Competency in the use of statistical tools (e.g., R), and an understanding of spatial statistics.
Proficient in remote sensing-GIS tools: ArcGIS, QT Modeler, QGIS. Other Skills and Attributes
Strong communication and interpersonal skills are essential.
Demonstrated ability to work on projects collaboratively as part of a team.

We sustainably manage forests and manufacture products that make the world a better place. We’re serious about safety, driven to achieve excellence, and proud of what we do. With multiple business lines in locations across North America, we offer a range of exciting career opportunities for smart, talented people who are passionate about making a difference.

BMD is Australia’s leading integrated engineering, construction and urban development business, with foundations built on the family values that underpin our unique, collaborative approach.Driven by a purpose of powering futures and creating enduring legacies through a commitment to collaboration, BMD is delivering infrastructure solutions that connect and transform communities. Support implementation of the ISMP and contribute to sustainability reporting and KPI achievement.
Prepare high‑quality environmental reporting for internal and external stakeholders.
Deliver environmental training, toolbox talks, and inductions.
Communicate proactively with the community, regulators, and the client regarding environmental matters.
Lead, mentor, and support a multidisciplinary environmental team.
Promote a positive, collaborative, and high‑performance culture.

Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or related field

Strong understanding of environmental legislation, best‑practice erosion and sediment control, and industry guidelines
Ability to build strong relationships with site teams, regulators, and stakeholders

Experience managing environmental approvals, incidents, audits, and reporting programs

jobs.title: Project Manager (Civil/Environmental Engineer)
jobs.description:
Project Manager – BINA Green Business Incubator

Senior Position | Mukalla, Hadramout, Yemen

Position: Project Manager (Civil/Environmental Engineer)
Duty Station: Mukalla, Hadramout, (Starting in Aden for 2-month orientation and planning, followed by frequent official travel to Aden and other project locations as required)
Reports to: Head of Programs or designated senior program lead
Announcement Period: 20 September – 1st October 2026
Contract: Full-time, project-based fixed-term contract (2 years)
About Action For Humanity

Action For Humanity (AFH) is an international humanitarian and development organization working with communities affected by crisis and poverty. In Yemen, AFH delivers humanitarian, recovery and development programming across sectors including livelihoods and economic recovery, health, WASH, food security, protection, education and other community-based interventions. AFH works with government institutions, universities, donors, civil society, the private sector and communities to deliver accountable, sustainable and locally relevant solutions.

Project and Role Background

The project is an Islamic Development Bank-funded green business incubator and entrepreneurship initiative to be established in Hadramout University with key local stakeholders. The project will combine a practical, environmentally responsible incubation facility with business-development services for youth, women, entrepreneurs, start-ups and micro and small enterprises.

The Project Manager will lead the project from technical preparation and construction/fit-out through operationalization and program delivery, ensuring the facility is safe, adaptable, cost-conscious, environmentally responsible and appropriate to the Yemeni context. The Project Manager is the senior focal point responsible for overall planning, technical leadership, delivery, quality, compliance and results. The role requires a strong engineer and manager who can connect civil works and green design with procurement, stakeholder coordination and the operational needs of a business incubator.

Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership and Delivery

Lead day-to-day implementation against approved scope, budget, schedule, results and donor requirements.
Maintain the implementation plan, milestone schedule, procurement plan, cash forecast, risk register and action tracker.
Coordinate Programs, Engineering, Operations, Procurement, Finance, MEAL and partners, and resolve implementation bottlenecks promptly.

Civil Engineering, Design and Construction

Lead and coordinate site assessments, design reviews, drawings, technical specifications, BOQs and construction schedules.
Ensure designs are durable, functional and adapted to Hadramout/Yemen, including heat, energy reliability, water efficiency, local materials, accessibility and maintenance costs.
Oversee construction, rehabilitation, fit-out and installation; monitor workmanship, materials, quantities, progress, variations and defects.
Coordinate inspections, testing, commissioning, handover, warranties, as-built documentation and defect follow-up.

Green Building and Environmental Management

Integrate practical green-building measures such as passive cooling/shading, energy and water efficiency, renewable-energy options, waste reduction, responsible materials and lifecycle-cost considerations.
Identify and manage environmental, social, health and safety risks during construction and operation.
Prioritize climate-resilient and locally maintainable solutions suitable for the Yemeni context.

Incubator Operational Readiness

Lead the transition from construction to a functioning incubator, including furniture, equipment, ICT, utilities, safety systems, maintenance plans and operating procedures.
Ensure the space supports training, co-working, mentoring, innovation, administration and inclusive access.
Work with enterprise-development colleagues to align the facility with incubation, mentoring, market-linkage and access-to-finance activities.

Procurement, Budget and Contract Oversight

Provide technical input to tender packages, specifications, bid evaluations, contractor/consultant selection and procurement tracking in line with AFH procedures.
Monitor expenditure, commitments, forecasts and variations; support value for money and disciplined change control.
Verify technical completion and quality before recommending certification/payment, subject to required independent checks and approvals.

Stakeholder and Donor Coordination

Coordinate with relevant donor representatives, Hadramout University, government counterparts, technical authorities, contractors, private-sector actors and other stakeholders.
Prepare technical meetings, field visits, presentations, action trackers and decision records, and represent the project when delegated.

MEAL, Reporting and Team Management

Work with MEAL to establish indicators, monitoring tools and evidence for infrastructure and program results.
Prepare high-quality technical and narrative inputs for donor reports, management updates and project reviews.
Maintain complete project records, including designs, approvals, inspection records, variations, progress evidence and handover files.
Supervise assigned staff and consultants and establish clear responsibilities, deadlines and performance follow-up.

Risk, Compliance and Safeguarding

Maintain an active risk register covering construction, environmental, safety, financial, procurement, schedule, stakeholder and operational risks.
Ensure compliance with AFH policies, applicable donor requirements, relevant Yemeni regulations, approved technical standards and contractual obligations.
Apply safeguarding, PSEA, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, conflict-of-interest and accountability requirements throughout implementation.
Qualifications and Experience

Education

Essential: Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering with strong civil/infrastructure background, or a closely related engineering field.
Preferred: Master’s degree in Civil/Environmental Engineering, Construction or Project Management, Sustainable/Green Building, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
Relevant professional certification in project management, green building, construction management, HSE or contract management is an advantage.

Experience

Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in civil/infrastructure, construction or engineering project management, including at least 3 years in a project leadership or senior coordination role.
Demonstrated experience delivering buildings, institutional facilities, training centers, incubators, innovation/enterprise spaces or comparable multi-use facilities.
Strong experience in design review, BOQs/specifications, tendering, contractor management, site supervision, quality control, variations, commissioning and handover.
Demonstrated experience integrating environmental sustainability, resource efficiency, climate resilience or green-building measures into infrastructure projects.
Experience with donor-funded projects, development organizations, development banks, universities or government institutions is highly desirable.
Experience in Yemen or comparable fragile/conflict-affected contexts is strongly preferred; knowledge of Hadramout is an advantage.
Exposure to entrepreneurship, MSMEs, innovation hubs or private-sector development is an advantage.
Mandatory Portfolio / Evidence of Work

Applicants must provide evidence of relevant previous work. The portfolio should briefly present 2–4 projects personally managed, designed, supervised or technically led.

For each project: location/client, candidate’s role, dates, scale, key technical features, sustainability/environmental features and the candidate’s contribution.
Relevant photographs, drawings, completion evidence, reference contacts or links may be included where permitted.
At least one example should demonstrate adaptation to local climate, resource constraints or a context comparable to Yemen.
Experience with incubators, innovation hubs, training centers, university facilities, green buildings or flexible multi-use spaces should be highlighted where available.
Required Competencies
Strong civil engineering judgment and ability to review drawings, BOQs, specifications and contractor proposals.
Understanding of green construction, passive design, energy/water efficiency, climate resilience and lifecycle costing.
Strong project planning, budget control, procurement, contract administration and risk-management skills.
Strong leadership, problem-solving, negotiation, reporting and stakeholder-management skills.
Professional fluency in Arabic and strong written and spoken English.
Strong computer literacy; familiarity with relevant engineering/design and project-management software is an advantage.
Duty Station and Travel

Based in Mukalla, Hadramout, with a strong field/site presence and frequent official travel to Aden for coordination with the Yemen Country Office. Additional project-related travel may be required.

FH may use a portfolio review, technical exercise, presentation, competency-based interview and reference checks during selection.

Equal Opportunity and Safeguarding

Action For Humanity is committed to fair and transparent recruitment, safeguarding and a respectful, inclusive workplace. Appointment is subject to satisfactory reference/background checks and compliance with AFH’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding, PSEA, anti-fraud, anti-corruption and conflict-of-interest requirements. AFH does not charge any costs for recruitment at any stage.

jobs.description:
Description

Senior Environmental Planner

Ready to Make a Difference?

ICF is seeking an Senior Environmental Planner to support our Mountain West planning team. ICF provides environmental planning, policy, permitting, and other services to clients. We prepare environmental impact statements and environmental assessments for complex and often controversial projects nationwide, including energy, transportation, and other infrastructure projects and regulatory programs. We manage environmental review processes that include consultation with regulatory agencies; public involvement; analysis of environmental, cultural, safety, socio-economic, and other impacts, and specification of measures to mitigate adverse impacts. Our clients include numerous federal, state, and international agencies and private companies.

Our Staff Work On The Most Current And Important Issues Facing The Nation Including Traditional And Renewable Energy Projects And Management Of Land Use, Water, Recreation, And Other Resources. Staff In This Position May Provide a Range Of Services Including

Federal, state, and local permitting and compliance for renewable and traditional energy, transmission, aviation, and other projects in compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and other regulations.
Federal agency headquarters environmental support, including NEPA compliance.
Technical services including biological surveys and studies, air quality analysis, noise impact assessments and other resource-related studies across a range of disciplines.

Why You Will Love Working Here

Quality of life: Flexible workplace arrangements, work-life balance
Investment of the community: Donation matching, volunteer opportunities
Investment in you: Tuition reimbursement, access to professional development resources, 401k matching, Employee Stock Purchase Plan
And many, many more (Ask your recruiter for more details!)

In this position you will be tasked with the following:

Planning and completing major project tasks related to the development and delivery of accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services (e.g., permitting, NEPA documents).
Organizing work on multiple projects and applying your academic and past work experience to a wide variety of complex projects.
Interacting with all levels of staff and clients, including experts in their fields of expertise.
Interfacing directly with key agencies and clients and help build and maintain great relationships.
This position trains, develops and may direct the work of junior staff.

What You Need To Have (minimum Qualifications)

Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent combination of education and experience in natural or physical science, public policy, economics, environmental management, or related subjects.
4+ years of environmental consulting experience (for government or private sector clients) with clients in the natural resources, energy, transportation, and related infrastructure and federal market sectors.

What We Would Like You To Have (preferred Experience)

Experience preparing NEPA documents and environmental permitting.
Experience supporting and serving on project management teams.
Experience with developing and maintaining project schedules, budgets, and writing proposals.

Professional Skills You Will Use

Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, MS Project, MS Teams).
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, including ability to prioritize and multi-task under strict deadlines.
Strong critical thinking skills and demonstrated ability to succeed with new and challenging tasks.
Understands task expectations and how tasks fit in the overall project.
Works collaboratively with project team and client to achieve established goals.
Organizes written work in a manner that is clear, easy to follow, and tailored for the intended audience.

We are the Environment & Planning Division. We are passionate about doing what’s right for our clients, our people, the communities where we live and work, and the environment. We are planners, scientists, program managers, communicators, economists, technologists, and strategists. We are collaborative, curious, and committed to excellence—these are qualities we value that make us who we are and inspire us to grow. If you perform well in a fast-paced, engaging and collaborative environment, and would like to work with a diverse team of industry professionals, we encourage you to learn more about ICF (www.icf.com) and consider applying to join our team.

This is an outstanding opportunity to work with talented and passionate individuals and to grow with a firm that believes in nurturing talent and developing long-term career success. ICF is a purpose driven company with a strong culture and underlying values that prize diversity, opportunity, equality, and respect. Our core values include Embracing Differences, and we seek candidates who are passionate about building a culture that encourages, embraces and hires dimensions of differences.

ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future.

We can only solve the world's toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re ready for more than a job, Trutech Wildlife Service offers a career with purpose.

Are you looking for a hands-on career, not just a job? Do you have experience in construction, roofing, insulation, or home improvement and want to put those skills to work in a stable, recession-resistant industry?

Trutech Wildlife Service specializes in wildlife management services for residential and commercial properties, providing humane wildlife removal, exclusion, and damage repair solutions nationwide. We help customers resolve wildlife-related concerns in safe, effective, and environmentally responsible ways while protecting homes, businesses, and communities.

This role is ideal for individuals with a background in construction, repair, or related trades who are committed to craftsmanship and accountability. You’ll play a critical role in preventing future wildlife intrusions by performing exclusion work, repairs, and remediation while maintaining high safety and quality standards.

Trutech Wildlife Service is a brand that invests in its people. If you are a driven professional who embraces our values and upholds our standards of excellence, you’ll find opportunities to succeed, grow, and advance within our organization.

Responsibilities

As a Wildlife Exclusion/Repair Service Technician
at Trutech Wildlife Service, you perform hands-on exclusion, repair, and remediation services for residential and commercial properties. You identify entry points, complete structural repairs, and implement humane wildlife prevention solutions while following safety, technical, and quality guidelines.

What Does a Day in the Life Look Like?

Perform interior and exterior property inspections, including roofs, attics, crawlspaces, and other confined spaces, to identify wildlife entry points and potential vulnerabilities.
Install preventative exclusion materials such as screens, chimney caps, vent covers, and other barriers to prevent wildlife access.
Complete minor repairs to roofs, siding, foundations, and other structural areas where wildlife may gain entry.
Safely remove wildlife using humane trapping and relocation techniques in accordance with company standards and regulations.
Maintain accurate documentation of services performed, materials used, and customer interactions.
Provide clear, detailed reports and review completed scopes of work with customers.
Collaborate with sales and customer service teams to ensure seamless and positive customer experience.
Follow up with customers to confirm satisfaction and address any additional concerns or recommendations.

What type of benefits will you receive?

Competitive hourly range: $20 - $20
Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.
401k with generous match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
6 Paid Holidays Annually!
PTO accrual based on tenure - 3 weeks beginning first full year!
Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250/year (federal max!) OR free tuition on approved programs through Purdue Global!!!
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities!
Supportive team environment with a focus on work-life balance.
Opportunities for career advancement within the Rollins Family of Brands!

Qualifications

What do you need to be successful?

High school diploma or equivalent; college degree is a plus
Valid driver’s license
Proven experience in construction, carpentry, roofing, or other related fields
Ability to work in the field independently
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Proficiency in using several types of software and applications

What does the work environment look like?

We go where the wildlife goes! Candidates must be physically capable of safely performing the following job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

Must be able to drive to various locations, often covering large territories.
Frequent walking, standing, and moving through diverse types of terrain, including uneven ground, stairs, roofs, and sometimes slippery or muddy areas.
Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions (extreme heat, extreme cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must have the ability to climb stairs and ladders safely.
Must be able to crouch, kneel, bend, and stretch frequently.
Capability to carry and use equipment necessary for inspections and minor control measures (Traps, ladders, inspection tools, etc).
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Clear verbal communication skills to interact effectively with clients and team members.

Join us in making a positive impact on nuisance wildlife management and become a part of our dedicated team today!

Trutech Wildlife Service is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.description:
Senior Business Development Manager, Biomass Supply

Location
: Houston, TX. Remote-friendly, strong preference for Texas or the Southeast. Frequent travel to supplier sites and deployment regions

The Company

Our client is a Series A climate technology company converting agricultural and forestry waste into biochar through mobile pyrolysis. The resulting carbon removal credits are registry-certified and sold to major corporate buyers, and through 2026 the company is deploying systems across partner sites in North America.

The Role

This role owns the company's feedstock supply. You'll identify, pitch, and close partnerships with businesses that generate dry biomass residuals, turning their waste streams into long-term supply and host-site agreements as the business expands from one facility to multiple sites.
You'll focus on feedstock sources including nut shellers (pecan in particular), sawmills, wood products manufacturers, and other woody waste generators. The goal is to secure reliable, high-quality feedstock ahead of new deployments, build lasting supplier relationships, and identify the regions and residual streams best suited to the company's growth.

Key Responsibilities

Build and manage a pipeline of feedstock suppliers across agricultural and forestry markets
Identify and qualify supply sites based on volume, material quality, moisture content, and logistics
Structure and negotiate long-term B2B supply and site-hosting agreements
Secure feedstock ahead of new facility and unit deployments
Serve as the primary relationship owner for supply partners from first conversation through deployment
Work with operations to plan site layouts, deployment timelines, and material handling
Track residual volumes, pricing, and competing uses across target regions
Build the supply development process and, as the business scales, help develop a regional team

Background:

5–8 years of business development, procurement, or sourcing experience in agriculture, forestry, wood products, or waste-to-value
Existing network among nut processors, sawmills, wood fiber buyers, or similar residual generators
Proven track record of structuring and closing B2B commercial agreements
Strong understanding of biomass residual streams, including material specs, seasonality, and logistics
Credibility with plant managers, operators, and agricultural or forestry businesses
Ability to pitch a new or unfamiliar solution and develop supply from the ground up
Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort operating in an early-stage environment
Willingness to travel frequently to supplier sites, facilities, and deployment regions
Valid driver's license and authorization to work in the U.S. without sponsorship

About Us

The Department of Environment and Climate Change's role is to protect the environment and human health through regulatory excellence, conservation, partnership, and promotion. To achieve this, we strive to develop legislation, regulations and policies, process notifications, applications, and approvals for regulated activities based on sound scientific knowledge and expertise.

Our goal is to educate, inspect and enforce to ensure compliance with legislation and regulations. We also proactively respond to environmental and human health risks and work to develop programs and deliver services to enhance protection in these areas.

About Our Opportunity

Reporting to the Manager of Drinking Water and Water Resources, the Environmental Data and GIS Innovation Lead will play a pivotal role in driving data-driven environmental solutions, spearheading improvements in how we collect, manage, report, and analyze critical environmental data. They will harness a suite of tools to build integrated solutions that streamline every step of the data lifecycle, including systems for environmental data management, geospatial mapping and field data collection, workflow automation, and dynamic reporting.

The Environmental Data and GIS Innovation Lead will also evaluate and document data workflows, contribute to data governance best practices, and manage essential databases and user systems to ensure high-quality, accessible information. This leadership role blends technical expertise, system innovation, and collaboration, working closely with environmental scientists, GIS specialists, and other stakeholders to transform data into actionable insights that drive impactful environmental decisions.

The Environmental Data and GIS Innovation Lead is a senior technical–strategic role that modernizes how Nova Scotia Environment and Climate Change collects, manages, and uses environmental and water resource data. Acting as a bridge between scientists, GIS specialists, and decision-makers, the role leads innovation in data systems, governance, and visualization—turning complex datasets into actionable insights that shape environmental policy and programs.

Primary Accountabilities

As the Environmental Data and GIS Innovation Lead, you will drive improvements in how environmental and water resources data are collected, managed, analyzed, and reported. You will develop tools, dashboards, and geospatial visualizations to support evidence-based decision-making while optimizing workflows using platforms such as WISKI, ArcGIS, and Microsoft Power Platform. This role also includes system administration, vendor coordination, and supporting change management through user engagement and testing. You will ensure data integrity through governance and QA/QC practices, provide training to users, and promote strategic collaboration across teams and departments. By fostering a culture of innovation and continuous improvement, you’ll help advance the department’s data capabilities and GIS strategies to inform environmental policy and programs. You may also be required to perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications And Experience

A bachelor’s degree in a related field (e.g. environmental science, water resources, geography, computer science) plus six (6) years of related experience; or an equivalent combination of training and experience.

Experience

You also possess the following:

Experience working with environmental and water resources datasets.
Proven experience improving data workflows and managing databases/systems (e.g., user access, performance, contracts/agreements).
Experience acting as a liaison between business users and software vendors, including support for change management and user testing.

Knowledge

Strong working knowledge of:
Environmental data management systems
ESRI ArcGIS platform (ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Experience Builder, Survey 123, etc.)

Microsoft Power Platform, Microsoft SharePoint, and Microsoft Teams
Knowledge of data governance principles and experience developing or implementing data governance frameworks.
Understanding of quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) practices for environmental data.

Capabilities

Skilled in designing tools, dashboards, and visualizations for data reporting and analysis.
Strong analytical, independent learning and problem-solving skills, with a continuous improvement mindset and the ability to identify innovative solutions using existing tools.
Effective communicator and facilitator with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Asset Qualifications

Master’s degree in a relevant field.
Experience with scripting or programming languages (e.g., Python, R, M, SQL, Arcade).
Experience leading user engagement and supporting data strategies in technical settings.
Familiarity with data science standards and practices at the national and international level.
Experience working in a government or regulatory setting.

Build and maintain services on Azure, using Container Apps and Service Bus to support scalable, event-driven data processing.

Share findings and technical approaches with stakeholders across regions and functions.

Strong hands-on experience with Python and numerical/data analysis libraries such as NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, or Polars.
Practical experience developing and deploying Dockerized applications.
Working knowledge of machine learning concepts and related statistical methods.
Proficiency in SQL for querying and managing large datasets.
Experience with time-series analysis and spatial interpolation techniques.

Familiarity with Microsoft SQL Server, PostGIS, or geostatistics is an advantage.

jobs.title: CIRES/ CSL Temporary Researcher, Lidar Scientist
jobs.description:
Summary

Job Summary

The Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences (CIRES) at the University of Colorado Boulder encourages applications for a Temporary Researcher within NOAA’s Chemical Sciences Laboratory (CSL). The successful candidate will join the Atmospheric Remote Sensing
program. You will work alongside a collaborative team of federal and university scientists. The primary focus is the post-processing and analysis of Doppler lidar data
. This data originates from key field campaigns. The work directly advances research in boundary layer dynamics, turbulence, and air quality.

Our group develops and deploys world-class active remote sensing instruments. We operate across airborne, ship-based, and mobile ground platforms. We require an expert with a strong background in atmospheric remote sensing or physics
. Deep expertise in active remote sensing architectures and boundary layer workflows is essential. A Ph.D. in Physics or a related field
is required. CSL relies on a highly collaborative work culture. We seek a candidate who actively subscribes to this team philosophy.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Who We Are

At CIRES , more than 900 people work to understand the dynamic Earth system, including people’s relationship with the planet. An institute at the University of Colorado Boulder, we have partnered with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) since 1967. Our areas of expertise include weather and climate, wildfire and water, changes at Earth’s poles, air quality and atmospheric chemistry, water resources, solid Earth sciences, and more. Our researchers work in 10 CU Boulder departments and eight NOAA laboratories and centers.

NOAA's Chemical Sciences Laboratory (CSL) is a world leader in atmospheric chemistry and composition, developing and deploying advanced technologies to ensure NOAA remains at the forefront in protecting lives, property, and livelihoods of the American people. https://csl.noaa.gov/

Responsibilities

What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

Analyze and interpret lidar measurements and use data for various boundary layer research studies including air quality, wildfires, and climate, as well as measurement studies designed to inform numerical model improvement efforts.
Participate in the planning of group short- and long-term research strategies.
Opportunities exist to actively participate in field campaigns; specifically, deploy the Doppler and/or ozone lidar systems for various projects, help to design and test optimal measurement strategies, and monitor instrument performance.

What You Should Know

This appointment is not eligible for vacation leave, holidays, annual merit pay increases, nor employee health, retirement, or related benefits, except those required by law.
This appointment will accrue 0.034 hours of sick leave for every hour worked.
The hours for this position may vary and are not guaranteed.
This temporary position cannot extend past a maximum of 12 months.
The targeted start date for the appointment is October 1, 2026.
This position will be rostered in CIRES at the University of Colorado Boulder but will be physically situated in the David Skaggs Research Center, 325 Broadway, Boulder, CO 80305, a federal campus.
If you are the selected finalist you will be required to pass a federal laboratory background clearance for site access. Non-US citizens without green cards may have limited building access, and may require an escort in the building.
Contact Michael Zucker (michael.zucker@colorado.edu) with any questions.
This position can accommodate a hybrid work modality.

What We Can Offer

The hourly rate for this position ranges from $48.56 - $64.42 per hour. Salary is commensurate with education and experience.

Benefits

Temporary positions at the University of Colorado are not benefits-eligible, however, all positions are eligible for paid sick leave .

Be Statements

Be creative. Be talented. Be Boulder.

What We Require

A Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, meteorology, atmospheric science, environmental engineering, or a closely related field.
Experience in experimental physical/atmospheric sciences.
Experience in data analysis and programming (such as MATLAB, IDL, or other image visualization software).

What You Will Need

Demonstrated ability to perform boundary layer research and publish in peer-reviewed journals.
The ability to work in a team and participate in the development of original research projects.

What We Would Like You To Have

Experience with ozone and/or Doppler lidars
Experience working with lidar data
Experience coding in MATLAB.
A record demonstrating the ability to communicate science through publication or conference presentations.
Specific examples of experimental physical sciences experience that are desired include the following:
Participate in field measurements.
Analyze complex data sets.
Troubleshooting and resolving problems with instrumentation.
Ability to work in a collaborative environment with a diverse group of scientists.
Commitment to supporting an inclusive laboratory.
Ability to work well in teams, be determined and meet deadlines.

Special Instructions

To Apply, Please Submit The Following Materials

Resume/CV.
If you are identified as a finalist, the search committee will request one letter recommendation at a later time.

If you are selected as the finalist, your degree will be verified by the CU Boulder Campus Human Resources department using an approved online vendor. If your degree was obtained outside of the United States, please submit a translated version as an optional attachment.

Please apply by September 23, 2026
to be considered for this position.

Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For consideration, please apply through CU Boulder Jobs .

jobs.title: Wetland Scientist
jobs.description:
What We're Looking For

At HNTB, you can create a career that is meaningful to you while building communities that matter to all of us. For more than a century, we have been delivering solutions for some of the largest, most complex infrastructure projects across the country. With our historic growth, it is an exciting time to join our team of employee-owners.

This opportunity entails being responsible for applying the principles and theories of geology, hydrology, chemistry, biology or other related sciences to analyze the potential effects a project may have on the environment and/or the potential effects the environment may have on the design and construction of a project. Participates in moderate to complex projects or all levels of project/program difficulty and/or may be responsible for an assigned phase of a project or program.

As a member of HNTB's wetland team, you'll have the opportunity to work on meaningful projects while collaborating with a diverse group of wetland scientists, planners, and engineers on a wide range of transportation and infrastructure projects. The Scientist III leads wetland delineations, ecological field studies, environmental permitting, mitigation planning, and compliance efforts, while providing technical guidance to project teams. This role offers opportunities to expand technical expertise and take on increasing leadership responsibilities while contributing to some of the region's most complex and impactful infrastructure projects.

What You'll Do

Conducts research, gathers scientific information and data, and leads field investigations among other supporting activities.
Determines or develops best methodology and technical approaches for conducting analysis in field work; sets up test equipment as necessary to obtain scientific data.
Using established prescribed templates, prepares data analysis, modeling, written reports, maps, etc. as appropriate to support findings as it pertains to the natural or man-made environment in the study area.
Reviews and evaluates technical reports and plans of scientific aspects of proposed projects for the environmental review of projects including permitting, and development of mitigation plans.
Examines and evaluates present and future potential environmental science effects relating to the planning, design, and construction of proposed projects.
Serves as task lead or principal author in the preparation of reports, graphs, and diagrams on scientific aspects relating to specific projects.
Provides technical support to project managers as situations arise during the construction of project that require scientific assistance.
Supports the marketing efforts as assigned.
Schedules of new and on-going projects.
Prepares permits for public and private clients with respect to acquisition and compliance for wetland impacts, bridge construction, and/or threatened/endangered species.
Assists in organizing, preparation of public meetings.
Attends various meetings with clients, other engineering firms, and staff.
Performs other duties as assigned.

What You'll Need

Bachelor's degree in Geology, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, Archeology, Anthropology or related field and 4 years relevant experience, or
Master's Degree in Geology, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, Archeology, Anthropology or related field and 3 years of relevant experience

What You'll Bring

Experience leading wetland delineations, ecological field studies, environmental permitting efforts, and natural resource assessments for transportation or infrastructure projects.
Strong working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including the Clean Water Act, Massachusetts Wetlands Protection Act, and other applicable environmental permitting requirements.
Experience identifying wetland vegetation, soils, and hydrology; interpreting field findings; and providing technical recommendations in accordance with applicable guidance and methodologies.
Ability to independently collect, analyze, and interpret environmental data and prepare technical reports, permit applications, environmental assessments, and regulatory correspondence.
Experience coordinating and leading field investigations while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary project teams.
Ability to research scientific literature, evaluate complex environmental issues, and apply technical findings to permitting and project development challenges.
Experience supporting agency coordination and responding to regulatory comments and information requests.
Ability and willingness to perform fieldwork in various weather conditions and terrain.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.

What We Prefer

Approximately 3+ years of experience conducting wetland and natural resource assessments, environmental permitting, and regulatory coordination.
Experience leading wetland delineations and preparing complex permitting packages throughout Massachusetts and New England.
Familiarity working with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, MassDEP, conservation commissions, and other regulatory agencies.
Experience supporting transportation, transit, bridge, railroad, resiliency, or other infrastructure projects.
Knowledge of wetland mitigation planning, restoration design, monitoring, and adaptive management strategies.
Experience with GIS software, including ArcGIS Pro, field data collection applications, and spatial analysis tools.
Strong technical writing, communication, and organizational skills
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), Wetland Professional in Training (WPIT), Certified Ecologist, or other relevant professional certification is a plus.

General Notes

The duration of this assignment is 15-months from the date of hire. Potential for renewal based on job performance, progress towards research goals, and available funding.

This position will be based in Kingsville, Texas, as well as Brackenridge Field Laboratory, which is located off-campus in Austin, Texas.

Purpose

The Invasive Ecology Lab at UT Austin’s Brackenridge Field Laboratory is looking to recruit a motivated and resourceful field research assistant to assist with field research into invasive Pasture Mealybugs in South Texas. The study goal is to document the ecology and phenology of Pasture Mealybugs and conduct surveys of mealybugs and their parasitoids on native grasses and other plants.

Responsibilities

Participate in field studies as directed by research scientists. This includes field surveys of Pasture Mealybug (PMB) abundance on grasses and other plants in quadrats and transects, and documenting PMB damage to different plant tissues. Estimate litter densities and collect soil samples. Follow protocols to determine the monthly abundance of life-stages and spatial patterns of PMB distributions.
Collect and identify plant specimens using dichotomous keys, focused on grasses. Collect, curate and process mealybug samples to send for identification. Maintain living mealybugs in insect containers to collect their parasitoids. Use microscope to measure or identify samples.
Collect data from weather stations, soil moisture sensors, GPS and other field equipment.
Keep detailed records in field notebooks and transcribe to Box. Manage data collection and curation from the field and lab and administer its input and management in online databases. Analyze and report summary statistics.
Perform workflow planning, submit weekly progress reports and work plans. Attend monthly meetings at BFL, Austin, as needed. Interact professionally with landowners and ranch management team.
Perform administrative tasks, materials and equipment preparation and purchases, specimen handling and shipping, and equipment and vehicle maintenance and cleaning.
Implement safety plans for field and lab work.

Required Qualifications

BS degree in a biological science, with relevant experience.
Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

Minimum of one year field research experience.
Passion for natural history studies.
MS degree in ecology.
Experience with field ecological studies and surveys of plant and insect communities.
Experience with fieldwork in South Texas.
Experience with rearing and maintaining insects.
Ability to identify plants to species level and insects to order or family level.
Field safety awareness and commitment to safety.
Experience with data management, data quality checks, and summary statistics.
Demonstrated ability to perform as a member of a dynamic research team.
Excellent communication skills: listening, written and verbal.
Self-motivated and goal-oriented mindset.
Effective problem-solving skills in a dynamic environment.

Driving Required

This job requires a class "C" operator's driver's license. The applicant selected must provide a current three year driving record from the current state of residence. If not currently a Texas resident, a Texas driver's license must be obtained within 30 days of becoming a Texas resident. Employees who are required to have a CDL are subject to drug and alcohol testing (pre-employment, post-accident, reasonable suspicion, random, return-to-duty, and follow-up drug and alcohol testing).

$47,000 + depending on qualifications and experience

Working Conditions

Exposure to all weather conditions
Ability to work outside in the summer
Outdoor work along at remote field sites
Exposure to insect bites/stings
Ability to drive up to 8 hours in a day
May require working with hazardous equipment or materials with appropriate PPE
May work around chemical fumes
Lifting and moving

Work Shift

Incumbent will provide their own accommodation at Kingsville or close to the study site.
Some data entry and management work may be assigned for offsite/home.
UT vehicle will be provided at the ranch study site for field work.
Travel expenses to meetings in Austin will be covered separately.
Depending on study needs set by the study leader, this may be 4x10 or 5x8 hour workdays.
Occasional work on weekends and holidays required.

Company Description
Skycraft UAV specialises in professional property marketing content across Yorkshire, helping estate agents and property developers present homes and sites in ways that attract attention and drive buyer interest online. jobs.description:
What We're Looking For

At HNTB, you can create a career that is meaningful to you while building communities that matter to all of us. For more than a century, we have been delivering solutions for some of the largest, most complex infrastructure projects across the country. With our historic growth, it is an exciting time to join our team of employee-owners.

This opportunity entails being responsible for applying the principles and theories of geology, hydrology, chemistry, biology or other related sciences to analyze the potential effects a project may have on the environment and/or the potential effects the environment may have on the design and construction of a project. Participates in moderate to complex projects or all levels of project/program difficulty and/or may be responsible for an assigned phase of a project or program.

As a member of HNTB's wetland team, you'll have the opportunity to work on meaningful projects while collaborating with a diverse group of wetland scientists, planners, and engineers on a wide range of transportation and infrastructure projects. The Scientist III leads wetland delineations, ecological field studies, environmental permitting, mitigation planning, and compliance efforts, while providing technical guidance to project teams. This role offers opportunities to expand technical expertise and take on increasing leadership responsibilities while contributing to some of the region's most complex and impactful infrastructure projects.

What You'll Do

Conducts research, gathers scientific information and data, and leads field investigations among other supporting activities.
Determines or develops best methodology and technical approaches for conducting analysis in field work; sets up test equipment as necessary to obtain scientific data.
Using established prescribed templates, prepares data analysis, modeling, written reports, maps, etc. as appropriate to support findings as it pertains to the natural or man-made environment in the study area.
Reviews and evaluates technical reports and plans of scientific aspects of proposed projects for the environmental review of projects including permitting, and development of mitigation plans.
Examines and evaluates present and future potential environmental science effects relating to the planning, design, and construction of proposed projects.
Serves as task lead or principal author in the preparation of reports, graphs, and diagrams on scientific aspects relating to specific projects.
Provides technical support to project managers as situations arise during the construction of project that require scientific assistance.
Supports the marketing efforts as assigned.
Schedules of new and on-going projects.
Prepares permits for public and private clients with respect to acquisition and compliance for wetland impacts, bridge construction, and/or threatened/endangered species.
Assists in organizing, preparation of public meetings.
Attends various meetings with clients, other engineering firms, and staff.
Performs other duties as assigned.

What You'll Need

Bachelor's degree in Geology, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, Archeology, Anthropology or related field and 4 years relevant experience, or
Master's Degree in Geology, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, Archeology, Anthropology or related field and 3 years of relevant experience

What You'll Bring

Experience leading wetland delineations, ecological field studies, environmental permitting efforts, and natural resource assessments for transportation or infrastructure projects.
Strong working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including the Clean Water Act, Massachusetts Wetlands Protection Act, and other applicable environmental permitting requirements.
Experience identifying wetland vegetation, soils, and hydrology; interpreting field findings; and providing technical recommendations in accordance with applicable guidance and methodologies.
Ability to independently collect, analyze, and interpret environmental data and prepare technical reports, permit applications, environmental assessments, and regulatory correspondence.
Experience coordinating and leading field investigations while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary project teams.
Ability to research scientific literature, evaluate complex environmental issues, and apply technical findings to permitting and project development challenges.
Experience supporting agency coordination and responding to regulatory comments and information requests.
Ability and willingness to perform fieldwork in various weather conditions and terrain.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.

What We Prefer

Approximately 3+ years of experience conducting wetland and natural resource assessments, environmental permitting, and regulatory coordination.
Experience leading wetland delineations and preparing complex permitting packages throughout Massachusetts and New England.
Familiarity working with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, MassDEP, conservation commissions, and other regulatory agencies.
Experience supporting transportation, transit, bridge, railroad, resiliency, or other infrastructure projects.
Knowledge of wetland mitigation planning, restoration design, monitoring, and adaptive management strategies.
Experience with GIS software, including ArcGIS Pro, field data collection applications, and spatial analysis tools.
Strong technical writing, communication, and organizational skills
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), Wetland Professional in Training (WPIT), Certified Ecologist, or other relevant professional certification is a plus.

jobs.title: Senior Civil/Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
At Salas O’Brien, we tell our clients that we’re engineered for impact. This passion for making a difference applies just as much to our team as it does to our projects. That’s why we’re committed to living our values every day: inspiring, achieving, and connecting as shared owners of our success with a focus on a sustainable future.

Building for the long-term means that all our team members can expect to work on amazing projects with a people-first approach to problem solving. It also means that each member of our team has truly limitless potential to build a unique, meaningful, and high-impact career—and they’ll receive great total rewards along the way.

About Us

Founded in 1975, Salas O’Brien is an employee-owned engineering and professional services firm dedicated to making a positive impact for our clients, our team, and the world. We recognize that tomorrow’s requirements are today’s opportunities, and we are committed to designing lasting solutions for pressing challenges.

We work across a variety of industries providing integrated engineering and consulting services. Our specialized experience includes design for data centers, healthcare, science and technology, high-rise buildings, clean energy, education, and other building types as well as structural and building sciences, infrastructure asset management, advanced robotics, and more.

Our technical expertise is complemented by an exceptional team of business development, human resources, finance and accounting, information technology, and marketing professionals, all of whom play a key role in bringing our commitments to life every day.

Job Summary

The Senior Civil/Environmental Engineer functions as the overall technical lead for the Fed-Florida Business Unit projects. Technical duties in civil and environmental engineering require adaptability and versatility. Examples of technical work to be performed include civil site design (greenfield and retrofit); water resource management planning, design and permitting; flat infrastructure design including utility (gravity and pressure systems) and roadway design; environmental assessments and permitting; minor structural (retaining wall and equipment foundations/pedestals) design.

Specific engineering tasks include but are not limited to developing design engineering documents (plans, specifications and calculations) for facility maintenance and repair projects and new construction. In support of the work, engineers will perform detailed cost analyses and material take-offs of a variety of building types and site infrastructure throughout the US and other countries and perform construction management for ongoing construction efforts.

This position operationally reports to the Director of Civil and Environmental Design Operations.

Technical Responsibilities (85-90%):

Perform project direct billable functions and responsibilities to maintain a personal utilization rate of 85%-90%.
Responsible for the overall technical quality of assigned projects to ensure design compliance to meet SOW requirements and all applicable codes and standards.
Oversees discipline-specific personnel and technical execution of design.
Responsible for performing engineering tasks such as site design, permitting, assessments, and construction management.
Adheres to Project Management Plans (PMP) and Quality Control (QC) programs as assigned but does not change them without approval.
May be assigned as Engineer of Record (EOR) and/or Design Lead.
Participates in Fed-Florida Quality Control Program providing final approval of all Civil and Environmental work products, performing Chief Engineer responsibilities, and/or performing Design Manager responsibilities when assigned (reference "Project Quality Control Policies and Processes").
Ensure adherence to Fed-Florida’s quality control standards, including pass-through services/consulting.

Business Development Responsibilities (10-15%)

Tactical business development – Support proposal narrative, assumptions, and exclusions writing and pricing efforts as assigned. Review RFP/RFQ/SOW as well as pre-bid drawings and specifications to determine resource requirements and risk/benefit potential for each assigned proposal opportunity.
Strategic business development – Support the Director in cultivating and maintaining Fed-Florida’s strategic growth targets and growth areas as requested.
Oversee design-build coordination for civil and environmental scope of work on assigned proposals. Coordinate subcontractor services that will be necessary or could impact the civil and environmental scope of work. Ensure the GC Prime has sufficient technical input to competitively price their means-methods to construct the project.
Coordinate with other design disciplines to ensure related scopes have adequate level of effort with minimal redundancies on assigned proposals.
Participate in go/no-go decisions, oral presentations, capture management, technical approach narratives, qualification packages, elevator pitches, industry days, and conferences as requested.
As requested, identify/suggest opportunity-specific teammates, subcontractors (geotechnical, survey, SUE, structural, hazmat sampling, biological, cultural resources), hardware, software, training, badging, certifications, licenses, safety and travel needs that are likely to be required to perform the civil and environmental scope of work. Clarify scope of services to clearly explain Fed-Florida’s understanding of the civil and environmental scope of work through clarifications, assumptions, and exclusions.

Operational Responsibilities (5-10%)

Assists the Director of Civil and Environmental Engineering in specialized projects to advance the growth of Fed-Florida. These tasks may include but are not limited to mentoring interns/new hires, providing input for process improvements, assisting in the development of our continuously growing training program.

Qualifications

BS Civil Engineering degree required from an ABET-accredited program
8+ years of professional Civil Engineering experience
PE Certification
Proficient in Microsoft 365 applications
Must have working knowledge of the ASCE, AWWA, FDEP, ICC, ASTM, and UFC codes; with a preference for knowledge of the FBC, IBC, USGBC LEED and AFMAN/SSMAN requirements.
Working knowledge of FDEP regulations and Florida Water Management District requirements is highly preferred.
Experience with Civil3D, AutoCAD, Revit, Bluebeam Revu, or other modeling/drafting software is highly preferred.

Additional Eligibility Qualifications

Valid/Unrestricted driver’s license

Work Authorization/Security Clearance

Must be a US Citizen for Security Clearance requirements.
Active/Interim or ability to obtain Secret Security Clearance.

Location: Merritt Island, FL/Bethesda, MD

Travel

Job Overview

Are you passionate about the environment, love working outdoors, and have a background in air, noise and water environmental technician work? We are seeking a talented and self-motivated Field Environmental Technician to join our team. This project contract role offers a unique opportunity to work in the field and contribute to the preservation and sustainability of our natural resources.
Field Environmental Technician Responsibilities & Duties
Core role: Conduct field work to collect environmental data, including: Establishment, operation, management of various air quality monitoring networks including: fine particulates, dust fallout; trace gas pollutants; meteorology etc. Undertaking day and night-time noise surveys with sound level meters. Environmental monitoring services may be expanded to include surface/ground water and soil sampling etc. Gathering of accurate environmental data and physical samples from field sites to support compliance monitoring and research. Use scientific equipment to record environmental parameters including but not limited to: Various hand held environmental monitors, sound level monitors, passive badge samplers, SANS 1137 dust fallout monitors, GPS, calibration equipment, fine particulate monitors, etc. Assist in the planning and execution of environmental monitoring projects.
Work Environment: Mix of outdoor fieldwork in varying weather conditions and at various times of the day (i.e. included day and night-time surveys) and indoor office or lab work for reporting. This position requires extensive travel away from the office (i.e. >50% of the time) as is primarily a fieldwork position and thus the candidate must be willing and able to travel based on ATB’s needs.
Sample collection and equipment care: Set up, operate, and calibrate field testing instruments and monitoring devices in and laboratory and field environment. Gathering of air, noise, dust samples using specialized scientific equipment. Sample collections may be expended into soil, surface water, groundwater fields.
Data Tracking: Maintain up-to-date records of field activities, results, accurate chain-of-custody documentation, field logs, and photo logs. Communicate findings to team members, clients, and stakeholders.
Health and safety : Comply with all health and safety regulations and procedures typical of mining and industrial manufacturing market sector clients. Follow strict health protocols and wear required personal protective equipment (PPE). Examine project areas for health and safety risks to allow for safe working in the field. The employee will often be required to work alone in the field and during the day and night and thus a good grip on safety procedures and following safety protocols is critical.

Field Environmental Technician Qualifications & Skills
1-2+ years of experience as an air, dust, noise environmental field technician or in a related role. Previous fieldwork or internship experience in environmental monitoring or related areas
Basic knowledge and understanding of environmental regulations and compliance practices
Proficiency in using environmental testing and sampling equipment for air, noise, dust (as a minimum). Additional experience in water and soil equipment advantageous

The work is primarily concerned with wildlife damage management (WDM) research relating to the assessment, reduction, and/or elimination of problems associated with wild and/or feral swine in urban, suburban, and rural environments.

Qualifications

Applicants must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of the announcement, including specialized experience and/or education, as defined below. BASIC REQUIREMENT: Degree: biological science that included: At least 9 semester hours in such wildlife subjects as mammalogy, ornithology, animal ecology, wildlife management, or research courses in the field of wildlife biology; and At least 12 semester hours in zoology in such subjects as general zoology, invertebrate zoology, vertebrate zoology, comparative anatomy, physiology, genetics, ecology, cellular biology, parasitology, entomology, or research courses in such subjects (Excess courses in wildlife biology may be used to meet the zoology requirements where appropriate.); and At least 9 semester hours in botany or the related plant sciences. OR Combination of education and experience: equivalent to a major in biological science (i.e., at least 30 semester hours), with at least 9 semester hours in wildlife subjects, 12 semester hours in zoology, and 9 semester hours in botany or related plant science, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In addition to the basic requirement applicants must also possess: FOR THE GS-09 LEVEL: Applicants must have one year of specialized experience (equivalent to the GS-9 level) that may have been obtained in the private or public (local, county, state, Federal) sectors which demonstrates: Working knowledge and experience related to a variety of technical procedures used in wildlife biology including animal capture, restraint, marking, and transport; collection and preservation of biological data and samples; chemical immobilization; and animal euthanasia and necropsy. Ability to gather, organize, and analyze data using techniques and technologies such as telemetry, GPS, GIS, web-based systems for data entry, app development for data entry, and administrative processes, wildlife population census and surveys, and wildlife monitoring and surveillance. Good Laboratory Practices training and experience for evaluating new pesticides for feral ungulates. Experience leading research teams in remote, sometimes dangerous, field settings for data collection activities. Proficiency in evaluating the risks of foreign animal diseases from feral ungulates to domestic livestock. Background in handling feral swine and deer, attaching GPS collars and ear tags, and monitoring their movements. OR 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree or master's or equivalent graduate degree in one of the following degree fields: Wildlife Biology, Wildlife Ecology, or Wildlife Management or closely related field. Equivalent combinations of education and experience are qualifying for this grade level. TRANSCRIPTS are required if: This position requires specific coursework or a degree in a specific field to be basically qualified. You are qualifying for the position based on education. You are qualifying for this position based on a combination of experience and education. This education must have been successfully completed and obtained from an accredited school, college, or university. COMBINATION OF EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE AT THE GS-09 GRADE LEVEL: Applicants may have combinations of successfully completed education and specialized experience to meet total qualification requirements. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent to qualify for that grade level. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Major Duties

The duties described are for the full-performance level. At developmental grade levels, assignments will be of more limited scope, performed with less independence and limited complexity. The duties may include, but are not limited to:Performs a variety of technical procedures including capture, restraint, chemical immobilization, marking, transport, euthanasia, and/or necropsy of wild ungulates.Conducts research design and data collection in field and pen settings.Conducts statistical analysis of experimental data, field and observational data, animal movement data, disease data, and camera data.Recommends research areas to supervisor, represents the program on committees and at meetings, presents to cooperators, stakeholders, and the public, and prepares written reports and peer-reviewed publications.Operates field equipment such as off-road vehicles, 4x4 trucks, trucks and trailers, firearms, remote cameras, cellular traps, and handheld data collection devices.Required to take extensive and recurrent training on wildlife damage/disease recognition, control methods, and techniques; monitoring and surveillance procedures; emergency response; and other training related to technical aspects of the job.Supports Wildlife Services’ (WS) safety program and procedures through participation in meetings, inspections, safety-related training, and implementation of safety requirements and protocols. Identifies safety-related opportunities and challenges.Assists other WS employees as requested and may assist in training new WS personnel. May be asked to provide technical direction and/or guidance to lower graded employees.May be responsible for procuring equipment and supplies necessary to conduct field activities and may be asked to complete other duties as assigned.May assist with research projects to increase knowledge of wildlife ecology and to develop or improve methods to reduce the risks of damage to resources or disease transmission to domestic animals and humans.Responsible for collecting, storing, and transporting biological data and samples; conducting telemetry; using Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and Global Positioning Systems (GPS) for surveys, surveillance, and data analysis.

Drogo Drones is looking for a Type Certification Engineer with experience or strong knowledge of UAV/drone certification, regulatory compliance, technical documentation, and testing processes.

•Manage and support UAS Type Certification activities in accordance with applicable DGCA requirements and certification standards.
