Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step into Your New Role

The Kleinfelder Los Angeles Area is seeking to fill a position of an Environmental Professional to support client needs
. The candidate will oversee and be directly involved in executing aboveground and underground storage tank (AST / UST) compliance for local transportation infrastructure projects. We are looking for someone with interest in providing quality technical field and documentation support and partnering closely with our clients. The position will be based in Los Angeles, CA.

The ideal candidate will be expected to:

Utilize their skills and experience to contribute to programmatic compliance projects.
Lead and perform field and desktop tasks (technical and non-technical) and independent analysis.
Provide technical quality oversight related to AST and USTs.
Develop accurate and complete documentation to support facility compliance.
Support with other environmental tasks, as requested.

Technical Skills:

Understanding of AST / UST fuel / petroleum storage tank components and systems (i.e., Healy, Bravo, Veeder Root, etc.).
Consulting / permitting / regulatory compliance experience in California, particularly with local CUPA agencies, SCAQMD, CARB, and Water Board.
Act as a Designated Operator if needed, including preparation and delivery of training as well as inspections and documentation
Working knowledge of Fire Code, NFPA, APSA, STI as it applies to fuel tanks.
Understanding of tank documentation requirements for Hazardous Materials Business Plans (HMBP) / California Environmental Reporting System (CERS).
Oversight of tank subconsultants regarding installation, modification, removal, operation, testing, and inspection.
Understanding of proper documentation required for USTs for compliance with Water Board and CUPAs.
Knowledge of Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure.
Ability to read and understand tank design drawings.

Project Management:

Oversee multiple projects simultaneously and ensure quality is achieved on project deliverables.
Coordination of testing (i.e., SB989, monitoring certification) and repairs of tank systems with clients and enforcement agencies.
Contractor oversight.
Organizational skills to ensure proper consulting of priorities to clients.

Experience:

4 - 8 years of directly related technical experience

Certification / Registration:

STI SP-001 Aboveground Tank System Inspector Certification
ICC Designated Operator
ICC Service Technician a plus
40-hour HAZWOPER a plus

Must have a positive work attitude and ability to work safely and efficiently when managing multiple tasks
Ability to work independently as an integral team member, using knowledge of industry and/or professional guidelines and protocols to accomplish goals and objectives and solve problems of diverse scope
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Excellent knowledge of MS Office, Including Word, Excel, and Power Point preferred
Position will require the candidate to adhere to work assignments/schedules, be self-motivated, organized and have a keen sense of detail.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of experience and education

jobs.title: Senior Director, Environmental Compliance
jobs.description:
Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country’s largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

The Senior Director of Environmental Compliance is responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight of Veolia Water New Jersey’s (VWNJ) environmental compliance programs, ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, in alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities, while advancing public health protection, environmental stewardship, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. This position provides executive oversight of all environmental compliance activities related to air, drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, waste management, hazardous materials, spill prevention and response, environmental permitting, emergency preparedness, and environmental auditing.

This position leads the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Company's environmental compliance management systems, environmental governance framework, and regulatory compliance programs across all VWNJ operations. The Senior Director provides oversight of all laboratory analysis required to demonstrate compliance, including outside laboratory services and the Haworth WTP laboratory.

The Senior Director serves as the organization's subject matter expert for environmental compliance, environmental permitting, drinking water quality, wastewater treatment compliance, environmental management systems, and environmental regulatory relations. The role partners closely with other functional areas including, operations, engineering, legal, finance, strategic relations, etc., to identify environmental risks, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure consistent compliance across all operations.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities

Lead, empower, and mentor a direct team of environmental professionals, driving cohesive collaboration and operational alignment across all functional disciplines within the position's scope (including Operations, Engineering, Legal, and Finance).
Serve as a strategic leader with external regulatory agencies, effectively interpreting complex regulations and guidelines to advocate for approaches that balance strict regulatory compliance with exceptional customer service and operational/business realities.
Provide environmental compliance leadership for VWNJ. Ensure alignment with corporate objectives and operational priorities.
Provide strategic oversight of compliance programs related to all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including requirements administered by the EPA and applicable state environmental agencies.
Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and communicate impacts to business leadership. Lead development of comments for submission during public comment period for draft regulatory requirements. Interpret emerging regulatory requirements and develop implementation strategies to ensure organizational readiness.
Support development of policies related to water treatment operations, laboratory quality assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Lead the design, implementation, and continual improvement of VWNJ’s environmental compliance management systems.
Lead environmental due diligence activities supporting capital projects and new business initiatives.
Evaluate environmental impacts associated with operational activities and infrastructure investments.
Direct internal environmental assessments and support external regulatory inspections. Oversee development, implementation, and closure of corrective action plans.
Lead VWNJ environmental auditing and compliance assurance programs.
Monitor environmental performance trends and ensure timely resolution of compliance issues.
Oversee environmental permitting activities across all operations.
Ensure timely submission of required regulatory reports and environmental compliance documentation.
Ensure maintenance of systems supporting environmental permits, compliance obligations, inspections, reporting, and regulatory commitments.
Provide oversight of environmental emergency preparedness and response programs.
Direct environmental incident investigations, including spill response and root cause analyses.
Serve as liaison with environmental regulatory agencies.
Build productive relationships with regulators, industry associations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the organization during inspections, audits, enforcement actions, and compliance negotiations.
Establish departmental goals, performance expectations, succession planning, and employee development initiatives.
Allocate resources to support business priorities and regulatory obligations.
Foster collaboration across Operations, Engineering, Legal,Finance, and Corporate leadership.
Develop departmental strategic plans, budgets, and resource forecasts.
Establish and monitor environmental performance objectives, key performance indicators (KPIs), and reporting metrics.
Recommend process improvements that enhance compliance, operational reliability, sustainability, and financial performance.
Support corporate sustainability and environmental stewardship initiatives.

Work Environment

Participation in environmental emergency response activities and on-call leadership, as required.
Combination of office and field environments, including visits to treatment facilities, construction sites, laboratories, and industrial operations.
Ability to conduct field inspections and work in varying environmental conditions while utilizing appropriate personal protective equipment.

Qualifications

Education/Experience/Background:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, or a related technical discipline.
Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 12 years of progressively responsible environmental compliance experience within a regulated utility, environmental services, industrial, manufacturing, or infrastructure organization.
Minimum of 7 years of leadership experience managing environmental professionals and cross-functional teams.
Demonstrated experience leading environmental compliance programs across multiple operating locations.
Experience interacting with federal and state regulatory agencies.
Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance management systems.
Experience supporting environmental due diligence, capital projects, and business development preferred.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including the Safe Drinking Water Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), Clean Air Act, and related environmental permitting requirements.
Knowledge of drinking water treatment, water chemistry, wastewater operations, hazardous materials management, and environmental risk management.
Strong understanding of environmental auditing, compliance assurance, and regulatory reporting.
Working knowledge of environmental compliance management systems and continuous improvement methodologies.
Experience developing environmental compliance strategies, policies, and governance frameworks.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders and build effective relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
Strong project management and organizational leadership capabilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office/Google applications and environmental compliance management systems.

Additional Information

$180000 to $200000 Per Year.

Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement. jobs.description:
ABOUT STREAM REALTY PARTNERS

Founded in 1996, Stream Realty Partners (Stream) began with a vision. Not one focused on bricks and mortar, but with people at its foundation. Headquartered in Dallas, TX and operating in core markets coast to coast, we complete billions in annual transactions in office, industrial, retail, healthcare, land, and data center properties. With millions of square feet of assignments, Stream is one of the fastest-growing, full-service commercial real estate services organizations in the country. Our team of talented individuals have come together to create our distinct culture, best summarized by our firm’s core values: smart, honest, nice, and passionate. For more information, visit www.streamrealty.com and follow Stream on LinkedIn, Instagram, X and Facebook.

IMMEDIATE IMPACT. MEANINGFUL CAREER.

At Stream, we know our success begins and ends with our people. It is the reason we work hard to attract and retain the best and brightest talent. From day one, you will be an integral member of our high-caliber, collaborative team. We will empower you to apply your energy, expertise, and creativity to meet our client’s needs while instilling you with unsurpassed market knowledge and development opportunities to succeed. When you join Stream, you won’t simply start a new job—you will build a meaningful and impactful career.

Job Description

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Senior GIS Analyst transforms spatial, demographic, labor, and real estate data into insights that help Stream professionals and clients make better location and real estate decisions.

Working across Stream’s national platform, this individual will lead sophisticated site selection, relocation, workforce, and market analyses while developing compelling maps, dashboards, and visual narratives that support business development, client strategy, and decision-making.

This role sits at the intersection of analytics, technology, and storytelling. The successful candidate will combine advanced GIS expertise with strong business judgment and the ability to translate complex analysis into clear, actionable recommendations for brokers, clients, and internal stakeholders.

The role reports to the Director of Business and Location Intelligence, collaborates closely with local market teams across the country, and is designed as a remote U.S. position.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Location Intelligence & Advanced Analytics

Lead complex analyses including site selection, relocation studies, labor and workforce analytics, demographic evaluations, and market assessments.
Perform drive-time, distance, trade-area, and origin-destination (OD) analyses to support real estate strategy and client needs.
Develop weighted suitability models, spatial scoring methodologies, and other analytical frameworks to identify and compare optimal locations.
Integrate and analyze data from Esri, Lightcast, commercial real estate platforms, public data sources, and client-provided datasets.
Evaluate data sources, assumptions, and methodologies to ensure analyses are accurate, defensible, reproducible, and appropriate for client use.

Client Strategy & Data Storytelling

Produce high-quality maps, dashboards, StoryMaps, reports, presentations, and other client-ready deliverables.
Translate analytical findings into clear, visually compelling narratives and recommendations that support leasing, investment, development, and location decisions.
Partner with brokers and business teams to determine how spatial insights can strengthen client strategy, pitches, pursuits, and business development.
Ensure deliverables are polished, accurate, consistent with Stream’s brand standards, and tailored to the needs of the audience.

Business Partnership & Advisory

Serve as a location intelligence advisor to brokers, marketing, research, and other business teams by helping define the analytical question, select the appropriate methodology, and interpret results.
Act as a subject matter expert on GIS capabilities, spatial analysis, data sources, and location intelligence methodologies.
Consult with stakeholders to scope projects, identify the right analytical approach, and translate technical findings into business value.
Contribute strategic perspective on how geospatial intelligence can improve client decision-making and differentiate Stream in the marketplace.

Standards, Automation & Innovation

Establish and maintain GIS standards, templates, methodologies, and best practices across the national platform.
Identify opportunities to improve and automate GIS workflows, analytical models, and recurring deliverables using Python, ModelBuilder, and other tools.
Explore and apply AI, automation, and emerging analytical technologies to accelerate research, analysis, and visualization while maintaining appropriate quality controls.
Share knowledge, methodologies, and best practices with GIS and analytical resources across the organization.
Stay current with emerging tools, datasets, and trends in GIS, location intelligence, commercial real estate, and spatial analytics.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Urban Planning, Economics, Data Analytics, or a related field; equivalent experience will be considered.
5+ years of progressively responsible experience in GIS, location intelligence, geospatial analytics, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience leading advanced site selection, market, demographic, workforce, or spatial analyses in a fast-paced, client-driven environment.
Experience translating analytical findings into recommendations for business or client audiences.
Portfolio or examples of advanced geospatial analysis and data visualization preferred.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS

Advanced proficiency in the Esri platform, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, Experience Builder, and Dashboards.
Strong experience with site selection, demographic analysis, labor and workforce analytics, and spatial analysis in a client-facing environment.
Demonstrated ability to build and interpret suitability models and other multi-variable spatial analyses.
Expertise in creating client-ready maps, visualizations, dashboards, reports, and presentations.
Ability to work with large, complex datasets from multiple sources and assess data quality, assumptions, and limitations.
Strong communication and consulting skills, with the ability to translate technical analysis into clear business recommendations.
Experience with Python, ModelBuilder, or other GIS automation tools preferred.
Familiarity with commercial real estate, corporate location strategy, economic development, or consulting environments strongly preferred.

Additional Information

Once you have completed your application, you will receive an email from notifications@smartrecruiters.com with a link to the Culture Index survey, which will help us gain a better understanding of your strengths and motivational drives. Please search for the " Senior GIS Analyst
" position in the Culture Index portal. We kindly request that you set aside 10 uninterrupted minutes within 48 hours of submitting your application.

Environmental Scientist

jobs.title: Autonomy Integration Engineer - Drone Stack
jobs.description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

About The Role

As an Autonomy Integration Engineer within our Drone Stack team at Applied Intuition, you will serve as the technical anchor bridging hardware, edge software, and field flight operations. Split roughly 50/50 between the lab and the airfield, you will be responsible for bringing autonomous aerial systems from initial benchtop configuration to live operational flight.

In this role, you will configure embedded Linux environments, deploy and validate containerized software stacks, wire up mesh network topologies, and write key middleware glue code to keep subsystems communicating seamlessly. You are as comfortable with a soldering iron and oscilloscope at the bench as you are SSH-ing into an onboard computer over a mesh radio under field conditions.

This opportunity can also be located at our HQ in Sunnyvale, CA or Ann Arbor, MI office (relocation offered).

What You'll Do

Lead System Bring-Up: Drive end-to-end hardware and software integration for unmanned aerial systems, moving platforms from benchtop prototyping to active flight test campaigns.
Deploy & Configure Edge Software: Manage, configure, and deploy software stacks using Docker images, shell scripts, and Linux system tools across onboard computes and peripheral hardware.
Field & Bench Troubleshooting: Troubleshoot vehicle networks, payload interfaces, and sensor links in real time using command-line tools (grep, less, journalctl, nano/vim) and hardware diagnostics (multimeters, oscilloscopes).
Build Test Tooling & Glue Code: Develop Python and C++ scripts for data reduction, log analysis, system validation, and real-time subsystem verification.
System Cabling & Electronics: Fabricate custom wiring harnesses, perform precision soldering, and define system-level architecture using clear block diagrams.
Manage Communications & Networks: Configure IP routing, subnets, and local network interfaces between flight controllers, companion computers, radios, and ground control stations.

What We're Looking For

Experience: 5+ years of experience in robotics integration, flight test engineering, embedded systems, or autonomous vehicles (aerial background preferred).
Linux & Networking Mastery: Deep practical comfort with the Linux CLI, file management, system logging, local IP routing, subnets, and containerized deployments (Docker).
Hardware & Electronics Capability: Proven hands-on skills in wiring, custom cable assembly, bench soldering, and physical diagnostics using oscilloscopes and multimeters.
Scripting & Glue Code: Strong proficiency in Python, C++, or Shell scripting for automation, test suite creation, and processing flight data logs.
Protocols: Direct experience working with serial and vehicle bus protocols (UART, CAN, Ethernet, SPI, I2C).
Leadership: Ability to lead major integration efforts independently and act as the technical link between software, GNC, and hardware teams.

Nice to Have

Active DoD Secret Security Clearance.
Deep experience with the MAVLink protocol and autopilot hardware (PX4, ArduPilot).
Experience with Persistent Systems, Silvus, or similar tactical mesh radios.
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate and hands-on R/C flight experience.
Background working with defense tech platforms or flight ranges.

Security Requirements

Must be a U.S. Citizen
Must hold or be eligible for a U.S. Secret security clearance

For more information about U.S. security clearances: click here.

jobs.title: Autonomy Integration Engineer - Drone Stack
jobs.description:
Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Eighteen of the top 20 global automakers, as well as the United States military and its allies, trust the company’s solutions to deliver physical intelligence. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co.

We are an in-office company, and our expectation is that full-time employees primarily work from their Applied Intuition office 5 days a week. However, we also recognize the importance of flexibility and trust our employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work, starting the day with morning meetings from home before heading to the office, or leaving earlier when needed to accommodate family commitments. This in-office expectation does not apply to contractor positions

About The Role

As an Autonomy Integration Engineer within our Drone Stack team at Applied Intuition, you will serve as the technical anchor bridging hardware, edge software, and field flight operations. Split roughly 50/50 between the lab and the airfield, you will be responsible for bringing autonomous aerial systems from initial benchtop configuration to live operational flight.

In this role, you will configure embedded Linux environments, deploy and validate containerized software stacks, wire up mesh network topologies, and write key middleware glue code to keep subsystems communicating seamlessly. You are as comfortable with a soldering iron and oscilloscope at the bench as you are SSH-ing into an onboard computer over a mesh radio under field conditions.

This opportunity can also be located at our Drone Lab near Fort Walton Beach, Florida or at out Ann Arbor, MI office (relocation offered).

What You'll Do

Lead System Bring-Up: Drive end-to-end hardware and software integration for unmanned aerial systems, moving platforms from benchtop prototyping to active flight test campaigns.
Deploy & Configure Edge Software: Manage, configure, and deploy software stacks using Docker images, shell scripts, and Linux system tools across onboard computes and peripheral hardware.
Field & Bench Troubleshooting: Troubleshoot vehicle networks, payload interfaces, and sensor links in real time using command-line tools (grep, less, journalctl, nano/vim) and hardware diagnostics (multimeters, oscilloscopes).
Build Test Tooling & Glue Code: Develop Python and C++ scripts for data reduction, log analysis, system validation, and real-time subsystem verification.
System Cabling & Electronics: Fabricate custom wiring harnesses, perform precision soldering, and define system-level architecture using clear block diagrams.
Manage Communications & Networks: Configure IP routing, subnets, and local network interfaces between flight controllers, companion computers, radios, and ground control stations.

What We're Looking For

Experience: 5+ years of experience in robotics integration, flight test engineering, embedded systems, or autonomous vehicles (aerial background preferred).
Linux & Networking Mastery: Deep practical comfort with the Linux CLI, file management, system logging, local IP routing, subnets, and containerized deployments (Docker).
Hardware & Electronics Capability: Proven hands-on skills in wiring, custom cable assembly, bench soldering, and physical diagnostics using oscilloscopes and multimeters.
Scripting & Glue Code: Strong proficiency in Python, C++, or Shell scripting for automation, test suite creation, and processing flight data logs.
Protocols: Direct experience working with serial and vehicle bus protocols (UART, CAN, Ethernet, SPI, I2C).
Leadership: Ability to lead major integration efforts independently and act as the technical link between software, GNC, and hardware teams.

Nice to Have

Active DoD Secret Security Clearance.
Deep experience with the MAVLink protocol and autopilot hardware (PX4, ArduPilot).
Experience with Persistent Systems, Silvus, or similar tactical mesh radios.
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate and hands-on R/C flight experience.
Background working with defense tech platforms or flight ranges.

Security Requirements

Must be a U.S. Citizen
Must hold or be eligible for a U.S. Secret security clearance

For more information about U.S. security clearances: click here.

Description

Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty in Environmental Health

Rice University invites applications for multiple tenured and tenure-track positions at the senior and junior levels in Environmental Health, with preferred focus areas in environmental and occupational epidemiology, environmental exposures and sustainability, environmental risk assessment, toxicology, infectious diseases, global environmental health, and climate impacts on health, as well as the intersection of these areas with environmental justice. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027. The ideal candidate(s) would bring an interdisciplinary approach, leveraging quantitative training in biostatistics, epidemiological modeling, spatial analytics (GIS), or AI/data science, with experience analyzing clinical (e.g., electronic medical records), registry (e.g., Texas Cancer Registry), or administrative (e.g., American Community Survey) health data.

Primary academic appointment will be in the Department of Kinesiology, ranked #1 nationally by the popular Niche™ rankings and home to Rice’s Public Health Sciences and Sports Medicine and Exercise Physiology undergraduate degrees. These positions are part of an initiative to support interdisciplinary environmental health scholarship, including a new Climate + Health Excellence Center ( FORECAST ) funded by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund. They will come with robust joint appointments in Departments of BioSciences, Chemistry, and Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences as most appropriate.

The successful candidate(s) will be expected to establish a vibrant, externally funded research program, collaborate across disciplines, and teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels. We especially encourage applications from scientists addressing climate impacts on human health and infectious disease, and contributing to broad themes of sustainability or One Health principles. Potential to connect to exercise science, the department’s other major intellectual theme, will also be explored, such as through interests in impacts of extreme heat, air quality, and toxicants on human physiology and performance.

Candidates must have a PhD, DrPH, or equivalent degree in public health science or a relevant field of natural science or engineering and have completed the requirements for the degree by July 1, 2027.

To apply, please submit the following materials online at https://apply.interfolio.com/193813 : (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) research statement (3 pages max); (4) statement of teaching philosophy (3 pages max); and (5) contact information for three references. The research statement and statement of teaching philosophy may also include plans for building a diverse and inclusive research group and fostering equitable and inclusive classrooms. Applications that are received by November 16, 2026,
will receive full consideration, but we will continue reviewing applications until positions are filled. For additional information, please visit our department website or contact the search chairs, Dr. Cassandra Diep ( csdiep@rice.edu ) and Dr. Scott P. Egan ( scott.p.egan@rice.edu) .

Rice University is located in Houston, Texas, USA, and is a private, coeducational, nonsectarian university that aspires to path-breaking research, unsurpassed teaching, and contributions to the betterment of our world. Rice fulfills this mission by cultivating a diverse community of learning and discovery that produces leaders across the spectrum of human endeavor. jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for an environmental permitting manager for our Rochester, New York
office. This is expected to be a hybrid position. The following locations will also be considered in Corning, Syracuse,
Buffalo, Binghamton, NY
. Be involved in projects with our Ecology & Environment team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our client’s objectives and solves their challenges.

Your Impact

Review Project scope and determine applicable permits. This is inclusive of municipal building permits, variances, special use permits, stream and wetland permitting,
PSC Article VII or Part 102, Army Corps, Natural Heritage or SHPO consultation, coastal zone development, DOT, FAA, etc.
Develops or coordinates the development of the required environmental permits
Manages progress against plans, performs risk assessment and take action to mitigate risks.
Verifies project adherence to federal, state and local environmental regulatory requirements.
Participates in project teams and participating in regular program/project planning, execution and delivery team meetings.
Represent the client at public or regulatory meetings.
Reviews and comments on proposed laws and regulations as they apply to company operations.
Manages or oversees implementation and inspection of wildlife, agriculture or wetland mitigation/management plans, and other regulatory requirements of permits which extend beyond construction phase of project.
Develops or oversees the development of SWPPPs
Escalates issues when necessary.
Conducts SWPPP inspections, oversees contracted SWPPP inspectors or environmental monitors, and conducts environmental inspections at construction projects.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Natural Resource Management, or a related sciences field.
7+ years of experience obtaining Regulatory Permits with state, federal and municipal agencies to achieve permits to meet project goals and execution schedules.
Experienced in the preparing, editing and interpreting studies for the development, submission and acquisition of certificates to build or other regulatory filings.
Experience working in team environment to site facilities in the energy sector minimizing environmental, visual and customer impacts considering the companies and projects business requirements.

The selected candidate must be authorized to work in the United States, or be able to obtain work authorized status in the United States prior to the start of employment. This role is eligible for employment visa sponsorship for eligible and qualified candidates.

to join our Environmental Planning team. Our team specializes in managing comprehensive environmental approvals from planning through construction, leveraging innovative engagement tools and deep regulatory knowledge to streamline project delivery.

Dillon Consulting Limited (Dillon) is a proudly Canadian, 100% employee-owned professional consulting firm specializing in planning, engineering, environmental science, and management. With over 25 offices and more than 1100 employees across Canada, we offer a wide range of services related to building and improving facilities and infrastructure, protecting the environment, and developing communities.

At Dillon, we strive to remain at the forefront of technology and innovation and thrive on interdisciplinary collaboration, empowering our people to challenge conventional thinking and build careers focused on creating a lasting impact in our communities. Contribute to Dillon’s corporate profile through active participation in professional associations and committees

A university degree or post-undergraduate college diploma in planning, environmental studies, biology or a related field

Strong communication, report writing, organization, interpersonal skills
Valid Class G Driver’s License

Experience

Knowledge of relevant municipal, provincial and federal environmental legislation, regulations, policies, guidelines, and regulatory permitting and approval requirements

Strong report writing, organization and interpersonal skills
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal

Desire to be a key member of a solution-oriented, multi-disciplinary team
Ability to work independently

jobs.title: Phoenix - Senior Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
Position Description

JOB DESCRIPTION

Nevada Gold Mines is looking for a Senior Environmental Engineer to join our team at the Phoenix operation and play a key role in protecting the environment while supporting safe and responsible mining operations. In this role, you’ll lead environmental programs that manage air, water, land, waste, and reclamation activities
, while mentoring junior team members and working closely with operations, engineering, and regulatory agencies.

As a senior member of the environmental team, you’ll help guide day-to-day compliance activities, oversee permitting and reporting, manage environmental risks, and contribute to continuous improvement efforts that support safe, sustainable mining.

At Nevada Gold Mines, we believe in developing our people, fostering a safe and sustainable workplace, and making a lasting impact in the communities where we operate. If you’re looking to build your career in environmental compliance and be part of a dynamic team, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

Manages all aspects of the site’s reclamation permits including the preparation of regulatory reports, reclamation cost model updates, as well as assisting with reclamation permit modifications.
Review and update site Trust Funds.
Ensures compliance with regards to the site’s Plan of Operations and corresponding U.S. Bureau of Land Management Record of Decisions.
Manages the site’s cultural resource programs including the oversight of cultural resource surveys and the development and execution of cultural mitigation plans, as needed.
Participates in regulatory inspections.
Assists with the development of Plan of Operations amendments and the completion of associated NEPA permitting activities.
Maintains accurate records of agency correspondence and environmental monitoring data.
Acts as a liaison between the mine and environmental regulatory agencies.
Develops, maintains, and updates environmental management plans, as necessary.
Plans and tracks reclamation activities in coordination with the site’s mine engineering personnel.
Manages contractors to ensure the safe delivery of project objectives.
Ensures conformance with internal mine closure standards.
Assists with providing guidance and training to employees and contractors regarding environmental obligations.
Aligns work practices with Environmental ISO 14001 and Occupational Health and Safety 45001 standards.
Responsible for periodic, after-hours on-call response to environmental incidents, as needed.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Manages budgets, including the development, forecasting, and tracking of reclamation/closure costs.
Coordinates with supply chain personnel to procure contractor and consultant services, as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, environmental science, environmental studies, hydrology, hydrogeology, mine engineering, ecology or related field - required
Five (5) years direct experience managing environmental compliance programs and projects, with a minimum of three (3) years in an industrial setting - required
Strong computer skills including experience with PowerPoint, Word and Excel - required
Excellent verbal, written, presentation and interpersonal skills - required
Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously - required
Ability to develop and maintain positive working relationships with others - required
Ability to identify and implement opportunities for improvement - required
General understanding of mining operations - preferred
Familiarity with environmental compliance systems and ISO 14001 - preferred
Ability to drive results and ensure completion of time sensitive deadlines – required
Ability and willingness to work outdoors throughout the year in all weather conditions - required
Ability to lift objects up to 50 lbs. - required

What We Can Offer You

A comprehensive compensation package including bonuses benefits, and stock purchase plans where applicable
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
An Opportunity to transform Traditional Mining into the future of Digital Mining
Opportunities to grow and learn with the industry colleagues are endless
Access to a variety of career opportunities across locations
Nevada Gold Mines is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer

Thank you for your application, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

About Us

Our mission is to be the world’s most valued gold and copper mining business. We are committed to partnering with our host countries and communities to transform their natural resources into tangible benefits and mutual prosperity.

Barrick is a leading global mining, exploration and development company. With one of the largest portfolios of world-class and life-long gold and copper assets in the industry - including six of the world's Tier One gold mines - Barrick's operations an projects span 18 countries and five continents. Barrick is also the largest gold producer in the United States. We create real, long-term value for all stakeholders through responsible mining, strong partnerships, and a disciplined approach to growth. Barrick shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "B" and on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol "ABX".

About The Team

Nevada Gold Mines (NGM) is a joint venture between Barrick (61.5%) and Newmont (38.5%) that combined our significant assets across Nevada in 2019 to create the single largest gold-producing complex in the world. NGM produces approximately 3.5 million ounces of gold a year. The massive mining operation comprises eight mines along with their associated infrastructure and processing facilities and hosts three of Barrick’s Tier One assets: Carlin, Cortez, and Turquoise Ridge. At NGM, our mission is to be the world’s most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and owning the best assets, with the best people, to deliver sustainable returns for our owners and partners.

jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

At HDR, our employee‑ownership model shapes everything we do, including how we support and care for our people. Our diverse service lines, including Water, Architecture, Building Engineering Services, Field Services, Power, Waste, Industrial, and Transportation reflect our commitment to shaping resilient, sustainable, and forward‑thinking communities around the world. Across these disciplines, our teams design and deliver solutions that safeguard public health, enhance quality of life, power innovation, and drive responsible growth. Whether advancing clean water, creating healing and learning environments, engineering next‑generation facilities, or building the infrastructure that moves people and energy, our work is rooted in technical excellence and a shared sense of purpose. Our employee‑owners collaborate across specialties, combining creativity, precision, and deep expertise to solve the most complex challenges facing our clients and communities.

HDR is seeking a Geomatics & Remote Sensing Area Business Class Lead to be a member of our Geomatics & Remote Sensing program, a global team of data acquisition specialists. Data is a common thread to everything we do at HDR. We collect it, generate it, manage it, analyze it, and deliver it to our clients. As a Geomatics & Remote Sensing Area Business Class Lead you will manage the area’s Geomatics & Remote Sensing team and program in HDR’s Missouri/Kansas area. This includes staff management, project management, and business development duties. You will be responsible for the team’s quality project delivery and Geomatics & Remote Sensing business performance and growth within the area across multiple infrastructure markets (e.g., transportation, water, power, building engineering). Our full-service geomatics & remote sensing offerings in Missouri/Kansas include land survey / boundary survey, lidar (outdoor terrestrial, indoor, manned aerial, and mobile), hydrographic survey, and aerial data acquisition via UAS.

Responsibilities:

Take responsibility for area coordination, monitoring and improvement of technical competencies of staff and products of the Geomatics & Remote Sensing teams in Missouri and Kansas to meet client needs and market drivers, all within direction and goals of business class plans
Participate in delivery of project services to meet client expectations
Collaborate on Geomatics & Remote Sensing business class efforts with area operations, marketing and project management
Participate in Geomatics & Remote Sensing business class practice and professional discipline groups, project teams and activities to continually improve standards and best practices, and implement effective quality assurance and quality control reviews
Serve as a seller-doer with the responsibility to pursue and win work and maintain a profitable utilization for the team and yourself. Be directly involved in marketing planning, proposals, and interviews, which includes maintaining strong client relationships, trends/drivers, and upcoming opportunities.
Participate in business class strategic planning, budgeting and plan implementation at local and regional levels, across all business groups.
Function as a project manager or technical manager, leading critical area and regional projects.
Perform other duties as needed

Preferred Qualifications

You have a service- and client-oriented personality.
Experience leading the development of scopes, schedules and budgets, and managing projects
Interest in infrastructure projects such as water, wastewater, transportation, transit, energy, solid waste, and architecture
Familiarity with the architecture and engineering consulting industry
You have an internal drive to try new things and explore new industry trends and technology while pushing your comfort zone every day.
You have strong organization skills.
You can adapt and thrive in a fast-paced environment.
Preference given to local candidates

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a Professional, Architecture, Engineering or closely related field
10 years of experience
Committed to quality, improvement and HDR values
Maintains a professional or engineering registration and has related technical experience
Experienced in development and management of diverse teams
Works cooperatively with other area business class leaders, operations managers, technical directors and marketing managers on business class efforts
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

jobs.title: Principal – Natural Capital (Flexible around location)
jobs.description:
Overview

Are you passionate about shaping a more sustainable future where measuring and valuing natural capital drives better decisions for people and the planet? Do you have technical environmental expertise, strong project management experience, and commercial awareness? If so, you may have the drive and skills to join AtkinsRéalis as a Principal Consultant in our Natural Capital and Environmental Economics team. You will play a key role in leading and delivering high-quality projects, managing multidisciplinary teams and developing strong client relationships. You will join our highly respected technical team at an exciting time and help grow our reputation for innovation and technical excellence, while further developing our services and pipeline of work across an extensive client portfolio.

We develop and use state-of-the-art approaches and our innovative in-house tools to assess, quantify and value the benefits of changes in ecosystem services at various scales, from strategic to scheme level. You can see some examples of our work here Valuing Our Natural Capital: The AtkinsRéalis Approach. Our natural capital team offers a unique blend of skills, comprising experts in environmental economics, environmental science and spatial analysis, with an ambitious strategy for continuous innovation. You will have the opportunity to work with and influence our clients directly, supporting them on tackling the climate and biodiversity crises.

Your role

You will play a central role in leading and delivering projects with a natural capital focus, while also supporting wider Biodiversity Net Gain, Nature Positive, Net Zero and Social Value initiatives across a variety of projects throughout the business. Working as a recognised specialist within your field, you will provide technical leadership and oversight, ensuring high-quality outputs are delivered to time, cost and quality requirements.
You will lead multidisciplinary project teams and coordinate inputs from colleagues across AtkinsRéalis, applying your professional judgement to complex challenges and helping clients navigate an evolving policy, regulatory and commercial landscape.
The role will involve managing project programmes, budgets and resources, building trusted client relationships, and identifying opportunities to deliver additional value through our wider environmental and infrastructure capabilities.
You will contribute to and lead proposals and bids, supporting the growth of our natural capital and environmental economics portfolio, while also helping to shape innovative approaches, methodologies and digital tools that strengthen our technical offer.
As a senior member of the team, you will coach and mentor junior colleagues, contribute to technical networks and capability development activities, and promote technical excellence both within AtkinsRéalis and externally through engagement with clients, industry groups and the wider profession.

About You

We are seeking an enthusiastic and ambitious Principal Consultant to join our growing Natural Capital and Environmental Economics team.

A degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. Environmental Economics, Environmental Science and Policy, Ecology or Geography) and preferably a relevant post-graduate qualification.
Chartered status with a relevant professional body such as CIWEM, CIEEM, ISEP, IES or equivalent.
Technical experience in the application of natural capital assessments, natural capital accounting and/or environmental economics techniques.
Experience of undertaking economic valuation and applying natural capital approaches to support decision-making.
Experience in project management, bid development, technical leadership and mentoring of junior colleagues.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to adapt your presentation style to different audiences, including non-specialists.
Strong organisational skills, commercial awareness and the ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously and to deadlines.
Excellent collaborative working skills to ensure we get the best from our working relationships with internal multidisciplinary teams, and build trusted relationships with clients.
Experience with emerging nature markets and green finance would be desirable.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career. Enjoy competitive salaries, employee rewards and a brilliant range of benefits you can tailor to suit your own health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle choices. Make the most of a myriad of opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise. And combine our hybrid working culture and flexible holiday allowances to balance a great job and fulfilling personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

About AtkinsRéalis

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

Find out more.

Additional information

Security clearance

This role may require security clearance and offers of employment will be dependent on obtaining the relevant level of clearance. If this is necessary, it will be discussed with you at interview. The vetting process is delivered by United Kingdom Security Vetting (UKSV) and may require candidates to provide proof of residency in the UK of 5 years or longer. If applying to this role please do not make reference to (in conversation) or include in your application or CV, details of any current or previously held security clearance.

We are committed to creating a culture where everyone feels that they belong - a place where we can all be ourselves, thrive and develop to be the best we can be. So, we offer a range of family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements and employee resource groups to support all employees. As an Equal Opportunities Employer, we value applications from all backgrounds, cultures and ability. As a Disability Confident Leader, we are committed to offering an interview to all applicants who have a disability and meet the essential criteria. If you would like to be considered under this commitment, please let us know at the application stage.

Our services cover the entire life cycle of the project implementation.

Currently, we are bidding for Semi High Speed Rail projects across India. The position of Chief Safety, Health and Environmental Expert - Elevated is the key position in these BIDs.

Missions/Main Duties

Develop and Enforce Project SHE Strategy: 📜 Establish the comprehensive Safety, Health, and Environmental (SHE) Management Plan and System Safety Program Plan (SSPP). This includes setting project-wide SHE targets, integrating specialized procedures for working at height (elevated sections), and ensuring compliance with all local, national, and railway-specific regulations.
High-Risk Activity Management & Oversight: Direct the rigorous assessment and control of high-risk construction activities, specifically related to elevated structures, such as pile foundation work, pier cap casting, segment launching, heavy lifting operations, and working over or adjacent to existing infrastructure and public traffic.
Incident Management and Prevention: Establish and manage the Incident/Accident/Near-Miss reporting, investigation, and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) process across all contractors. Ensure the timely implementation and verification of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) to prevent recurrence.
Environmental Impact and Compliance: Oversee the implementation of the Environmental Management Plan (EMP), focusing on unique elevated rail concerns like noise and vibration control, dust suppression, hazardous waste management, and minimizing impact on sensitive areas during construction and operation.
SHE Auditing, Training, and Culture: Lead and coordinate all internal and external SHE audits (including regulatory and client audits) and site inspections. Under the supervision of the Senior Technical Manager the duties and responsibilities include:
  

Assist with GIS data management and spatial analysis for the UN Biodiversity Lab (UNBL), including processing, uploading, maintaining, and updating spatial datasets.
  

Provide coding support for scripts, GitHub repositories, the elsaR package, and related data\-processing and implementation pipelines.
  

Support geospatial analysis for ELSA activities, including preparing data layers and spatial data stacks and assisting with country\-specific ELSA tools.
  

Assist with stakeholder engagement and training activities, including sessions with governments, UN agencies, NGOs, academia, and other partners.
  

Provide technical and operational support to UNBL, including platform testing, user support, guidance materials, knowledge management, minor website updates, and related coordination.
### **About the Region**

The UNOPS Global Portfolios Office (GPO) brings together diverse expertise to help partners deliver impact worldwide. With hubs in New York, Geneva, and Vienna, and expert teams operating globally, GPO leads multi\-regional initiatives that advance sustainable development, climate action, and peacebuilding \- including in some of the world’s most challenging environments.


By leveraging our collective expertise and global networks, GPO supports UNOPS’ strategic priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals across more than 130 countries. We work closely with major global partners \- including governments, international financial institutions, and UN agencies \- to deliver a wide range of services, such as project management, fund management, hosting services, and HR support.


Our thematic focus spans climate action and energy, health, peace and security, sustainable development, and humanitarian action, supporting high\-impact initiatives across critical global priorities.

  


### **About the Country/Multi\-Country Office**

UNOPS Development and Special Initiatives team works with UN partners and Member States. This portfolio offers support for various initiatives and priorities of the UN Secretary\-General in pursuit of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Additionally, it helps the UN Secretariat in implementing global programs in areas such as political affairs, climate, counterterrorism and peacebuilding, among others.


### **About the Group**

UNOPS has signed an agreement with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to implement the project activities for the Global Programme on Nature for Development.  

UNDP’s Global Programme on Nature for Development brings together three different initiatives \- the Equator Initiative, Learning for Nature, and the National Biodiversity Initiative under one program in order to identify, foster, showcase and celebrate nature\-based solutions that help achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development at local, national, and international levels. The work of the Global Programme on Nature for Development contributes to UNDP's Strategic Plan 2026\-2029 by charting sustainable development pathways through the conservation, restoration and sustainable management of biodiversity and ecosystems; and by promoting inclusive and effective democratic governance in the area of natural resources.  

The Equator Initiative brings together the United Nations, governments, civil society, businesses and grassroots organizations to recognize and advance local sustainable development solutions for people, nature and resilient communities. The Equator Initiative seeks to:* Recognize the success of local and indigenous initiatives;
* Create opportunities and platforms to share knowledge and good practice;
* Inform policy to foster an enabling environment for local and indigenous community action; and
* Develop the capacity of indigenous peoples and local communities to scale\-up their impact.

  

The National Biodiversity Initiative supports countries to manage their ecosystems and biodiversity in order to improve national planning and governance of biodiversity, ecosystems, and development, and to promote resilience for sustainable development. The National Biodiversity Initiative works in three project areas: National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) Support, National Reporting, and Capacity Building. The use of spatial data for spatial planning is a cross\-cutting theme across these project areas, including work through our flagship platform UN Biodiversity Lab, created in partnership with the UN Environment Programme and the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity.  

Knowledge Sharing is a main goal of the Equator Initiative, Learning for Nature and the National Biodiversity Initiative. Purpose Of The Position

The UAH Lab for Applied Science (LAS) under the Earth System Science Center (ESSC), based in Huntsville, Alabama, is seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to support the Biological Diversity and Ecological Conservation (BDEC) research and application activities at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center.

This is an exciting opportunity to help advance one of NASA’s most compelling Earth science efforts: using satellite observations, models, in situ data, and geospatial analysis to better understand the richness of life on Earth, how and why it is changing, and how that knowledge can be translated into practical conservation action. The position will focus on both implementing Economic Impact Assessments (EIA) and conducting remote sensing analyses to support BDEC activities by integrating EIA into both new and existing projects across the BDEC portfolio. This position will work closely with BDEC VC scientists and end-users as well as other experts in EIA across NASA.

This Research Associate will contribute to the development, testing, and refinement of EIAs that support BDEC’s mission to better connect NASA Earth observations to various stakeholders, including scientists and land managers. Work will include designing and implementing economic impact assessments, which may entail interviews with stakeholders, running economic models, among other activities. The role will also support cross-center collaboration, technical coordination, and capacity-building activities tied to BDEC activities. Processing of satellite remote sensing datasets to support tasks for data production is also expected for this position.

BDEC is designed to bridge NASA Earth science and on-the-ground decision-making by helping scientists, land and water managers, and conservation partners turn observations into action. The Virtual Center emphasizes early engagement with end users, cross-center collaboration, and the creation of actionable products and services that support biodiversity science, ecological conservation, and real-world stewardship of landscapes and ecosystems.

Duties/Responsibilities

Support BDEC scientific and application activities
Provide scientific and technical support in remote sensing data applications for specific projects
Translate complex technical results into products, presentations, and materials that are accessible to scientific collaborators and end users.
Coordinate with BDEC scientists and stakeholders to assess needs and support the needs-to-solutions pipeline
Support capacity-building activities, including training and knowledge transfer related to remote sensing methods, Economic Impact Assessments, and BDEC workflows.
Contribute to the creation of prototype tools, tutorials, and documentation that support deployment and use of BDEC-related remote sensing products.
Participate in cross-center collaboration, technical discussions, and stakeholder-facing efforts that support BDEC VC goals.
Support and conduct Economic Impact Assessments (EIA)
Support coordination and data collection for EIA projects, including interviews with a variety of stakeholders
Provide economic modelling support to EIA projects
Coordinate with other NASA EIA efforts
Assist with documentation of the methodology, tools, and other scientific literature for relevant EIA projects
Lead and contribute to peer-reviewed publications and present at scientific conferences
Contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, and other dissemination products.

Minimum Requirements

A Bachelor’s degree in economics, environmental and social science, or a related field.
Minimum of 2-4 years of verifiable, full-time work experience.
Basic experience in remote sensing and GIS applications or a master’s degree in remote sensing and GIS applications with experience in working with EO data impact assessments.
Experience in Earth Observation-driven methods and models and geospatial data analysis.
Experience in math, statistical & scientific data processing automation (State, Python, R).
Record of publication commensurate with level of experience.
Familiarity with NASA Earth science datasets, remote sensing products, and applied conservation or biodiversity applications.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, demonstrated leadership experience, and experience working with diverse groups of people.
Ability to work collaboratively in a technical, interdisciplinary team and communicate clearly with scientists and stakeholders.

Desired Qualifications

A Master's or PhD in economics, environmental and social science, or a related field
Experience working with NASA and/or other federal, state, local, tribal, or private sector organizations is desired.

jobs.description:
Company Description
Ambienta Inc. is an environmental services company focused on conserving and managing natural ecosystems and wildlife resources. The organization collaborates with public agencies, private entities, and community partners to support science-based habitat preservation and sustainable land-use practices. Ambienta Inc. emphasizes field-based research, data-driven decision-making, and practical solutions to complex ecological challenges. Team members work in multidisciplinary settings where safety, integrity, and environmental stewardship are prioritized. The company values professional growth, collaboration, and inclusive work environments for all employees.
Role Description
The Wildlife Biologist will work in either a part-time or a full-time capacity, isoabd wide, remotely or from Ambienta’s office, conducting field surveys, monitoring wildlife populations, assessing habitat conditions across various ecosystems, followed by corresponding reports. Day-to-day responsibilities include collecting and analyzing biological data, documenting species presence and behavior, and preparing technical reports, maps, and summaries for project stakeholders. The role involves collaborating with botanists, fisheries specialists, and land managers to develop and implement wildlife and habitat management plans that align with regulatory requirements and conservation goals. The Wildlife Biologist will support environmental impact assessments, contribute to permit applications, and provide recommendations to minimize project-related effects on wildlife. The position also requires maintaining accurate records, following safety protocols in the field, and communicating findings clearly to internal teams and external partners.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in Wildlife Biology and Wildlife Management, with the ability to design and conduct field studies and interpret ecological data.
Knowledge of Wildlife and Fish ecology, including species identification, population dynamics, and habitat requirements.
Understanding of Botany and plant community ecology, particularly as it relates to habitat quality and restoration.
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Wildlife Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.
Experience with field methods such as transect surveys, live-trapping, camera monitoring, and habitat assessments.
Ability to work outdoors in variable conditions, hike over uneven terrain, and adhere to field safety standards.
Proficiency in data management and basic analysis; experience with GIS, statistical software, or mapping tools is a plus.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with experience preparing technical reports or regulatory documentation preferred.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in diverse, interdisciplinary teams and to respect inclusive, non-discriminatory workplace practices.

jobs.description:
Description

Wildlife Biologist On-Call Southern and East-Central California

Job Description

The On-Call Biologist will be responsible for a range of environmental consulting services, including preconstruction field surveys, construction compliance monitoring, avian species identification and nest surveys, supporting general and focused biological field surveys, assisting with writing and reviewing biological reports and supporting documents such as Biological Technical Reports, Biological Assessments, technical memos, FRED database forms, and providing as-needed field and office support to our local and regional Natural Resource team members.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate, plan and execute field assignments for southern and east-central California-based work. Conduct general and species-specific biological surveys and construction compliance monitoring pursuant to the relevant environmental commitments, laws, regulations, codes and/or industry standards. Document field findings in monitoring logs, reports, memos and email communications, as appropriate. Communicate routinely with client field contacts and ICF project managers and senior biologists. The on-call biologist must be able to travel to remote field sites in other counties, including but not limited to Los Angeles, Orange, Kern, San Bernadino, Riverside, Inyo, and San Diego Counties.

About On-Call Employment With ICF

Given the seasonal or project-specific nature of our environmental compliance work, ICF often hires environmental professionals as "On-Call" employees. On-Call employees are scheduled for work hours as they become available (we usually schedule work hours a few weeks ahead of time, depending on client notifications), and each on-call employee is free to accept or refuse the hours assigned to them in a given week. On-Call employees may work concurrent projects outside of their ICF assignment (along as their outside work does not create a conflict of interest with the work they do for ICF).

Requirements

A BA/BS in Wildlife Biology, Botany, Ecology, or related discipline
2+ years of environmental/consulting and biological field experience.
Must have prior experience conducting construction field compliance monitoring on 2+ projects including 6+ months total field compliance monitoring experience
Must have valid driver's license and successfully pass a Motor Vehicles Records (MVR) check

Preferred Skills

Avian nest monitoring and species identification skills with experience conducting nesting bird field surveys and avian habitat assessments on 3 or more projects with at least 2 of these projects located in the southwestern U.S.
Experience leading all three phases of western burrowing owl protocol surveys on 3 or more projects including positive identification of individual owls in the wild
Experience conducting native special status reptile or amphibian species surveys or monitoring on 3 or more projects with positive results and identification of target species
Experience leading field surveys or trapping for small mammals on 3 or more California projects including possession of a CDFW scientific collecting permit
Basic field observation documentation/data management experience
Experience working in the environmental compliance and/or construction fields (i.e., biological or aquatic construction monitoring).
Basic botanical knowledge of east-central and southern California with demonstrated participation in 5 or more field botanical rare plant surveys and habitat mapping assessments in California of which at least 3 of these projects in southern or east-central California
Geographic Information System (GIS) software skills
Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
Strong written and oral communication skills
Strong organizational skills
Ability to respond timely to deployment requests (i.e., sometimes next day)
Ability to travel to field sites in east-central and southern California and assist with field surveys and compliance monitoring in rugged, undeveloped terrain
Ability and experience conducting work in active construction sites and communicating with construction foreman and equipment operators
Proficiency in MS Office Applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, Teams)

TACOM (RRAD): Environmental Supervisor (Contingency)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

The U.S. Army Tank-automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) sustains the Army’s mission to develop, acquire, field, and sustain ground combat, tactical, and support systems throughout their lifecycle. The program focuses on ensuring operational readiness, reliability, and safety of automotive and ground support equipment critical to Army operations.

Under this contract, supervisory personnel provide first-line leadership and operational oversight for maintenance and sustainment teams, ensuring work is performed in accordance with Army Technical Manuals (TMs), safety standards, quality requirements, and contractual performance metrics.

Job Summary

The Environmental Supervisor provides first‑line leadership and oversight of environmental compliance activities in support of TACOM operations. This role is responsible for supervising environmental technicians and staff, ensuring adherence to environmental regulations, and maintaining compliance with all applicable laws, permits, and policies. They will supervise environmental personnel in adhering to all federal, state, local, and Army environmental regulations (e.g., RCRA, Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act).

This position is contingent upon award

Supervise and directly manages the hazardous material and hazardous waste programs.
