jobs.title: CPW Wildlife Technician IV - (Fort Collins, CO)
jobs.description:
Department Information

The primary duties of this position are located within 30 miles of the state border; therefore, this position is exempt from the residency requirements. Applications will be considered from residents and non-residents of Colorado.

This is a term-limited position. Funding cannot be guaranteed beyond October, 2029. The incumbent in this position must be willing and able to resign on this date or when funds run out, whichever comes first.

Consider joining the dedicated people of the Colorado Department of Natural Resources. It’s our mission to manage and conserve Colorado’s natural resources for the benefit of people today – and tomorrow. That means we have to balance development with conservation so the state we all love provides similar opportunities for our children and their children.

We invite you to explore our website at https://dnr.colorado.gov/about-us to find out more about the work we do to manage Colorado’s natural resources for today – and tomorrow.

The State of Colorado believes that equity, diversity, and inclusion drive our success, and we encourage candidates from all identities, backgrounds, and abilities to apply.

In Addition To Offering Rewarding, Meaningful Work, We Offer

Medical and Dental plans
Strong, flexible retirement plans including PERA Defined Benefit Plan or PERA Defined Contribution Plan, plus pre-tax and Roth 401K and 457 plans
Paid life insurance
Short- and long-term disability coverage
Employee Wellness programs
Flexible Spending Accounts
Health Savings Accounts
11 paid holidays per year plus generous vacation and sick leave
Flexible work schedule options and remote-work options
Career advancement opportunities throughout the State system
Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program .

COLORADO PARKS AND WILDLIFE

Our Mission is to perpetuate the wildlife resources of the state, to provide a quality state parks system, and to provide enjoyable and sustainable outdoor recreation opportunities that educate and inspire current and future generations to serve as active stewards of Colorado's natural resources.

Wildlife Health conducts disease monitoring and surveillance for all terrestrial wildlife species, as well as rigorous scientific-based original research deemed valuable to CPW in order to better understand and enhance the health, management, and conservation of Colorado’s terrestrial wildlife resources; the program also provides field and laboratory services and training to CPW staff, as well as captive wildlife research support and captive wildlife holding for other CPW research and management programs.

Description Of Job

The position exists to: (a) provide technical support for necropsy services through statewide coordination of necropsy submissions, assistance during necropsy procedures, and maintenance of the necropsy laboratory; (b) provide technical support in executing statewide chronic wasting disease and other disease surveillance; (c) provide technical support for necropsy and laboratory services by maintaining records, filing paperwork, maintaining databases, and summarizing data (d) provide technical support for management or research projects conducted in the field or at the Foothills Wildlife Research Facility.

Provide technical support for necropsy services through coordination of necropsy submissions, assistance during necropsy procedures, and maintenance of the necropsy laboratory

Coordinate transportation of carcasses or tissues to the Wildlife Health Laboratory, including travel to retrieve carcasses when necessary. Coordinate sample submissions, and accession and process samples as they arrive at the Wildlife Health Laboratory. Adhere to protocols for ongoing disease surveillance projects. Maintain adequate facility and supplies/inventory for necropsy and other diagnostic services. Maintain clean and sanitary work, freezer, and cooler spaces, including timely disposition of tissues after processing either through disposal at a landfill or via incineration. Monitor freezers and coolers for adequate temperature control. Monitor hazardous waste tanks and coordinate disposal of hazardous material as needed. Provide support during necropsy including dissection, tissue removal, assessment of tissue integrity/disease, radiology, photography, proper sample handling for diagnostics or archival, and submission to external and internal laboratories for testing. Mail coolers back to submitters. Take personal responsibility for the use of personal protective equipment when dealing with potentially hazardous tissues or chemicals. Maintain archives of samples, photographs, reports, and other documents pertinent to casework. Special care must be taken for forensics cases that may provide evidence for legal investigations.

Provide technical support to the laboratory technologist in executing statewide chronic wasting disease and other disease surveillance

This position will also perform duties related to CWD surveillance and other disease surveillance. Duties may include, but are not limited to Construct and mail out supplies for CWD sampling (CWD kits). Provide training for CWD sampling. Process CWD samples as they arrive at the Wildlife Health Laboratory. Extract CWD samples from whole head submissions. Assure sample quality for submissions. Organize samples for submission to the diagnostic laboratory. Submit samples to the diagnostic laboratory. Enter data and provide quality control for data entries in the CWD database. Communicate with field personnel and other staff to assure quick resolution of any issues. Accession and process samples arriving at the lab for purposes other than CWD or necropsy (for example blood or tissue samples received from research staff). Properly archive samples in accordance with existing protocols.

Provide technical support for necropsy and laboratory services by maintaining records, filing paperwork, maintaining databases, and summarizing data

This position will manage paperwork from necropsy and sample submissions to the wildlife health laboratory and develop mechanisms to organize and track diagnostic data.

Provide technical support for management or research projects conducted in the field or at the Foothills
Wildlife Research Facility.

Assist veterinary staff, researchers, managers, and biologists with ongoing projects including animal care and husbandry, observation, veterinary care and support, sample collection and handling, data collection, or other duties to support this work. Travel may be required.

Other Duties As Assigned.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

Minimum Qualifications

Four (4) years of relevant experience in wildlife health, processing biological samples, post-mortem tissue handling and sampling or an occupational field related to the work assigned to the position. You must adequately demonstrate your experience in your application as it relates to the duties of this position.

OR

A combination of related education in wildlife biology, natural resources, animal science, biology and/or relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned equal to four (4) years.

Substitutions

Appropriate education in wildlife biology, natural resources, animal science, biology, laboratory science or a related field of study will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.

You must adequately demonstrate your experience in your application as it relates to the duties of this position.

Class Code:
TECHNICIAN IV

Preferred Qualifications

Current or former Colorado Parks & Wildlife work or volunteer experience is considered.
Experience collecting and processing a wide array of biological samples.
Experience managing detailed records and quality control of data.
Experience working with strong smells and decaying tissues with varying amounts of maggots or other insects.
Experience collecting post mortem samples.
Current or former State experience relevant to this position.

Required Competencies

Excellent organizational and time management skills.
Strong level of written and oral communication skills.
Ability to use and operate computers and email and basic data management (e.g., Excel, Access).
Ability to strictly follow laboratory protocols and procedures.
Ability to move smoothly between highly variable tasks.
Attention to detail and quality assurance during sample processing.

Conditions of Employment

Will be required to operate a State vehicle. Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license.
Occasional assistance with field work may require travel.
Must willing and able to obtain record of rabies vaccine for consideration of employment.
Employee will be exposed to biological materials as well as formalin, a hazardous chemical must be fit for a respirator (such as an N95 face mask) as they will be exposed to animal carcasses positive for infectious diseases such as rabies, highly pathogenic avian influenza, plague, and tularemia PPE during necropsy activities.
Employee must be capable of lifting up to 50 pounds and performing varied physical tasks such as bending, crouching, lifting, and reaching.
Former State employees who were disciplinarily terminated or resigned in lieu of termination must disclose the information on the application and provide an explanation why the prior termination or resignation should not disqualify their application from the current position. (Please Note: Absent extraordinary circumstances, prior disciplinary termination or resignation in lieu of termination will disqualify the applicant from future State employment with DNR).
Pursuant to the DNR-120 Fleet and Driving Standards Administrative Directive , any worker who will be expected to drive a State-owned vehicle is responsible for maintaining a safe driving record and a valid driver license prior to driving any State-owned vehicle.

To Be Compliant With The New Fleet Vehicle Policy, Motor Vehicle Records (MVRs) Will Be Pulled For Review For Workers Who

Have an assigned State fleet vehicle
Are required to operate a vehicle as part of the position
Utilize a State fleet vehicle as a pool vehicle

Appeal Rights

It is recommended that you contact the Human Resources Specialist listed below to resolve issues related to your possession of minimum qualifications. However, if you receive notice that you have been eliminated from consideration for this position, you may file an appeal with the State Personnel Board or request a review by the State Personnel Director.

An appeal or review must be submitted on the official appeal form, signed by you or your representative. This form must be delivered to the State Personnel Board by email (dpa_state.personnelboard@state.co.us), postmarked in US Mail or hand delivered (1525 Sherman Street, 4th Floor, Denver CO 80203), or faxed (303.866.5038) within ten (10) calendar days from your receipt of notice or acknowledgment of the department’s action.

For more information about the appeals process, the official appeal form, and how to deliver it to the State Personnel Board; go to spb.colorado.gov; contact the State Personnel Board for assistance at (303) 866-3300; or refer to 4 Colorado Code of Regulations (CCR) 801-1, State Personnel Board Rules and Personnel Director's Administrative Procedures, Chapter 8, Resolution of Appeals and Disputes, at spb.colorado.gov under Rules.

Supplemental Information

The Assessment Process

All applications received by the closing of this announcement will be reviewed by an HR Specialist against the Minimum Qualifications in this announcement.
Colorado Revised Statutes require that state employees are hired and promoted based on merit and fitness through a comparative analysis process. Part of, or all of, the comparative analysis for this position will be a structured application review by Subject Matter Experts.
Resumes, cover letters and other attachments are not considered as part

Position Summary:
Position (K0229186)

The Bureau of Air, Permitting Unit, is seeking a candidate for an Environmental Specialist position. Responsibilities include review of construction and operating permit applications, source information, air emission calculations, and other documents provided by permit applicants for compliance with the Clean Air Act federal regulations and Kansas Air Quality Regulations.

Job Responsibilities may include but are not limited to the following:

Reviews air quality applications from assigned facilities for State Construction Permits; State Construction Approvals; Class I Operating Permits and Class II Operating Permits. Applications are reviewed to ensure compliance with provisions of the Clean Air Act, including National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), New Source Performance Standards (NSPS), National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAPs), and State of Kansas air quality regulations. Applications are reviewed to ensure all necessary air quality information is provided by permit applicant. Incumbent reviews technical air quality reports, environmental plans and specifications for the construction or modification of air pollution control facilities to determine if facility designers have made accurate and appropriate conclusions in their preparation of air permit applications. Air quality permit applications emission calculations are analyzed to ensure compliance with sound engineering practices and established air quality standards. Analysis of air quality control technology to reduce emissions and ensure compliance with environmental regulations in air permits is performed. Incumbent directly contacts environmental and engineering consultants, planners, and designers to resolve any questions. Verifies that all air quality regulations in permit applications are appropriate for the type and class of permit requested.

Develop permits including Class I and Class II Operating permits and Construction permits. Review must ensure that emissions from both new construction and modifications do not cause or contribute to violations of the NAAQS and assure new construction and modifications will comply with all applicable air quality regulations. Operating Permits consist in the development of a single document which contains all air quality requirements with which the source must comply. Permits are developed to ensure adherence to all federal and State regulations and Bureau of Air policies and procedures. Once a draft permit has been completed and gone through an internal concurrence process, the permit is issued to the applicant. All construction approvals, construction permits, and operating permits are reviewed by supervisor and section chief. All reviews occur at the time a draft permit has been submitted for concurrence.

Assured that all statutory, regulatory, contractual and procedural requirements have been satisfied prior to issuance of a permit, including notifications to EPA required by agreement with the EPA. This final step in the issuance of less complex and routine permits is to ensure that EPA air permit requirements have been met by verifying compliance with all aspects of the Clean Air Act, as indicated by the state's air pollution control strategies listed in the State implementation Plan submitted to EPA. These requirements are usually reviewed during the internal concurrence process; however, EPA does review and comment on some of these permits, in addition to auditing the Bureau of Air's permit program. During the permit concurrence process, work is reviewed by supervisor and section chief for compliance with Kansas Air Quality Act, related regulations and federal Clean Air Act requirements.

About Us

Quantum Computing Inc. (QCi) (Nasdaq: QUBT) is an innovative, integrated photonics company that provides accessible and affordable quantum machines to the world today. QCi products are designed to operate at room temperature and low power at an affordable cost. The Company’s portfolio of core technology and products offer unique capabilities in the areas of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, cyber security as well as remote sensing applications.
Position Description 

The Quantum Optical Engineer will contribute to the design, development, testing, and optimization of QCi’s advanced remote sensing and secure communication systems. This role combines hands-on laboratory work with system-level optical design, supporting products from initial concept through production.
The successful candidate will have a strong background in optical engineering, photonics, quantum optics, and optoelectronics, along with experience testing and troubleshooting optical systems and analyzing experimental data. Working closely with a cross-disciplinary engineering team, this individual will help improve system performance, reliability, and scalability, while also contributing to quality assurance processes and workflow improvements.
This position is based in Hoboken, NJ, with optional partial work-from-home flexibility. Occasional business travel (less than 10%) may be required. We are seeking a proactive, detail-oriented engineer who thrives in a fast-paced, growing environment and is eager to apply optical engineering principles to real-world, cutting-edge technologies.
Duties and Responsibilities

Design and development of optical setups for LiDAR experiments, including beam shaping, collimation, and range-gating techniques. 
Development and testing of single-photon sensitive vibrometer and communications systems. 
Experimental validation and characterization of optical components and subsystems. 
Support of research on optical fault detection methodologies based on vibrometry. 
Development of recording techniques for entangled photons used in secure communication and data processing systems.
Gage Repeatability and Reproducibility (G R & R) testing to ensure measurement consistency and reliability in field and lab environments. 
Collaborations with multi-disciplinary teams (hardware, software, firmware) to refine system performance. 

Required Skills and Experience

Master’s or PhD degree in Optical Engineering, Physics, Photonics, or equivalent experience. 
3-5 years Hands-on experience with laser systems, free-space optics, and fiber optics. 
Background in optoelectronics and WDM techniques for telecom applications.
Familiarity with LiDAR principles, time-of-flight measurements, and single-photon detection. 
Experience with optical metrology and statistical measurement systems analysis (G R & R studies).

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Mammalian Conservation Ecology
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Department of Fish and Wildlife Conservation in the College of Natural Resources and Environment at Virginia Tech invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor of Mammalian Conservation Ecology. We seek a collaborative scholar and educator whose work advances understanding and conservation of mammals and strengthens the department’s core missions in biodiversity conservation and experiential education.

The successful candidate will develop an internationally visible research program in mammalian conservation ecology. The candidate should have a strong track record studying the conservation and ecology of wild mammal populations, with research addressing contemporary socio-environmental challenges such as climate change, emerging infectious diseases, invasive species, and habitat loss. The Department and the University are highly collaborative environments, creating the opportunity for diverse collaborations across Virginia Tech and with state and federal natural resource agencies, conservation organizations, and other partners. The position is envisioned as approximately 25% teaching, 65% research, and 10% service.

Teaching and Mentoring Expectations

The department boasts a high-quality teaching environment that emphasizes modern pedagogical techniques and ample experiential learning opportunities. Teaching will include a 1:1 teaching expectation, including FIW 4334 Mammalogy, a high-enrollment, field-oriented course central to the Wildlife Conservation curriculum. During the first two years, the faculty member is also expected to develop or contribute to a graduate course in their area of expertise and, as the appointment matures, contribute (e.g., team teach) to general education or other high-demand undergraduate courses. The faculty member will mentor undergraduate researchers and M.S. and Ph.D. students and provide field-based, experiential learning opportunities.

Research, Scholarship, Extension, and Engagement Expectations

The successful candidate will establish a highly productive, externally funded research program that supports graduate students and produces high-quality, peer-reviewed scholarship. Expectations include publishing impactful research in respected peer reviewed journals. The candidate will be expected to apply for McIntire-Stennis (USDA NIFA capacity grant) funding in the first year. The candidate should pursue annual external funding from appropriate federal and state agencies and foundations, including opportunities through NSF, U.S. Geological Survey, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, National Park Service, U.S. Forest Service, Natural Resources Conservation Service, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, Department of Defense, the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources as well as state wildlife agencies in surrounding states or beyond. Externally-funded research should contribute to science-based wildlife conservation and management and strengthen interdisciplinary collaborations across the department and Virginia Tech.

Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in wildlife science, ecology, biology, zoology, natural resources, forestry, range management, or a closely related field by appointment start date.
Demonstrated expertise in mammalogy and mammalian conservation ecology.
Evidence of potential for excellence in university teaching, field-based instruction, and student mentoring.
Evidence of strong potential to develop a productive, externally funded research program and peer-reviewed scholarship.

Preferred Qualifications

Postdoctoral or comparable professional research experience.
Experience with modern quantitative, geospatial, field, laboratory, technological, and/or experimental techniques relevant to mammalian conservation ecology.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with natural resource agencies, conservation organizations, and/or interdisciplinary research teams.
Experience mentoring graduate and undergraduate students.

Exempt: Not eligible for overtime

Regular

40

10/15/2026

Additional Information

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

The successful candidate will be required to have a criminal conviction check.

About Virginia Tech

Dedicated to its motto, Ut Prosim (That I May Serve), Virginia Tech pushes the boundaries of knowledge by taking a hands-on, transdisciplinary approach to preparing scholars to be leaders and problem-solvers. A comprehensive land-grant institution that enhances the quality of life in Virginia and throughout the world, Virginia Tech is an inclusive community dedicated to knowledge, discovery, and creativity. The university offers more than 280 majors to a diverse enrollment of more than 36,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students in eight undergraduate colleges, a school of medicine, a veterinary medicine college, Graduate School, and Honors College. The university has a significant presence across Virginia, including Blacksburg, the greater Washington, D.C. area, the Health Sciences and Technology Campus in Roanoke, sites in Newport News and Richmond, and numerous Extension offices and research institutes. A leading global research institution, Virginia Tech conducts more than $650 million in research annually.

Virginia Tech endorses and encourages participation in professional development opportunities and university shared governance. These valuable contributions to university shared governance provide important representation and perspective, along with opportunities for unique and impactful professional development.

Techniques for dealing with a variety of individuals from various socio-economic, ethnic and cultural backgrounds.

The Environmental Senior Project Manager is responsible for the successful execution of environmental consulting projects from proposal development through project closeout and collection. This role provides technical leadership, project oversight, client management, staff development, and financial accountability across multiple projects. The Environmental Senior Project Manager serves as the primary client contact on assigned projects, mentors technical staff, and ensures projects are delivered safely, profitably, and in accordance with company standards while demonstrating ECS Core Values.

Responsibilities

Performs Phase I Environmental Site Assessments independently as an Environmental Professional
Reviews Phase I ESA reports prepared by junior staff
Oversees project scheduling, execution, reporting, and closeout
Communicates project findings and recommendations to clients and Principals
Performs detailed technical reviews of reports and conclusions
Leads and mentors junior staff and supports professional development across the team
Manages environmental consulting projects from proposal through project closeout
Serves as the primary client contact for assigned projects
Maintains and expands client relationships and business opportunities
Manages project budgets, profitability, invoicing, and collections
Reviews and approves project change orders and budgeting adjustments
Schedules, trains, and oversees technical staff assigned to projects
Coordinates project staffing and resource allocation
Oversees multiple projects simultaneously and ensures successful project execution
Reviews and approves proposals, scopes of work, and fee estimates
Prepares and reviews environmental reports, analyses, and recommendations
Conducts senior-level reviews of project deliverables before Principal review
Leads client meetings and project discussions
Supports staffing decisions in collaboration with department leadership
Provides guidance on technical, operational, and project management issues
Performs additional project leadership and technical duties as assigned

Required Qualifications

5 years of related experience
Bachelor's and/or Master's of Science in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Natural or Environmental Science, Geology, or other degree relevant to the practice of Environmental Consulting
Must have the ability to obtain a local license through reciprocity within three months of hire date
Additional licensure or certifications may be required depending on the type of work performed

Extensive knowledge of environmental principles, regulations, and consulting practices
Extensive knowledge of permitting requirements and environmental investigation methodologies
Excellent project management and consulting skills
Strong leadership, coaching, and team development capabilities
Strong financial management and budgeting skills
Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously
Ability to build and maintain long-term client relationships
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Ability to review and evaluate technical work produced by others
Strong business development and client growth capabilities
If driving for or on behalf of any ECS subsidiary, a valid driver's license is required

Military Qualifications

The following US Military ranks will qualify for this position IF they also meet the education and licenses requirements from the above section titled "Required Qualifications":
E-7

ECS Group of Companies (ECS) was founded in 1988 with the goal to raise the standards of professional engineering consulting. Today, we are a leader in geotechnical, construction materials, environmental and building science + infrastructure consulting services. We are employee-owned with more than 3,00 employees in 100+ offices and testing facilities coast to coast. ECS is currently ranked #60 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 500 Design Firms (April 2026), #148 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 200 Environmental Firms (October 2025) and #38 in Zweig Group’s Hot Firm List (June 2026). For additional information about ECS, visit: www.ecslimited.com.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist II
jobs.description:
Position Summary

Inspect, monitor and enforce established health codes, regulations and ordinances for Environmental Health Department's Consumer Health Protection Division; conduct inspections of assigned facilities for code and regulatory conformance; operate technical equipment; interpret data collected; identify and evaluate new and unusual situations based on professional knowledge ; interpret and disseminate environmental health information to industry, the general public and other agencies; reduce the risk and severity of public exposure to environmental health hazards; perform a variety of professional and technical tasks in support of assigned division.

Job descriptions are intended to present a general list of tasks/duties performed by employees within this job classification. Job Descriptions are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job.

Essential And Supplemental Functions

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Essential functions may include; but are not limited to the functions listed below. Mustbe able to perform the essential functions of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation.

Ensure compliance of assigned environmental health areas with applicable laws, rules and regulations related to the provision of environmental health protection and related services.
Detect community environmental health hazards based on scientific knowledge; reduce the risk and severity of public exposure to environmental health hazards through surveillance and intervention; develop recommended policies and plans of action.
Conduct inspections and monitor assigned facilities for code and regulatory conformance; issue citations and secure facilities for failure to comply with codes and regulations.
Develop survey instruments; conduct surveys, interpret data collected and record survey results; implement program changes in response to results.
Identify and evaluate new and unusual environmental health situations based on professional knowledge and scientific background.
Receive and investigate environmental complaints relative to assigned areas.
Consult with parties failing to meet established codes and regulations; develop, plan and recommend alternative solutions; design, develop and conduct workshops concerning assigned area of responsibility.
Review permit applications relative to assigned area; approve or deny the issuance of permits.
Maintain records and develop reports concerning new or ongoing programs and program effectiveness within assigned area of responsibility.
Operate specialized technical equipment used in monitoring environmental conditions; interpret and apply information obtained.
Coordinate assigned environmental health activities with other divisions, departments and outside agencies.
Develop, coordinate and administer training; proctor exams, and issue documents of certification.
Assist in the preparation of legal cases pertaining to permitted facilities and represent the City of Albuquerque by personal testimony.

When assigned to Consumer Health Protection Division:

Conduct field inspections of public swimming pools/spas; implement and enforce the City's swimming pool/spa certification program.
Conduct field inspection of food establishments; ensure compliance with applicable codes and regulations including principles of Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point.
Identify, interpret and respond to unusual situations that occur resulting from routine inspection and public interaction.
Respond to noise complaints from the general public; enforce and resolve the City's noise ordinance.

SUPPLEMENTAL FUNCTIONS:

Attend and participate in professional group meetings; stay abreast of new trends and innovations in the assigned field of environmental health
Perform related duties and responsibilities as required.
Use, maintain and monitor electronic database for quality assurance.

Minimum Education, Experience And Additional Requirements

Education and experience directly related to the minimum requirements below may be interchangeable on a year for year basis.

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in engineering, chemistry, mathematics, geology, ecology, biology, or public health; and

Four (4) years of experience monitoring and enforcing ordinances, codes or regulations.

Experience in monitoring and enforcing environmental ordinances, codes or regulations is preferred.

Additional Requirements

Possession of a valid New Mexico Driver's License, or the ability to obtain by date of hire.

Possession of a City Operator's Permit (COP) within six (6) months from date of hire.

When assigned to Consumer Health Protection Division possession of Certified Professional - Food Safety (CPFS) Credential or ability to obtain within three (3) years from date of hire.

When assigned to Consumer Health Protection Division possession of National Swimming Pool Foundation Certified Pool Operator (CPO) certification or Certified Pool & Spa Inspector (CPI) credential or ability to obtain within one (1) year from date of hire.

Working Conditions

Environmental

Office, shop or field environment; travel from site to site; possible exposure to hazardous chemicals, smoke, fumes, gases and pathogens carried by insects and/or animals. Working outside in hot and cold environmental conditions.

Physical

Essential and supplemental functions may require maintaining physical condition necessary for climbing ladders, standing, walking and sitting for prolonged periods and medium to heavy lifting and carrying of monitors and equipment.

When assigned to the Environmental Services or Air Quality Division:

Essential and supplemental functions may require maintaining physical condition necessary for performing field work and wearing a respirator while performing light to moderate lifting and carrying, standing, walking and sitting for prolonged periods; participate in the medical monitoring program as per OSHA regulation.

We have an exciting opportunity to join the Enabling Team in Engineering Technical Services (ETS)
at Southern Water as a Senior Environmental Advisor
. You will play a key role in delivering environmental solutions that protect water resources, enhance ecosystems, and contribute to long-term sustainability.

What You Will Be Responsible For

Providing expert environmental advice throughout project lifecycles, from concept and design through to construction.
Leading or overseeing environmental assessments, surveys, investigations, and mitigation strategies.
Ensuring projects comply with environmental legislation, planning requirements, permits, licences, and industry best practice.
Advising on water resources, pollution prevention, waste management, and environmental permitting matters.
Managing specialist environmental consultants and contractors, ensuring high-quality technical outputs.
Supporting stakeholder engagement with regulators, local authorities, statutory bodies, landowners, and community groups.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

We're looking for someone who combines strong technical environmental knowledge with excellent communication and stakeholder management skills but most importantly, a deep passion for the environment.

A degree (or higher qualification) in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Ecology, Geography, Environmental Engineering, or a related discipline.
Experience working within environmental consultancy, utilities, infrastructure, construction, engineering, or a similar environment.
Excellent organisational, written and verbal communication skills.
Strong knowledge of UK environmental legislation, planning processes, and environmental management practices.
Experience undertaking or managing environmental assessments and coordinating environmental inputs to projects.
Experience managing specialist consultants and coordinating multiple stakeholders.
Membership of a relevant professional institution such as ISEP, CIWEM, or equivalent.
Chartered status, or working towards chartership, would be advantageous.

jobs.title: GIS Specialist
jobs.description:
Nau mai, haere mai ki a Fulton Hogan | Join us at Fulton Hogan

We're looking for a GIS Specialist to join our team in Canterbury. In this role, you'll design and support web-based geospatial solutions, turn complex spatial data into practical tools for our projects, and help teams make smarter decisions on the ground. Good Work here means building digital products that people actually use and improving how we deliver infrastructure for our communities.

Mō te tūranga | About the role

As a GIS Specialist, you'll help shape how geospatial technology supports the design, construction and delivery of resilient infrastructure across Aotearoa. This role works across digital, project and operational teams, with a strong focus on web GIS, data quality, analysis and practical solution delivery. You'll work with a broad mix of spatial data, from design models and imagery through to survey and project information, creating tools that make it easier for teams to understand what's happening and what to do next. It's a role for someone who likes solving real problems, working side by side with good people, and turning ideas into useful outcomes.

Ngā kawenga matua | Key responsibilities

Design, configure and support geospatial solutions using the ArcGIS ecosystem, with a strong focus on web mapping applications.
Manage and maintain web maps, apps and content across ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Enterprise.
Deliver GIS services including data processing, spatial analysis, quality control and interactive digital information products.
Gather technical requirements, document business processes and help shape practical geospatial solutions for project and business needs.
Build strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders and support wider adoption of geospatial technology across the business.
Identify opportunities to improve data integration, efficiency and decision-making; while keeping safety, quality and environmental standards front of mind.

Kei te kimi mātou i tētahi e whai ana i ēnei pūkenga | We're looking for someone with

At least 3 years' experience configuring and deploying geospatial solutions using ArcGIS.
Strong understanding and the ability to implement spatial workflows, ideally across the Esri ArcGIS ecosystem and Safe Software FME Form/Desktop and Flow/Server.
Experience delivering web GIS, data processing, analysis and quality assurance in a practical business environment.
A confident, collaborative approach and the ability to build strong relationships across technical and non-technical teams.
Strong planning, organisation and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage changing priorities and keep moving forward.
A genuine focus on safety, quality and doing the job properly, especially when the stakes are high.
Experience in infrastructure, construction or related industries would be an advantage.
Experience with Autodesk AEC Collection, 12D or similar digital engineering tools would also be useful, but not essential.

He pai te mahi, he pai ngā painga | Good work, good benefits

At Fulton Hogan, we genuinely care about the wellbeing of our people and giving them the tools and opportunities they need to succeed and grow with us. You'll have access to:

Medical insurance and Life insurance after the eligibility period.
KiwiSaver employer contributions after service milestones, up to 7%.
Parental leave top‑up payment with additional return‑to‑work support.
Ongoing training and development, with clear career growth and progression opportunities.
Great discounts at a wide range of retailers.

Ko wai mātou | About us

Fulton Hogan is an integrated infrastructure, construction and services business working across New Zealand and Australia. We partner with clients and communities to design, build, operate and maintain critical assets - from bitumen and quarries to roads, water and energy. Our people are united by a simple purpose: to create, connect and care for communities, while reducing environmental impact and supporting more sustainable futures.

Learn more about us at Homepage - Fulton Hogan and apply to be part of our growing industry.

Me pēhea te tono | How to apply:

If you're keen to build smarter geospatial solutions and do good work that makes a real difference across our projects and communities, apply now and start your journey with our Fulton Hogan whānau.

All successful candidates must undergo and pass a pre‑employment medical and drug screen prior to employment.

jobs.title: Ecological Program Specialist
jobs.description:
THE POSITION

NOTE: THIS IS A REPOSTING OF CS-2026-52941-54485. IF YOU APPLIED UNDER THE PREVIOUS POSTING WHICH WAS OPEN FROM JULY 6, 2026 TO JULY 20, 2026, YOU CANNOT SUBMIT A NEW APPLICATION.

Join a team that safeguards the natural places people and wildlife depend on every day! The Ecological Program Specialist with the Pennsylvania Game Commission plays an important role in protecting wildlife and guiding responsible natural resource use. This position offers a chance to work across forests, wetlands, and open lands to support healthy habitats. The work is meaningful and supports conservation efforts that benefit people and wildlife across the state. It is a great role for someone who enjoys science, outdoor work, and teamwork!

DESCRIPTION OF WORK

This position supports statewide environmental and land management efforts that guide safe and responsible oil, gas, and mineral activities on State Game Lands. It helps protect wildlife, habitats, and natural resources through careful planning, evaluation, and coordination. As a Ecological Program specialist, you will perform the following duties:

Field Inspections: Conduct site reviews to check resource development activities and identify impacts to wildlife and habitats
Plan Evaluation: Review and assess construction and permit plans to reduce or prevent harm to species and ecosystems
Issue Investigation: Investigate and address environmental problems caused by oil or gas operations on State Game Lands
Data Management: Maintain lease records, agreements, spatial data, and other information used for program decisions
Collaboration: Work with regional staff and other partners to restore sites and support responsible resource development
Technical Guidance: Provide recommendations on regulations, environmental requirements, and protection of wildlife resources

Interested in learning more? Additional details regarding this position can be found in the position description .

Work Schedule and Additional Information:

Full-time employment
Work hours are 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday - Friday, with a 30-minute lunch.
Telework: You may have the opportunity to work from home (telework) part-time. Telework is not permitted during the initial six-month probationary period; eligibility may be granted upon its successful completion. In order to telework, you must have a securely configured high-speed internet connection and work from an approved location inside Pennsylvania. If you are unable to telework, you will have the option to report to the headquarters office in Harrisburg. The ability to telework is subject to change at any time. Additional details may be provided during the interview.
Salary:In some cases, the starting salary may be non-negotiable.
You will receive further communication regarding this position via email. Check your email, including spam/junk folders, for these notices.

QUALIFICATIONS

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE, TRAINING & ELIGIBILITY

Minimum Experience and Training Requirements:

One year of experience as a Wildlife Biologist 2 or Natural Resource Program Specialist 1 (Commonwealth job title or equivalent Federal Government job title, as determined by the Office of Administration); or
Three years of experience as a Forester (Commonwealth job title or equivalent Federal Government job title, as determined by the Office of Administration); or
Three years of professional experience in management of plant, wildlife, or natural resources and a bachelor's degree in biology, botany, ecology, environmental science, forestry, natural resources management, or a closely related field; or
An equivalent combination of experience and training.

Other Requirements:

You must meet the PA residency requirement . For more information on ways to meet PA residency requirements, follow the link and click on Residency Guidelines.
You must be able to perform essential job functions.

How to Apply:

Resumes, cover letters, and similar documents will not be reviewed, and the information contained therein will not be considered for the purposes of determining your eligibility for the position. Information to support your eligibility for the position must be provided on the application (i.e., relevant, detailed experience/education).
If you are claiming education in your answers to the supplemental application questions, you must attach a copy of your college transcripts for your claim to be accepted toward meeting the minimum requirements. Unofficial transcripts are acceptable.
Your application must be submitted by the posting closing date . Late applications and other required materials will not be accepted.
Failure to comply with the above application requirements may eliminate you from consideration for this position.

jobs.title: Environmental Inspectors (Field Based)
jobs.description:
ERM
is hiring Environmental Inspectors
to conduct inspections at construction sites in South Bay
,
California.
Successful candidates must be flexible and responsive to a changing work environment where schedules, site locations, and tasks fluctuate according to the needs of the project. They must understand industry safety procedures and practices, including experience implementing them on the job. The individual needs to be focused on safety and the need to keep the whole team safe. They need to be a proactive communicator and be able to work with construction personnel in the field to educate them about the project requirements and problem solve when issues arise. They need to practice frequent and clear communication with the whole team to relay and resolve issues and make sure the team is delivering the services our clients expect. Must be able to inspect construction sites to ensure compliance with client internal procedures, permit conditions and landowner agreements. Inspectors may need to deliver environmental tailboard trainings to crews in the field. The EI should be familiar with typical construction BMPs and good housekeeping procedures. The role of an environmental inspector requires technical skills, as well as strong organizational and communication skills. This is a part-time (20+ hours/week), limited-term role with a duration of 12 months
and the possibility of renewal.

Responsibilities

Conducting field inspections, monitoring and field survey work as directed.
Interacting with and serving as a point of contact with agency officials, regulatory agency staff, landowners, contractors, clients, and other project members.
Reviewing and implementing project documents and providing support and critical judgment on environmental compliance issues.
Critically assessing environmental conditions in the field to evaluate potential environmental impacts from construction.
Evaluating potential issues and concerns ahead of construction activities.
Overseeing the proper implementation of mitigation measures.
Conducting environmental sampling (hydrostatic test water, soil, etc.) and/or collect samples of stormwater at designated locations and visually inspect the quality of the sample.
Overseeing and verifying flagging of wetland boundaries, cultural and biological resources exclusion zones, refueling zones, etc.
Inspecting and documenting compliance with a project's environmental requirements by preparing daily written inspection reports that provide up-to-date and consistent written and photo documentation of activities observed in the field.
Participating in various construction meetings.
Evaluating restoration activities.
Support compliance with environmental regulations concerning spill prevention, wastewater, stormwater, storage tanks, and waste management.
Perform work safely, complying with ERM and client requirements and always wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including hardhat, safety boots, safety glasses, hearing protection, and orange high-visibility vest.
Work within quality/budget/schedule expectations and scope-specific assignments.
Communicate with ERM Project Manager, Senior EIs, various regulatory agencies, and client staff and subcontracts at the various client facilities. Key aspect of work is to develop relationship with client personnel at the facilities to promote environmental stewardship.

Requirements

A minimum of 2 years of construction inspection or monitoring is required; stormwater inspection experience is a plus.
Bachelor’s Degree in an environmental discipline is preferred.
A general knowledge of environmental disciplines including, SWPPP BMP installation and maintenance, water resource protection, biology, materials storage and stockpiles, air quality and dust control, Hazmat storage, spill control and countermeasures, water and soil management and waste management
Ability to communicate effectively and a willingness to learn and take direction from more senior Environmental Inspectors.
A working vehicle, valid driver’s license, and a good driving record; ability to drive to the various project locations.
Effective observational and organization skills; experience recording detailed technical data a plus.
Effective communication skills with ERM and client staff.
Experience with water and soil sample collection a plus.
Proficient in basic computer skills (i.e. Microsoft Outlook, Work, Excel) for communication and preparation of inspection documentation.
Daily hours and duration are variable depending on the site location and work to be completed.
Other desired experience includes soil and water sampling, SWPPP certifications, Hazmat evaluations and or sampling, species specific biology or nesting bird experience and cultural resources.

jobs.title: Outdoor Recreation and Interpretation Program Coordinator (Natural Resource Program Specialist 2)
jobs.description:
THE POSITION

Step into a role that makes Pennsylvania’s outdoor spaces come alive! As the Outdoor Recreation and Interpretation Program Coordinator for the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, you help people discover new ways to explore nature. We partner with leading insurance carriers and handle everything from emergency cleanup to complete rebuilds, with a focus on safety, integrity, and advocacy. As entrepreneurs, we take full ownership of the work we do and the families we serve.

At Merit, our purpose is simple and non-negotiable: we work together as a team so we can change lives.
Teamwork is the foundation of everything we do—because teamwork creates impact, and impact changes lives. We exist to help people, and the only way we do that at the highest level is by moving as one team, aligned in mission, values, and execution.

Why we exist.
We exist for two families. The families we serve and the families inside this company. When we work together and serve our clients at the highest level, both families win.

The Contents Technician
is responsible for the hands-on packing, cleaning, and restoration of customer contents affected by fire, water, or other covered losses, helping return items to pre-loss condition. This role documents and inventories customer belongings from the moment of pack-out through final return, maintaining accurate photographs, itemized records, and disposition notes throughout the process.

The Contents Technician communicates directly with customers with care and professionalism, inspects completed work for quality, and helps maintain the contents processing facility and equipment. This role supports the broader Contents team by keeping daily logs current and coordinating closely with Project Managers, Supervisors, and Managers to keep every job on track.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Core duties and responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

Contents Packing & Documentation

Photograph, identify, and inventory customer's contents at the time of pack-out
Wrap, package, and label contents for transport to the cleaning facility
Maintain accurate inventory of all processed contents and their disposition
Complete a daily log of work performed

Cleaning & Restoration

Unwrap, assess, and clean contents according to established procedures
Identify, re-wrap, package, and label cleaned contents for storage or return
Inspect completed work to confirm it meets quality standards
Perform basic maintenance on contents cleaning equipment

Customer Service & Communication

Communicate effectively and professionally with customers throughout the contents process
Return cleaned and restored property to the customer once building restoration is complete
Wait on shop customers as needed

Facility & Shop Maintenance

Vacuum and maintain cleanliness of the shop
Clean the shop bathroom and drying rooms
Wash shop towels and moving blankets
Pull trash and recycling
Provide the Branch Manager with a list of supplies needed

Collaboration & Reporting

Determine the appropriate sequence of steps for cleaning and restoring each customer's contents
Maintain timely and effective communication with Project Managers, Supervisors, and Managers

Requirements

High school diploma or GED
Ability to apply basic math skills to determine appropriate equipment type and quantity needed for a job
Basic proficiency with computers, email, and mobile devices used to record and report daily activity
Familiarity with contents inventory or job-tracking software is a plus, or a fast learner
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy in documentation and quality control
Clear, professional communicator, comfortable interacting with customers in stressful situations
Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
IICRC certification in contents processing or a related discipline is a plus, though not required for this position
Valid driver's license and reliable transportation preferred

WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The employee is regularly required to sit, use hands to finger, handle, or feel, reach with hands and arms, and talk or hear, and is frequently required to stand and walk
The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 40 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds
Work is carried out both on customer property and within the company's contents processing facility
The employee may encounter properties without utilities or heat, fire damage, or mold and other organic growth, and should follow appropriate safety protocols and use provided personal protective equipment when handling contaminated or hazardous materials
Daily exposure to the contents processing area where inventory, supplies, and equipment are stored and maintained is typical
The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate

We believe water is more than a resource, it's a shared responsibility. As part of our Water Business Group, you’ll help shape how communities manage water for generations to come. From delivering safe drinking water and treating wastewater responsibly to developing sustainable water supplies and protecting lives and property through flood control, your work will directly support public health, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure resilience. We bring together experts across disciplines to solve complex challenges with bold thinking and technical excellence. Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

The Business Class Lead (BCL) will work with the Business Class Director (BCD) and HDR peers on monitoring and improvement of technical competencies, staff development, and execution of work associated with water resource planning that meets federal planning standards and expectations. The overall goal of the role is to promote a quality culture, drive or support BC initiatives that drive growth and project delivery, and work with areas to hire, train and support career progression of staff within this technical service area.

The successful candidate will bring a vision for delivery, mentoring, and market growth; and have a proven ability to work broadly with teams to deliver positive outcomes for projects. The BCL will collaborate on business class efforts with market sector directors, business group regional directors, other business class leaders, local business group leaders, local market sector (marketing) leaders, cross sector leadership, and area staff.

The BCL responsibilities include the following:

Fostering a quality culture though project delivery excellence and staff coaching. Serve as a Quality Control lead, technical advisor, and technical lead (i.e., Project Manager or Task Manager) for specific projects. Work with project teams to field needs and align staff to meet delivery expectations and develop strategy to promote knowledge transfer and staff development within water resource plan formulation.
Leading or supporting Business Class sponsored standards and guidelines (i.e., best practices) technical tools, checklists, workflows, and techniques to enhance service quality and efficiency. Promoting forward thinking delivery and strategy approaches as well as technology use and adoption.
Participating in tactical planning including engagement others within HDR to align initiatives with market drivers and client needs. Maintain awareness related to industry trends and drivers. Implementing actions associated with annual planning including leading or supporting recruiting key positions in partnership with others.
Working with others within HDR including client facing and marketing staff to track, develop and share qualifications and project approaches. Engage on specific pursuits as a lead or team member. Drive industry facing strategies associated with technical service area (e.g., professional association engagement, webinars, workshops, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading plan formulation for Federal clients. Specific experience with the USACE’s Principles, Requirements and Guidelines (PR&G) ideal.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams to successful project outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
A minimum of 10 years experience
Professional registration, license or certification may be required based on role
Strong communication and listening skills
Ability to handle multiple assignments
Good leadership and organizational skills
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. jobs.title: Associate Environmental Health & Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Associate Environmental Health and Safety Specialist supports the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of environmental health and safety programs that promote regulatory compliance and a safe campus environment. Working under general supervision, the incumbent independently performs technical assignments, conducts inspections and investigations, develops training, and collaborates with campus stakeholders to identify and mitigate environmental health and safety risks. The position applies professional judgment to ensure compliance with applicable regulations, enhance operational safety, and contribute to university-wide environmental health and safety initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Implement, maintain, and continuously improve environmental health and safety programs, procedures, and compliance initiatives.
Conduct facility inspections, hazard assessments, and risk evaluations; document findings and recommend corrective actions.
Investigate incidents, accidents, complaints, and near-misses to identify root causes and support corrective action implementation.
Develop, deliver, and support environmental health and safety training and educational programs for campus stakeholders.
Monitor changes in environmental health and safety regulations and assist with updating policies, procedures, and compliance practices.
Coordinate hazardous waste management activities, routine waste inspections, and equipment calibration in accordance with established procedures.
Prepare reports, maintain accurate records, and analyze environmental health and safety metrics, trends, and program performance.
Serve as a primary contact for assigned environmental health and safety programs while providing technical guidance to university departments and external agencies.
Respond to emergency incidents and urgent campus safety needs to minimize risk and ensure regulatory compliance.
Provide lead work direction, training, and guidance to staff and student employees, while supporting continuous improvement initiatives.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Thorough knowledge of environmental health and safety principles, programs, regulations, and industry best practices.
Ability to conduct inspections, risk assessments, and incident investigations while developing effective corrective actions.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate complex issues and recommend practical solutions.
Knowledge of applicable environmental health and safety laws, regulatory requirements, and compliance standards.
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively collaborate with diverse stakeholders and deliver training.
Proficiency using environmental health and safety software, information systems, and reporting tools.
Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and handle sensitive information professionally.
Ability to build collaborative relationships, influence decision-making, and provide high-quality customer service.
Ability to work independently while adapting to changing priorities and supporting continuous improvement initiatives.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in a related field
An advanced degree in a related field may be substituted for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.
Two years of experience working in an environmental health and safety role.
Additional experience which demonstrates acquired and successfully applied knowledge and abilities shown above may be substituted for the required education on a year-for-year basis.

License

A valid driver's license is required for this position. Out of state candidates selected for the position must obtain a State of California driver's license within 10 days of hire in accordance with the California Department of Motor Vehicles regulations.

Once hired the employee must successfully complete the Defensive Driver Training Program provided by the State of California for California State University campuses.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in a related field
One or more EHS related certifications such as CSP, ASP, CIH, CHMM, REHS.
Working in an EHS role in higher education

Classification: Environmental Health & Safety Professional II

jobs.location: Newcastle Upon Tyne, England, United Kingdom
jobs.description:
Job Description

Your New Role

We are seeking an Associate Director or Technical Director in Freshwater Ecology to join our expanding Aquatic Ecology team. This is an outstanding opportunity for an established technical specialist who thrives on leading complex programmes, advising clients and regulators, and raising the bar for best practice across the industry.

You’ll act as a trusted authority on freshwater ecology, providing expertise across major UK and international infrastructure schemes, including DCO/NSIP projects, regulated water company frameworks, and long term capital programmes.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this influential role, you will:

Lead and guide the design of freshwater and aquatic ecology baseline survey programmes for EIAs and regulatory submissions.
Author highquality technical reports, including EIA chapters, WFD assessments, and planning deliverables for both UK and international clients.
Line manage and mentor talented aquatic ecologists, supporting their growth, wellbeing, and workloads.
Prepare competitive tenders and fee estimates for medium and large-scale freshwater ecology projects.
Support the management of the wider aquatic team—including health & safety, training, resource planning, and technical excellence.
Build and maintain a strong profile as a recognised technical expert, contributing to WSP’s Practice Area Networks and representing the business externally.

About The Team

Our Aquatic Ecology team works across freshwater, estuarine, and marine environments on a truly exciting range of projects.

Typical Portfolio Areas Include

River restoration and catchment enhancement schemes
Design of ecological monitoring programmes
Biodiversity Net Gain assessments
EIA and Water Framework Directive assessments
Salmonid habitat restoration and NEP projects for water companies
Routine biological monitoring
International development and R&D projects
You will collaborate closely with in-house experts in fluvial geomorphology, BNG, hydrology, and environmental planning, giving you the opportunity to influence multi-disciplinary solutions and shape future industry standards.

What We’re Looking For

You will bring:

Extensive professional experience in consultancy, regulatory bodies, or industry settings.
Advanced technical expertise in freshwater ecology, including protected species and habitat assessment.
A proven ability to deliver technically robust, scientifically rigorous reports for WFD assessments, EIAs, and Environmental Statements.
Strong understanding of UK water and ecology legislation and its application within the planning process.
Demonstrated experience managing and developing teams.
Proven project management skills, including tender preparation and budgeting.
A positive, collaborative, and engaging leadership style with excellent communication skills.

Why Join WSP?

At WSP, You’ll Be Part Of a Culture That Values Curiosity, Innovation, And The Drive To Make a Difference. You’ll Have

The freedom to define the direction of your specialist area
The support of a global ecology and environmental network
A variety of UK and international projects to grow your portfolio
Real opportunities for career development, leadership, and technical influence

This is your chance to lead, inspire, and help create healthier freshwater ecosystems for generations to come.

Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.

Work on landmark projects around the world and embrace opportunities to make an even bigger impact in the communities you care about.

What if you could do the best work of your life and create a legacy for yourself?

With us, you can. Apply today.

jobs.title: RECLAMATION WORKER
jobs.description:
Responsibilities

Responsible for soil investigation (SI), geotechnical investigation and ground condition assessment for large-scale reclamation and soil improvement projects.
Plan, coordinate and supervise various soil investigation works.
Supervise SI contractors and ensure works are carried out in accordance with approved method statements, specifications, ITP and project requirements.
Review and interpret borehole logs, CPT/CPTu data, vane shear results and laboratory test results.
Assist in developing and updating geotechnical/soil profiles and ground models.
Coordinate and supervise installation of geotechnical instrumentation.
Establish baseline readings and coordinate regular instrumentation monitoring and interpretation.
Monitor ground response during different stages of reclamation, filling, surcharge and consolidation.
Coordinate with soil improvement contractors, SI contractors, instrumentation contractors, surveyors, laboratories, consultants and client representatives.
Review instrumentation installation records, calibration certificates and monitoring data.
Verify the quality and reliability of SI and instrumentation data and coordinate laboratory testing.
Prepare daily, weekly and monthly SI/geotechnical monitoring reports.
Maintain proper records of boreholes, CPT/CPTu, VST, instrumentation and monitoring results.
Assist the Geotechnical Engineer/Project Manager in assessing settlement, consolidation, stability and ground improvement performance.
Provide technical recommendations where actual ground conditions differ from design assumptions.
Participate in site inspections, technical meetings, toolbox meetings and coordination meetings.
Ensure all geotechnical and SI activities comply with Singapore project requirements, safety requirements and relevant standards.
Perform other geotechnical and soil-investigation related duties as required by the project team.

Requirements

Degree/Diploma in Geotechnical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Engineering Geology, Geology or a related discipline.
Minimum 5 years of experience in construction projects with experience in geotechnical instrumentation, monitoring and site investigation.
Experience in reviewing geotechnical investigation reports, instrumentation data and onsite test results as well as preparing geotechnical monitoring and SI reports.
Good understanding of soil settlement, consolidation, pore pressure and lateral ground movement.
Good communication and coordination skills with the ability to work independently and supervise site investigation and instrumentation subcontractors.
Able to work in Tuas, 5.5 day work week

jobs.description:
SUMMARY:

JOB DESCRIPTION

This position's primary responsibilities include supporting utility projects by conducting environmental assessments, including stream/wetlands delineation, and permitting, plant and animal inventories, habitat assessments, environmental protection and mitigation planning, and environmental permitting. In addition, the position will provide support to the siting of electric transmission line and substation projects through the analysis of environmental, land use, cultural resource, and visual issues using a Geographic Information System (GIS) to determine the most viable siting opportunities.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
:

 Conducts field environmental assessments by traversing cleared and uncleared linear utility corridors and site-specific parcels to delineate, GPS, and map streams, wetlands, habitat, and identify plants and animal species.

40%

 Prepares environmental and technical reports to document the findings of the natural resource assessments and supports environmental protection, mitigation planning, and permitting.

20%

 Provides regulatory and permitting application support; including but not limited to those associated with NEPA, SEPA, Army Corps of Engineers, US Fish and Wildlife Service, and other state and local environmental review authorities. Coordinates with applicable review agencies.

20%

 Supports line and substation siting by applying environmental principles

10%

 Prepares, estimates, and budgets for specific environmental activities and monitors project costs

5%

 Perform other duties as assigned by management.

5%

:

Moderately routine: general policies applied. Some decision making.

Exchange of information, which occasionally requires tact and/or diplomacy.

:

Who We Are

The Town of Harrisburg is one of the fastest-growing communities in North Carolina and considered one of the top ten affluent zip codes in the surrounding region. While growth has been exponential over the past ten years, the Town has been able to maintain its tight knit community-based mindset and strategically foster a work culture where customer service excellence is our #1 priority.

What We Need

An employee in this class is responsible for the administration, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Town's Geographic Information System (GIS), including enterprise geospatial databases, data integrity, spatial analysis, cartographic production, and GIS application support. Responsibilities include managing and maintaining geospatial datasets; developing maps, data visualizations, and analytical reports; conducting research and spatial analyses to support planning, infrastructure, and operational decision-making; and ensuring the accuracy, accessibility, and reliability of GIS information. Required Education And Experience

Graduation from a four-year college or university with a major coursework in Geography, Geospatial Science, Planning, Computer Science, Engineering, or a closely related field and at least 3 to 5 years of professional GIS experience, including data management, spatial analysis, and map production; or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience working in local government or supporting municipal operations, including planning, engineering, public works, utilities, parks and recreation, or other public sector environments. STV is seeking an experienced Geospatial Manager to help lead and grow our survey, reality capture, and digital delivery capabilities across Texas. This opportunity will be based primarily in Frisco, Texas, there the flexibility for it to be in any STV Texas office and offers the chance to manage high-impact infrastructure work, guide technical teams, and shape how high-quality project data is captured, processed, and delivered.

Why STV?
You will join a collaborative team that is investing in the future infrastructure delivery—combining survey expertise, reality capture, automation, and digital tools to deliver better data, faster for our clients.

If you are a geospatial leader who enjoys mentoring teams, building strong client and project relationships, and turning complex field data into practical project intelligence, this role offers the platform to make a measurable impact across a growing Texas operation.

What You’ll Do

Manage and guide UAV/UAS, laser scanning, mobile mapping, LiDAR, GNSS, and reality capture efforts for transportation, utility, municipal, construction, and infrastructure projects.
Process, manage, and quality-check geospatial data using tools such as Trimble Business Center, Leica Cyclone, DJI Terra, Pix4D, Civil 3D, and related platforms.
Develop accurate digital deliverables, including point clouds, orthomosaics, terrain models, surface models, existing conditions models, utility mapping, and 3D reality capture datasets.
Collaborate with survey crews, engineers, utility teams, construction professionals, and project managers to turn field data into reliable project intelligence.
Support boundary, deed, easement, right-of-way, survey, utility, construction, and as-built deliverables in coordination with licensed survey professionals.
Integrate geospatial data into design and digital delivery workflows using Civil 3D, OpenRoads, ArcGIS, MicroStation, and related applications.
Help advance STV’s Better Data, Faster initiative by improving workflows, applying automation, and supporting the use of AI, digital twins, and reality capture technology.
Lead technical input for scopes, proposals, estimates, client discussions, standards, and best practices for geospatial and reality capture services.
Serve as a trusted technical and managerial resource for field teams, CAD staff, survey technicians, engineers, and multidisciplinary project teams while maintaining safe and compliant practices.

What You’ll Bring

10+ years of experience in surveying, geomatics, geospatial technology, reality capture, or a related field.
Hands-on experience with UAV/UAS, LiDAR, laser scanning, photogrammetry, GNSS, and geospatial data processing workflows.
Strong knowledge of survey principles, coordinate systems, control networks, field-to-finish workflows, and data quality standards.
Experience supporting transportation, municipal, utility, land development, construction, or infrastructure projects.
Proficiency with tools such as Trimble Business Center, Civil 3D, Microsoft Office, Leica Cyclone, Pix4D, DJI Terra, ArcGIS Pro, OpenRoads, MicroStation, Carlson Survey, or similar platforms.
Strong communication, problem-solving, organization, and collaboration skills.
