jobs.title: Scientist (Water Ecology)
jobs.description:
Company Description

Job Description

***IMPORTANT NOTE: Candidate(s) selected for the Scientist (Water Ecology) position through this posting will be hired on a provisional basis. To be considered for permanent employment in this role, provisional employees will need to take and pass the next civil service examination for Scientist (Water Ecology) and obtain a list number issued by the NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services. Please be aware that employees who do not take and pass the exam may not be able to continue in the provisional position.***

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) enriches the environment and protects public health for all New Yorkers by providing 1.1 billion gallons of high quality drinking water, managing wastewater and stormwater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal water and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 6,000 employees. DEP's water supply system is comprised of 19 reservoirs and 3 controlled lakes throughout the system's 2,000 square mile watershed that extends 125 miles north and west of the City.

The Bureau of Wastewater Treatment (BWT) is responsible for the operation and maintenance of all facilities related to the treatment of sewage within the five boroughs of the City. This includes 14 wastewater treatment plants, sludge dewatering facilities, collections facilities (pumping stations, combined sewer overflow retention facilities, regulators, tide gates, etc.), wastewater laboratories and harbor vessels.

Under supervision, with some latitude for the exercise of independent initiative and judgment, the selected candidate will be responsible for participating in year round sampling in all weather conditions during Harbor Survey Cruises and field surveys for the Remote Monitoring Program; assisting in the production of annual reports and assisting with the development and review of additional sampling programs. Duties will include: On board processing of samples following strict SOPs; assist in the calibration and repair of instruments; schedule and perform routine maintenance on instruments and stations; assist the field supervisor with placement of monitoring locations; prepare graphics, maps, and/or text for Annual report; perform data analysis as requested; proofread and perform QA/QC for report production; develop new sampling initiatives as required; assists with memos/reports and other documents related to additional sampling; and lift and carry coolers weighing up to 50 pounds.

SCIENTIST (WATER ECOLOGY) - 21538

Qualifications

A masters degree from an accredited college or university in one of the following areas of study: environmental or chemical engineering, limnology, environmental science, marine science, geology, biology, earth science, chemistry, physics, or health science; or
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university with 24 semester credits in one or a combination of the areas of study described in ""1"" above, at least 12 of which must have been in one of these areas of study; and at least one year of satisfactory full time experience, which may not have been part of graduate or undergraduate course work, working in the field of water quality planning, management or

research or performing environmental laboratory analyses, and/or environmental field sampling of water; or

An associate degree from an accredited college or university including or supplemented by 24 semester credits in one or a combination of the areas of study described in "1" above, at least 12 of which must have been in one of these areas of study; and at least three years of satisfactory full time experience as described in "2" above.

Additional Requirements

To be assigned to Assignment Levels II or III, all candidates must have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university as described in "2" above and must have one additional year of the experience described in "2" above for a total of two years of experience.

Special Note

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for an Environmental Engineer (Professional Engineer)
for our Columbus, Ohio office. We will also consider applicants for our Cincinnati, Dayton, Ohio; Cleveland, Ohio; Indianapolis, Indiana; Lexington and Louisville, Kentucky offices.

At WSP, you can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates different perspectives and innovative thinking. As part of our Earth & Environment team, you will collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry to help clients solve complex environmental challenges, protect natural resources, and build a more sustainable future. You'll have access to national expertise, global resources, and meaningful opportunities to grow your career while doing the work the world needs. With us, you can.

As an integral member of our Earth & Environment Team, you will actively participate in a variety of projects that support a growing organization focused on achieving client objectives and addressing their challenges. You will join a team of professionals dedicated to providing environmental consulting services.

At WSP, you'll find the culture, flexibility, and opportunities to build a career as unique as you. Our people are empowered to explore new challenges, collaborate across disciplines, and make a lasting impact on communities around the world. We foster an environment that is:

Open – We seek out different perspectives, ideas, and ways of working.
Curious – We nurture innovation and encourage new thinking.
Passionate – We take pride in delivering meaningful work that positively impacts society and the environment.
Adaptable – We embrace change and view it as an opportunity for growth and development.

Whether your goal is to deepen your technical expertise, lead complex projects, mentor future professionals, or expand your influence across the business, WSP offers the tools, resources, and support to help you grow. From mentorship and technical learning opportunities to leadership development and multidisciplinary collaboration, you'll be empowered to shape your own career path.

Key Tasks and Areas of Focus Assist in developing processes and infrastructure related to water supply, wastewater treatment, hazardous or solid waste disposal, air emission sources, and pollution control.
Work to preserve environmental quality of air, water, and land resources.
Generate accurate and concise reports and documentation detailing field conditions.
Assess and provide guidance regarding short- and long-term risks to ecological and human health.
Ensure that responsibilities are executed and maintained at a quality level that meets or exceeds industry standards.
Experience in environmental, health and safety compliance.
Support business development activities as part of your role within the team.

Your Impact

As a member of our Earth & Environment Team, you will collaborate closely with team members to provide strategic direction and support for existing client relationships. In the capacity of Project Engineer, you will be responsible for managing current and future projects, engaging with clients daily to establish and guide the strategic direction for project execution.
You will independently manage and execute projects to ensure compliance with established schedules. This role involves performing moderately complex technical tasks within broad work scopes, as well as planning, scheduling, conducting, and coordinating project work for large-scale assignments.
Your responsibilities include preparing technical proposals and reports, either in whole or in part, based on the size and complexity of each document. You will demonstrate competency across several areas, including engineering, field supervision, technical expertise, and task management. Additionally, you will motivate, train, and mentor junior staff assigned to your tasks or projects.
The position comprises approximately 80% office work and 20% field work, covering a variety of projects such as industrial, commercial, and State and Federal sites. You will be responsible for preparing technical reports and related documents and assisting with business development.
Further duties include preparing components of investigation and engineering reports, such as work summaries, data summaries, engineering calculations, summary tables, figures, engineering drawings and specifications, and report text. You will also conduct technical evaluations and provide recommendations as required.
As the primary point of contact for subcontractors, you will direct junior-level staff overseeing field activities, organize field work, assign tasks, and provide guidance to staff specialists in field task management. Your role also involves assisting in subcontractor procurement and overseeing field activities such as drilling (including DPT/Geoprobe, HSA, and Sonic), soil excavation, demolitions, and remediation system installations.
You will review contractor submittals, including equipment documentation, Work Plans, and QA/QC plans, and will be responsible for tracking payment applications, requests for information, change order requests, and general construction phase submittals. The role requires travel to project sites as needed, which may include overnight travel.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Master's degree in Environmental Engineering or equivalent discipline.
7–10 years of relevant experience.
Current Professional Engineer (PE) license or ability to obtain within six months of hire.
Strong computer and writing skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Ability to interact effectively with regulatory agencies, stakeholders, and clients.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond a typical work schedule.
Ability and willingness to travel to project sites as necessary.
Excellent time management and compliance tracking skills.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated initiative, attention to detail, and ability to work independently.
Proficiency with technical and business writing, office automation, and communication software.
Proficiency with discipline-specific design software and engineering tools.
Proven commitment to workplace safety and adherence to WSP health and safety policies.
Experience managing small to mid-size projects, including project scoping, budget tracking, and resource management.
Ability to plan and conduct inspections and investigations of facilities and structures.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to mentor junior staff while maintaining strict adherence to QA/QC procedures.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Experience managing small to mid-size projects.
40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120) with annual refresher preferred.
Basic First Aid and Adult CPR training desired.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

jobs.title: Radiation Field Scientist, Bureau of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
jobs.description:
Company Description

Job Description

The Office of Radiological Health (ORH) licenses and inspects more than 7,000 facilities using radioactive materials and x-ray producing equipment throughout New York City to ensure compliance with public health and safety regulations. The program is managed in accordance with statutory authority, delegations from, or agreements with NRC, FDA, and NY State The Bureau of Environmental Sciences and Engineering (ESE) is looking to hire a Scientist Level II for the Office of Radiological Health (ORH). The candidate will inspect medical and research facilities that use radiation producing equipment, assess compliance with New York City Health Code and other applicable regulations, and ensure the safety of patients, staff and the public. This position plays a critical role in protecting public health by ensuring that facilities are properly registered and are implementing policies and procedures that reduce unnecessary exposure to ionizing radiation.

Duties Will Include But Not Be Limited To

Schedule and inspect facilities that use radiation-producing equipment throughout New York City for compliance with NYC Health Code and applicable State and Federal regulations.
Perform on-site tests of radiation-producing equipment installations.
Review and verify facility license and registration information and evaluate quality control procedures.
Prepare reports of inspection using agency protocols, forms and tools.
Prepare and serve court summons and tribunal hearing notices when specific violations of applicable City, State and Federal laws and regulations are found, and appear before tribunal to testify when necessary.
Participate in emergency training exercises and drills and assist in emergency response.
Operating a motor vehicle to perform job duties.

Preferred Skills

Knowledge of applicable federal, state and local regulations, standards, and protocols pertaining to radiation safety and control, including New York City Health Code Article 175.
Ability to read, comprehend and interpret written materials such as laws, regulations, policies and procedures.
Ability to interpret radiological measurements and survey results.
Knowledge of radiation safety, dosimetry, and radiation protection principles.
Knowledge of radiation detection instruments and equipment.
Ability to read and interpret data from meters and other measuring devices.
Ability to prepare and interpret data presented in graphs, tables, charts and narrative formats.
Ability to accurately document inspections and evaluations.
Ability to recognize unsafe or inadequate conditions and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to think critically and solve problems.
Excellent organizational and time management skills

Why You Should Work For Us

Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. For more information, please visit the U.S. Department of Education's website (https://studentaid.gov/pslf/)
Benefits: City employees are entitled to unmatched benefits such as:
a premium-free health insurance plan that saves employees over $10K annually, per a 2024 assessment.
additional health, fitness, and financial benefits may be available based on the position's associated union/benefit fund.
a public sector defined benefit pension plan with steady monthly payments in retirement.
a tax-deferred savings program and
a robust Worksite Wellness Program that offers resources and opportunities to keep you healthy while serving New Yorkers.
Work From Home Policy: Depending on your position, you may be able to work up to two days during the week from home.
Job Security - you could enjoy more job security compared to private sector employment and be able to contribute to making NYC a healthy place to live and work.

Established in 1805, the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC Health Department) is the oldest and largest health department in the U.S., dedicated to protecting and improving the health of NYC. Our mission is to safeguard the health of every resident and cultivate a city where everyone, regardless of age, background, or location, can achieve their optimal health. We provide a wide array of programs and services focused on food and nutrition, anti-tobacco support, chronic disease prevention, HIV/AIDS treatment, family and child health, environmental health, mental health, and social justice initiatives. As the primary population health strategist and policy authority for NYC, with a rich history of public health initiatives and scientific advancements, from addressing the 1822 yellow fever outbreak to the COVID-19 pandemic, we serve as a global leader in public health innovation and expertise.

Come join us and help to continue our efforts in making a difference in the lives of all New Yorkers!

jobs.description:
Department: Manatt Real Estate

Job Number: 100589

Offices: Los Angeles; Orange County; San Diego

With 500+ professionals and 350+ business professionals, Manatt, Phelps & Phillips, LLP is a multidisciplinary, integrated national professional services firm known for quality and an extraordinary commitment to clients. The Firm’s groundbreaking approach, combining legal services, advocacy, and business strategy, differentiates Manatt and delivers a distinct value proposition.

Opportunity

Manatt, Phelps & Phillips, LLP is seeking a Real Estate, Land Use & Environmental Paralegal to support attorneys on commercial real estate transactions, with a primary focus on title and survey review, due diligence, and closing coordination. The role also supports land use and environmental matters and requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple matters concurrently.

Responsibilities

Conduct detailed title review and analysis, including commitments, policies, pro formas, and endorsements.
Identify and analyze title exceptions, easements, covenants, restrictions, liens, and encumbrances; flag issues for attorney review.
Review title exception documents; prepare title review memoranda and title objection letters; track responses; and monitor cure items through closing.
Request and negotiate pro forma title insurance policies, including lender and owner policies.
Prepare estoppel certificates and SNDAs and coordinate execution with clients and third parties.
Review and analyze ALTA/NSPS surveys, including boundary lines, easements, encroachments, access, and survey exceptions.
Review and summarize third party reports and flag any issues for attorney review.
Order and track third party reports including zoning, property condition and environmental.
Coordinate with title companies, escrow agents, surveyors and other third parties to resolve title and survey issues.
Prepare and manage title objections letters, track responses, and monitor cure items through close.
Order and track title updates, bring-downs, and endorsements and confirm compliance with transaction requirements.
Reconcile title and survey materials to identify and resolve discrepancies.
Prepare, manage, and update closing checklists.
Review Preliminary closing statements and closing binders.
Organize and maintain due diligence materials, including title, survey, zoning, and environmental reports.
Order and review zoning reports and coordinate revisions with zoning consultants.
Support leasing matters by drafting leases and amendments incorporating LOI terms and assisting with related leasing documents, including consents and broker agreements.
Prepare and review organizational documents, including consents and resolutions, and assemble and circulate entity records.
Order and review certified organizational documents and good standing certificates; obtain EINs for newly formed entities; and file and register entities with secretaries of state, including qualifications to do business.
Order and review judgment and lien searches and obtain missing information needed to complete closing deliverables.
Prepare closing instructions and coordinate settlement statements with title companies and clients.
Finalize documents for execution and recording, assemble exhibits, and coordinate delivery of closing packages.
Prepare and file UCC financing statements and related amendments, assignments, and terminations and coordinate related filings.
Support post-closing by following up on recorded documents and title policies and reviewing post-closing deliverables for accuracy.
Maintain transaction timelines and ensure deadlines are met; calendaring all deadlines.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and/or a paralegal certificate from an ABA-approved program.
At least 7+ years of paralegal experience, strong emphasis on commercial real estate transactions and tile and surveys.
Demonstrated experience reviewing and analyzing title commitments and ALTA/NSPS surveys.
Familiarity with title insurance products, endorsements, and closing processes.
Understanding land use and environmental due diligence is a plus.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and document management systems.

Key Competencies

Advanced attention to detail, particularly in reviewing technical title and survey documents.
Strong analytical and issue-spotting skills.
Ability to manage multiple transactions and deadlines.
Effective communication with attorneys, clients, and third-party vendors.
Strong organization and follow-through.

The base annual pay range for this role is $100,000–$140,000. Compensation will vary based on skills, qualifications, experience, and location, and internal equity will be considered. A full range of medical, financial, and other benefits (depending on position) is also offered.

jobs.title: Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science and Policy and Program Director, Tenured, Augus
jobs.description:
Description

Chapman University invites applications for an Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science & Policy and Program Director in the Schmid College of Science and Technology starting August 2027. This is a full-time, tenured position that requires work to be performed in the State of California with specific in-person teaching responsibilities and required on-campus availability at Chapman's Orange campus.

Chapman University is a nationally ranked R2 institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern California's most diverse and vibrant regions. Our faculty are academic leaders who excel in both research and teaching. Dedicated to forward-looking, personalized education, we create an environment for unlimited achievement by both our students and faculty. More information about Chapman University is available at www.chapman.edu.

The Environmental Science & Policy Program is uniquely seated within two colleges at Chapman University: the Schmid College of Science and Technology and the Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges embody Chapman's mission of providing students with personalized educational experiences by fostering an outstanding community of teacher-scholars across a broad range of undergraduate and graduate programs. Schmid College has a new 140,000 sq ft home, the Keck Center for Science and Engineering. More information about Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges is available at www.chapman.edu/science
and www.chapman.edu/wilkinson
, respectively.

The undergraduate-only serving Environmental Science & Policy Program is home to a diverse group of faculty with interdisciplinary specializations across the breadth of environmental sciences (ecology, engineering, hydrology, remote sensing) and environmental studies (anthropology, environmental justice, natural resource governance, political science, sociology). The program serves the interdisciplinary Environmental Science & Policy B.S. degree, the Environmental Science minor, and the Environmental Studies minor.

We seek candidates with an active research program in areas including but not limited to:

Environmental health
Environmental toxicology
Water, soil, and/or air quality
Environmental contaminants
Natural resource governance

We value candidates who can identify avenues for collaboration both within and outside of the institution.

Faculty Role Responsibilities

The successful candidate will teach lower- and upper-level courses that contribute to the major and minors within the Environmental Science & Policy Program, maintain an active research program, and advise/mentor undergraduate research students. Significant scholarship, including publishing in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at relevant research conferences, and obtaining and managing extramural grants is an expectation of the position.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Teach lower- and upper-division Environmental Science & Policy courses, including core and elective courses. Current course descriptions are available at https://catalog.chapman.edu.
Continue a research program in interdisciplinary environmental sciences, including publishing papers and presenting work in this area at local and national conferences.
Actively contribute as an integral member of the Schmid College of Science and Technology in the ongoing development, implementation, and assessment of their academic and degree programs.
Perform service to the unit, college, university, profession, and wider community as expected of a tenured faculty member.

Program Director Responsibilities

The successful candidate will lead the Environmental Science & Policy faculty and degree program as Program Director for a minimum of three years in an at-will, compensated appointment separate from their faculty role.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Provide leadership, vision, and a voice for affiliated faculty, students, and degree programs.
Oversee program budget and advocate on behalf of the program for resource use.
Lead curriculum alignment and revisions, assessment reports, and course scheduling for the program.
Coordinate and participate in program and college events, including events for student recruitment and commencement, as appropriate.
Assign faculty to courses and hire appropriate part-time lecturers where needed.
Facilitate communication and collaboration between Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges pertaining to the support of this interdisciplinary program.

Qualifications

An earned Ph.D. in one of the environmental sciences (e.g., Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science & Management) or related field by the start of employment from an accredited institution.
Earned tenure at the current institution of employment or equivalent.
A strong history of interdisciplinary environmental science research, including evidence of an independent, nationally recognized, externally funded research program.
Evidence of effective teaching at the undergraduate level, particularly in experiential learning courses, such as a senior capstone course, or upper division coursework.
Experience in curriculum development and learning outcome assessment.
Experience in leadership or administrative roles in academic service settings, such as college governance, curriculum, or assessment committees, ideally connected to interdisciplinary endeavors.

Application Instructions

Qualified Candidates Should Submit The Following Electronically Via Interfolio:

Cover letter detailing qualifications related to the position description.
Curriculum Vitae.
Statement of teaching philosophy that includes a brief description of past teaching experience, no more than two pages.
Research Statement that details current and future environmental science research, no more than two pages.
Statement of leadership philosophy that includes a brief description of administrative and leadership experiences as they relate to Program Director-level service, no more than one page.
Contact information for three professional references. Letters will be requested from short-listed candidates.

Inquiries may be directed to Richelle Tanner, Search Committee Chair, at schmidcollege@chapman.edu. Please use "Environmental Science & Policy Faculty Position" as the email subject line.

Application review will begin October 11, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. This position is subject to final budget approval. Salary range for this position is $105,000 - $125,000. Successful completion of a background check is required for the final candidate.

Who We Are

Enel North America is a proven renewables leader delivering clean, flexible and sustainable energy solutions.

As part of the Enel Group, we develop, build, own and operate renewable power plants and demand response solutions, with over 11 gigawatts (GW) of installed wind and solar capacity, over 1 GW of energy storage and nearly 5 GW of demand response in the US and Canada.

For nearly 25 years, we've reliably powered modern life and driven climate action with our people, partners and communities by putting sustainability at the center of everything we do. Responsible for providing technical, regulatory, and programmatic direction on environmental issues for Enel’s North American Fleet of renewable energy facilities. Assures that the highest level of compliance is maintained with all applicable environmental rules and regulations. Responsible for governance, oversight, and completion of specific environmental regulatory filings in one or more environmental programs including, but not limited to, solid and hazardous waste management, environmental management system (EMS), facility operational permits and compliance reporting, biodiversity, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG)

In accordance with Holding guidelines, and liaising with Central Health, Safety,

Environment and Quality Unit, responsibilities, include, but not limited to:

Prepare, review and submit agency applications, reports and filings, and respond to agency inquiries. Support agency negotiations and comment on proposed permits.

resource allocation, scheduling and budget development and stewardship.

Manage consultants and other vendors associated with environmental projects and

monitoring activities.

Provide programmatic direction and facilitate development, implementation, and

maintenance of environmental aspects of Enel’s ESG program.

Oversee Facility Operational handover process and post-construction operational

compliance matters (PCMM, SWPPP, SPCC, Habitat Restoration)

the unit and company.

Maintain data integrity within all data systems, including SAP
Position has a direct impact on plant operation and serves as in-house technical

expert/consultant to fleet-wide Power facilities in area of expertise.

Work with Environmental Permitting group to provide guidance to sites on upcoming

regulatory compliance issues.

Position requires a high level of independence and ability to make decisions in areas of

subject matter expertise.

Position requires communication and interaction with Enel business units that include but are not limited to operations, sustainability, strategy, government affairs, supply, legal,

communications, auditing, and financial

Who You Are & What You’ve Accomplished:

BS in engineering, natural or physical sciences, chemistry, or environmental science with 5+ years professional experience OR
Associate's degree with 10+ years' experience and 5+ years exempt-level experience
In-depth knowledge of environmental regulatory requirements for power plants

Strong computer skills, including knowledge and proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite

products. Ability to be on call or work off hours as needed

Availability for local, domestic and international travel; up to 25%
Superior written and verbal communication skills
Experience working within integrated management systems/quality systems ((ISO 9001,

14001 & 45001, 37001 helpful)

Strong initiative and drive for high achievement and continuous improvement
Superior communications, interpersonal, and organizational skills required

About The Role

Company: Geo-Informatie Nederland (GIN) Title: GIS Specialist Geo Informatie Do you want to help Lansingerland municipality advance toward becoming a data-driven organization? Are you energized by complex challenges that prepare the municipality for the future—such as housing development, the energy transition, and the ecological main structure? With GEO-informatie (geospatial information), you create insight and support well-founded decisions for residents, the municipal council, and the organization. If you’re considering submitting an application, please ensure you click the application button below after reading the full job description. Description Lansingerland is actively working toward developing a smart municipality, where data and geospatial information play a central role in policy, implementation, and service delivery. As a GIS Specialist, you translate policy questions into geospatial products, integrate internal and external data sources, and advise on the potential of GIS. Can you make a direct contribution to this transition? This might be your next role! Key Responsibilities As a GIS Specialist, you will gather, analyze, and visualize data. Your work makes geographic information accessible and actionable—for both colleagues and residents—thereby supporting data-driven decision-making. Collecting, analyzing, and evaluating geographic data using various GIS software tools; Proactively promoting the use of geospatial data to foster a data-driven culture; Developing customized products such as dashboards, apps, or maps, and making them available via online portals; Managing and optimizing GIS systems, including GIS Viewers, QGIS, ArcGIS, and FME Flow; Providing technical support to GIS users, including troubleshooting and resolving issues. What We’re Looking For Minimum HBO (higher professional education) work and thinking level; Strong communication skills in Dutch (minimum B2 level); Experience with GIS applications such as QGIS, ArcGIS Online, and ArcGIS Pro. Preferred qualifications: Experience with FME Desktop/Server, GIS system administration, and/or (geo)database management. What We Offer Individual Choice Budget (IKB): 17.05% of salary; Company-provided laptop and mobile phone; Extensive range of training and development opportunities; Sustainable pension through ABP (70% subsidized by the municipality); Fixed-term contract of 12 months with the prospect of a permanent position.

jobs.title: Graduate GIS Consultant
jobs.description:
Job title: Graduate GIS Consultant

Location: Manchester or Southampton

Start Date: September 2027

Joining Tetra Tech as a graduate is more than starting a new job – you’ll become part of our Next Gen Talent development programme, designed to support you as you build your career with us. Alongside hands-on experience and exposure to real projects, you’ll benefit from a structured programme of regular learning, training and development opportunities, helping you grow your technical and professional skills as you progress.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech.

Looking to start your career in a role where geospatial data, technical problem-solving and real project delivery come together? Join Tetra Tech and help shape how information is mapped, analysed and used across major sectors.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

Tetra Tech is a leading technical, engineering and environmental consultancy delivering data-driven solutions across water, environment, infrastructure, energy and international development. Our Geospatial team within the Management & Surveying Business Unit works across single and multi-disciplinary projects for clients in sectors including water, defence and nuclear. This graduate role offers varied work across different project locations, technical requirements and sectors, with support from a collaborative team in a global organisation with a strong local presence.

Your Impact in this position

You’ll help turn complex data into clear, usable information for non-GIS users and support project delivery through mapping, analysis and reporting. From maintaining datasets to improving the way we use GIS technology, your work will help raise quality, efficiency and project outcomes.

5 Core Capabilities

Mapping Support
– Respond to mapping requests across the business and produce clear, accurate outputs.

Data Analysis & Reporting
– Source, prepare and analyse data to create graphics, metrics and reports.

Digital Tools & Applications
– Use Survey123, Dashboards and Insights to build internal applications that support client delivery.

Dataset Management
– Capture, update and maintain datasets for internal and external use.

Project Support & Collaboration
– Assist on data-heavy projects and support the wider GIS team as needed.

GIS Improvement
– Help develop our use of GIS technology, including new tools and approaches to improve quality and efficiency.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

You’ll need a minimum 2:1 BSc in GIS, environmental sciences or geographical sciences, plus knowledge of GIS software or equivalent experience. Experience with the ESRI stack, especially ArcGIS Pro, Survey123, Field Maps and AGOL, is highly desirable, alongside strong communication, presentation, organisation and time management skills. Knowledge of UK environmental and Ordnance Survey datasets is also required. Security clearance suitability is essential.

Working Environment

Based in Manchester or Southampton, with hybrid working supported in line with team and project needs. As a graduate role, you can expect to spend more time in the office initially to support learning, collaboration and development, with flexibility available as you grow in the role.

Application Closing Date: 31st October 2026

Assessment Centre to be held: February 2027

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is a leading provider of consulting and engineering services working across the full project lifecycle worldwide. We have a wide range of expertise across our teams, providing a global support network with a personalised approach to client relationships to better understand where we can add value. We provide a collaborative environment that supports individual performance, innovation, and creativity.

We support public and private sector clients on local, national, and international projects to deliver sustainable and resilient solutions. Our operations in the UK, Ireland, and the Netherlands include more than 6,000 employees who are Leading with Science® to solve our clients’ most complex problems.

In alignment with the Equality Act 2010, we will make reasonable adjustments to support candidates and employees requiring additional arrangements. This could include adaptations to work schedules, training approaches, or the physical workspace. Please inform us if you need any accommodations during the recruitment process or in your day-to-day role

jobs.description:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

MITRE’s Model-Based Analytics Department (L144) is looking for qualified applicants to bring their geospatial, machine learning, advanced analytics, and applied research skills to bear on solving problems of critical national importance. MITRE’s diverse work program provides opportunities to apply your expertise and creative thinking in challenging domains such as healthcare, transportation, and national security. Employees may also participate in MITRE’s internal research and development program, which provides funding for innovative applied research that addresses our sponsors’ hardest problems.

Our department is an interdisciplinary department that thrives on having a large toolbox to support data- and model-driven decision making. Are you passionate about biomass feedstocks as a means to decarbonise heavy industry applications? Do you bring expertise in the technical, economic and climate policy aspects of biomass availability, processing and use? Are you excited to work in a diverse, multi-disciplinary and international team? Then, this is the perfect opportunity for you!

Reaching a climate-neutral industry will require unprecedented investments in a wide range of GHG mitigation technologies, due to the sector’s inherent complexity and regional diversity. While a significant share of emissions can be reduced by advancing energy efficiency and expanding direct electrification powered by renewable energy, there is also the need for more complex and costly measures as well as alternative feedstocks for processes, where biomass and hydrogen technologies can be implemented. To tap into this potential, climate-effective biomass uses in industry require thorough understanding of availability and costs across different regions to give recommendations on policies that help to decarbonise industry in a competitive way, incorporating ecological sustainability boundaries.

Under the umbrella of the Agora Think Tanks, Agora Industry develops politically feasible and science-based strategies and solutions for the transformation to climate neutrality – in Germany, Europe, and internationally. As a think tank and policy lab we facilitate a productive exchange of ideas amongst stakeholders from politics, business, science and civil society. As a non-partisan, non-profit organisation funded by foundations and public institutions, we are independent of corporate and partisan interests. Our exclusive mission is to serve the climate and the common good.

To strengthen our team, we are looking for a

Project Manager or Project Officer Biomass Value Chains (f/m/d)

Full- or part-time (min. 32 hours)– based in Berlin

You will work on the supply side of biomass as a feedstock for hard-to-electrify applications in industry. The geographical scope will be global, covering different conditions and contexts that vary across geographies. This position is part of Agora Industry’s central Technologies & Analysis team, working closely with regional teams.

Your responsibilities include

Contributing to the development and implementation of international projects focused on climate-effective biomass solutions for industrial decarbonisation, encompassing farm- and forest-level availability, logistics and conversion technologies, as well as biomass supply for industrial carbon dioxide removal (CDR).
Analysing biomass supply costs, availability and potentials for different agriculture and forestry products across multiple geographies, taking into account competing uses in different sectors and market implications.
Conducting and coordinating projects on biomass for industrial applications and related technological enablers and policy support mechanisms
Analysing policy and regulatory gaps that hinder biomass use in various regions with a focus on economic, regulatory, and governance frameworks.
Monitoring the development of technology and business models related to the scaling, mobilization and system integration of biomass value chains and logistics.
Supporting stakeholder engagement with policymakers, industry, civil society, funders, among others, to inform discussions around biomass applications across different industry sectors.
Pro-actively contributing to building partnerships and working closely with network partners across the globe.
Liaising with expert colleagues across the Agora Think Tanks (including Agora Agriculture) to facilitate their contributions to projects and knowledge sharing across different regions.
Actively contributing to internal discussions.
Managing subcontractors including preparing agreements and work plans, supervising and guiding project progress, and managing the quality of deliverables.
As Project Officer, the focus is on contributing to the technical management of specific projects with smaller budget, largely independent research, contributing to the conceptualisation and development of complex topics, and of project-related reporting and communication.
As Project Manager, the focus is on technical management and responsibility for specific projects with smaller budgets, independent comprehensive research, conceptualisation and development of complex topics, technical supervision of students and interns, and project-related reporting and communication.

Design Engineer – Drone & CFD Specialist
Location:
Manesar, Haryana

4-6 years

Role Overview

We are looking for a hands-on Design Engineer to join our core engineering team and drive the design, development, testing, and optimization of next-generation drone and UAV systems.

The ideal candidate is a practical, field-tested engineer with strong expertise in mechanical design, UAV structures, aerodynamics, CFD, materials, and manufacturing
- someone who has independently taken UAV components or complete systems from concept through CAD, analysis, prototyping, manufacturing, testing, and real-world field deployment
, not just theoretical or simulation work.

Key Responsibilities

UAV & Mechanical Design

• Independently design UAV/drone airframes, structural components, and mechanical sub-assemblies.
• Develop production-ready 3D models and 2D engineering drawings (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, AutoCAD, or equivalent).
• Own designs end-to-end — from concept through prototyping, manufacturing, and field deployment.
• Balance weight, strength, stability, durability, and manufacturability in every design decision.
• Partner with electronics, flight-control, and systems teams on integration and weight distribution. Aerodynamics & CFD

• Apply practical aerodynamics and fluid mechanics knowledge to real UAV flight scenarios.
• Run CFD simulations (ANSYS Fluent/CFX or equivalent) to optimize lift, drag, stability, and efficiency.
• Translate simulation results into concrete design changes.
• Diagnose and resolve aerodynamic issues that surface during actual flight testing, not just on paper.
Manufacturing & Materials

• Select materials (carbon-fiber composites, high-strength polymers, lightweight alloys, aerospace-grade materials) based on strength, weight, cost, and durability requirements.
• Apply design-for-manufacturing (DFM) principles to keep designs production-ready and repeatable.
• Coordinate with fabrication teams on CNC machining, 3D printing, and composite molding. Testing & Field Validation

• Validate designs through prototyping, ground testing, and flight testing.
• Use field feedback and test data to drive continuous design iteration.
• Demonstrate a track record of designs that are personally developed and currently operating in the field - not shelved prototypes.
Documentation & Compliance

• Produce detailed engineering drawings, specifications, and BOMs.
• Ensure designs meet applicable engineering, safety, and regulatory standards.
• Maintain configuration control and documentation throughout the product lifecycle.
Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Work closely with flight-control, electronics, manufacturing, and operations teams to resolve design and performance issues.
• Support fast design iteration cycles based on test data and operational needs.

Required Qualifications & Skills

• Education Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Aeronautical, Mechanical, or Mechanical Design Engineering, or a related field.
• Proven, independent ownership of UAV/drone mechanical and structural designs — not just design support.
• Demonstrable experience with UAV components or systems that have been manufactured, tested, and deployed in the field.
• Strong practical grounding in aerodynamics, fluid mechanics, and UAV structural design.
• Proficiency in SolidWorks, Fusion 360, AutoCAD, or equivalent CAD tools.
• Hands-on CFD analysis experience using ANSYS Fluent/CFX or equivalent.
• Working knowledge of composite materials, lightweight structures, CNC machining, and additive manufacturing.
• Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to turn theory into flight ready hardware.

Preferred

• FEA/structural and multi-physics simulation experience.
• Experience with fixed-wing UAVs, multirotors, VTOL, or other autonomous aircraft.
• Direct experience working with manufacturing/fabrication teams and running flight tests.
• Background in aerospace, defence, aviation, drone, or robotics industries.
• Strong technical communication skills.

Ideal Candidate

Someone who can point to a real design lifecycle they've owned: Design → Analysis → Manufacturing → Testing → Field Deployment.

Application Deadline
: Applications will be accepted through September 16, 2026 at 5:00 PM CDT.

About SWCA

SWCA Environmental Consultants is a 100% employee-owned environmental consulting firm providing full spectrum environmental services across the United States. Our North Star is to be the best place to work and a leader in sustainability, delivering sound science and creative solutions to complex environmental challenges.

We are guided by our core values every day. We collaborate as #OneSWCA, we are #AlwaysLearning, we #NeverSettle, and we #GiveBack to our communities. With offices nationwide, SWCA offers a collaborative, team focused environment where employees can build meaningful and long-term careers.

What you will accomplish

Strategic Project Leadership: Strategically consults on and leads complex projects in pursuit of client objectives, overseeing the technical approach and ensuring quality assurance and quality control.
Exemplary Leadership: Leads by example in both technical and soft skills, navigating client and team priorities to deliver projects that meet professional and oversight agency standards.
Technical Expertise & Innovation: Innovates standards and practices to enhance the quality and efficiency of client projects and outcomes, ensuring alignment with industry and regulatory standards. Serves as a go-to technical expert and consultant, providing novel project strategies and applying technical excellence that considers client needs to meet project requirements.
Project Accountability: Continuously guides projects, executing accountability for the performance of projects or delegated tasks and ensuring that project milestones are met and outcomes align with SWCA’s values and client expectations. Assesses risks and implements strategies for problem-solving. Revises or suggests revisions to project scopes, schedules, and budgets as necessary to meet evolving project requirements and ensure successful outcomes.
Business Growth & Innovation: Drives business growth and client success through technical excellence, innovation, and development of new methods and standards that advance SWCA's technical reputation. Contributes to SWCA's strategic planning.
Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration: Champions cross-disciplinary collaboration, working closely with specialists to provide comprehensive technical support for projects.
Mentorship & Team Development: Mentors staff for impactful influence, coaching others in technical excellence, leadership, and strategy, and also develops specialized programs and protocols. Fosters team development and cross-training, modeling and promoting knowledge sharing and collaboration among team members to enhance project outcomes, as well as team depth and redundancy.
Relationship Management: Establishes and grows effective consultative relationships with external and internal clients and/or agency regulators and industry partners (if applicable) to support successful projects.
Follows applicable federal, Tribal, state, local, industry, contractual, and company regulations, standards, and specifications.
Performs related work as assigned.

Additional Job-Specific Responsibilities

In this role, you will be responsible for managing multi-disciplinary projects and overseeing project field studies, reporting, and permitting. You will play a key role in shaping technical approaches, strengthening client relationships, and advancing SWCA’s reputation for quality and innovation. Periodic travel throughout the region will be required to support client engagement, project oversight, and team collaboration.

Coordinate and support multidisciplinary teams providing environmental planning, natural resources, cultural resources, and permitting services to clients.
Manage and lead project teams supporting energy, infrastructure, land development, and other client projects, including FERC and BLM-regulated projects and third-party NEPA documentation.
Act as the regulatory and permit compliance liaison between agencies and clients, proactively addressing compliance issues.
Work closely with corporate accounting to review invoices, expenditures, and project audits.
Provide peer review for technical reports and environmental permits, ensuring scientific and professional integrity.
Implement and enforce SWCA's safety procedures and ethical standards.
Communicate effectively with diverse project stakeholders, including regulatory agencies, field crews, trade workers, clients, and third parties.
Utilize strong organizational, verbal, written, and graphic communication skills in project execution and stakeholder engagement.

Minimum Qualifications

Six years of relevant, progressively responsible experience, including 3 years of managing projects and some experience managing others. Eight years of related experience and PMP certification is preferred; or any equivalent combination of experience, performance, training, and/or education. Knowledge normally obtained through a bachelor's degree.

Experience And Qualifications For Success

Bachelor’s Degree in Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or other related field.
Experience with project financials (budgets, forecasting, invoicing).
Demonstrated client management and business development experience (seller-doer).
Demonstrated ability to develop and supervise staff.

Preferred Or Helpful Qualifications

At least five (5) years of project management experience in a consulting environment, including proposal writing, scheduling, setting and adhering to project budgets and delivery schedules, change management, and leading meetings with clients and agencies.
First-hand experience in developing environmental permit applications and documents pertaining to FERC, BLM, USACE and similar federal agency permit authorizations.
Established credibility with reviewing agencies and clients.
Effectively engaged in resource agency consultations, received stakeholder/agency input and provide informed responses.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent communication skills, both verbal and technical writing, in a variety of professional settings.

Pay Range

SWCA is committed to salary equity and transparency.

The expected pay range for this Houston, Texas - based position is $87,141/year to 114,660/year
. Actual pay may vary based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other factors permitted by law. Eligible employees may also receive performance-based bonuses.

As a 100% employee-owned company, we invest in your future. Our Total Rewards package includes an Employee Stock Ownership Plan, 401(k) with profit sharing, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, wellness programs, and professional development opportunities.

Closing

If you need accommodation due to a disability, please contact accommodations@swca.com or call 1 480 581 5378. If you require assistance with the application process, please contact recruiting@swca.com.

Job Summary

The Assistant Sustainability Manager for Beaver Creek Resort leads the resort's environmental sustainability efforts in support of Vail Resorts' Commitment to Zero. This role reports to the Beaver Creek Resort Base Area Operations Manager and dotted line report structure the Senior Sustainability Manager for Colorado and works closely with resort leadership, the broader Vail Resorts Sustainability Team, and employees across business units to identify and implement sustainability programs.

The position is primarily focused on zero-waste operations, including waste reduction, recycling, composting, material diversion, vendor coordination, data reporting, employee engagement, and environmental compliance support. The role integrates sustainability goals into resort operations through program development, oversight, training, and hands-on partnership with operational teams. The position also supports representation of Beaver Creek Resort on environmental matters with local communities, public agencies, and external partners.

This position is based at Beaver Creek Resort, with primary responsibilities performed in person at the resort and alongside operations teams.

Job Specifications

Starting Wage: $25.00/Hr - $28.60/Hr
Employment Type: Year Round
Shift Type: Full Time hours available
Minimum Age: At least 18 years of age
Housing Availability: No

Job Responsibilities

Initiate, oversee, and implement Commitment to Zero and environmental sustainability programs at Beaver Creek Resort, with primary emphasis on waste reduction and material diversion.
Serve as a resort-level sustainability leader who drives practical and innovative programs in waste, recycling, composting, responsible purchasing, and other relevant areas to engage employees and guests.
Own day-to-day management and execution of zero-waste programs across Beaver Creek Resort operations and hospitality locations.
Prioritize progress toward resort waste and diversion goals and build consistent practices across operational departments.
Manage waste and recycling pickup schedules and coordinate with resort teams to ensure reliable service, appropriate infrastructure, and accurate data.
Lead waste data collection, tracking, analysis, and reporting to support performance monitoring, budgeting, and decision-making.
Drive resort engagement through Commitment to Zero onboarding, training, communications, and behavior-change programs for year-round and seasonal employees.
Serve as a key on-site sustainability resource, providing operational guidance and troubleshooting to resort departments.
Coordinate and support environmental teams, hybrid roles, and other employees assigned to waste rounds, training, tipping, sorting, and related activities.
Oversee recycling and material-staging operations, including coordination of metals, wood, electronic waste, and other specialty material streams.
Establish and maintain working relationships with waste haulers, Rubicon, recyclers, composting partners, and other program vendors; resolve service issues and identify opportunities to improve diversion and efficiency.
Partner with resort departments to coordinate waste and recycling needs for events, seasonal transitions, maintenance activities, and special projects.
Support resort environmental compliance in coordination with Environmental Health and Safety and operational teams, including universal and hazardous waste collection, labeling, storage, documentation, and proper disposal.
Support sustainability-related capital and operating projects involving multiple departments, budgets, timelines, and external partners.
Promote safe work practices across environmental operations and coordinate with resort safety partners to address operational risks.
Effectively communicate environmental initiatives through appropriate channels to demonstrate leadership and build employee, guest, and community engagement.
Act as a contributor and leader within the Beaver Creek Resort leadership team and the broader Vail Resorts Sustainability Team.
Represent Beaver Creek Resort environmental programs with local communities, public agencies, vendors, and external partners as requested.
Occasional travel may be required to other Colorado resorts, the corporate office, and off-site events.

Required

Job Requirements:

Primary work location at Beaver Creek Resort and ability to work in person across resort operational areas.
Three or more years of experience in waste, recycling, environmental operations, sustainability program coordination, resort operations, or a related field.
Knowledge of waste reduction, recycling, material diversion, and responsible disposal practices.
Ability to facilitate strategic dialogue and problem-solving across multiple departments.
Comfort speaking in front of groups, conducting training, and building new relationships.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, prioritize responsibilities, and coordinate multiple projects.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
Valid driver license and ability to meet company driving requirements.
Ability to work outdoors in variable mountain weather and occasionally perform physical tasks associated with waste audits, sorting, inspections, and operational troubleshooting.
Ability to meet travel and scheduling requirements, including occasional early mornings, evenings, weekends, holidays, or special events.
Intermediate or greater skiing or snowboarding ability for safe winter travel within the resort.

Preferred

Bachelor's degree in sustainability, environmental studies, business, hospitality, operations, or a related field.
Mountain resort, hospitality, facilities, or public-venue experience.
Experience with waste diversion programs, vendor coordination, universal waste, hazardous waste coordination, or environmental compliance support.
Experience leading seasonal employees, environmental teams, or cross-functional projects.
Ability to obtain applicable certification for forklifts or other material-handling equipment if required.

Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

For over 15 years, Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud computing platform. What is cloud computing? Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of IT resources over the Internet.

In 2019, Amazon announced The Climate Pledge, which includes our commitment to power our operations with 100% renewable energy by 2025, on the path to achieving net zero carbon across our businesses by 2040.

To learn more about AWS, visit https://aws.amazon.com and https://sustainability.aboutamazon.com/environment/the-cloud.

The ideal candidate is a mid-level data engineer who takes ownership of tools and technologies, demonstrates strong data analytics capabilities, and works independently while knowing when to seek guidance. They balance short and long-term priorities, mitigate risks, and deliver practical, scalable solutions. They communicate clearly with stakeholders at all levels, contribute to team growth through mentoring, and collaborate effectively across functions. A genuine commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion guides how they build products and work with others.

Key job responsibilities

Build and maintain integrated environmental data solutions connected to internal digital tools, supporting due diligence, permitting, design, and construction tracking workflows.
Develop monitoring and tracking systems that apply analytics to environmental metrics, including due diligence risk, permitting delivery timelines, and construction risk indicators.
Implement predictive analytics models to forecast environmental risks and support automated risk assessment processes.
Design and maintain intelligent data pipelines and real-time monitoring dashboards that convert environmental compliance data into actionable insights.
Integrate environmental technology solutions with existing systems and data architectures, partnering with stakeholders to translate business requirements into practical digital solutions.
Contribute to the ongoing improvement of digital tools and systems, ensuring they scale to meet evolving business, customer, and stakeholder needs.

About The Team

Why AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. T

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of developing and operating large-scale data structures for business intelligence analytics using data modeling experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines
3+ years of Tableau Desktop, Quicksight or other relevant data visualization software experience
Experience with EHS management software development or analytics.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions
Experience formulating and solving predictive modeling, machine learning, forecasting or statistical modeling problems
Experience in communicating technical concepts to a non-technical audience
Knowledge of software development lifecycle, including design, development, test, build, deployment processes and timelines

Hudbay's operating portfolio includes the Constancia mine in Cusco (Peru), the Snow Lake operations in Manitoba (Canada) and the Copper Mountain mine in British Columbia (Canada). Hudbay's growth pipeline includes the Copper World project in Arizona (United States), the Cactus project in Arizona (United States), the Mason project in Nevada (United States), the Llaguen project in La Libertad (Peru) and several expansion and exploration opportunities near its existing operations.

Get in at the ground floor with our South Railroad Project — a construction-ready, open-pit heap leach project located on the world-class Carlin Trend in Nevada, one of the most prolific gold-producing regions on the planet. The project is backed by a completed feasibility study outlining an average of 130,000 ounces of gold per year over the first five years and an initial 10-year mine life. Join us at this pivotal stage and help bring Nevada's next gold mine to life.

Position Title: Environmental Coordinator

Position Summary

As Equinox Gold continues to grow, we are seeking an Environmental Coordinator to join our team. In this role, you will work under the supervision of the Environmental Manager or Environmental Superintendent to support environmental compliance and permitting activities. Responsibilities include helping ensure compliance with all mine permits, seeking and maintaining permits for current and future operations, coordinating and managing environmental consultants, and engaging with government agencies as needed.

You will also provide compliance training and field support, including conducting and coordinating environmental sampling, participating in inspections with operations, and communicating regulatory and operating permit requirements. This role will help maintain existing permits and support the permitting process for future mine expansions.

Key Responsibilities

Acquire site-specific knowledge of applicable environmental regulations.
Assist in regulatory reporting and compliance activities (air, water, land, wildlife, and waste).
Coordinate environmental sampling, testing, and analysis, working with staff and/or consultants.
Assist in obtaining and maintaining required and appropriate certifications (e.g., EPA Method 9, DOT HAZMAT, CN Code, ISO 14001, and other necessary programs).
Assist in supporting monitoring and mitigation plans through Agency requirements, including but not limited to requirements from BLM, USFWS, SHPO, USACE, NDOW, NDEP, and others.
Maintain environmental records.
Assist in investigating and reporting environmental incidents and assist with mitigation plans.
Assist with Cyanide Code certification and ISO 14001.
Perform safety and environmental audits.
On-call rotations.
Assist in permitting minor and major federal actions with BLM (DNAs, EAs, SEISs), USFWS, USACE, EPA, or other as needed.
Assist in permitting minor and major state actions with NDEP and Bureaus, NDWR, or other as needed.

Required Experience & Skills

Minimum of 1 year of experience in environmental work, preferably in a coordinator or similar role.
Minimum of 1 year of experience in the mining industry or a related industry.
Experience with environmental permitting, compliance, and regulatory requirements preferred.
Minimum of 3 years of experience with EMS, Datamine Discover 3D, ArcGIS, or other GIS software.
Strong computer skills, including intermediate proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.
Attention to detail.
Strong critical, strategic, and logical thinking skills.
Effective communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively with operations, consultants, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and perform field work, including walking long distances over uneven terrain, climbing stairs, and working in extreme hot and cold temperatures.
Must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer.
Must possess a valid driver's license.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Compliance, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management, or related fields.

The Conservation Technician will help carry out the next phase of Lost River Cave’s natural resource conservation efforts.  To date, invasive plant removal and native plant restoration efforts are yielding results in the upland prairie and karst valley mesic meadow.  This position will continue to focus on those areas, grow relationships with key partners, volunteers, and plan for possible future restoration expansion. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Carry out manual, mechanical, and chemical control methods of invasive plants
Operate tractor, bush hog, side by side, chainsaw, weed eater, hedge trimmer, backpack sprayer, and any other needed equipment after being trained and approved to operate

Evaluate and integrate plans from KDFWR, KDF, and past LRC Resource Management Plan

Build on species inventories of flora and fauna

Carry out conservation-based volunteer events

Maintain existing partnerships and build new relationships with key partners which may include KDFWR, KDF, KNPS, WKU, regional universities, County Extension Office, volunteers, and others

Coordinate with Maintenance Department on shared projects

Occasionally support fundraising initiatives by participating in events with donors and prospective supporters

Present occasional programming on invasive species, identification, and best management practices

Maintain accurate, detailed records of work done, results, etc.  Prepare reports accordingly. 

Maintain all regulatory record keeping in compliance with the UK Department of Agriculture

Help maintain native plant demonstration garden and assist in native plant landscaping

Participate in other duties as assigned which may include trail work, landscaping, special event support, & other

Assist in coordinating program budget development

Potentially coordinate conservation grazing

Potentially research grant opportunities and write applications for funding on rainy days or when requested

Degree in ecology, natural resource management, biology, horticulture, related field or qualifying real-world experience
Knowledge of invasive and native plant species of this region or willingness to gain that knowledge

Excellent communication skills

Ability to work project list independently

Ability to do solo work on a daily basis

jobs.title: Data Analyst Consultant - LiDAR DoT
jobs.description:
Precision Federal has been awarded a firm-fixed-price contract by the U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Highway Administration, to evaluate 3D LiDAR and smartphone-based platforms for collecting motor vehicle traffic and roadway geometry data.

Part time consultant roel

What you would do

- Run quality checks on incoming trip data as it arrives: completeness, GPS and sensor sanity, timestamp continuity, coverage of each site per driver
- Keep the quality-control log that goes to the Government with the dataset: what was checked, what was rejected, why
- Build the horizontal curve inventory for each site from the trip and LiDAR data: curve start and end points, radius, superelevation, and speed through each curve
- Compare posted speed limits against design-supported safe speed at each curve, working with our licensed Professional Engineer who reviews the findings
- Produce the figures and tables for the Task 3 and Task 4 reports and the final report, reproducible from code
- Join a short progress call once a month

Requirements

- Python with GeoPandas, Shapely, or GDAL, and SQL with PostGIS or an equivalent spatial database
- Experience checking real sensor or GPS data for quality: gaps, drift, outliers, clock offsets
- Comfortable computing geometry from coordinates: distances, headings, curve fitting, radius of curvature
- Reproducible work habits: scripts and notebooks under version control, results a second person can rerun
- Clear written English. Your QC notes go to a federal research center
Preferred
- Transportation or roadway geometry work: AASHTO Green Book concepts, superelevation, design speed
- Experience with vehicle telematics, naturalistic driving data, or smartphone sensor logs (GPS, accelerometer, gyroscope)
- Point-cloud experience: PDAL, Open3D, CloudCompare, or LiDAR-derived surfaces
- Prior work on a federally funded research project, or a state department of transportation

The Department of Ecology is hiring two

Duties

Are you an engineer eager to apply your technical skills to real-world climate work? As a Greenhouse Gas Emissions Engineer, you will help ensure the accuracy and reliability of Washington’s greenhouse gas reporting under the Climate Commitment Act. In this role, you will review emissions data, apply engineering principles to verify calculations, and learn the details of state and federal climate regulations. You will work closely with other experienced engineers who will provide mentoring, guidance, and support as you take on increasingly complex assignments. You will also interact with regulated facilities and assist them in understanding reporting tools and requirements. This position is a great opportunity to grow as an engineer while contributing to meaningful climate policy, improving reporting systems, and building your expertise across a range of industries.

What You Will Do

Under the oversight of a Professional Engineer, review greenhouse gas emissions report submissions from electric power entities, natural gas and other fuel suppliers, and industrial facilities, for accuracy and completeness.
Apply engineering knowledge and core tenets to calculate and review report submissions.
Conduct engineering analyses and review protocols, policies, and guidance for effective and consistent implementation of the greenhouse gas reporting program.
Cultivate and maintain relationships and ongoing communication with reporting and regulated entities and interested parties by providing proactive, timely information and answering technical questions.
Conduct environmental inspections, audits, and studies, to include engineering review of industrial equipment and procedures to verify application of sound engineering design, and practices.
Identify complex and emerging issues with electricity and fuel supply markets.
Develop reporting tools, guidance documents and training for all regulated entities (including the electricity, facilities, natural gas, and other fuel supplier sectors), and interested parties.
Assist with rulemakings pertaining to the electricity, natural gas, and fuel supply sectors.

Greenhouse Gas and Climate Concepts – Demonstrated knowledge of greenhouse gases, climate change science. Experience performing emissions calculations, or energy accounting to support accurate analysis and informed engineering review.
