Regulatory Interpretation – Ability to interpret federal and state greenhouse gas rules and related regulations to determine applicability and support consistent implementation across assigned reporters and sectors.
Analytical Problem Solving – Ability to evaluate data and calculations, identify discrepancies, and recommend corrective actions to improve accuracy and regulatory compliance.
Sector Relationship Development – Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with electric power entities, fuel suppliers, and industrial facilities to support effective communication, outreach, and understanding of reporting requirements.

Professional Work Management – Demonstrated competence in organizing engineering tasks, maintaining documentation, and meeting deadlines to ensure accurate and timely verification work.
Multi-Party Communication and Collaboration – Ability to communicate technical information clearly to consultants, industry representatives, local authorities, agency staff, and the public to support understanding of environmental engineering problems and regulatory requirements.

ducation

In office attendance may be required for meetings such as weekly 1-on-1’s with the Supervisor, periodic Unit Meetings, monthly Section Meetings, all Key Project Meetings, and team building events.

Duties

Join our team as a Cleanup Site Manager and apply your technical expertise to some of the Northwest Region's most complex cleanup projects. In this senior-level role, you will manage a portfolio of contaminated site projects through investigation, design, and remediation. You will be responsible for applying engineering knowledge and sound judgment to ensure the cleanup actions for your projects protect both human health and the environment. You will be accountable for managing the scope and regulatory milestones for multiple complex projects with a high degree of independence. You will also be accountable for evaluating reasonable and necessary costs for projects that receive state remedial action grant funding. This opportunity requires that you proactively collaborate with other experienced engineers, geologists, scientists, and technical specialists to oversee your projects through cleanup to ultimately reach closure. Joining our team provides the opportunity to shape cleanup outcomes, innovate within established frameworks, and contribute to lasting environmental change. If you are ready to take on challenging projects that require both technical depth and strategic thinking, we encourage you to consider joining us.

What You Will Do

Serve as the principal engineer and project manager for complex cleanup sites to guide a portfolio of projects past investigation, through feasibility studies, into remedial design, and finally through cleanup action implementation.
Provide formal engineering oversight to ensure all formal project activities comply with the Model Toxics Control Act (MTCA), Sediment Management Standards (SMS), Sediment Cleanup User’s Manual (SCUM), and other applicable regulations, policies, and guidance documents.
Lead Key Site Meetings with Liable Parties to advance formal cleanup projects through MTCA stage-gates.
Conduct annual field visits for all assigned sites to observe investigation, monitoring, sampling, pilot testing, full scale remediation, and other cleanup activities; travel is required to complete these visits.
Review technical documents such as work plans, environmental assessments, remedial investigation reports, feasibility study reports, models, cleanup action plans, and remedial designs to ensure documents are complete, technically sound, and compliant with regulatory requirements.
Prepare clear and explicit directives to liable parties and the public through written communication, including letters, memos, technical reports, bulletins, and fact sheets.
Manage project scope, schedule, and data, including organizing electronic and physical records, ensuring required data submittals, and maintaining information in agency systems.
Oversee Washington State Remedial Action Grant (RAG) funding for assigned projects by reviewing payment requests progress reports (PRPRs) and approval/denial processes for reasonable and necessary costs.
Develop new Agreed Orders, Consent Decrees, and Enforcement Orders in partnership with Attorney General’s Office and in accordance with agency policies and procedures.
When necessary, develop and manage project support contracts in partnership with a Program Contracts Officer and in accordance with agency policies and procedures.
When necessary, provide environmental engineering expertise to colleagues, support review of complex Unit projects, and contribute to activities such as initial investigations, State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) reviews, or periodic reviews.

Required Qualifications

Registration as a Professional Engineer in the state of Washington or another state based on registration requirements equivalent to those in Washington AND
Five years of experience in environmental engineering, which includes the following:

Communication and Professional Judgment – Ability to prepare clear, accurate, and directive written and verbal communication that supports sound technical decisions and conveys expectations to others.
Collaboration and Coordination – Skill in organizing and coordinating project information and activities with a range of internal and external parties to support progress and resolve complex issues.
Project Management – Ability to plan, prioritize, and guide project activities to meet milestones, regulatory requirements, and schedules.
Project Financial Skills – Ability to evaluate project costs, review consultant invoices, and understand the financial aspects of environmental engineering tasks.
Cleanup Project Implementation – Experience applying environmental laws, rules, and guidance (such as Model Toxics Control Act, Sediment Management Standards, and Sediment Cleanup User’s Manual, or similar) to move contaminated sites through cleanup processes and ensure regulatory compliance.
Environmental Cleanup Engineering – Ability to evaluate contamination data, assess remedial alternatives, and review technical documents that support the selection and approval of cleanup actions protective of human health and the environment.

Applicants qualifying through the licensing equivalency option must achieve registration as a Professional Engineer in the state of Washington within six months of appointment to this class.

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Shorelands & Environmental Assistance (SEA) Program Manager

Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

We are looking for a transformational leader who is ready to partner with a dedicated team of professionals to guide Washington’s statewide efforts to protect and restore shorelands, wetlands, coastal areas, and floodplains; strengthen community resilience; advance clean energy siting; and support conservation and hazard-mitigation initiatives across diverse landscapes.

In this role, you will serve as the executive leader for the Department of Ecology’s Shorelands and Environmental Assistance (SEA) Program—a statewide program that integrates science, planning, policy, permitting, funding, and community partnerships to protect Washington’s environment and help communities thrive. You will provide strategic leadership and direction for major state and federal programs, oversee complex regulatory and policy work, and cultivate partnerships that support resilient ecosystems, sustainable community development, and climate preparedness.

Responsibilities Include

Planning, leading, organizing, and directing the statewide Shorelands and Environmental Assistance Program by negotiating program scope, priorities, resources, and outcomes.
Overseeing the development and implementation of policies, rules, and guidance that shape statewide shorelands, wetlands, floodplain management, clean energy coordination, and coastal resilience—affecting all 39 counties and numerous regulated entities.
Leading the program’s strategic direction to align shorelands protection, watershed-based planning, coastal management, hazard mitigation, clean energy siting, and community conservation initiatives with Ecology’s mission and statewide environmental priorities.
Administering state and delegated federal programs including the Shoreline Management Act, State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA), the Coastal Zone Management Act, the Clean Water Act Section 401 Water Quality Certification Program, and wetland and floodplain management authorities.
Managing the program’s operating and capital budgets, personnel, and resources to ensure responsible, transparent, and effective stewardship of public funds.
Hiring, leading, and developing managers, supervisors, and senior policy staff while fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing workplace that supports diversity, staff engagement, and professional growth.
Ensuring high-quality, defensible regulatory and scientific outcomes across program functions including planning, permitting, wetlands and flood hazard review, clean energy coordination, coastal hazard mitigation, and community-based conservation.
Overseeing major statewide initiatives such as Floodplain by Design; Wetland Mitigation Banking; Shoreline Management Act; critical areas ordinances under the Growth Management Act; and the stewardship, research, education, and community science missions of the Padilla Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, the Northwest Straits Commission, and the Washington Conservation Corps.
Serving as Washington’s designated Coastal Manager, representing the state before federal agencies and negotiating on matters related to the Coastal Zone Management Act.
Coordinating Ecology’s disaster response activities related to severe storms, catastrophic floods, wildfires, and other natural hazards through deployment of Washington Conservation Corps resources.
Building and maintaining strong partnerships with Tribes; federal, state, and local government partners; conservation organizations; environmental justice advocates; regulated entities; and community-based organizations.
Integrating SEA’s work across Ecology programs—especially Water Quality, Water Resources, Toxics Cleanup, Climate Pollution Reduction, and Environmental Assessment—to promote watershed-based, cross-program alignment and effective statewide outcomes.

Who are we looking for?

We Are Seeking An Experienced, Collaborative Leader Ready To Guide a Diverse, Multi-disciplinary Program With Statewide Reach. You Will Need The Ability To

Think strategically, anticipate long-term needs, and adapt to emerging opportunities and challenges affecting Washington’s shorelands, wetlands, floodplains, and coastal communities.
Communicate effectively with a wide range of partners—including Tribal governments, local communities, environmental and industry partners, scientists, planners, and elected officials—to support informed decision-making and build durable, trust-based relationships.
Navigate complex state and federal environmental laws, policies, and regulatory frameworks and translate them into cohesive, strategic program direction.
Understand the interconnectedness of the program’s regulatory, scientific, and community-driven work—and how these efforts impact ecosystems, communities, and statewide resilience.
Advance equitable, science-based outcomes that protect Washington’s environment and support community wellbeing.

A Key Member of Ecology’s Executive Leadership Team

This position serves as a key member of the Washington State Department of Ecology’s Executive Leadership Team and plays a critical role in advancing the agency’s mission to protect, preserve, and enhance Washington’s environment for current and future generations.

It is essential that this position model the highest standards of personal, professional, and ethical conduct in support of efficient, effective, and accountable government.

This is a highly visible executive role responsible for providing statewide leadership on shorelands, wetlands, floodplains, coastal management, hazard mitigation, conservation partnerships, and clean energy project coordination. The position represents Ecology’s environmental, scientific, and policy interests with Tribal governments, environmental justice advocates, local communities, academic institutions, regulated industries, partner agencies, elected officials, and the public.

Represent the Director and agency leadership before federal, state, local, Tribal, and elected officials; partner agencies; environmental organizations; environmental justice advocates; and the public.

Advocate for a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and respectful workplace culture that supports innovation, accountability, and staff engagement.

You will work with dedicated colleagues, Tribal and community partners, and leaders across all levels of government to deliver lasting, meaningful benefits for people and places statewide.

Duties

Do you want to help solve real-world water quality challenges through green infrastructure? Do you have experience with planning, designing, constructing, or maintaining public infrastructure projects? Are you interested in partnering with local governments and Tribes to protect important cultural resources?

Join the Ecology Stormwater Action Team (SWAT). SWAT partners with communities statewide to fund and implement stormwater quality, green infrastructure, and low-impact development projects. With more than 250 active projects across Washington, this team helps local governments navigate funding, project design, construction, and long-term performance to ensure meaningful water quality outcomes.

As a Senior Stormwater Project Specialist, you will build strong working relationships with local stormwater and capital project managers, helping them develop high-quality proposals and avoid common project pitfalls. You will participate in evaluating new project applications, negotiate funding agreements, and provide technical assistance throughout the life of each project—ensuring compliance with state and federal funding requirements.

You will also play an important part in protecting cultural resources. You will represent SWAT on the Ecology Cultural Resources Environmental Workgroup and coordinate Cultural Resource Reviews in partnership with Tribes and the Department of Archaeology and Historic Preservation to ensure state-funded stormwater projects are sited and constructed responsibly.

What You Will Do

Coordinate with local government project managers to monitor project progress on Ecology-funded stormwater quality projects. This includes review of quarterly reports, payment requests, and project deliverables and performing site visits.
Solicit and coordinate input from internal project management teams to provide oversight for funded projects. Ensure that funded projects maintain compliance with funding agreement terms, funding program guidelines, agency policy, and state and federal funding program requirements.
Negotiate and write new funding agreements. Incorporate input from project evaluators, Ecology engineers, financial management staff, and other Ecology subject matter experts during the agreement negotiation process and throughout the life of the project.

jobs.title: Data Analyst — DoT LiDAR
jobs.description:
Precision Federal has been awarded a firm\-fixed\-price contract by the U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Highway Administration, to evaluate 3D LiDAR and smartphone\-based platforms for collecting motor vehicle traffic and roadway geometry data. The work is performed for the Turner\-Fairbank Highway Research Center. Purchase order 693JJ326P000024, awarded September 4, 2026, period of performance 24 months.

Nine drivers will record a month of their daily trips on their own phones through two Iowa road sites, an innovative interchange and a winding two\-lane segment. A vehicle\-mounted 3D LiDAR survey covers the same roads. You are the person who makes sure the data that reaches the Government is complete, correct, and reproducible.

What you would do

\- Run quality checks on incoming trip data as it arrives: completeness, GPS and sensor sanity, timestamp continuity, coverage of each site per driver

\- Keep the quality\-control log that goes to the Government with the dataset: what was checked, what was rejected, why

\- Build the horizontal curve inventory for each site from the trip and LiDAR data: curve start and end points, radius, superelevation, and speed through each curve

\- Compare posted speed limits against design\-supported safe speed at each curve, working with our licensed Professional Engineer who reviews the findings

\- Produce the figures and tables for the Task 3 and Task 4 reports and the final report, reproducible from code

\- Join a short progress call once a month

Requirements

\- Python with GeoPandas, Shapely, or GDAL, and SQL with PostGIS or an equivalent spatial database

\- Experience checking real sensor or GPS data for quality: gaps, drift, outliers, clock offsets

\- Comfortable computing geometry from coordinates: distances, headings, curve fitting, radius of curvature

\- Reproducible work habits: scripts and notebooks under version control, results a second person can rerun

\- Clear written English. Your QC notes go to a federal research center

Preferred

\- Transportation or roadway geometry work: AASHTO Green Book concepts, superelevation, design speed

\- Experience with vehicle telematics, naturalistic driving data, or smartphone sensor logs (GPS, accelerometer, gyroscope)

\- Point\-cloud experience: PDAL, Open3D, CloudCompare, or LiDAR\-derived surfaces

\- Prior work on a federally funded research project, or a state department of transportation

How this works

Part\-time consulting on a funded federal contract, performed remotely on your own schedule. Roughly 80 to 150 hours between March 2027 and September 2028, concentrated in the collection month and the analysis and reporting periods. Hourly, invoiced monthly. You will be named on the project team and credited in the final report.

Pay: $50\.00 per hour

Application Question(s):

* Describe one dataset where you found and fixed a quality problem in sensor or GPS data. What was wrong and how did you catch it?
* Which of these have you used in the last two years: GeoPandas, GDAL, PostGIS, PDAL, QGIS, ArcGIS?
* Have you computed curve radius or superelevation from coordinate or survey data? Where?
* Are you willing to be named on the project team and credited in a report delivered to the Federal Highway Administration?

Work Location: Remote

Working at Mecklenburg County for LUESA, (Land Use and Environmental Service Agency) you will help to provide key services that will contribute to an exceptional quality of life for Mecklenburg County residents. LUESA’s responsibilities range from enforcing building and zoning codes to managing water and air resources for future generations.

More About The Role

The Mecklenburg County Solid Waste management program has two vacancies in our Environmental Specialist II class. We are seeking highly motivated individuals that have environmental backgrounds that enjoy working outdoors. As an Env. Specialist II, you would perform environmental sampling activities at our various facilities, as well as inspections of facilities that hold environmental permits.

What Will I Be Doing

Work will include sampling of groundwater wells, collecting surface water samples, and monitoring landfill gas wells. This job will require the successful applicant to spend a significant amount of time in the field, and not in an office environment. The position will also inspect some non-County facilities, and this job will require driving County vehicles and a valid driver’s license. The successful applicant will gather data, prepare reports, and present to internal management. Knowledge of environmental regulations is desired. The incumbents may also assist the Solid Waste Management Program in developing and implementing outreach, operational and environmental programs involving waste and recycling. Work will be centric around: developing and implementing waste management strategies, building, and maintaining relationships with the impacted communities.

The position will be involved with the implementation of the Solid Waste Program Environmental Management System (EMS). The position will be part of a team that monitors and regulates the community about solid waste management and waste minimization strategies and incumbent must have strong communication skills. Around the world, SYSTRA’s specialists plan, design, integrate, test, commission, project manage and deliver mass transit and mobility solutions that are relied on by more than 50 million people every day.

For more than 60 years, the Group has been committed to helping cities and regions contribute to their development by creating, improving and modernising their transport infrastructure with sustainability, accessibility and innovation at the heart of our designs. With over 10,300 colleagues globally and around 1000 in the UK & Ireland we are growing significantly and seeking out the very best talent to join the SYSTRA signature team and be part of leading the way in infrastructure design.

Context

We currently have an opportunity for an experienced Senior Environmental Consultant to join our growing team. This position within our environmental team will suit a committed and ambitious Environmental Consultant who can demonstrate strong growth, leadership and interpersonal skills combined with commercial awareness and the ability to play their part in growing a dynamic high-performance team.

The Senior Environment Consultant will support our environmental team in Ireland as our workload continues to grow, with a clear objective to further expand both the workstream and the team in the region.

Support the delivery of Environmental Impact Assessments and environmental assessments:

Ensuring thorough coordination of multidisciplinary teams, including authoring chapters and technical reviews of specialist chapters
Involvement across all project life stages (feasibility, option selection, outline design, to detailed design and construction).
Critical eye for detail to ensure deliverables are produced to the highest quality standards

Monitoring and forecasting project performance and undertaking project reviews
Stakeholder engagement, including client communication and public consultations
Support and mentor junior team members

Supporting tender preparations

Assisting with team business development and marketing

Demonstrable experience working within an environmental consultancy
Membership or chartership of a recognised environmental professional body (e.g., ISEP, CIWEM)

Experience in coordinating EIAs and environmental assessments and managing multidisciplinary environmental inputs
Experience in supporting bids, proposals or other business activities
Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Commitment to continuing professional development

jobs.description:
About Atlas

Atlas is a trusted leader in environmental and infrastructure consulting services; we provide services that enable communities to flourish and thrive. With a team of 3,500 employees and offices throughout the US, we combine local expertise and a network of relationships to deliver solutions to both public and private clients. Our services help improve the quality of life in the communities where we live and work. We always aim for smart, safe, and sustainable results. At Atlas we understand that our future is everyone’s responsibility, and we create a better experience at every stage of a project.

Job Description

At Atlas, we're providing services that enable communities to flourish and thrive, and if you’re an Environmental Project Assistant
ready to assist with the daily coordination and writing of technical reports in support of local clients and are committed to doing meaningful work, then this is your moment. You may also be completing various other important tasks using Microsoft applications. Join a dynamic, value-driven, client and community-focused environment where your work creates a lasting positive impact for the people and communities we serve.

Core Responsibilities

Gathering and Reviewing Documents from Field Team and Analytical Results from Laboratory
Drafting written reports based on project documents
Providing status updates on progress to senior team members
Communicating and coordinating with field team members to obtain clarification and/or project documents
Attend periodic team meetings

You’ll thrive here if you have

High School Diploma or GED Required
3-5 years of report writing experience preferred
1-2 year's experience with bachelor's degree considered
Familiar with all Microsoft applications
Background in Environmental Science or another science-related field preferred
Strong knowledge of Microsoft Applications, such as Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft Word, and Excel, is a must.
Must be able to communicate clearly
Must take a pro-active approach to work and require minimal supervision once trained

Health & Wellness: We offer medical, dental and vision coverage with multiple plan options, including no-cost employee-only medical coverage.

jobs.description:
Company Description
Flood Emergency Services is recognized as an honest, hard-working disaster response company, trusted by clients across the country. Feedback from customers highlights clear communication, fast action, and effective coordination of technicians. The team is known for reducing stress during challenging situations and restoring properties efficiently. Prospective team members can expect a supportive work environment focused on professionalism, integrity, and high-quality service.
Role Description
As a Water Restoration Specialist at Flood Emergency Services, you will perform on-site assessments of water damage, extract standing water, and set up drying equipment in residential and commercial properties. You will document damage, take photos, prepare basic reports, and communicate clearly with clients about the restoration process and timelines. Daily tasks include cleaning and sanitizing affected areas, removing damaged materials, and assisting with minor repairs to help return properties to a safe condition. This is a full-time hybrid role based in West Footscray, VIC, with a combination of on-site work and some work-from-home tasks such as documentation and follow-up calls.
Qualifications

Experience in water damage restoration, disaster recovery, or a related trade (e.g., construction, plumbing) and familiarity with restoration tools and equipment.
Strong communication and customer service skills, with the ability to work calmly and professionally in high-stress situations.
Solid organizational skills, including accurate recordkeeping, basic reporting, and attention to detail in following safety and industry standards.
Physical ability to perform manual labor such as lifting equipment, moving damaged materials, and working in confined or damp spaces.
Willingness to work flexible hours, including some evenings, weekends, and emergency call-outs as needed.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transport to attend jobs in and around West Footscray, VIC.
Commitment to honest, ethical work practices and contributing positively to a team-focused, service-oriented culture.
Relevant certifications in restoration or safety (e.g., IICRC Water Damage Restoration, first aid) are advantageous but not mandatory.

jobs.title: Environmental Practice Leader Transportation & Natural Resource
jobs.description:
We Make Everything Around Us Better

At PRIME AE, that’s not a slogan, it’s how we work.

Every bridge, building, campus, park, and roadway we design exists to improve how people live, move, learn, and connect. Through architecture, engineering, planning, and consulting, we partner with clients to create thoughtful, practical solutions that leave communities stronger than we found them.

If you want your work to matter, and to be surrounded by smart, collaborative people who care about doing things the right way, you’ll feel at home here.

Who We Are:

PRIME AE Group, Inc.
( www.primeeng.com ) is a nationally ranked, full-service architecture and engineering firm driven by collaboration, innovation, and a commitment to strengthening the communities we serve. With a growing footprint of offices across the country and a diverse team of more than 550 professionals, we partner with public and private sector clients to deliver thoughtful, high-impact solutions across transportation, education, healthcare, municipal, federal, commercial, and recreational markets.

Our culture blends entrepreneurial energy with the resources of a scaled, multidisciplinary platform—giving our people the opportunity to shape meaningful projects while influencing the future direction of the firm. As PRIME AE continues to expand its capabilities, geographic reach, and leadership bench, this is an exciting time to join a team that is building momentum, investing in growth, and empowering leaders to make a lasting impact.

The Opportunity:

We are currently seeking an Environmental Practice Leader – Transportation & Natural Resources to join our Indianapolis, Akron, New Albany, Columbus, Cincinnati, or Louisville office.

The position may be structured as either an Environmental Project Manager or Environmental Practice Leader depending on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and leadership background.

This is an exciting opportunity for an environmental professional who wants to remain actively involved in technical project work while helping build and grow PRIME AE’s environmental capabilities. We are seeking someone with approximately 6–15 years of experience who brings a strong technical foundation in environmental services and an interest in taking on increasing responsibility for project management, client relationships, staff development, and team leadership.

In this role, you will initially work alongside PRIME AE’s Transportation and Natural Resources teams to deliver environmental services for infrastructure projects while helping establish and grow an environmental team. As the practice expands, you will have the opportunity to take on greater responsibility for managing staff, developing client relationships, supporting business development, and helping shape the long-term direction of the environmental practice.

You will collaborate with transportation, water resources, roadway, bridge, traffic, survey, and planning professionals on projects for state DOTs, local agencies, municipalities, and other infrastructure clients. The ideal candidate will bring experience in areas such as NEPA documentation, wetland and stream delineations, waterway permitting, natural resources, agency coordination, and environmental compliance.

What You’ll Do:

As an Environmental Practice Leader – Transportation & Natural Resources, you will serve in a hands-on seller/doer role that combines technical project delivery with the opportunity to play a key role in shaping and expanding PRIME AE's environmental practice.

You will perform and manage environmental work on transportation and infrastructure projects, coordinate with regulatory agencies and multidisciplinary design teams, and provide technical guidance throughout project development. Depending on your experience, you may lead projects independently or work alongside senior leaders while continuing to expand your project management and leadership responsibilities.

As the environmental workload and team grow, you will help recruit and mentor staff, coordinate resources, develop client relationships, support strategic pursuits, and establish processes that position the environmental practice for long-term success.

Key Responsibilities:

Perform and manage environmental services for transportation and infrastructure projects involving state DOTs, local agencies, municipalities, counties, and other public-sector clients.
Prepare, manage, and review environmental documentation in accordance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and applicable state and federal requirements.
Prepare and/or review Categorical Exclusions, environmental technical studies and memoranda, environmental commitments, alternatives analyses, agency coordination documentation, and public involvement materials.
Conduct and/or oversee wetland and stream delineations, jurisdictional waters evaluations, habitat assessments, threatened and endangered species reviews, impact assessments, and other environmental field investigations.
Prepare and coordinate environmental permits, including Clean Water Act Section 404 permits, Section 401 Water Quality Certifications, state waterway and floodplain permits, and other applicable environmental approvals.
Coordinate with regulatory and resource agencies, including USACE, USFWS, IDEM, IDNR, Kentucky Division of Water, Ohio EPA, and other applicable agencies.
Collaborate with roadway, bridge, traffic, drainage, water resources, and other project teams to identify environmental constraints early and incorporate environmental commitments into project development.
Serve as an environmental project manager and/or technical lead on multidisciplinary transportation and infrastructure projects.
Develop project scopes, fees, schedules, budgets, staffing plans, and technical approaches.
Monitor project schedules, budgets, quality, and client expectations.
Provide technical review and QA/QC of environmental documents, studies, permit applications, and other deliverables.
Maintain awareness of changing environmental regulations, agency procedures, and permitting requirements.
Build and maintain relationships with transportation agencies, municipalities, regulatory agencies, clients, and teaming partners.
Identify environmental project opportunities and support proposals, letters of interest, qualifications packages, interviews, and other pursuit activities.
Help forecast environmental workload and staffing needs as the practice grows.
Support the recruitment, mentoring, and development of environmental scientists, planners, and specialists as workload increases.
Help develop technical standards, quality-control procedures, and consistent project-delivery practices for the growing environmental team.
Support the expansion of environmental prequalification’s, certifications, and service capabilities.
Participate in industry organizations, conferences, agency meetings, and professional events.
Balance technical project responsibilities with client development and business development activities to help establish a sustainable environmental workload and backlog.

What You’ll Bring:

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Planning, Natural Resources, Civil/Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
7+ years of progressive environmental consulting, natural resources, or transportation environmental experience.
Experience supporting transportation and/or infrastructure projects.
Working knowledge of NEPA, Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, wetlands, streams, natural resources, environmental permitting, and applicable state and federal requirements.
Experience preparing and/or supporting NEPA documentation and environmental technical studies.
Experience with wetland and stream delineations, environmental field investigations, and/or waterway permitting.
Experience coordinating with state and federal regulatory agencies.
Project management experience or demonstrated readiness to take on increasing project management responsibilities, including scopes, fees, budgets, schedules, and staffing.
Strong analytical, technical writing, communication, and organizational skills.
Ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary engineering and planning teams.
Interest in mentoring others and helping build and develop an environmental team.
Ability and willingness to support client relationships, proposals, and business development activities.
Experience working with INDOT, KYTC, ODOT, FHWA, and/or local public agencies is preferred.
Familiarity with applicable Indiana, Kentucky, and/or Ohio environmental procedures and permitting requirements is preferred.
Existing environmental qualifications, certifications, or the ability to obtain applicable agency prequalification’s is preferred.
Established industry or agency relationships within Indiana, Kentucky, and/or Ohio are a plus.
Professional certifications or credentials relevant to environmental or natural resources services are preferred.

Why PRIME AE:

We don’t just fill positions; we invest in people.

At PRIME AE, you’ll find a supportive, flexible environment where careers are built intentionally, not accidentally. You’ll work on projects that improve everyday life, alongside colleagues who challenge and respect one another.

What sets us apart:

Career Growth: Flexible career paths across disciplines, from technical expertise to project and people leadership.
People-First Culture: We value trust, integrity, and collaboration, and we mean it.
Meaningful Work: Projects that strengthen communities, infrastructure, and public spaces.
Growth with Purpose: Strategic expansion backed by strong leadership and investment.
National Reach, Local Feel: Big-firm resources with the agility and relationships of local offices.

Our Commitment:

PRIME AE Group is committed to creating an inclusive environment where differences are respected, voices are heard, and everyone has the opportunity to succeed.

Job Summary

Supports environmental compliance at existing and proposed Renewable Project sites through active onsite support.

Job Duties/Responsibilities

Provide expert guidance to project and site personnel regarding environmental issues
Work in direct support of the projects and sites to ensure regulatory compliance
Maintain thorough knowledge of project and site-specific environmental permits and plans
Conduct project and site inspections to assess environmental compliance and performance with all applicable permit conditions and regulations, documenting findings as required, and taking necessary action to close any identified gaps
Prepare regulatory required environmental reports
Maintain required environmental records and documentation for the projects and sites
Deliver environmental training to project and site personnel as required by applicable regulations and company procedures and programs
Provide environmental compliance support to respond to spills and releases, and make notifications as required by applicable regulations
Manage waste handling and disposal, and manifesting activities
Coordinate environmental sampling and testing activities as required by applicable regulations and permits
Participate in work groups to support new and ongoing projects
Identify and execute continuous improvement opportunities
Manage records and documentation pertaining to compliance programs in accordance with the records retention policy

Minimum Requirements

Minimum Education:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent work experience

Minimum Experience

Analyst – Environmental I-II: 0- 2 years of experience handling environmental compliance activities.
Analyst – Environmental III: 3 - 5 years of experience handling environmental compliance activities.
Analyst – Environmental Sr.: 5- 6 years of experience handling environmental compliance activities

Minimum Skills

Applicant must be physically able to conduct field environmental investigations
Excellent communication skills (verbal and written)
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple work tasks simultaneously
Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a team setting
Strong attention to details
Strong analytical skills
Strong problem solving and critical thinking skills
Self-starter and requires little or no supervision
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite of products
Excellent organizational skills, ability to organize and prioritize work
Ability to work effectively on multiple assignments
Flexible and able to adjust to changing priorities
Willing and able to perform other unrelated duties as required and learn new processes and technologies

Desired

Experience managing environmental programs in an industrial or power generation setting
Experience in preparing environmental reports for an industrial or power generation facility
Experience in managing oil storage and use including oil spills in accordance with federal and state requirements
Experience in managing hazardous materials and hazardous waste shipments in accordance with DOT and RCRA requirements
Knowledge of power generation fundamentals

Office environment with minimal physical requirements
Available to work periodic overtime

( www.primeeng.com ) is a nationally ranked, full-service architecture and engineering firm driven by collaboration, innovation, and a commitment to strengthening the communities we serve. With a growing footprint of offices across the country and a diverse team of more than 550 professionals, we partner with public and private sector clients to deliver thoughtful, high-impact solutions across transportation, education, healthcare, municipal, federal, commercial, and recreational markets.

Our culture blends entrepreneurial energy with the resources of a scaled, multidisciplinary platform—giving our people the opportunity to shape meaningful projects while influencing the future direction of the firm. As PRIME AE continues to expand its capabilities, geographic reach, and leadership bench, this is an exciting time to join a team that is building momentum, investing in growth, and empowering leaders to make a lasting impact.

The Opportunity:

We are currently seeking an Environmental Practice Leader – Transportation & Natural Resources to join our Indianapolis, Akron, New Albany, Columbus, Cincinnati, or Louisville office.

The position may be structured as either an Environmental Project Manager or Environmental Practice Leader depending on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and leadership background.

This is an exciting opportunity for an environmental professional who wants to remain actively involved in technical project work while helping build and grow PRIME AE’s environmental capabilities. We are seeking someone with approximately 6–15 years of experience who brings a strong technical foundation in environmental services and an interest in taking on increasing responsibility for project management, client relationships, staff development, and team leadership.

In this role, you will initially work alongside PRIME AE’s Transportation and Natural Resources teams to deliver environmental services for infrastructure projects while helping establish and grow an environmental team. As the practice expands, you will have the opportunity to take on greater responsibility for managing staff, developing client relationships, supporting business development, and helping shape the long-term direction of the environmental practice.

You will collaborate with transportation, water resources, roadway, bridge, traffic, survey, and planning professionals on projects for state DOTs, local agencies, municipalities, and other infrastructure clients. The ideal candidate will bring experience in areas such as NEPA documentation, wetland and stream delineations, waterway permitting, natural resources, agency coordination, and environmental compliance.

What You’ll Do:

As an Environmental Practice Leader – Transportation & Natural Resources, you will serve in a hands-on seller/doer role that combines technical project delivery with the opportunity to play a key role in shaping and expanding PRIME AE's environmental practice.

You will perform and manage environmental work on transportation and infrastructure projects, coordinate with regulatory agencies and multidisciplinary design teams, and provide technical guidance throughout project development. Depending on your experience, you may lead projects independently or work alongside senior leaders while continuing to expand your project management and leadership responsibilities.

As the environmental workload and team grow, you will help recruit and mentor staff, coordinate resources, develop client relationships, support strategic pursuits, and establish processes that position the environmental practice for long-term success.

Key Responsibilities:

Perform and manage environmental services for transportation and infrastructure projects involving state DOTs, local agencies, municipalities, counties, and other public-sector clients.
Prepare, manage, and review environmental documentation in accordance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and applicable state and federal requirements.
Prepare and/or review Categorical Exclusions, environmental technical studies and memoranda, environmental commitments, alternatives analyses, agency coordination documentation, and public involvement materials.
Conduct and/or oversee wetland and stream delineations, jurisdictional waters evaluations, habitat assessments, threatened and endangered species reviews, impact assessments, and other environmental field investigations.
Prepare and coordinate environmental permits, including Clean Water Act Section 404 permits, Section 401 Water Quality Certifications, state waterway and floodplain permits, and other applicable environmental approvals.
Coordinate with regulatory and resource agencies, including USACE, USFWS, IDEM, IDNR, Kentucky Division of Water, Ohio EPA, and other applicable agencies.
Collaborate with roadway, bridge, traffic, drainage, water resources, and other project teams to identify environmental constraints early and incorporate environmental commitments into project development.
Serve as an environmental project manager and/or technical lead on multidisciplinary transportation and infrastructure projects.
Develop project scopes, fees, schedules, budgets, staffing plans, and technical approaches.
Monitor project schedules, budgets, quality, and client expectations.
Provide technical review and QA/QC of environmental documents, studies, permit applications, and other deliverables.
Maintain awareness of changing environmental regulations, agency procedures, and permitting requirements.
Build and maintain relationships with transportation agencies, municipalities, regulatory agencies, clients, and teaming partners.
Identify environmental project opportunities and support proposals, letters of interest, qualifications packages, interviews, and other pursuit activities.
Help forecast environmental workload and staffing needs as the practice grows.
Support the recruitment, mentoring, and development of environmental scientists, planners, and specialists as workload increases.
Help develop technical standards, quality-control procedures, and consistent project-delivery practices for the growing environmental team.
Support the expansion of environmental prequalification’s, certifications, and service capabilities.
Participate in industry organizations, conferences, agency meetings, and professional events.
Balance technical project responsibilities with client development and business development activities to help establish a sustainable environmental workload and backlog.

What You’ll Bring:

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Planning, Natural Resources, Civil/Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
7+ years of progressive environmental consulting, natural resources, or transportation environmental experience.
Experience supporting transportation and/or infrastructure projects.
Working knowledge of NEPA, Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, wetlands, streams, natural resources, environmental permitting, and applicable state and federal requirements.
Experience preparing and/or supporting NEPA documentation and environmental technical studies.
Experience with wetland and stream delineations, environmental field investigations, and/or waterway permitting.
Experience coordinating with state and federal regulatory agencies.
Project management experience or demonstrated readiness to take on increasing project management responsibilities, including scopes, fees, budgets, schedules, and staffing.
Strong analytical, technical writing, communication, and organizational skills.
Ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary engineering and planning teams.
Interest in mentoring others and helping build and develop an environmental team.
Ability and willingness to support client relationships, proposals, and business development activities.
Experience working with INDOT, KYTC, ODOT, FHWA, and/or local public agencies is preferred.
Familiarity with applicable Indiana, Kentucky, and/or Ohio environmental procedures and permitting requirements is preferred.
Existing environmental qualifications, certifications, or the ability to obtain applicable agency prequalification’s is preferred.
Established industry or agency relationships within Indiana, Kentucky, and/or Ohio are a plus.
Professional certifications or credentials relevant to environmental or natural resources services are preferred.

Why PRIME AE:

We don’t just fill positions; we invest in people.

At PRIME AE, you’ll find a supportive, flexible environment where careers are built intentionally, not accidentally. You’ll work on projects that improve everyday life, alongside colleagues who challenge and respect one another.

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a Senior Technical Manager, Environmental Engineer
in Greensboro, NC
to provide subject matter technical support and leadership for multi-site/phase environmental engineering work processes, due diligence, investigation, remediation, impact assessment, and environmental permitting projects. Ensures project elements and processes relating to water supply, hazardous or solid waste disposal, air emission sources, pollution control, and preserving the environment. are conveyed and acted upon with a high level of quality and compliance. Responsible for providing situational guidance to PMs and managers that address current and future environmental challenges, and that documentation and recommendations accurately account for and address long-term risks to ecological and human health. Leads environmental site assessments, corrective strategies, classification of contaminated materials, and treatment, disposal, and/or onsite remediation activities to avert degradation of air, water, and land resources. Ensures that responsibilities are delivered and adhered to with a level of quality that meets or exceeds acceptable industry standards.

jobs.title: Environmental Programs Specialist I/II
jobs.description:
Summary

Environmental Programs Specialist I: $63,236 - $84,742 annually

Environmental Programs Specialist II: $78,973 - $105,831 annually

If you want to join a hardworking team that shares a commitment to provide top-quality municipal services in a prime North County location, consider a career with the City of Escondido. We have an opening for the position of Environmental Programs Specialist I/II in our Utilities Department/Environmental Programs Division. For a complete listing of job duties and qualifications, please refer to the corresponding job description, which can be obtained from the Human Resources Department or downloaded from the City's website.

Under general supervision (Environmental Programs Specialist I) or general direction (Environmental Programs Specialist II), administers the City’s storm water program and other related environmental programs or projects through the development and facilitation of various activities with other departments, divisions, outside agencies, and the general public, as well as provides responsible and moderately complex (Environmental Programs Specialist I) or specialized and complex (Environmental Programs Specialist II) professional staff assistance to the Environmental Programs Supervisor and Utility Manager.

DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS

Environmental Programs Specialist I:
This is the entry-level class in the Environmental Programs Specialist series. Positions at this level are not expected to function with the same amount of program knowledge or skill level as positions allocated to the Environmental Programs Specialist and exercise less independent discretion and judgment in matters related to work procedures and methods. Work is usually supervised while in progress and fits an established structure or pattern.

Environmental Programs Specialist II:
This is the full journey-level class in the Environmental Programs Specialist series. Positions at this level are distinguished from the Environmental Programs Specialist I level by the performance of the full range of duties assigned, working independently, applying well developed knowledge, and exercising judgment and initiative. Positions at this level receive only occasional instruction or assistance as new or unusual situations arise, and are fully aware of the operating procedures and policies of the work unit. Work is normally reviewed only upon completion and for overall results. Positions in this class series are flexibly staffed and positions at the Environmental Programs Specialist II level are normally filled by advancement from the Environmental Programs Specialist I level.

Key Responsibilities

The following duties are typical for this classification. Incumbents may not perform all of the listed duties and/or may be required to perform additional or different duties from those set forth below to address business needs and changing business practices.

Plans, organizes and participates in the permitting, monitoring, inspection, enforcement, pollution prevention, and data management activities of the Storm Water Program and other related environmental programs or projects as assigned in accordance with federal, state and local laws and National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits.

Coordinates and participates in the investigation of storm water runoff, industrial related storm water quality problems, as well as complaints and violations of storm water regulations and codes.

Prepares outreach materials, conducts outreach efforts and trains City staff on storm water and environmental protection provides information to property and business owners, tenants, City employees, and the general public through individual contact in the field, over the counter, at workshops or community events, and by telephone or other appropriate means.

Coordinates with other City departments to improve levels of compliance with the NPDES permit; coordinates with and provides information and technical assistance to other departments, agencies, and organizations related to environmental programs

Prepares notices of violation and compliance schedules in cooperation with violators; prepares and maintains records of investigations and actions taken.

Coordinates and implements the City’s annual dry weather monitoring program in compliance with its NPDES Storm Water Discharge permit.

Reviews construction plans to identify storm water discharge sources and best management practices (structural and non-structural) to maximize storm water and water quality protection.

Evaluates and interprets technical reports, documents, manifests, applications and permits related to environmental regulations and compliance with local, state, and federal regulations.

Maintains inspection files, records, and logs; writes reports and chronologies; schedules work activities and inspections independently to meet program objectives in a timely manner; maintains records and prepares reports concerning new or ongoing programs and program effectiveness; maintains and updates various databases and filing and record keeping systems for assigned program; participates in researching and collecting data and information for inclusion into database and record keeping systems; conducts surveys; analyzes and interprets data collected; prepares reports and distributes requested information to appropriate parties in a timely manner including reports to regulatory agencies.

Assists in the development and implementation of policies, procedures and other program requirements for education, inspections, complaint response, watershed activities, water quality monitoring, annual report writing, inter-departmental training and coordination.

Coordinates actions and/or programs with other agencies, e.g., other cities, the county and state departments, such as coordinating regional inspections, education, or enforcement measures; represents the City at regional meetings; serves as liaison and provides support to assigned program activities with those of other City departments and staff as well as community organizations, the general public, and other groups.

Develops, writes, and maintains a variety of reports, documents, correspondence and records related to areas of assigned responsibility; prepares and writes compliance reports and associated correspondence to regulatory agencies.

Researches availability of grant monies for projects related to the department’s responsibilities, as well as writes and administers successful applications.

Provides training, direction and guidance for City staff as directed by the Environmental Programs Supervisor and Utility Environmental Programs Manager.

Provides responsible professional level staff assistance and technical and administrative support to the Environmental Programs Supervisor and Utility Environmental Programs Manager and other management staff, as well as boards and committees; researches, prepares, and presents technical, fiscal, and administrative studies, surveys, and reports.

Conducts and represents the City at various meetings and makes presentations to public interest groups, City personnel and others as directed.

Keeps current with federal, state and local regulations and their impacts on the City’s storm water and environmental quality and protection.

Provides vacation and temporary relief as needed.

Performs related duties as required.

QUALIFICATIONS

Knowledge of:

Operational characteristics, services, and activities of assigned environmental program area.

Pertinent federal, state and local laws, codes, and regulations including those affecting NPDES permits, the Storm Water Program, and other environmental permits and programs.

Permitting, legal, regulatory, and technical requirements of storm water quality management, including Illicit Connection and Illegal Discharge prevention and elimination, best management practices programs, and environmental monitoring and assessment.

Modern principles and practices of chemistry, biology, microbiology, or environmental protection applicable to storm water, wastewater, hazardous materials or waste, or industrial waste.

Laws and ordinances pertaining to storm water and environmental protection.

Inspection, investigation or code enforcement principles and practices.

Pollutant detection methodology related to storm water runoff or other wastes.

Proper use of monitoring, sampling, and basic testing equipment.

Principles and practices of record keeping and records management.

Methods and techniques of data collection, research, and report preparation.

Principles of supervision and training.

Terminology used in area of assignment.

Modern office procedures, methods, and equipment including computers and various software packages.

Organization and operation of municipal government.

Ability To:

Plan, organize, direct, coordinate, administer, and evaluate assigned environmental programs or projects.

Exercise sound judgment to determine environmental program and permit compliance with existing laws and regulations.

Review documents and reports for completeness and accuracy.

Perform a full range of responsible advanced professional level analytical, programmatic, and administrative duties in support of assigned programs, functions, and/or department involving the use of independent judgment and personal initiative.

Recommend and implement goals, objectives, policies, and procedures for providing assigned program services and activities.

Conduct accurate and thorough research and prepare clear, complete, accurate, and concise analysis, reports, and recommendations.

Understand, interpret, and apply general and specific administrative and departmental policies and procedures as well as applicable federal, state, and local policies, laws, and regulations.

Use computer applications to assist in performing duties, e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, database and presentation applications.

Apply procedures and techniques involved in the investigation, documentation, and enforcement of codes and regulations.

Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions, and implement recommendations in support of goals.

Apply procedures and practices for issuing notices of violation and schedules for compliance.

Analyze and evaluate technical and scientific data, reaching sound conclusions.

Analyze and evaluate situations, take appropriate action and document violations being investigated.

Respond to emergency situations involving actual or suspected illegal discharges or spills to the storm drain system or environment.

Understand the organization and operation of the assigned department, other City departments, and outside agencies as necessary to assume assigned responsibilities.

Operate and use modern office equipment including a computer and various software packages.

Work under steady pressure with frequent interruptions and a high degree of public contact by phone or in person.

Develop and maintain effective interdepartmental coordination.

Facilitate, develop, and work with teams and groups on various programs and projects and to create partnerships and coalitions.

Respond tactfully, clearly, concisely, and appropriately to inquiries from the public, City staff, or other agencies on sensitive issues in area of responsibility.

Represent the City in a professional manner when working with boards, community groups, and the general public.

Exercise independent judgment within established policy guidelines.

Demonstrate an awareness and appreciation of the cultural diversity of the community.

Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.

Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.

Minimum Requirements

Environmental Programs Specialist I/II

Education/Training:

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in environmental sciences

With us, you can. Apply today.

jobs.title: GIS Specialist
jobs.description:
Position Description

Position Overview:

The Harris County Fire Marshal's Office (HCFMO) is seeking a skilled and motivated Geographic Information System (GIS) Specialist to join the Operations Support Bureau. This role supports fire investigation, hazmat operations, emergency management, and multi-agency coordination through the development and maintenance of geospatial tools, data systems, internal GIS web applications, and analytical products.

The GIS Specialist will design, maintain, and analyze spatial datasets; produce maps, dashboards, and reports; and serve as the HCFMO's primary geospatial resource in support of operational, investigative, and strategic decision-making. The position interfaces regularly with fire, EMS, and law enforcement agency partners across Harris County, and may support Emergency Operations Center (EOC) events.

The ideal candidate is technically proficient in ESRI products, comfortable with data integration and automation, able to support configuration-level maintenance of internal mapping applications (e.g., layer setup, symbology, access/permissions settings), and capable of translating complex geospatial information into clear, actionable products for command staff, public officials, and partner agencies.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Geospatial Analysis & Decision Support
Perform spatial analysis to support fire investigation, hazmat incident response, deployment planning, prevention, and risk reduction activities.
Develop and maintain data layers and geodatabases integrating internal records (incident, investigation, inspection) with external datasets (county parcels, Census, CAD feeds, utility infrastructure).
Analyze incident patterns, coverage gaps, response time performance, and risk density to support strategic and operational planning by command staff.
Produce recommendations and briefings derived from geospatial analysis for use by the Fire Marshal, division leadership, and partner agencies.
Evaluate data and access requirements for internal geospatial applications and recommend configuration changes to layers, symbology, or user permissions to better support analytical and operational needs.

Data Management & Quality Assurance
Design, build, and maintain geodatabases from multiple internal and external data sources in various formats.
Ensure spatial data accuracy, integrity, and consistency through systematic quality control and error-checking procedures.
Maintain geospatial data feeds required by Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) systems used by the HCFMO and regional dispatch partners.
Develop and document data standards, coding structures, and metadata to support business continuity and interoperability.
Apply change-control practices (e.g., testing and validating configuration or data changes before deployment to production systems) to minimize disruption to operational users.
Support maintenance of user and facility access permissions within internal geospatial applications, ensuring data governance and access-control settings remain accurate and current.

Cartography & Application Management
Produce and maintain print and digital maps for fire investigation, hazmat operations, fire prevention, special events, and administrative use.
Create and maintain ArcGIS Online web maps, dashboards, Survey123 forms, and mobile mapping applications used by field personnel.
Provide geospatial products and field support during large-scale incidents.
Maintain and update the mobile mapping environment for fire investigators and inspectors.
Configure and maintain layer settings, symbology, and feature-service connections within HCFMO's internal geospatial application(s), coordinating with technical/IT staff as needed for deeper platform-level changes.

Reporting & Data Visualization
Design and maintain operational and strategic reports and dashboards tailored to varied audiences, from field supervisors to elected officials.
Translate complex spatial data into clear visualizations (maps, charts, heat maps, infographics) that support retention and informed decision-making.
Integrate GIS products with other software platforms to support enterprise data workflows.

Coordination & Consultation
Serve as the HCFMO's GIS representative in regional geospatial working groups and inter-agency coordination bodies.
Collaborate with HCFMO divisions (investigations, hazmat, fire prevention, operations) and partner agencies to identify GIS needs and solutions.
Provide technical consultation and training to HCFMO personnel on GIS tools, data applications, and spatial query methods.
Support integration of GIS capabilities with UAS (drone) operations for incident mapping, post-fire documentation, and aerial data collection.

Automation & Workflow Development
Develop Python scripts, Model Builder workflows, and other automation tools to streamline routine data processing and reporting.
Evaluate and recommend new geospatial technologies, extensions, and integrations to improve HCFMO workflows.
Document all procedures, scripts, and automated workflows to ensure knowledge continuity.

Harris County is an Equal Opportunity Employer

https://hrrm.harriscountytx.gov/Pages/EqualEmploymentOpportunityPlan.aspx

If you need special services or accommodations, please call (713) 274-5445 or email ADACoordinator@bmd.hctx.net .

This position is subject to a criminal history check. Only relevant convictions will be considered and, even when considered, may not automatically disqualify the candidate.

Requirements

Education and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Geographic Information Systems/Science, Geography, Computer Science, Emergency Management, or a closely related field

OR

An Associates degree plus
Three (3) years of directly relevant full-time experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree requirement

WITH

Minimum three (3) years of full-time experience in GIS analysis, data management, and cartography.
Demonstrated experience using ESRI ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and related extensions (Spatial Analyst, Network Analyst).
Experience creating and maintaining geodatabases and ensuring geospatial data quality and integrity.
Experience producing maps, dashboards, and analytical reports for operational or decision-making purposes.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

GIS concepts, analytical techniques, and digital mapping principles.
ESRI product suite: ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online/Enterprise, and extensions.
Geodatabase design, maintenance, and spatial data quality assurance methods.
Statistical and analytical methods applicable to spatial data (clustering, network analysis, proximity, density).
CAD system geospatial data requirements and integration methods.
Emergency management frameworks including ICS/NIMS; EOC operations and GISS function.
GPS concepts and field data collection procedures.
Data governance and access-control principles as applied to enterprise GIS applications.
Perform complex spatial analysis to support tactical, operational, and strategic decision-making in a public safety environment.
Produce clear, accurate, and audience-appropriate maps, reports, and visualizations under time pressure.
Manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize effectively in a dynamic, operational environment.
Explain technical geospatial concepts clearly to non-technical users, including command staff, investigators, and partner agency personnel.
Work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining alignment with organizational priorities.
Establish effective working relationships with internal divisions and external partner agencies.
Respond and deploy for large-scale incidents, EOC activations, or other deployments as directed.

NOTICE:
Applicants for this position will be subject to a criminal background check that includes being fingerprinted. This applies to any position with network access to Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) or access to an area where CJIS is received, maintained, or stored either manually or electronically (i.e. custodian, maintenance).

Automatic Disqualification:

Convictions, probation, or deferred adjudication for any Felony, and any Class A Misdemeanor.
Convictions, probation, or deferred adjudication for a Class B Misdemeanor, if within the previous 10 years.
Open arrest for any criminal offense (Felony or Misdemeanor).
Family Violence conviction.

NOTE
:
Qualifying education, experience, knowledge, and skills must be documented on your job application. You may attach a resume to the application as supporting documentation but ONLY information stated on the application will be used for consideration. "See Resume"
will not be accepted for qualifications.

Preferences

Experience in a public safety, emergency management, or law enforcement environment.
ICS GISS (GIS Specialist) credential or eligibility to obtain.
GISP certification or Esri technical certification(s).
Proficiency with Python scripting or GIS Model Builder for workflow automation.
Experience with SQL, relational databases, Microsoft SQL Server, or Power BI.
Familiarity with UAV/UAS operations and integration of aerial imagery into GIS workflows.
Experience with AutoCAD, Survey123, QuickCapture, or similar field data collection platforms.
Familiarity with reading or editing basic JavaScript/TypeScript or JSON configuration.

General Information

Position Type and Typical Hours of Work:

Regular Full-time
Hours will be discussed during departmental interview.

Salary:

Minimum: $31.54 Hourly
Depends on Qualifications
Based on 26 Pay Periods
Plus, benefits

Work Environment:

Work is primarily performed in an office environment with regular use of computers and mapping systems.
The position may require field deployment to fire scenes, hazmat incidents, or EOC activations, including evenings and weekends.
Field work may involve exposure to outdoor conditions and environments associated with fire or hazmat incidents.
The GIS Specialist may be required to lift and carry equipment up to 50 pounds and must possess manual dexterity, clear speech, and visual/hearing acuity sufficient to perform the duties of the position.

Employment may be contingent on passing a drug screen and meeting other standards.

Due to a high volume of applications positions may close prior to the advertised closing date or at the discretion of the Hiring Department.
