jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Earth Observation
jobs.description:
About The Role

Muon seeks a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead earth observation programs for U.S. Government customers. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of payload engineering and rapid-cycle space vehicle development. These programs span the full mission lifecycle — concept development and design through integration, launch, and on-orbit operations — and are executed under formal government contract structures with defined deliverables and milestones. The Senior TPM runs the program end to end: executing every contractual commitment and positioning Muon to win the work that follows.

The Senior TPM holds single-point accountability for delivering the program on schedule, within budget, and to technical performance standards. Operating with high autonomy on an accelerated contractual schedule, you will drive key milestones and lead cross-functional technical exchanges spanning systems engineering, payload, flight software, ground segment, and mission operations.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

Responsibilities

Program Execution

Serve as the single accountable owner for the program's cost, schedule, and technical baselines
Own the integrated master schedule, cost baseline, and risk register; track and report progress against contract milestones
Plan and run formal program events — internal readiness reviews, and customer-facing milestone deliverable reviews
Maintain tight cost and schedule discipline; surface deviations to the customer promptly and with a recovery plan

Customer Interface

Act as the primary programmatic interface to the Government customer, including contracting and technical representatives
Lead technical exchange meetings and convert customer input into actionable program direction
Own the delivery and quality of all contract data deliverables

Cross-Functional Leadership

Direct a cross-functional team spanning systems engineering, payload, flight software, ground processing, and mission operations
Partner with mission operations when program activities involve Muon's operational systems — without disrupting existing missions
Drive design trades and study conclusions to closure on schedule, escalating crisply when decisions stall

Security, Compliance, and Growth

Execute the program in full compliance with its government security requirements, including handling of controlled information and strict public-release restrictions
Ensure compliance with ITAR/EAR export controls and U.S.-only performance requirements
Support program growth: convert program artifacts into proposal-ready material and support capture of follow-on opportunities

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering or a technical field, or equivalent experience.
8+ years of program management experience on complex aerospace or defense development programs, including direct ownership of cost, schedule, and technical baselines
Experience executing U.S. Government contracts: statement-of-work and CDRL deliverables, milestone-based structures, and day-to-day work with government contracting and technical representatives
Experience leading engineering teams through concept development, trade studies, and preliminary design
Exceptional written communication skills — you will author and own the quality of customer-facing reports, design artifacts, and contract deliverables

Preferred Qualifications

Satellite or instrument program leadership across the full lifecycle (design, build,
integrate, test, operate)
Domain experience with remote sensing systems — EO/IR, RF, or both — at the payload or mission level
Direct experience working with USSF Space Systems Command or JPL
PMP certification or equivalent program management credentials
Ability to obtain a security clearance

Salary

The salary range for this role is $206,000 - $232,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

ITAR/EAR Requirements

This position requires access to export controlled information. To conform to U.S. Government export regulations applicable to that information, applicant must either be (A) a U.S. person, defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C.

1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C.
1158, (B) eligible to access the export controlled information without a required export authorization, or (C) eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the required export authorization from the applicable U.S. government agency. The Company may, for legitimate business reasons, decline to pursue any export licensing process.

jobs.title: Wildlife Repair/Exclusion Technician
jobs.description:
Overview

If you’re ready for more than a job, Critter Control offers a career with purpose.

Are you looking for a hands-on career, not just a job? Do you have experience in construction, roofing, insulation, or home improvement and want to put those skills to work in a stable, recession-resistant industry?

Critter Control Operations specializes in wildlife management services for residential and commercial properties, providing humane wildlife removal, exclusion, and damage repair solutions nationwide. We help customers resolve wildlife-related concerns in safe, effective, and environmentally responsible ways while protecting homes, businesses, and communities.

This role is ideal for individuals with a background in construction, repair, or related trades who are committed to craftsmanship and accountability. You’ll play a critical role in preventing future wildlife intrusions by performing exclusion work, repairs, and remediation while maintaining high safety and quality standards.

Critter Control is a brand that invests in its people. If you are a driven professional who embraces our values and upholds our standards of excellence, you’ll find opportunities to succeed, grow, and advance within our organization.

Responsibilities

As a Wildlife Exclusion/Repair Service Technician
at Critter Control, you perform hands-on exclusion, repair, and remediation services for residential and commercial properties. You identify entry points, complete structural repairs, and implement humane wildlife prevention solutions while following safety, technical, and quality guidelines.

What Does a Day in the Life Look Like?

Perform interior and exterior property inspections, including roofs, attics, crawlspaces, and other confined spaces, to identify wildlife entry points and potential vulnerabilities.
Install preventative exclusion materials such as screens, chimney caps, vent covers, and other barriers to prevent wildlife access.
Complete minor repairs to roofs, siding, foundations, and other structural areas where wildlife may gain entry.
Safely remove wildlife using humane trapping and relocation techniques in accordance with company standards and regulations.
Maintain accurate documentation of services performed, materials used, and customer interactions.
Provide clear, detailed reports and review completed scopes of work with customers.
Collaborate with sales and customer service teams to ensure seamless and positive customer experience.
Follow up with customers to confirm satisfaction and address any additional concerns or recommendations.

What type of benefits will you receive?

Competitive hourly rate: $20-$20/Hour
Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.
401k with generous match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
6 Paid Holidays Annually!
PTO accrual based on tenure - 3 weeks beginning first full year!
Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250/year (federal max!) OR free tuition on approved programs through Purdue Global!!!
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities!
Supportive team environment with a focus on work-life balance.
Opportunities for career advancement within the Rollins Family of Brands!

Qualifications

What do you need to be successful?

High school diploma or equivalent; college degree is a plus
Valid driver’s license
Proven experience in construction, carpentry, roofing, or other related fields
Ability to work in the field independently
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Proficiency in using several types of software and applications

What does the work environment look like?

We go where the wildlife goes! Candidates must be physically capable of safely performing the following job duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

Must be able to drive to various locations, often covering large territories.
Frequent walking, standing, and moving through diverse types of terrain, including uneven ground, stairs, roofs, and sometimes slippery or muddy areas.
Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions (extreme heat, extreme cold, rain, snow, etc.).
Must have the ability to climb stairs and ladders safely.
Must be able to crouch, kneel, bend, and stretch frequently.
Capability to carry and use equipment necessary for inspections and minor control measures (Traps, ladders, inspection tools, etc).
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Clear verbal communication skills to interact effectively with clients and team members.

Join us in making a positive impact on nuisance wildlife management and become a part of our dedicated team today!

Critter Control Operations is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.description:
Description

You’ll join a diverse team within our new manufacturing division for AWS supporting hardware, software, network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, plant managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards of production for our datacenters and our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As an Environmental Program Manager, you will be responsible for environmental compliance at AWS manufacturing facilities in the Central AMER region. You will assist in facility permitting and development, develop standards and policies to support regulatory compliance, complete environmental performance analysis, establish and monitor metrics, and guide the teams in implementation of Amazon environmental programs. You will provide guidance and build effective relationships with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, design, construction, operations and other key stakeholders.

This position is based in Florence, Ky

Key job responsibilities

Performing due diligence and permitting for new manufacturing faculties.
Develop new compliance programs for first of a kind operational processes.
Manage and oversee compliance with environmental regulations and Amazon policy;
Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization;
Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards;
Develop environmental metrics to measure, monitor and forecast performance;
Conduct thorough and accurate environmental audits for continuous improvement;
Prioritize and manage multiple technically complex assignments concurrently;
Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company;
Build collaborative relationships with various stakeholders to ensure risks are identified early and managed appropriately;
Assist in time-critical report submission to various governmental agencies;
Complete thorough and accurate environmental incident investigations and associated regulatory reports and develop appropriate corrective action.

About The Team

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security within our manufacturing process. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of technical infrastructure management experience
Knowledge of best practices and emerging technologies, related to infrastructure (i.e. network, data center, hardware, software)
Experience with varying scenarios of infrastructure builds
BA/BS degree in biology, environmental science, chemistry, chemical or environmental engineering, or related field of study
Broad knowledge of US environmental regulations
5+ years of environmental, regulatory and risk management experience

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with due diligence and permitting for manufacturing faculties
Experience successfully implementing environmental systems and compliance programs in a manufacturing settings

Responsible for Environmental Services at the Hawthorne Army Depot. Company Description

Help shape the future of one of New Zealand's fastest-growing cities.

At Hamilton City Council, our people are united by a shared purpose: helping make Hamilton the best place to live, work, and play. As one of New Zealand's largest city councils, we're proud to serve a growing and vibrant community while delivering services and projects that improve the wellbeing of Hamiltonians every day.

You'll join a team that values collaboration, innovation, and community impact. Together, we're on track to being one of New Zealand's leading community-focused councils, where everyone matters and every contribution helps shape the future of our city.
Hamilton is growing rapidly, and we're looking for a talented GIS Analyst to join our Strategy, Growth and Planning Group. If you're passionate about geospatial data, thrive on solving complex problems, and want your work to influence planning and growth decisions that impact our city, we'd love to hear from you.
If you're looking for meaningful work, a supportive team, and the opportunity to make a real difference in your community, you'll find it here.

Job Description

He angituutanga: The opportunity 

Reporting to the Team Lead Urban & Spatial Planning, you'll work closely with planners, analysts, and stakeholders across Council to deliver high-quality GIS services and insights that support Hamilton's growth and development.
You'll be responsible for managing and analysing planning-related spatial data, maintaining critical District Plan datasets, and delivering innovative geospatial solutions that inform planning and policy decisions. You'll also help develop reports, data models, and GIS workflows that support business needs and improve decision-making

What you'll be doing

Undertake spatial analysis and modelling to support planning and growth decisions.
Develop, maintain, and enhance planning spatial databases and datasets.
Manage District Plan spatial data and ensure information remains accurate and up to date.
Create maps, reports, and visualisations that communicate complex information clearly.
Design and implement GIS dataflows and innovative spatial solutions.
Support the development and maintenance of Council's online zoning platform.
Work closely with internal stakeholders to understand business requirements and deliver tailored GIS solutions.
Collaborate with Information Services, GIS Services, and Commercial & Analytics teams to achieve organisational outcomes.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, systems, and workflows through technology and innovation.

Why join us?

At Hamilton City Council, you'll have the opportunity to work on projects that directly influence the future growth and development of our city. You'll be part of a supportive and collaborative team that values innovation, continuous improvement, and making a real difference for our communities.
If you're ready to use your GIS expertise to help shape Hamilton's future, we'd love to hear from you.

Qualifications

We're looking for someone with a strong GIS foundation who enjoys working in a dynamic environment and turning spatial data into actionable insights.

A relevant tertiary qualification, such as Geography, GIS, Geospatial Science, Urban or Environmental Planning or a related discipline.
At least 4 years’ experience using the Esri suite, including ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online.
Strong spatial analysis, data management and map production skills.
Experience gathering requirements, solving business problems and communicating findings to a range of audiences.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
A collaborative, innovative and customer-focused approach.

It would be an advantage if you also have experience with:
InDesign, Photoshop or similar
AutoCAD, Sketch-up or similar
Project-based delivery environments
Local government
Applying local government policies, regulations and legislation

Circa $107,715 dependent on skills and experience.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Planner – MTO / Provincial Transportation
jobs.description:
In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. Imagine Next!

At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description

Parsons has been a leader in the planning, design and delivery of transportation infrastructure for more than 75 years. We are seeking an experienced Environmental Planner with strong Ontario Ministry of Transportation (MTO) experience to join our Infrastructure team in the Greater Toronto Region.

The successful candidate may be based in our Toronto, Markham, Oakville or London office, with flexibility for hybrid work. You will help deliver provincial highway projects while strengthening Parsons’ environmental planning capabilities and relationships with MTO and other transportation clients.

Position Overview

The Senior Environmental Planner will lead the environmental planning and assessment components of MTO highway assignments through planning and preliminary design and support the implementation of environmental commitments during detail design and construction.

The position will coordinate multidisciplinary environmental studies, consultation, environmental documentation, permits and approvals, and the integration of environmental requirements into project design and contract documentation.

The successful candidate will also contribute to proposals, client development, technical quality, and the mentoring of junior and intermediate planners.

Responsibilities

Lead environmental planning and assessment for MTO highway projects in accordance with the current Class Environmental Assessment for Provincial Transportation Facilities and Municipal Expressways (2024).
Serve as Environmental Lead on planning, preliminary design and detail design assignments, coordinating environmental specialists, engineers, subconsultants and project managers.
Establish environmental work plans, study requirements, schedules, budgets and deliverables appropriate to the applicable Class EA requirements, project classification and potential environmental effects.
Apply the MTO Environmental Reference for Highway Design (ERD) and applicable MTO environmental guides, policies, directives, standards, forms and technical guidance.
Prepare and review Transportation Environmental Study Reports, environmental assessment documentation, consultation records, environmental commitment records and design-phase environmental reports.
Lead the identification and evaluation of environmental effects, avoidance opportunities, mitigation measures, monitoring requirements and environmental commitments.
Coordinate public, stakeholder, agency and municipal consultation, including notices, Public Information Centres, presentations, comment-response tracking and issue resolution.
Support MTO-led consultation with Indigenous communities and organizations, including consultation planning, documentation, comment tracking and the consideration of potential impacts on Aboriginal or treaty rights.
Support issue resolution under the Class EA and assist MTO in responding to Section 16 Order requests, where applicable.
Develop and coordinate environmental permitting and approvals strategies with technical specialists, project teams and regulatory agencies.
Ensure environmental commitments and approval requirements are carried forward into detail design, drawings, specifications, contract documents and construction requirements.
Provide technical review and quality assurance for environmental planning deliverables.
Build and maintain productive working relationships with MTO, municipal clients, regulatory agencies and project partners.
Lead or support proposal preparation, including methodologies, work plans, schedules, staffing plans, budgets and level-of-effort estimates.
Mentor junior and intermediate environmental planners and support consistent environmental planning practices across the team.
Monitor changes to environmental legislation, MTO processes, policies and industry practices that may affect project delivery.

Requirements

University degree in environmental planning, urban or regional planning, environmental studies, geography, environmental science or a related discipline. A relevant graduate degree is an asset.
Minimum of 10 years of environmental planning or environmental assessment experience, including substantial recent experience delivering MTO highway assignments in a consulting environment.
Demonstrated experience acting as an Environmental Lead or senior environmental planner on MTO planning, preliminary design or detail design projects.
Strong working knowledge of the Class Environmental Assessment for Provincial Transportation Facilities and Municipal Expressways (2024), including project classification, consultation, evaluation, documentation, issues resolution and transition requirements.
Familiarity with the previous MTO Class EA process and the transition of projects from the 2000 Class EA to the 2024 Class EA is an asset.
Knowledge and practical application of the MTO ERD and associated environmental guides, policies, standards, procedures and technical requirements.
Experience preparing or reviewing MTO Transportation Environmental Study Reports, consultation materials, environmental commitments and multidisciplinary environmental reports.
Experience coordinating environmental specialists covering areas such as natural heritage, fisheries, archaeology, cultural heritage, noise, contaminated property, excess soil, groundwater, drainage and stormwater management.
Experience supporting public, agency, stakeholder and Indigenous consultation for provincial transportation projects.
Strong understanding of applicable provincial and federal environmental legislation and associated permitting and approval requirements.
Demonstrated project-management experience, including managing scope, schedule, budget, risk, subconsultants and multidisciplinary teams.
Strong technical writing, presentation, consultation and issue-resolution skills.
Demonstrated ability to build client relationships and contribute to proposals and business development.
Membership or eligibility for membership with the Ontario Professional Planners Institute or Canadian Institute of Planners is an asset. An RPP or MCIP designation is also considered an asset.
Experience with the Transit and Rail Project Assessment Process under O. Reg. 231/08, federal impact assessment processes, and municipal environmental assessment processes—including the transition from the Municipal Class EA to the Municipal Project Assessment Process—is considered an asset.
Valid Ontario Class G driver’s licence and ability to travel to project sites and client meetings when required.

This position is part of our Critical Infrastructure team.

For more than 80 years, our experts have designed and delivered the critical infrastructure that connects and protects communities around the world. We work in collaborative teams, both within the company and with our partners and customers, to plan, design, build, and modernize infrastructure. We take special pride in projects and solutions that improve communities as well as people’s quality of life by promoting economic growth, enhancing mobility, and increasing sustainability and resiliency. Powered by our people, we provide the imagination necessary to support our customers’ visions—and to help them see what's next!

Salary Range: $85,000 - $135,000

This job posting is for a current addition or replacement opportunity within Parsons.

We value our employees and want our employees to take care of their overall wellbeing, which is why we offer best-in-class benefits such as health, vision, dental, employer paid provincial care premiums, Defined Contribution Pension Plan (DCPP), Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA), Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP), life insurance, paid time off, sick leave, all province observed holidays off, and gym membership discounts to fit your busy lifestyle!

Parsons is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility in the workplace. Parsons equally employs representation at all job levels for indigenous peoples, women, individuals with disabilities, and visible minorities.

We truly invest and care about our employee’s wellbeing and provide endless growth opportunities as the sky is the limit, so aim for the stars! Imagine next and join the Parsons quest—APPLY TODAY!

Overview

ACS Professional Staffing is looking for an employee to work on-site with our client. This Energy Conservation Business Analyst 3 will provide business analyst support for energy conservation engineering initiatives and emerging technologies within Energy Conservation. Under the guidance of the manager or team lead, this role will analyze and interpret varying facts and circumstances, make deductions, and document how new initiatives, products, and emerging technologies can be developed into Energy Conservation Measures or programs. The position will provide recommendations to managers, executives, and stakeholders, as appropriate. The role will support the group manager and Engineering Technical Leads in the development and implementation of energy conservation engineering initiatives and the Energy Conservation Emerging Technology Program, including recommending and developing business practices, conducting technology assessments and analyses, preparing reports, and providing primary analytical and program support to federal staff. This full-time position is located in Portland, OR.

Responsibilities

Provide technical/analytical advice and recommendations to the program manager regarding resource needs to support the goals and objectives of a variety of energy conservation projects and initiatives.
Provide development recommendations, guidance expertise, organization and coordination of a high profile, multi-million-dollar emerging technology portfolio and its individual projects as well as monitor the progress of portfolio efforts against defined metrics.
Under direction of the emerging technology program manager and in collaboration with federal staff , facilitate and provide technical expertise to a collaborative of key stakeholders both regionally and nationally including, the U.S. Department of Energy (USDOE), Pacific Northwest National Labs (PNNL), Washington State University Energy Extension Office (WSU), select electric utilities, industrial associations, and manufacturers to investigate and recommend adoption of innovative emerging energy conservation technologies.
Assist the program manager in analyzing options to address any resource allocation issues.
Provide support to the PEJ Manager, Technical Leads, and Emerging Technology Program Manager for managing, tracking, budgeting, and reporting the progress of energy conservation initiatives and energy conservation emerging technology program.
Maintain the project tracking system to track and monitor organizational initiatives and projects, as requested by manager and emerging technology program manager. Provide support to energy conservation engineering staff to update the system as necessary.
Provide hands-on assistance to Energy Conservation project managers, including support with change management, internal/external communications, issue/risk management, and status tracking

Developing project team(s) as needed, requesting and resolving resource issues with the assistance of the Program Manager.
Facilitating and coordinating project team(s) to develop/draft project plans and schedules for management review, consideration and approval.
Developing and maintaining effective internal communications between project team members, stakeholders, manager and others.
Coordinating, scheduling, and monitoring project activities.
Providing regular status reports as requested.
Perform, conduct and provide Emerging Technology Portfolio analysis, including:
Monitor and document product development and emerging technology research.
Perform research, analysis and gap-analysis on numerous technologies for potential inclusion in Energy Conservation programs; present findings and provide recommendations to management, executives and/or stakeholders for review and consideration.
Document other emerging technology work and identify research gaps that are preventing emerging technologies from becoming Energy Conservation measures; present findings and provide recommendations to management, executives and/or stakeholders for review and consideration.
Consult and collaborate with Energy Conservation and Technology Innovation department personnel on the development of management-approved emerging technologies into new Energy Conservation measures.

May be requested to draft presentations and/or conduct presentations for management, executives and/or stakeholders.
Perform research of existing Energy Conservation measures and assist the Engineering group, as requested by manager, lead or program manager.
Develop and recommend a strategic and effective process for getting new technologies into EE Programs to management, executives and/or stakeholders for review and consideration, as appropriate.
Provide reports, conduct presentations and make recommendations based on the research findings to appropriate managers, project managers and stakeholders as requested.
Coordinate with the energy conservation marketing group to assist with updating and maintaining the emerging technology program web content in accordance with organizational standards.
Coordinate with energy conservation marketing group to draft, prepare and present information on program activities and accomplishments. Draft materials must be reviewed and approved by manager, team lead or other authorized federal staff.

Use a variety of software tools to track, coordinate and communicate program activities, including but not limited to SharePoint and Microsoft Suite programs.

Requirements

Possess a solid background in overall energy conservation with emphasis on emerging technologies in various facets including program framework development, modification, program manual creation, industry best practices, data analysis, and report writing.
An Associate or Bachelor’s Degree in Energy Conservation, Business Administration and/or Management, Environmental Science, Energy Management or a related field is strongly preferred.

With an applicable associate degree, 10 years of experience is required.

Experience with Microsoft Office Suite Software (MS Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Teams).
Experience with project management and project tracking software.
Experience in change management as it applies to implementing new programs and initiatives.
Demonstrate proficiency in program/project analyses, presentations, correspondence, and proposals.

MAKE A DIFFERENCE IN OREGON’S NATURAL RESOURCES!

Opportunity Awaits, Apply Today!

Required

As a District Wildlife Technician (Fish and Wildlife Technician) in Roseburg, Oregon, you will assist district wildlife biologist and assistants in performing all wildlife management functions and related activities required to carry out the Department's programs in the Douglas County, Umpqua Watershed District. Duties include:

Perform farming and forage enhancement operations on public and private lands.
Help landowners resolve wildlife conflict.
Assist with wildlife population monitoring from both air and ground.
Trap ungulates, carnivores, upland and migratory game birds and other wildlife as needed using a variety of methods including immobilization drugs, drive/walk-in/ corral traps, rocket nets, drop nets and net guns.
Apply agricultural husbandry knowledge, including tillage, fertilization, and planting of grasses and legumes.
Build, repair, and maintain fencing.
Operate, maintain, and repair farm and construction equipment including trucks, tractors, backhoes, loaders, graders, dozers, plows, trailers, augers, disks, harrows, spreaders, seeders, pumps, motors, winches, generators, four‑wheelers, and shop tools.

Fabricate and install nesting devices for birds.

This position requires obtaining an All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) Safety Education Card through the Oregon State Parks and Recreation Department within six months of appointment.

Fish and Wildlife Technician ($3798 - $5193)

Option 1: An Associate's degree in Wildlife Technology or Agriculture;

OR-

Option 2: Eighteen months of experience in the care of livestock, agricultural research and experimentation, monitoring game or wildlife, or farming. (Six months of fisheries or related habitat work experience will count toward this experience).

Equivalency Notes

A higher level degree in Wildlife Science, Agriculture, or a closely-related degree with at least 45 quarter (30 semester) hours of biological/ecological coursework will substitute for the Associate’s degree.

Fish and Wildlife Technician Entry Option ($3515 - $4312):

jobs.title: Director of Planning & Environmental
jobs.description:
The future of ONT starts now.
Through the ONT BOLD (Building Our Legacy & Destiny) Program, you can be a part of one of Southern California’s most ambitious airport development programs. ONT BOLD is transforming Ontario International Airport with a new terminal, modernized facilities, and infrastructure improvements designed to support future growth—and we’re looking for visionary leaders to help make it happen.

COMPENSATION

$135,000 - $195,000 annual salary + a generous benefits package to include medical, dental, vision and 10% employer paid 401A through VOYA Financial.
*Hiring Salary Range: $135,000 - $165,000 annual salary
(starting salary will be within this range based upon qualifications)

SUMMARY

The Airport Director of Planning and Environmental is responsible for leading the strategic planning, environmental planning, environmental compliance, sustainability, and airport development functions within the Capital Development Division. This position provides direction, oversight, and management of the Airport Planning and Environmental Department and serves as the Authority's subject matter expert on aviation planning, environmental regulations, and long-range airport development. Reporting to the Vice President of Capital Development, the Director oversees the planning and implementation of the Airport Capital Improvement Program (CIP), airport planning initiatives including ONT
BOLD
(Building our Legacy and Destiny), environmental review processes, and regulatory compliance activities while ensuring alignment with the Ontario International Airport Authority's (OIAA) Strategic Plan, Board priorities, and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Important and essential duties may include, but are not limited to the following:
Direct, manage, and oversee all airport planning, development, environmental planning, environmental compliance, and sustainability programs.
Lead the development, implementation, and periodic update of the Airport Capital Improvement Program (CIP), Airport Layout Plan (ALP), and other short- and long-range planning documents.
Direct, manage and coordinate the preparation of complex planning and environmental studies for the development and improvement of airport properties and facilities.
Oversee environmental planning and other system planning projects to ensure compliance with applicable Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) design standards, operating requirements, federal, state and local policies and regulations.
Establish planning priorities that support airport growth, operational efficiency, customer experience, and long-term infrastructure investment, and align with OIAA's Strategic Plan, ONT BOLD initiatives, Board directives, and aviation industry best practices.
Evaluate proposed airport development projects to ensure consistency with approved planning documents, operational requirements, and future development objectives.
Ensure airport development projects comply with FAA design standards, Advisory Circulars, engineering criteria, airport design requirements, and approved planning documents.
Oversee planning analyses related to airfield development, terminal expansion, landside improvements, utilities, transportation systems, and airport support facilities.
Plan and prioritize capital projects; develops and manages project budgets, implementation schedules, and stakeholder coordination during implementation.
Direct the preparation of federal, state, and local grant applications for funding; develops and oversees implementation of FAA infrastructure grants.
Direct and manage revisions to, as required, the Airport Layout Plan (ALP) to reflect as-constructed conditions and changes to future development plans.
Provide oversight of environmental permitting, mitigation monitoring, sustainability initiatives, and environmental compliance programs.
Lead environmental planning efforts that support responsible airport growth while balancing operational, community, and environmental considerations.
Review and monitor airport development projects for compliance with FAA requirements and environmental regulations, including but not limited to, the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA) and all other local, state and federal regulations.
Work across Departments and Divisions to facilitate various planning and environmental activities to ensure efficient coordination of projects including scope, schedule, budget, and resources to ensure the ongoing development of the airport will meet the priorities set by leadership and the OIAA Board.
Direct the preparation of Professional Services Agreements, technical specifications and plans for various studies and technical services; recommends and approves contract awards; and organizes, coordinates and supervises the work of consultants.
Represent and serve as the OIAA representative on local, regional and/or national organizations regarding planning and environmental technical issues.
Lead and direct the activities of assigned staff; reviews work plans; meets with staff to identify and resolve problems; assigns work activities and projects; monitors workflow; evaluates employee performance and work products.
Communicate airport planning and environmental objectives, goals and progress to OIAA senior management and stakeholders.
Meet with officials of public and private agencies, community groups, and individuals to explain aviation development related issues; effectively communicates with internal and external stakeholders on technical subject matter expertise.
Direct, plan, manage and coordinate the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities; establishes, within OIAA policy, appropriate service and staffing levels; allocates resources accordingly.
Does related work as required.
May occasionally be assigned to other duties for training purposes, technological changes or deficiencies or for emergency response.
Required to visit project sites at terminal, airside or landside locations. Attendance at off-site meetings for presentations, networking and other industry events also required.

PROFILE OF THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

Extensive experience leading airport planning and environmental programs at a commercial service airport or similarly complex aviation organization.
Comprehensive knowledge of airport planning principles, airport master planning, capital improvement programming, transportation planning, and aviation infrastructure development.
Thorough understanding of FAA regulations, Advisory Circulars, Orders, Airport Improvement Program (AIP) requirements, and airport planning guidance.
Extensive knowledge of environmental planning and regulatory compliance, including NEPA, CEQA, permitting requirements, environmental documentation, and sustainability initiatives.
Knowledge of federal, state, and local grant administration, funding programs, and reimbursement requirements.
Experience developing long-range strategic plans and implementing complex capital development programs.
Strong project and program management skills with the ability to manage multiple high-profile initiatives simultaneously.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing consultants, technical professionals, and cross-functional project teams.
Demonstrated success developing departmental budgets, strategic priorities, performance objectives, and organizational policies.
Strong political acumen and the ability to effectively navigate complex governmental, regulatory, and stakeholder environments.
Excellent leadership, coaching, mentoring, and employee development skills.
Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and negotiation skills.
Strong analytical, organizational, and decision-making abilities with sound professional judgment.
Ability to effectively communicate complex technical information to executive leadership, elected officials, regulatory agencies, community organizations, and the public.
Ability to establish and maintain productive working relationships with employees, tenants, airlines, consultants, contractors, governmental agencies, and community stakeholders.
Knowledge of current and emerging technologies affecting airport planning, infrastructure development, environmental compliance, and asset management.
Familiarity with airport operations, airline requirements, aviation industry trends, and the communities served by Ontario International Airport.
Ability to consistently model and demonstrate the Ontario International Airport Authority's Core Values through ethical leadership, accountability, innovation, collaboration, and exceptional public service.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any combination of education, training, and experience that would likely provide the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform in the position.
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Airport Planning, Engineering, Architecture, Urban Planning, Environmental or a related field is required. A Master's degree in a related field is highly desirable.
Eight (8) years of progressively responsible and recent professional experience or consultant work, in aviation planning projects and programs, preferably at a FAA Part 139 Certified Airport, including a minimum of three (3) years in a lead or supervisory capacity.
Experience at a commercial airport and working with an appointed board or elected officials is highly desirable.
Familiarity with and work experience in the Southern California region is a plus.
Experience with CEQA preferred.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and database programs.

LICENSES / CERTIFICATION

Valid Driver's License equivalent to a California Class C Driver's License
Acceptable driving record at time of appointment and throughout employment
Ability to pass all background / reference checks, knowledge examinations, as well as aptitude tests necessary to obtain an OIAA employee badge at ONT

jobs.description:
Description

GSI is seeking an Environmental Data Analyst who combines technical ability, analytical creativity, and business acumen to strengthen our data management, analysis, and visualization team. The ideal candidate is comfortable across the full data lifecycle—building and maintaining relational databases, developing analysis and automation pipelines in SQL, Python, and/or R, and providing query, reporting, and visualization support in a collaborative organization working closely with technical staff. Familiarity with environmental chemistry data generated from field investigations of water, soil, sediment, air, and biological matrices is valued. The candidate should know how to analyze system requirements and be familiar with relational databases, statistical analysis, and modern data visualization techniques using relevant and current tools.

GSI provides high-quality technical and regulatory expertise to industry and government to address a broad range of environmental issues. We specialize in solving complex environmental problems by leveraging our extensive knowledge of environmental regulations, stressing accurate data collection and analysis, and applying new technologies to our clients' most difficult challenges.

Responsibilities

Support environmental investigation projects by maintaining relational databases of environmental chemistry data from historical reports, laboratory test results, web sources, and third-party databases.
Build and maintain ETL (extract, transform, load) and analysis workflows in SQL, Python, and/or R to clean, transform, validate, and analyze environmental datasets.
Work with multi-disciplinary teams of engineers and scientists to support statistical and spatial analyses.
Build dashboards and visualizations, and format tables, charts, and graphs to style guidelines for technical reports and presentations.
Organize data in structures that support automation and downstream analysis.
Perform quality assurance on analytical databases to ensure data integrity, and identify and correct data gaps, errors, and relational table issues.
Support a wide variety of projects ranging from litigation support and site investigation to data mining for research and development.
Effectively communicate findings to internal and external clients.
Complete assigned tasks on schedule and within budget while meeting quality standards on deliverables.

Qualifications

BS/BA or higher degree in data science, computer science, statistics, environmental science, or a related field.
2-5 years of work experience in data management or analysis, with strong relational database skills using PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft Access, or other database management systems.
Comfortable writing advanced SQL for data management (beyond basic create, read, update, delete), to clean, transform, and structure data in relational databases.
Familiarity with relational database design, data modeling, and normalization.
Awareness of data compilation, migration, and backup/retention considerations.
Shell scripting (Bash) and comfort working in Linux and command-line environments.
Experience using Python and/or R (Tidyverse, Shiny) for data analysis, visualization, dashboards, and web applications, including hands-on project work.
Self-motivated and eager to learn, with a drive to adopt new data and analysis techniques, AI, and emerging technologies to improve workflows.
Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines with limited supervision.
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

Additional preferred skillsets and qualifications include:
Familiarity with chemistry data, laboratory information management systems (LIMS), data validation, and extraction of data from online sources.
Version control (Git) and reproducible, scripted analysis workflows.
Application development and deployment, including web frameworks for data tools (e.g., Django, Flask/FastAPI, Dash, Streamlit, R Shiny). Familiarity with containerization (Docker) is a plus.
Experience with embedded and analytical database engines (e.g., SQLite, DuckDB) for local analysis, prototyping, and data interchange.

Job Perks

Competitive salary and benefits
Quarterly and year-end bonuses
Flexible work environment with potential for remote work
On-the-job training, mentorship, and professional development
Participation in conferences, technical presentations, and papers
Collaborative atmosphere
Base salary will vary depending on qualifications and experience.

This range represents GSI's good-faith estimate of the base salary for the position and is provided in accordance with applicable pay transparency laws. Starting salary will be determined based on several job-related factors, including relevant experience, education, professional licensure, certifications, technical expertise, geographic location, internal equity, and overall qualifications.

jobs.description:
Entarian is seeking a Pacific Northwest Habitat Restoration Specialist
to provide technical, programmatic, data management, environmental compliance, outreach, and restoration planning support for the NOAA Office of Habitat Conservation, Restoration Center. This position will support habitat restoration projects and related NOAA programs and initiatives in the Pacific Northwest, with a near-term emphasis on the Community Based Restoration Program (CRP) and additional support to Damage Assessment, Remediation, and Restoration Program (DARRP) cases. The position requires periodic on-site meetings in Portland, OR, and regional site visits and meetings with partners throughout Oregon, Washington, and Idaho, with regular off-site work acceptable. The contractor may be required to travel for meetings, workshops, trainings, and conferences.

Duties Include

Support fishery habitat restoration planning and implementation, including the evaluation, identification, prioritization, design, implementation, and monitoring of restoration projects, with particular emphasis on salmon and steelhead habitat and other biological resources in the Pacific Northwest.

Provide technical and programmatic support for CRP and DARRP restoration projects, including coordination with NOAA staff, local partners, state and federal trustees, responsible parties, technical professionals, and other stakeholders to support project development, implementation planning, monitoring, adaptive management, and reporting.
Support project solicitation, review, and tracking activities, including distribution of requests for proposals, review and scoring of proposals, participation in technical review discussions, development of monitoring plans, participation in implementation planning, review of progress reports, and tracking of project accomplishments.
Provide technical management and oversight of trustee or responsible-party restoration projects, including coordination of draft restoration plans, assessment reports, environmental compliance documents, monitoring and evaluation plans, permit requests, project budgets, adaptive management plans, and restoration scaling activities.
Support Natural Resources Damage Assessment (NRDA) planning and stewardship activities, including gathering information from state and federal trustees, supporting case strategy and decisions through literature and expert-opinion research, preparing topic papers, supporting use of settlement funds, and applying an integrated watershed-based approach to restoration portfolios.
Provide programmatic management support by coordinating and inspecting field activities and contract deliverables; supporting subcontractor oversight; identifying potential contract deviations; and providing technical input to the NOAA Project Lead and COR without exercising technical direction or final contract acceptance authority.
Develop and support environmental compliance documentation and permitting, including NEPA documentation using established NOAA and CEQ methods and guidance; Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act; and documentation needed to support compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Endangered Species Act and Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act.
Develop outreach and communication products, including draft press releases, project fact sheets, briefing packets, maps, story maps, and other materials; and support public meetings, events, and other outreach activities as needed.
Perform data management and reporting activities, including compiling and inputting project data into the Restoration and Conservation Database (RCDB), DARRTS, and other reporting databases; coordinating information requests; and working with the IT team on potential process improvements.

This person will work with BC Hydro staff, consultants, community stakeholders, regulatory agencies and First Nations to provide decision advice for project and operational activities related to capital development projects and Water Use planning initiatives. The team provides advice to support operational and project decisions to mitigate/minimize impacts that may have regulatory, First Nations, operations, and/or social implications. The successful candidate will:
• Be a primary subject matter expert (SME) for fish and aquatic issues, with a critical recognition of environmental risks, business requirements, and opportunities.

• Lead and facilitate external committees that include multiple stakeholders representing a variety of interests with the objective of advancing and implementing program activities.

Job Description

Under supervision of a Wildlife Biologist or Senior Biologist, the Wildlife Technician may assist in conducting surveys, investigations, and developments to enhance wildlife. Technicians perform a variety of duties depending on the specific program or area they are assigned to. Below is a short summary of each type of Technician position.

POSITION: Wildlife Technician

LOCATION: Eufaula WMA

Wildlife Management Area (WMA)Technician - Maintain buildings, grounds, signage and equipment and/or implement assigned programs. Provide current regulations, WMA specific information and assistance to users on assigned areas. Periodically inspect and coordinate work of contractors on assigned areas. May assist in the management of more than one wildlife area or program with multi-management objectives. Develop and maintain fireguards using area equipment, including removing hazardous fuels, such as snags and eastern redcedar, before, during and after the burn. Assist in prescribed burning on WMAs. Mix and apply chemical herbicides using appropriate label rates and application methods. Utilize MSDS and necessary safety supplies for proper application and record keeping. Assist with surveys and data collection at the WMA and regional level. Required to haul loads of various sizes on short and long-distance trips utilizing various types of trailers, often over challenging terrain; may be required to obtain a CDL. Maintain and repair roads, construct and maintains fences in assigned areas. Must be able to operate and maintain equipment, including tractor with front end loader & various implements, skid steer, and other heavy equipment as assigned. Assist in the maintenance and operation of active grazing leases on multiple WMA’s including fencing, water structures, stocking rates and keeping good communication with grazing lessees.

Oklahoma Land Access Program (OLAP) Technician
– Set up, periodically inspect, and maintain OLAP Walk-in Areas, equipment, and signage. Assist OLAP Biologist with maintaining and expanding the OLAP. Monitor and document habitat of prospective and enrolled areas. Assist with implementation of lease agreements with private landowners. Utilize legal land descriptions, GIS mapping hardware/software, and contract stipulations.

Big Game Technician
- Conduct animal surveys on foot, UTV, watercraft or aircraft, and gather, analyze, and report biological data. Assist/lead wildlife necropsies of cervids with unknown mortality causes, maintaining sample integrity and personnel safety. Coordinate with inter-division staff and volunteers on various programs and activities. Proficient in big game identification, biology and management, and will assist with Damage Control Assistance Program, Deer Management Assistance Program, Herd Health Evaluation (will require the collection of cervids via firearms), and other ODWC programs.

Waterfowl / Migratory Bird Technician
- Assume lead responsibility for nuisance goose program coordinator. Assists with conducting the annual aerial mid-winter survey. Assist/lead necropsies of migratory birds with unknown mortality causes, maintaining sample integrity and personnel safety. Gather, analyze, and report biological data through bird banding activities and other research. Coordinate and conduct ODWC sponsored youth waterfowl hunts. Proficiency in migratory bird identification, biology, diseases, and management techniques.

Wetland Technician
- Act independently or with others to assess, design, bid, and install/repair wetland management infrastructure, remain current on infrastructure innovations and suppliers, and provide onsite direction and approval of contracted or Departmental work. Coordinate and oversee wetland projects statewide, working with biologists, technicians, and contractors. Assist in prioritizing program budgeting needs and monitoring contracts. Haul, operate, and coordinate the use of various heavy equipment on WMA’s as needed, statewide. Proficiency in wetlands management techniques.

Job Duties May Include

Post informational, boundary and highway signs.

Assist in completion of wildlife and hunter surveys.

Supplies information to area users and the general public.

Maintain buildings, grounds and equipment performing tasks such as carpentry, masonry, painting, litter removal, welding, mowing and general equipment repair and maintenance.

Develop and prepare food plots and perform other necessary farming operations.

Assist in monitoring the performance of contract work and agreements.

Supervising a small group of hourly employees by assigning daily duties and checking to maintain flow of work.

Required to make purchases needed according to state purchasing guidelines and agency policy.

Maintain complete and accurate daily records, inventory, and prepare required reports.

Assist with agency education and outreach programs.

May be required to perform other periodic duties as assigned by Supervisor.

Must have the ability to

Operate boats, motor vehicles, lawn mowers, UTVs/ATVs and skid loaders/tractors with various attachments.
Operate and use firearms, cutting torch, and welding equipment.
Lift and carry a minimum of 50 pounds for a distance of 100 yards.
Push / pull a minimum of 50 pounds to hook up trailers, load boats, and various other equipment.
Walk and jog over rough terrain for extended periods of time.
Must be able to swim.
Work alone in remote areas.
Endure various extremes of outdoor weather conditions.
Work extended hours, weekends, and stay overnight out of town.
Handle wild animals in live and dead condition, including field dressing wild game.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships, work independently, and be professional and courteous with the public and other agencies.
Communicate clearly and effectively in public speaking situations and be able to express oneself clearly and concisely in writing.
Operate and use small and handheld equipment and supplies.
Use personal computer and various office equipment.
Operate and use field traps, survey gear, and lab equipment.
Conduct day / night audio and visual surveys.

Requirements

EDUCATION:
Associate degree or a minimum of two years college to include course work in Wildlife Management or closely related field. Four years’ experience in a Wildlife Conservation Technician position may substitute for education requirements.

Please attach an official copy of your transcript to the application. Applications without an attached transcript will not be considered.**

EXPERIENCE
: One year’s related experience. A total of five years’ experience is required in lieu of education requirement. A completed bachelor’s degree in Natural Resource Management with an emphasis in Wildlife Management or related field may substitute for the experience requirement.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:
Thorough knowledge of capabilities and use of medium to heavy contractual and farming equipment. Have knowledge and competence in use of small hand tools and carpentry tools. Knowledge of techniques used in wildlife surveys and inventories and all aspects of agriculture practices. Skill in exercising good judgment in analyzing situations and making decisions and in establishing effective working relationships with other employees and with the general public. Be proficient in use of computers and various software applications.

GSI is highly respected nationally and internationally for the quality of its professional environmental services and the technically advanced projects it has completed over its 39 years of operation.

Role

GSI employs cross-disciplinary teams of environmental engineers and scientists, including toxicologists, geologists, hydrogeologists, ecologists, chemists, oceanographers, and data scientists with seamless collaboration over both technical disciplines and offices. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, GSI operates offices in Texas (Austin and Houston), California (Irvine, the San Francisco Bay Area, and Folsom), Colorado (Lakewood), Washington (Olympia), Montana (Missoula and Helena), North Carolina (Raleigh), and New York (Syracuse). Our talented staff of environmental professionals perform projects nationwide and internationally. Key opportunities of the Principal role will include:

Join a Thriving Firm: Be part of a privately-owned company renowned for its technical excellence and strong industry reputation. We are committed to measured, purposeful growth that maintains the integrity of our unique culture.
Be a Leader and Owner: Take on a significant role in managing a mid-sized company with over 250 employees. Enjoy meaningful ownership and profit-sharing opportunities that recognize and reward your contributions.
Advance the Science: Lead and innovate in the fields of toxicology, health sciences, and risk assessment. Your expertise will drive advancements and make a tangible impact on our projects and the industry.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be responsible for leading a practice area that is complementary to GSIs existing technical service offerings. Preferred environmental disciplines include (but are not limited to) engineering, hydrogeology, toxicology, water resources, groundwater modeling, air quality, risk assessment, and compliance. The candidate will be responsible for the professional, technical, and administrative activities of the company. Develop long-range plans; provide effective leadership; and develop and recommend corporate objectives, goals, and budgets. Negotiate critical and controversial issues with officers of other organizations and companies. Take responsibility for a large segment of the company in area of specialization. Directly supervises technical staff and plays major role in maintaining staff utilization.

We support this role through our Houston and Austin, Texas offices and are open to engaging highly qualified candidates based in these markets, as well as in Dallas and San Antonio, Texas.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will have a strong track record of leadership and business development with the following qualifications:

Advanced degree in geosciences, engineering, toxicology, or related field.
15-20 years of work experience with heavy emphasis on environmental consulting for the private sector.
Professional licensure, such as Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geoscientist (PG), Diplomate American Board of Toxicology (DABT) certification.
Direct experience with groundwater/soil/air contamination, contaminant fate and transport, and site investigation/remediation.
Litigation experience as a consulting and/or testifying expert.
Experience serving as a primary point of contact with clients and managing project teams and budgets.
Experience developing sampling plans for remedial investigations, constructing conceptual models, conducting data analysis and visualization, and preparing technical reports.
Ability to perform independent research and analysis.
Ability to work across geographies with experts in different offices.
Strong mentoring, professional development of staff, and recruiting skills.
