jobs.title: Saltmarsh Ecology Researcher
jobs.description:
Your job

As a Saltmarsh Ecology Researcher, you will contribute to the saltmarsh research programme at Wageningen Marine Research (WMR). Working closely with the saltmarsh team, you will carry out field measurements and analyses to investigate long-term vegetation dynamics and sediment accretion, the impacts of land subsidence caused by gas extraction, and carbon sequestration in saltmarsh ecosystems. You will translate this knowledge into reports and provide advice on saltmarsh restoration plans and management strategies. In doing so, you will also contribute to the development of nature-based solutions for coastal areas and to understanding how these can be implemented in an ecologically responsible manner.

You will work with colleagues on several projects simultaneously, with responsibilities allocated according to capacity and individual interests. Engagement with clients and other stakeholders is an integral part of our work.

Your Responsibilities As a Saltmarsh Ecology Researcher Include

carrying out annual monitoring of sediment accretion and vegetation development across various saltmarshes in the Wadden Sea;
analysing and interpreting monitoring data;
writing reports for clients;
assisting in the acquisition of new projects and the preparation of research proposals;
publishing and presenting your research in scientific journals and at conferences.

Wageningen Marine Research

Your primary area of work will be the Dutch Wadden Sea, although opportunities may also arise to contribute to projects elsewhere in the Netherlands and internationally. Wageningen Marine Research (https://www.wur.nl/en/about-wur/our-research/wageningen-marine-research) (WMR) is a leading organisation in the Netherlands in the field of marine ecological data collection, covering benthic fauna, marine mammals, fish, birds, coral, shellfish, and more. Many of these datasets have been collected and maintained using standardised methodologies for decades. In this role, you will contribute to the continuation and development of the saltmarsh monitoring dataset, which contains more than 60 years of valuable ecological data.

Your qualities

You are an enterprising researcher with expertise in the ecology of saltmarshes and saline vegetation communities, and a broad interest in the Wadden Sea and coastal ecosystems. You are able to work effectively under time pressure and manage your workload to meet deadlines. You are motivated, proactive, collaborative, client-focused, and possess strong communication skills.

In Addition, You Have

a completed relevant academic degree in the Natural or Life Sciences, with a specialisation in Wadden Sea and coastal ecosystems. A PhD in a field relevant to this position would be an advantage;
knowledge of saltmarsh vegetation;
experience with nature-based solutions;
strong report-writing skills;
experience in applying statistical analyses to long-term and spatial datasets;
a full Category B driving licence;
proficiency in Dutch would be an advantage.

In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale) C1.

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. We offer, depending on your experience, a competitive gross salary of between € 3,554.- and € 5,698.- for a full-time working week of 36 hours, in accordance with the CLA Wageningen Research (scale 10). Additionally, for this role a contract for 32 to 36 hours can be discussed. We initially offer a one-year contract, with the possibility of renewal subject to satisfactory performance and depending on the organisation’s financial situation.

We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

Coming from abroad

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. If you come with a partner, we offer a Dual Career group program organized by our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/). This program helps your partner to get familiar with the Dutch culture, labour market and assists your partner to find a job.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. jobs.title: Environmental Technology Researcher
jobs.description:
Your job

As an Environmental Technology Researcher at Wageningen Livestock Research, you will work on innovative solutions for emission reduction and sustainable manure processing. Please note that an excellent command of Dutch is essential for this role.

You will develop, investigate and support technological applications that contribute to a circular and future-proof livestock sector. Combining applied research with systems analysis, you will work both in the laboratory and on-site at livestock farms and manure processing facilities to test and optimise technologies under practical conditions. You will also use modelling and scenario analysis to assess the potential impact of new technologies at both regional and national levels.

Your Responsibilities As An Environmental Technology Researcher Will Include

designing and carrying out research into manure processing technologies, including anaerobic digestion, drying and nutrient recovery from manure;
measuring ammonia and greenhouse gas emissions from manure storage and processing systems;
analysing and optimising environmental technologies used in livestock farming and advising on future technological developments;
translating research findings into practical applications for the agricultural sector and government;
collaborating with fellow researchers, industry partners, government bodies and other stakeholders;
contributing to innovative projects focused on circular agriculture, renewable energy and sustainable farming.

Your Team

You will join a team of around 40 colleagues - including researchers, project leaders, measurement technicians and laboratory analysts - who are working together to develop innovative solutions for the livestock sector of the future. As a researcher, you will collaborate within the Emissions and Manure Valorisation (https://www.wur.nl/en/research/livestock-research/greenhouse-gases-livestock-farming) multidisciplinary project teams.

Within the department, you will work alongside an enthusiastic group of approximately 40 colleagues with diverse expertise and responsibilities. The team also collaborates extensively with other parts of Wageningen University & Research and with a broad network of external partners.

You will be based within the Emissions and Manure Valorisation department of Livestock Research. (https://www.wur.nl/en/about-wur/our-research/wageningen-livestock-research)

Our Mission

The livestock sector faces significant challenges. Reducing ammonia and greenhouse gas emissions is essential for achieving a sustainable future and maintaining the sector's licence to operate. The Environmental Technology and Manure Valorisation team develops and evaluates technologies that reduce emissions and nutrient losses from manure. At the same time, we increasingly view animal manure as a valuable resource. By converting manure into renewable energy, supporting circular applications and developing new bio-based products, we contribute to a resilient agricultural sector that is less dependent on fossil resources.

Your qualities

You are a proactive and results-oriented researcher who works effectively both independently and as part of multidisciplinary teams. You actively contribute to scientific impact by disseminating knowledge through publications, technical reports, and presentations at national and international conferences and symposia.

You Will Also Have

a completed university degree in Environmental Technology, Process Engineering, Agricultural Engineering, Animal Sciences, or a related discipline;
experience with manure processing technologies and applied research into technological innovations in livestock production;
a strong interest in emission reduction, circular agriculture and sustainable farming systems;
an excellent command of both Dutch and English.

working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. We offer, depending on your experience, a competitive gross salary of between € 3,554.- and € 5,698.- for a full-time working week of 36 hours, in accordance with the CLA Wageningen Research (scale 10). Additionally, for this role a contract for 32 to 36 hours can be discussed. We initially offer a one-year contract, with the possibility of renewal subject to satisfactory performance and depending on the organisation’s financial situation.

We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

However, for applicants for this specific position from outside the EU/EFTA zone, immigration restrictions may apply based on Dutch and EU immigration laws. Such candidates may be eligible for an “ orientation year ” in the Netherlands or a visa as a “ knowledge migrant ”.

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

jobs.title: Post-doc co-producing solutions for climate justice and desirable biomass uses
jobs.description:
Your job

Post-doc to engage stakeholders in co-producing solutions for climate justice and socially desirable biomass uses

We are looking for a highly motivated post-doctoral researcher. Do you want to work on the big challenges of climate (in)justice in the global North and South, and on the desired use of biomass across Europe? Do you want to work in two large projects with more than ten case studies across the world by engaging with a wide range of stakeholders and co-producing mental models, scenarios, and solutions on these issues? Do you want to work in large interdisciplinary teams? Then maybe this is the job for you!

As post-doctoral researcher you will be involved in two large European projects that recently started – BALANSED and Just in Clime. Both deal with some of the largest (environmental) issues that the world is facing today. The overall topic of Just in Clime relates to climate change impacts, the possible solutions that are put forward, and particularly issues with climate justice that this raises, also between the Global North and the Global South. The overall topic of BALANSED relates to the different ways biomass can be used (for food, feed, biofuel, etc.) and how these uses can be socially desirable. Despite topical differences, both projects have a similar approach to centralising stakeholders and stakeholder perspectives, with a large focus on a process of co-producing solutions to the issues of climate justice and biomass uses. Series of workshops in multiple case studies are planned to engage with stakeholders. In both projects, issues are seen as complex/messy problems that need a systemic approach to understand how systems function and how they are perceived by stakeholders. A range of methods and tools will be used to in a flexible methodology that is catered to specific case-study circumstances, but with similar elements to facilitate synthesis and upscaling. One crucial tool in both projects is a group-model building tool called Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping. This tool will be used to co-produce ‘mental models’ of how stakeholders perceive the system, focusing on feedbacks and complex interactions. An increased understanding of how stakeholders perceive problems and value possible solutions is one of the main outputs of the part of the work. Note that there is no need to be familiar with the specifics of FCMs.

As post-doctoral researcher, you will contribute to activities in both projects – BALANSED and Just in Clime. With a small team of researchers within the Environmental Systems Analysis Group (ESA), you will be responsible for streamlining the process, methods, and co-production of mental models and FCMs and linking outputs to other parts of the projects. Overall, you will closely interact with many other partners in both projects, both scientific and case study partners, and act as a main contact person for ensuring co-produced outcomes fit objectives of local case studies, of social learning and deliberation, and useful outcomes for quantitative models.

Concretely, Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

Develop a (flexible) methodology to co-produce knowledge with stakeholders
Help executing workshops and interviews
Develop mental models that allow understanding of stakeholder perspectives
Summarise, synthesise, and upscale case-study findings to European recommendations
Work with a large variety of scientific partners from both qualitative social sciences and quantitative environmental modellers

Your team

You will work with colleagues within ESA to form a core team to execute activities, but also closely with partners across Europe and the world in the context of both BALANSED and Just in Clime. You will be stationed in Wageningen, but you are expected to travel regularly to case studies to assist with the stakeholder engagement work.

You will work here

We are the Environmental Systems Analysis Group, where we advance understanding of complex systems, including interconnected challenges across food, biodiversity, water, and climate, requiring integrated, nexus-based approaches linking environmental and societal processes across scales. The sub-group that you will be part of – Empower Sustainable Futures – is specifically working on stakeholder engagement and human-nature relationships.

BALANSED and Just in Clime total about 30 partners across Europe and the world, many of which you will interact with, providing a rich interdisciplinary knowledge base.

Your qualities

This position is unique in that it relates to applying the same methodology and the same tool, but in two very different large projects. First and foremost, we are looking for someone who is comfortable and has experience with working in larger interdisciplinary projects. You need to possess demonstratable skills in working not only with scientists from a range of different disciplines, but also with local case study partners, as well as non-science stakeholders. For this, you need to have excellent communication and collaboration skills, while you need to be capable of handling sometimes conflicting interests. As most of the case studies will involve non-English workshops, speaking multiple languages besides English can be an advantage. Given these considerations, we prefer someone with a few years of working experience after PhD graduation.

You Also Possess

a PhD-degree or equivalent in environmental or social sciences, or a related field
broad academic skills and you are a dedicated, creative individual with excellent communication and collaboration skills
a genuine affinity with integrated, multidisciplinary issues and a demonstrated interest in interacting with decision makers and other stakeholders
knowledge of / familiarity with co-production techniques and/or quantitative models
excellent English language proficiency (a minimum of CEFR C2 level). For more information about this proficiency level, please visit our special language page (http://www.wur.nl/upload_mm/d/7/b/fa964c14-bf33-4148-8722-002cb3b1bef9_Common%20European%20Framework.pdf)

In our international working environment, there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale) C1 .

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. Depending on your experience, we offer a competitive gross salary of between € 3.546,- and € 5.538,- for a full-time working week of 38 hours, in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (https://www.universiteitenvannederland.nl/en/collective-labour-agreement-of-dutch-universities) (scale 10). Additionally, a contract for 32 hours per week can be discussed. As for your contract, we initially offer a one-year contract that can be extended - if possible within (company) organizational circumstances - on good performance, for the duration of the project (3 years in total).

We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment.

Coming from abroad

jobs.description:
About

Please refer to our Notion Job Board for the full job description and priority in your application process!

CarbonFarm
is creating a sustainable, profitable future for smallholder farmers.

We believe in a future where the 1 billion land stewards in this world can live profitably while taking care of the planet. That’s why we are aligning the two: profitability and climate impact.

Why CarbonFarm?

Impact-focussed company helping to fight climate change
Beautiful office spaces in (the very cool) Station F
Agile team of brilliant problem solvers
International team with international ambitions (22 people, 14 nationalities)
Deep-tech startup using modern, cloud-based technologies

How To Apply

A good CV is a short one (two pages good, one page better)
No need to write a cover letter, but you can highlight something from your CV or experience
You can send us a couple of examples that best showcase things you’ve done (e.g. links to code, or projects from your studies)

Job Description

We are searching for a data scientist/engineer who can own technical scientific delivery and communication for customer missions end-to-end
, and who can grow into a role combining operations, engineering, and product.

CarbonFarm’s work combines remote sensing data, agricultural data and machine learning. We work closely with worldwide customers to turn complex carbon projects into reliable and valuable outcomes, while feeding what we learn back into product and engineering.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer you will apply our models to each client project, adapting each time to the reality on the ground.

This role sits at the intersection of data science, engineering, and customer delivery operations
. You will work closely with operations, engineering, product, and R&D to deploy and adapt CarbonFarm’s technical capabilities. That includes everything from running data pipelines and validating model outputs to shaping requirements and helping identify what should become part of the core product.

On the client-facing front, you will be working closely with our Customer Success Managers. They will manage client expectations. You will help translate client needs into technical delivery requirements and intervene in client communication when things get too technical.

This is not a consulting role. We are looking for someone who is comfortable working directly with data, code, and technical systems, and who can bridge the communication gap between a technical product and the real world in which our clients operate.

Preferred Experience

What you’ll do

Adapt pre-built models and data processing to the idiosyncrasies of each client project
Collaborate with the Customer Success Manager to deliver technical results to commercial partners
Run and maintain customer mission workflows from data intake to final output
Work with Python, SQL, cloud systems and machine-learning pipelines
Validate model outputs and investigate issues in data or execution
Support reporting and communicating the environmental outcomes for multiple customers in parallel
Translate customer needs into actionable technical requirements
Identify recurring delivery patterns that should be improved or productised
Contribute to product improvements over time as delivery work reveals missing capabilities
Leverage AI tooling to drive rapid iteration, with a strong bias for technical accuracy

What We’re Looking For

2 years experience in data science or in a similar technical role
Masters degree or equivalent in engineering, computer science or similar
Excellent communication skills, notably with regards to communicating scientific concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Comfortable interpreting technical results in a commercial context
Autonomous coding in Python with 2+ years professional experience
Ability to understand technical systems end to end, even when not every component is owned directly
Comfortable navigating and querying SQL databases
1+ years experience creating or adapting data visualisations in Python or a data visualisation platform (e.g. Superset)
Experience working with cloud platforms
Experience working with data pipelines
Experience applying and adjusting machine-learning models, preferably in a professional context
English fluency
Paris-based, with the ability to work in person with the team

Nice to have

Experience with machine-learning pipeline operations, deployment, or monitoring
Familiarity with workflow orchestrating tooling such as Airflow or Dagster
Remote sensing or earth observation familiarity, notably SAR imagery
Familiarity with GIS tools or geospatial software concepts

Additional Information

Contract Type: Full-Time
Location: Paris
Experience: > 2 years
Occasional remote authorized

jobs.title: Senior Technical Environmental Fate Metabolism Expert - Team Leader
jobs.description:
Company Description

Syngenta Crop Protection is a leader in agricultural innovation, bringing breakthrough technologies and solutions that enable farmers to grow healthy and nutritious food while taking care of the planet. We offer a leading portfolio of crop protection solutions for plant and soil health, as well as digital solutions that transform the decision-making capabilities of farmers. Our 17,900 employees serve to advance agriculture in more than 90 countries around the world. Syngenta Crop Protection is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, and is part of the Syngenta Group.

Our employees reflect the diversity of our customers, the markets where we operate and the communities which we serve. Regardless of your position, you will have a vital role in safely feeding an ever-increasing population while taking care of our planet. Join us and help shape the future of agriculture.

Job Description

Are you a proactive problem solver with a passion for driving technical innovation? Do you enjoy solving complex analytical problems and delivering innovative technical solutions? Are you passionate about people development and enjoy working collaboratively? If so, we have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Technical Environmental Fate Metabolism Expert with people leadership experience to join our Analytical Methods & Metabolism (AMM) team and take on the challenge of elucidating the metabolic fate of our active ingredients in the environment whilst leading a team of highly collaborative study managers and technical experts. Within the role you will also drive both technical excellence and team development whilst building strong relationships with Contract Research Organisations (CROs) to deliver critical data. Your work will directly enable the global registration of sustainable, ground-breaking crop protection technologies such as our recent breakthrough TYMIRIUM® technology which protects crops against soil-borne pests. Key responsibilities will include:

People Leadership and Strategy

Developing talent: Leading, coaching and mentoring a collaborative team of study managers and technical experts, guiding performance and building tailored training plans.
Fostering a dynamic culture: Instilling a highly collaborative, inclusive environment that prioritises the well-being and growth of individual team members.
Strategic Influencing: Contributing to the effective running and future strategic direction of the broader AMM team.

Scientific and Technical Excellence

Holistically elucidating the environmental fate of our active ingredients: Generating key insights from environmental fate metabolism data, translating complex scientific results into expert conclusions for stakeholders.
Driving technical solutions: Acting as a key scientific leader within the environmental fate expert area, providing critical technical assistance to internal teams and external partners to resolve diverse analytical challenges.
Regulatory alignment: Maintaining and building upon your expert knowledge of environmental fate metabolism and global regulatory guidance ensuring study designs meet evolving international standards.

External Collaboration and Delivery

Resource management: Working with internal stakeholders to manage resources to meet project timelines.
CRO partnership: Building strong, collaborative relationships with Contract Research Organisations (CROs) to ensure the timely delivery of business critical data.

Qualifications

What we are looking for

Degree or equivalent in a biology/chemistry or related discipline.
Significant experience of conducting environmental fate metabolism studies for global regulatory submissions.
Deep technical expertise of compound metabolism in the environment.
Proven experience in people leadership, coaching and mentoring scientific staff.
Experience of generating key insights from data sets, with the ability to present complex data clearly to multiple stakeholders.
Ability to collaborate effectively in diverse teams, demonstrating strong organizational and analytical problem solving skills in scientific experiments.
Active scientific participation and collaboration with colleagues in industry, contract research organisations or regulatory agencies.
Keen attention to detail with a proactive mindset and ability to learn and apply new skills promptly in a fast-paced R&D environment.

Additional Information

Our site

Jealott's Hill International Research Centre UK is situated in pleasant semi-rural surroundings between Bracknell and Maidenhead and is the place of work for approximately 800 Syngenta scientists and support staff. Jealott’s Hill is one of the main global research and development sites and key activities include research into discovery of new active ingredients, new formulation technologies, product safety and technical support of our product range.

What We Offer

Extensive benefits package including a generous pension scheme, bonus scheme, private medical & life insurance.
Up to 31.5 days annual holiday.
Large campus environment.
A position which contributes to valuable and impactful work in a stimulating and international environment.
The chance to work as part of a global team to address the current and future needs of the agricultural sector.
Learning culture and wide range of training options.

Syngenta has been ranked as a top 5 employer
and number 1 in agriculture by Science Journal.

Syngenta is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or any other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. Learn more about our D&I initiatives here: https://www.syngenta.com/careers/working-syngenta/diversity-and-inclusion

Jealott’s Hill has Disability Confident certification.

We are committed to making all stages of our recruitment process accessible to all candidates and our Jealott’s Hill site are a Disability Confident Level 2 Employer. Please let us know if you need any assistance or reasonable adjustments throughout your application and we will do everything we can to support you.

jobs.title: Environmental Laboratory Auditor-Organic Chemist-Liquid Chromatography Specialist (Chemist 4)
jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring an Environmental Laboratory Auditor-Organic Chemist-Liquid Chromatography Specialist (Chemist 4)
within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Laboratory Accreditation Office in Manchester, WA
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

The position must work in-person at the Laboratory Accreditation Office on Mondays, our weekly Team Day, with additional on-site days required during onboarding and training.
This position conducts fieldwork at laboratories across Washington state, requiring regular travel to various lab sites.
After onboarding and training is complete, this position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by August 24, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

As a Chemist 4, you will help protect Washington’s environment and public health by accrediting environmental laboratories. You will help ensure laboratories can produce accurate and defensible analytical data, critical for state agencies and public health. In this role, you will evaluate laboratory capabilities, conduct on-site and virtual audits, and serve as the program’s subject matter expert in Organic Chemistry by Liquid Chromatography. You’ll provide technical guidance for implementation of accreditation standards. This position offers meaningful scientific work with opportunities to broaden your technical expertise, support statewide environmental initiatives, and take on responsibility within the accreditation program.

What You Will Do

Process initial and renewal applications for laboratory accreditation.
Review quality assurance manuals, standard operating procedures, analytical data, and performance testing results submitted in support of applications for accreditation.
Make recommendations to the Laboratory Accreditation Unit supervisor on whether laboratories can produce accurate and defensible analytical data.
Prepare correspondence informing laboratories of their accreditation status and maintain accurate records in the accreditation database.
Serve as the program’s liquid chromatography specialist, reviewing documentation and analytical data generated through LC/MS/MS instrumentation.
Conduct on-site and virtual audits of laboratories, either independently or as the organic chemistry specialist on an audit team.
Prepare clear, detailed audit reports and recommend corrective actions to improve laboratory procedures.
Track and verify laboratory compliance with audit findings.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Ten (10) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which must include all the following:

A minimum of five (5) years of experience employed in the conduct of bench scale laboratory testing, using similar methods and techniques for which auditing services would be provided.
Organic Chemistry Assessment – Ability to evaluate Organic Chemistry procedures, QA/QC, SOPs, detection limit studies, and analytical data to determine whether laboratories can produce valid results.
Communication – Clearly communicates technical and regulatory information in writing and verbally, including explaining requirements, analytical procedures, good laboratory practices, and documentation standards to ensure accuracy, traceability, defensibility, and consistent understanding across all interested parties.
Liquid Chromatography Expertise – Ability to perform specialized technical reviews in Liquid Chromatography to ensure accurate and defensible data.
Attention to Detail – Ability to review complex documents, data, and records carefully to support accreditation decisions.
Professional Judgment – Ability to interpret information, apply policy, and make sound, objective recommendations that support program goals.
Collaboration and Relationships – Ability to work effectively with colleagues, laboratories, and external partners to support consistent accreditation practices.
Analytical Method and Data Evaluation – Ability to assess laboratory procedures, instrument data, performance results, and demonstrations of capability, and to interpret technical information to validate analytical results and determine whether laboratory practices meet required standards.

Education
involving a major study in chemistry, environmental science, microbiology, or a related scientific field with a minimum of 30 semester hours or 45 quarter hours of college-level chemistry.

Examples Of How To Qualify

10 years of experience.
9 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
8 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
7 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
6 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
5 years of experience AND a Master’s degree or higher.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must be able to obtain and maintain a federal EPASS for the Manchester Lab facility.

Desired Qualifications

Regulatory Application – Ability to interpret and apply state and federal regulatory standards to ensure laboratories meet required compliance expectations.
Audit and Evaluation – Ability to conduct audits and assess laboratory practices to identify issues and recommend corrective actions that improve performance.
Database and Software Use – Ability to use accreditation databases and standard office software to document work, communicate findings, and support program operations.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are helpful but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:
We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How To Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach:

Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position
Resume

Because we base our selection on the information you provide, it is in your best interest to complete the application thoroughly. A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website.

Application Attestation: By submitting an application, you are affirming that the information contained in your application and on all attachments is complete and truthful. The state may verify this information, and any false or misleading answers may result in rejection of your application or dismissal if employed.

Need an Accommodation?

If you need reasonable accommodation during the application and/or screening process, including this job announcement in an alternate format:

Please contact us at 360-407-6186 or careers@ecy.wa.gov
If you are deaf or hard of hearing, you may call through the Washington Relay Service by dialing 711 or 1-800-833-6384.

Questions?

For specific questions about the position location options, schedule, or duties, please contact Rebecca Wood at Rebecca.Wood@ecy.wa.gov
If you need assistance applying for this job, are inquiring about the status of your application, would like to request the full position description, or have any other questions, please contact the Recruitment Team at careers@ecy.wa.gov

About The Environmental Assessment Program

The mission of the Environmental Assessment Program (EAP) is to measure, assess, and communicate environmental conditions in Washington state. We work to improve the environment for current and future generations through innovative and excellent science and thriving partnerships. This position is in the Laboratory Accreditation Unit within EAP’s Business Operations Section.

As the State of Washington’s environmental protection agency, we are deeply committed to protecting, preserving, and enhancing Washington’s environment for current and future generations. Joining Ecology means becoming part of a team dedicated to protecting and sustaining healthy land, air, water, and climate in harmony with a strong economy. A career in public service at Ecology allows you to help solve some of the most challenging problems facing our state, while keeping your health and financial security a priority. We invest in our employees to create and sustain a working environment that encourages creative leadership, effective resource management, teamwork, professionalism, and accountability.

You’ll be supported throughout your development by experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to learn, build your network and develop the skills and experience needed for a successful long-term career with Tetra Tech. .

Build your career on projects that help regenerate land, protect communities and support a more sustainable future. At Tetra Tech, you’ll work with experienced specialists on challenging geo-environmental projects while developing the technical skills, practical experience and professional confidence to succeed.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As a Graduate Geo-Environmental Consultant, you will join our Geo team, delivering geo-environmental consultancy services supported by in-house ground investigation expertise. You will work across contaminated land, site investigation, groundwater, environmental due diligence and advisory services for clients in sectors including property and regeneration, defence estates and transport.

Your Impact in this position

You will support the design, procurement, supervision and management of geotechnical and geo-environmental ground investigations. Your responsibilities will include desktop studies, accurate collection and analysis of site data, ground gas and groundwater monitoring, assessment of findings and preparation of detailed technical reports. This is an excellent opportunity to gain varied project experience and progress your career across a diverse portfolio of work.

5 Core Capabilities

Ground investigation: Assist with planning, procuring, supervising and managing geotechnical and geo-environmental investigations across a range of sites and sectors.
Geo-environmental assessment: Develop your knowledge of contaminated land, site investigation, groundwater, brownfield redevelopment, environmental due diligence and geotechnical engineering.
Site data and monitoring: Collect and analyse site information accurately, including ground gas and groundwater monitoring data, to support robust technical assessments.
Technical reporting and GIS: Produce clear, detailed reports and use Geographic Information Systems to create, manage and analyse environmental and site information.
Professional development and teamwork: Work collaboratively, communicate effectively, use initiative and commit to studying towards a professional qualification as your technical capability develops.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

You will have, or expect to achieve, a minimum 2:1 degree in geology, engineering geology, environmental science or a related subject. Enthusiasm for geo-environmental consultancy, strong analytical, written, communication and presentation skills, and a commitment to learning are essential. Relevant experience, such as a work placement, is desirable. You will also need a full driving licence and ideally access to a vehicle.

Working Environment

Based in Belfast, you will work across office, project and site environments, with travel to client and investigation sites required. Hybrid working is available; however, as a graduate, you will spend more time in the office initially to support training, mentoring and your development. Greater flexibility may be available as your knowledge and confidence grow, subject to project and team requirements .

Job Description

As the Environmental Impacts Project Manager, you will lead the planning, delivery and commissioning of sustainability and environmental initiatives across the Leonardo Helicopters (LH) UK portfolio. Working collaboratively with key stakeholders and delivery partners, you will help ensure initiatives are delivered safely, efficiently and to the highest standards, while meeting agreed budgets, timelines and performance targets.

Your impact

This is not a traditional end-to-end project management role. While you will take ownership of projects and initiatives, the role is equally about identifying opportunities, bringing people together, influencing positive change and turning sustainability ambitions into meaningful environmental improvements. You will be a passionate advocate for sustainability, using your knowledge, initiative and influence to make a tangible difference across the organisation.

You will provide day-to-day leadership and coordination across environmental and sustainability initiatives, driving performance against key metrics, managing risks and dependencies, and supporting successful implementation.

A key part of the role will be ensuring that Site Facilities environmental and sustainability activities remain fully compliant with UK legislation, LDO UK and LH UK policies, standards and procedures. You will identify opportunities for continuous improvement, challenge existing ways of working and work with stakeholders to develop practical solutions that reduce environmental impact and support the organisation’s wider sustainability ambitions.

Success in this role will require more than technical and project management capability. You will demonstrate a proactive, collaborative and purpose-driven approach, taking ownership, building strong relationships and role-modelling the behaviours needed to influence change. You will be comfortable working across organisational boundaries, engaging stakeholders at all levels and using your passion for sustainability to inspire action.

For the awareness of internal applicants, this role is a JFF level 6. This position is predominantly site based in Yeovil, with occasional working from home.

What you will do as a Site Facilities Environmental Impacts Project Manager:

Provide professional/technical advice in support of the successful delivery of infrastructure projects contributing to the 5-year business planning cycle and delivery of long-term strategies.
Ensure that suitable and sufficient HSE arrangements are deployed and practiced on all projects in accordance with current UK Legislation, LDO UK Policies and Procedures and the LHUK HSEMSM.
Collaborate with specialists such as Energy Managers, Sustainability Managers and local Government Officials for Permits and Licences.
Ensure all legal requirements, building regulations, safety codes, safety inspections, and local and national regulations are met.
Manage HSE issues, ensuring Contractors have a safe working environment within which to operate.
Ensure compliance with the LHUK Facilities project governance processes.
Effectively manage the Site Facilities related elements of audits by Regulatory and Assurance Bodies and Internal Auditors, including ISO14001, ISO45001 and ISO50001.
Manage the delivery of the ISO 50001 Energy Management System for LHUK.
Manage external audits.
Conduct annual review with Integrated Facilities Management (IFM) Energy Partner.
Review and chair the monthly Utilities Working Group (UWG).
Ensure the continuity of Utilities supplies to the LHUK property portfolio.
Responsible for the publication of monthly utilities management reports.
Act as lead for Yeovil Site Utilities management, including gas, water and electricity.
Manage the reduction of Utilities consumption as part of the LHUK commitment to the LDO UK Carbon Net Zero targets.
Ensure that LHUK is compliant with UK legislation for Utilities, including but not limited to CCA, CRC, CCL and Gas Safety.
Help drive innovative ways of working and tools for the wider Energy Decarbonisation Team.
Act as the lead for Social Value (SV) outputs from contract award.
Responsible for the management of EV provision.
Management of solar initiates, both internal and external to the Yeovil site.

Emergency Preparedness and Business Continuity

You may be called upon to support the LHUK Emergency Preparedness processes and procedures supporting the Command Emergency Control Centre (ECC), responsible for the management and delivery of the Site Facilities responsibilities, focussed on the management of incident consequences relating to People, Environment, Assets and Reputation (PEAR).

What You’ll Bring

Qualified professional and/or in-depth experience in a relevant environmental, sustainability or facilities discipline.
Working knowledge of sustainability and environmental best practice, legislation, risk management, policies, procedures and market trends.
Willingness to attain Practitioner Membership Standard of the Institute of Sustainability & Environmental Professionals by the end of Year 2 in role, and attain Full membership by the end of year 5
Strong stakeholder engagement, influencing and negotiation skills, with the ability to work effectively with employees, managers, customers, suppliers and regulatory authorities.
Clear understanding of business and functional strategy and how the role contributes to business objectives.
Understanding of real estate, infrastructure and Facilities Management processes, including CDM.
Experience and knowledge of LHUK manufacturing processes.
Financial competence, including budgetary control.
Self-motivated, purpose-driven and proactive, with the ability to deliver positive environmental and business change.

Who We Are

XCaliber Technologies is building the next generation of autonomous air defense. We develop integrated Counter UAS systems combining autonomy, sensing, command and control, and purpose built aircraft to detect, track, and defeat evolving aerial threats at machine speed and at scale.
At XCaliber, the connection between your work and the mission is direct. You will build systems whose performance can shape outcomes on the battlefield, protect people, and strengthen national security.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Drone Design and Integration Engineer to own the design, architecture, and vehicle level integration of our unmanned aircraft platforms.
This is a deeply hands on technical leadership role. You will take aircraft from early concepts to flight proven systems while driving engineering decisions across airframe, propulsion, power, avionics, sensing, communications, payloads, and manufacturing.
You will be responsible for making the aircraft work as a complete system, balancing performance, weight, endurance, reliability, manufacturability, cost, and development speed.

What You Will Do

Own aircraft architecture and vehicle integration from initial requirements through prototype development, flight testing, iteration, and production.
Define aircraft configurations, subsystem requirements, and major interfaces across airframe, propulsion, power, avionics, sensors, communications, and payloads.
Drive aircraft level engineering tradeoffs across weight, center of gravity, speed, endurance, payload capacity, reliability, and cost.
Lead component selection and mechanical, electrical, and hardware and software integration across the complete aircraft.
Establish and manage key aircraft constraints and budgets, including mass, center of gravity, power, thermal performance, and payload capacity.
Drive prototype builds, ground and flight testing, troubleshooting, failure investigation, and rapid design iteration.
Use engineering analysis, test data, and flight results to validate performance and guide vehicle level design decisions.
Lead design, integration, and flight readiness reviews while coordinating multidisciplinary engineering work and resolving problems across aircraft subsystems.
Guide aircraft from rapid prototypes toward reliable, repeatable, and manufacturable production hardware.

What We Are Looking For

Strong hands on experience designing, building, and integrating unmanned aircraft systems, aircraft systems, or closely related autonomous vehicles, with demonstrated ownership through prototype development and testing.
Ability to define aircraft architecture, subsystem interfaces, and engineering requirements, and make practical tradeoffs across performance, weight, power, reliability, manufacturability, cost, and technical risk.
Strong mechanical engineering fundamentals and practical CAD capability, with experience turning designs into working hardware.
Solid understanding of aircraft performance, flight dynamics, and the integration of airframe, propulsion, power, avionics, sensors, communications, and onboard computing.
Experience integrating hardware and software and troubleshooting issues across aircraft subsystems, including flight controls, electrical systems, avionics, and communications.
Experience planning and conducting ground and flight tests, using engineering analysis and test data to identify problems, validate performance, and improve designs.
Demonstrated ability to lead technical decisions and coordinate multidisciplinary engineering efforts while remaining directly involved in design, builds, troubleshooting, and field testing.
A degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to Have

Experience taking aircraft or complex robotic hardware from prototype toward repeatable manufacturing and production.
Familiarity with autopilot platforms such as PX4 or ArduPilot, and programming or scripting skills such as Python or C/C++ for testing, analysis, or integration.
Additional depth in electric propulsion, aircraft controls, composite structures, lightweight design, modeling and simulation, radio frequency systems, or payload integration.
Experience with multirotor, fixed wing, or vertical takeoff and landing aircraft.
Experience in defense or counter drone applications is valuable but not required.

jobs.title: Activating Agricultural Land Use for the Bernalillo County Community
jobs.description:
Bernalillo County, NM aims to improve residents’ quality of life and support small agricultural entrepreneurs through access to open space. The Executive Fellow will promote this goal by engaging internal and external stakeholders, researching agricultural hub models, and developing contract templates for small growers. As a result of this work, the Executive Fellow will help transform a 34-acre plot into land that promotes wellbeing, enables education, and unlocks opportunities for new farmers.

Fellowship Dates: October 26, 2026 – October 22, 2027

Salary:
Executive Fellows are FUSE employees and receive an annual salary of $95,000. Fellows can also access various health, dental, and vision insurance benefits. This amount is not representative of market-rate salaries for the experienced professionals in our program but is intended as compensation for a year of public service.

ABOUT THE FUSE EXECUTIVE FELLOWSHIP

FUSE is a national nonprofit dedicated to increasing the capacity of local governments to work more effectively for communities. We embed private sector executives in city and county agencies to lead projects that improve public services and accelerate systems change. Since 2012, FUSE has led over 400 projects in 58 governments across 26 states, impacting a total population equivalent to 1 in 10 Americans.

Executive Fellows are embedded in government agencies working with senior leaders for at least one year of full-time work. Prospective responsibilities may include thorough data analytics and research, developing enhanced operations and financial models, building change management and strategic planning processes, and/or building broad coalitions to support project implementation efforts. Executive Fellows are data-driven and results-oriented and able to effectively manage complex projects. They build strong relationships with a broad array of stakeholders, foster alignment within and across various layers of government, and build partnerships between governments and communities.

Throughout the fellowships, Executive Fellows receive training, coaching, and professional support to help achieve their project goals.

PROJECT BACKGROUND

Bernalillo County’s Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space aims to improve residents’ quality of life, with an emphasis on community health, economic development, and cultural heritage. Access to open space advances all three pillars. Parks and green space help people maintain their physical and mental health. Leasable plots would give agricultural entrepreneurs the chance to start or further their businesses with ensured access to land and lower capital requirements. Demonstration and education gardens allow the next generation to learn about their agricultural heritage. Additionally, as New Mexico’s farming community ages, encouraging young farmers to join the profession could help Bernalillo County preserve its food security.

To promote these goals, the County purchased a 34-acre property to steward as an agricultural open space. The land is across the street from a high school and less than a 10-minute walk from two other schools, making it ideal for educational use. After a round of planning and community engagement, the County decided to dedicate it to three main purposes: agricultural education, demonstration plots and gardens, and gathering space for educational and community events; leasable fields (approximately 0.25-2 acres each) for small growers (including graduates of the Department’s beginning farmer training program; and a habitat space with walking paths for conservation and recreation. These agricultural uses will support regenerative practices, including promoting food grown on public land. The Rio Grande High School cluster received a US Department of Education grant to carry out K-12 STEM pathways.

As the County finishes the planning phase for this property, it requires additional support to advance implementation of the master plan. The FUSE Executive Fellow will support the Bernalillo County Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space by facilitating and documenting stakeholder engagement, coordinating communications and updates about the site’s master plan, researching operational models, and creating contract templates for future growers. As a result of this work, Bernalillo County residents will be able to learn, play, gather, and grow businesses on this land.

PROJECT APPROACH

The first 90 days of the fellowship will focus on in-depth discovery and relationship-building. Beginning Fall 2026, the FUSE Executive Fellow will develop deep relationships with a broad range of stakeholders, including government (e.g., , school leadership, Ciudad Soil and Water Conservation District, County Extension, and ), local agri-food businesses (e.g., produce aggregators, South Valley Economic Development Center), community organizations (e.g., acequia associations, neighborhood associations) and community members (with an emphasis on Grow the Growers, Youth Ag Corps participants and residents living in the property’s walkshed). In addition, the Executive Fellow will review policies and best practices for creating inclusive open space and promoting small agriculture in communities similar to Bernalillo County.

Based on insights gathered, the Executive Fellow will develop and present proposed refinements to project goals, priorities, and anticipated deliverables for review and approval by the Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space and the Executive Sponsor.

Next, the Executive Fellow will engage internal and external stakeholders to advance implementation of the master plan. This will include facilitating and documenting discussions with community members and potential partners, working with consultants and the Open Space Manager to promote the updated plan to the public, and engaging County officials to provide inputs and approve decisions as appropriate. The Executive Fellow will ensure consistent communication, effective community building, and appropriate follow-up on decisions affecting the property. When the Executive Fellow identifies a potential partnership, they will assist the stakeholder in formalizing and launching the collaboration. If successful, the Executive Fellow will have helped the County form the relationships and identify the input necessary for the project to be effective.

In addition, the Executive Fellow will conduct extensive research on how other communities have leveraged open space to promote small agricultural entrepreneurship. This will include how communities fund and manage ongoing site operations and how they structure leases and relationships with small growers to be fair and inclusive–with an emphasis on supporting new businesses with limited cash on hand. They will use this research to create an operational plan to guide future management and to develop contract templates for future lessees that include alternate payment options (e.g., labor in lieu of cash). If successful, the County will have the insights and tools they need to continue managing the land after development is complete.

By the end of the fellowship, the Executive Fellow will have helped launch initial operations in part of the property and built the foundation the County needs to finish development and continue operations in the future. The Executive Fellow will be responsible for working with the Department of Parks, Recreation, and Open Space staff to ensure knowledge transfer, facilitate introductions to new stakeholders, and handover of any remaining responsibilities prior to departure.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES

By October 2027, the Executive Fellow will have overseen the following:
External Community Building – Engage external stakeholders (including schools, community organizations, neighbors, and other partner agencies) to implement the master plan and foster partnerships for its development and use.
Internal Facilitation – Ensure master plan consultants receive and incorporate stakeholder input. Prepare materials for presentation to management staff and county officials.
Operational Plan – Conduct research on how other communities have successfully promoted small agricultural hubs. Identify potential models for ongoing operation and management. Develop an operational plan to guide the County’s work.
Contract Templates – Develop templates for land lease contracts. Include options for alternative forms of payment that are achievable for target lessees/users.

KEY STAKEHOLDERS

Executive Sponsor –
Andre Dickson, Director, Department of Parks, Recreation, & Open Space
Project Supervisor –
Mari Simbaña, Open Space Manager, Department of Parks, Recreation, & Open Space

QUALIFICATIONS

15+ years of progressively responsible experience in organizational transformation and change management, from practitioner to enterprise-level leadership.
Synthesizes complex information into clear and concise recommendations and action-oriented implementation plans.
Develops and effectively implements both strategic and operational project management plans.
Generates innovative, data-driven, and result-oriented solutions to complex challenges.
Respond quickly to changing ideas, responsibilities, expectations, trends, strategies, and other processes.
Communicates effectively verbally and in writing and excels in active listening and conversing.
Fosters collaboration across multiple constituencies to support more effective decision-making.
Establishes and maintains strong relationships with diverse stakeholders, both inside and outside of government, particularly community-based relationships.
Embraces differing viewpoints and implements strategies to find common ground. Demonstrates confidence and professional diplomacy while effectively interacting with individuals at all levels of various organizations.

Did you know that Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation proudly hosts many community events each year? Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation Department (MCPRD) strives to enrich the lives of our residents. We do this by providing exciting and safe recreational amenities and programs, change to improve our resident’s fitness levels and decrease health care costs. This contributes to a sense of community through events and spaces for the public to socialize, thereby increasing property values and providing tourism venues. We play a critical role in ensuring Mecklenburg County achieves its vision that the county “will be a community of pride and choice for people to LIVE, WORK and RECREATE.” The department serves a population exceeding one million residents and serves the City of Charlotte, six towns, and the unincorporated areas of the county covering 523 square miles. The Mecklenburg County Park & Recreation Department is continually recognized for its cutting-edge programs, state-of-the-art facilities and unique partnerships. Our success is rooted in our staff. If you are interested in joining a dynamic team, dedicated to building a better community, and being recognized as leaders both in our community and across the country, then Mecklenburg County has great opportunities for you.

Position Summary

Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation is excited to welcome an innovative and dynamic Environmental Education Manager to our Nature Preserves and Natural Resources Division. The Environmental Education Manager is responsible for planning and directing all operational and environmental education program initiatives at 5-7 nature center facilities in support of our mission to protect natural and cultural resources for the benefit of future generations. The incumbent will directly supervise five to seven Nature/Cultural Center Managers, the Sr Aquarist, Master Naturalist Coordinator and Historian. Among other duties, this position is responsible for participating in strategic planning, developing and monitoring annual budgets, employee performance management, working cooperatively with other agencies, divisions and departments, researching and/or modifying existing procedures, facilitating communication between divisions and among staff, cost recovery and revenue projections, and will oversee interpretation in parks and preserves. The selected candidate may be required to work evenings and weekends based upon business needs. They may also be required to respond to emergency situations as they arise.

By applying to this position, you are eligible to be considered for a similar role, in which you meet the minimum qualifications for, at other Park and Recreation locations should they become available. If you are looking to grow in your career, or transition laterally into a new role, don't miss this opportunity to apply!

Preferred Qualifications

10 years of experience in environmental education and/or natural resource management with at least 5 years of supervisory experience
Master’s degree in related field

jobs.title: Strategic Environmental Assessment - Principal / Associate / Associate Director
jobs.description:
Job Description

What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you.

A Little More About Your Role…

As a Principal, Associate / Associate Director in the Infrastructure Planning and Environmental Assessment team, you will collaborate with a diverse team of technical specialists and professionals to lead and coordinate the delivery of key environmental and sustainability assessment projects. Your work will support our clients to address long term strategic challenges such achieving net zero, providing sustainable water resources, providing homes and disposing of radioactive waste.You will help ensure that sustainability is embedded into plan-making and decision taking.You will be instrumental in growing opportunities and the team, driving improvements and enhancing our client offer.

The role would suit an enthusiastic individual looking to influence, lead and deliver environmental and sustainability appraisal and assessment projects. You will have responsibility for leading project delivery, sector business development, service innovation and team development.

You Will

Play a leading role in growing our assessment and appraisal offer, working with sector leads and client account managers to drive thought leadership and win new business.
Build strong client relationships and identify opportunities to support project strategy, resourcing and delivery.
Take responsibility for defining medium and long-term market opportunities, and contribute towards developing appropriate business plans.
Take responsibility for scoping individual commissions, prepare proposals and winning work.
Provide project/task management to our multi-disciplinary teams working on projects across the UK and overseas. Work will involve client facing activity and managing projects and subcontractors
Work with colleagues, environmental specialists, and clients to promote and deliver evidence lead outcomes from assessment and appraisal work, taking responsibility for the delivery of high-quality outputs.
You will collaborate to design and implement new assessment tools, considering emerging and new practice, including digitisation and assessment automation.
Drive performance improvement and career advancement opportunities across team.
Promote an inclusive and positive team environment, acting as a trusted advisor and mentor.
Promote an inclusive workplace, demonstrating an understanding of Health and Safety whilst living the values of our health, safety, and wellbeing culture.
Undertake actions that contribute towards the success of the WSP business strategy, whilst being self-motivated towards goals relevant to the role, team, and your projects.

What we are looking to you to demonstrate…

Experience of leading the successful delivery of Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) and or Sustainability Appraisal (SA) to clients in the public and private sector.
A detailed understanding of SEA regulatory requirements, case law and guidance and the implications of Environmental Outcome Reporting (EOR).
Experience of working with Integrated Impact Assessment (IIA), Habitats Regulations Assessment (HRA), Water Framework Directive (WFD) Assessment, Health Impact Assessment (HIA) and Equalities Impact Assessment (EqIA).
Familiarity with project and scheme development impacts in variety of sectors e.g., housing, water, waste and resources, energy.
Relevant environmental or planning degree (or equivalent experience), with chartered status or actively working towards chartership.
Knowledge of emerging environmental and planning policy trends.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong report writing and review capabilities, attention to detail, and a focus on quality assurance.
Proven people management experience and a track record of developing and upskilling internal teams.
Demonstrated ability to contribute to strategic planning, win new work through bids and proposals, and enhance reputation in the assessment and appraisal sector.
Ability to work across multiple technical disciplines and manage competing priorities.
Excellent understanding of how GIS software is used to inform SEA/ SA, including the potential opportunities for the automation of assessment outputs.
Confidence engaging with clients, regulators and stakeholders.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel.

Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.

Join our close-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact. Our global team includes more than 69,000 employees, working together to make a difference in communities both close to home and around the world.

With us, you can. Apply today.

jobs.title: 2027 Remote Sensing Architecture Technical Engineer
jobs.description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Job Summary

The Enterprise Effects Division (EED) drives integration of Aerospace’s strategic capabilities across the national space enterprise. The division leverages a broad array of engineering disciplines against a diverse and dynamic portfolio of programs, customers, and national challenges. EED spans the capability lifecycle from concept and architecture design to performance assessment to application of space and space-enabled capabilities.

The Surveillance and Navigation Architecture Performance Department (SNAPD) in the Integrated Performance Subdivision aspires to be the premier force advising the evolution of national security and civil space enterprises, leveraging our modeling and simulation (M&S) expertise to evaluate end-to-end architecture performance.

We are seeking a Remote Sensing Architecture Technical Engineer
that will make use of sophisticated modeling and simulation tools in support of requirements verification, analyses-of-alternatives (AoA), and performance modeling for space-based remote sensing architectures.

Work Model

This full-time position requires work on-site at our facility in Chantilly, VA. Alternative locations that may be considered include El Segundo, CA, or Colorado Springs, CO.

What You’ll Be Doing

Support analysis in one or more of these specific mission areas: geo-spatial intelligence, signals intelligence, space surveillance, navigation systems, and/or space protection supporting defense or intelligence capabilities.
Independently apply standard engineering techniques, procedures, and criteria to support recommendations for research, development, and acquisition decisions of legacy and emerging customer space-based sensing architectures.
Perform architecture evaluation modeling overall performance using in-house or custom-developed analysis tools.
Work closely with senior staff, management, and teams to plan and conduct deep dives, trade studies, and assessments, translating customer needs into project objectives and providing quality deliverables to customer organizations.
Develop and present timely and technically accurate presentations and reports that clearly communicate analysis results and provide recommended solutions to technical leads, management, and customers.
Aid in sustainment, development, and growth of the organization’s analysis and simulation capabilities to support increasing functional areas for our diverse customer base.

Minimum Requirements

What You Need to be Successful:

M.S.degree in aerospace engineering, physics, operations research, mathematics, or a related field from an accredited program (pursuing or conferred within last 12 months)
0 - 1 yr of industry experience in relevant topic areas post bachelor’s degree (e.g., modeling and simulation, mission analysis, astrodynamics, or space operations.)
Knowledge or project experience with one or more of the following subjects: space-related modeling and simulation, geolocation, mission data processing, signal processing, space threats, resilient systems, advanced PNT technologies, algorithm design, software development, or mathematical modeling.
Familiarity with one or more software languages that may include Python, C/C++, and/or High-Performance Computing/Linux environments.
Minimum GPA 3.0
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.
Transcripts are required for this position

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

PhD degree in aerospace engineering, physics, operations research, mathematics, or a related field from an accredited program (pursuing or conferred within last 12 months) Experience in relevant topic areas post bachelor’s degree (e.g., modeling and simulation, mission analysis, astrodynamics, or space operations.)
Proficiency with one or more software languages that may include Python, C, C++, MATLAB, Fortran, Java
Significant experience in one or more of the functional/mission areas listed above.
Proficiency with one or more software languages that may include Python, C, C++, MATLAB, Fortran, Java.
Knowledge of Intelligence Community or U.S. Department of Defense business practices, acquisition policies, or space mission portfolios.
Demonstrated responsible professional engineering/scientific experience, to include the ability to:
Self-manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and deliverables
Maintain deliverable quality and manage customer expectations
Take direction, work independently, and develop productive working relationships
Interact and collaborate across a diverse team in different locations

Current TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills.

(Min - Max)

$100,000.00 - $140,000.00

Pay Basis: Annual

Leadership Competencies

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

Operate Strategically
Lead Change  
Engage with Impact  
Foster Innovation  
Deliver Results

Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. A few highlights include:

Comprehensive health care and wellness plans
Paid holidays, sick time, and vacation
Standard and alternate work schedules, including telework options
401(k) Plan — Employees receive a total company-paid benefit of 8%, 10%, or 12% of eligible compensation based on years of service and matching contributions; employees are immediately eligible and vested in the plan upon hire
