The division leverages a broad array of engineering disciplines against a diverse and dynamic portfolio of programs, customers, and national challenges. EED spans the capability lifecycle from concept and architecture design to performance assessment to application of space and space-enabled capabilities.

The Surveillance and Navigation Architecture Performance Department (SNAPD) in the Integrated Performance Subdivision aspires to be the premier force advising the evolution of national security and civil space enterprises, leveraging our modeling and simulation (M&S) expertise to evaluate end-to-end architecture performance.

We are seeking a Remote Sensing Architecture Technical Engineer
that will make use of sophisticated modeling and simulation tools in support of requirements verification, analyses-of-alternatives (AoA), and performance modeling for space-based remote sensing architectures.

We offer competitive cash compensation plus stock options.

Raw Data Processing:
Process multi source satellite, airborne, and ground based hyperspectral and multispectral raw data, including radiometric calibration, atmospheric correction, geometric correction, and orthorectification.

Apply hyperspectral and multispectral remote sensing to spectral analysis, mineral mapping, and alteration mapping, with a focus on copper, lithium, and other critical minerals.

, or similar software. Strong experience with hyperspectral, multispectral, and SAR data processing, including complete processing and analysis from raw data.

Strong English communication skills, with the ability to read technical literature and prepare technical reports in English.

Field geology experience and the ability to correlate remote sensing interpretations with geological outcrops.

Strong independent problem solving skills, teamwork, and cross disciplinary communication.

We simplify the adoption of geospatial data to understand better the world and enable people to act in an aware and timely manner to live better and preserve the Earth.

Planetek Hellas

We deal with the continuous monitoring with satellite data of Earth’s surface, infrastructures, worksites, urban dynamics, or marine coastal areas in support of decision-making and operational activities. Our focus on innovation has recently generated Rheticus®, a cloud platform designed to provide accurate data and real-time information about our changing world for the public and private sectors working to preserve our planet and improve the quality of our lives. This new type of service has led to a decisive transformation of the business model in geo-information services and today represents the synthesis of Planetek Italia’s skills and ability in producing high value-added services.

As a Senior
Remote Sensing Technical Specialist
, you will develop innovative applications and services for geospatial projects, leveraging your expertise in remote sensing technologies. Your role will involve processing and analyzing Earth observation data using specialized software and custom tools.

We seek proactive individuals with a solution-driven mindset who thrive in dynamic environments. In return, you will join a motivated and highly skilled team, contributing to the company's growth and success.

Key Responsibilities:

Remote Sensing Expertise:
Utilize your deep understanding of optical, SAR, and hyperspectral remote sensing to analyze and process geospatial data.

Software Proficiency:
Employ EO software such as ERDAS Imagine, QGIS, and ArcGIS to manage and interpret geospatial datasets.

Technical Documentation:
Develop reports, publications, and project proposals related to EO applications.

Collaboration:
Work with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders to ensure the successful execution of projects.

Apply expertise in EO data formats and processing tools to enhance analytical capabilities.

Engage with Data and Information Access Services (DIAS) to facilitate seamless EO data sharing.

Bachelor's degree in Surveying Engineering, Forestry, Environmental Science, Geography, Physical Sciences, or Geology.

Technical Skills:

Solid knowledge of EO (multispectral, SAR), including data management and metadata.

Hands-on experience with geospatial data processing and AI (ML/DL) applications.

Proficiency in scripting and spatial data analysis using Python or other programming languages.

Language Skills:

Fluency in Greek and English.

Additional Skills:

Ability to multitask under tight deadlines.

Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.

Effective communication and teamwork abilities.

What We Offer

At Planetek Hellas
, we prioritize results and value individuals for their passion and sense of responsibility. Ethics, professionalism, and teamwork define our work culture. If you are looking for a company that fosters enthusiasm and innovation, join us to contribute to the advancement of geospatial technologies.

Your office will be based in Marousi (Athens), with the flexibility to work remotely three days a week. Occasional travel across Europe may be required.

We recognize that exceptional work comes from a diverse and talented team. Our inclusive culture ensures that everyone feels valued and empowered to innovate. The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of California, Berkeley, seeks an Assistant/Associate Project Scientist to work with Professor Kenichi Soga on performance-based monitoring and risk assessment tool of lifeline infrastructure systems as part of research projects funded by the California Energy Commission, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and East Bay Municipal Utility District in Professor Kenichi Soga's lab entitled "Center for Smart Infrastructure". The outcome of the research will serve the infrastructure engineering community, leveraging real-time monitoring technologies to reduce construction and operational costs.

Conducting laboratory and field experiments in the area of infrastructure sensing, such as distributed fiber optic sensors and wireless sensor network

Writing reports from the investigation
Organizing meetings with the funding agencies
Tracking and managing the day-to-day operation of the Berkeley Center for Smart Infrastructure.

jobs.title: Environmental Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description

Anglo American Australia

Grosvenor Mine – an underground steelmaking coal mine produced its first longwall coal in May 2016 and is located in Moranbah, about 190 km south-west of Mackay.

We are building the team to deliver the next chapter of Grosvenor Mine. With a planned return to longwall production by Q4 2027, this is a unique opportunity to contribute to a major mine restart and help shape the future of underground mining.

Working alongside experienced professionals, you will play a role in implementing leading-edge technology, automation, monitoring systems and operational improvements that will define how the mine operates for years to come.

Job Description

Grosvenor Mine

We have an exciting opportunity for an Environmental Officer to join the team on a permanent basis at our Grosvenor Mine, based in Moranbah, QLD. The Environment Officer supports all aspects of the environment function for the underground coal mine.

Working together with Environment team and Operations, this role will see you contribute to driving the environmental performance of the mine, maintain compliance with corporate and legislative requirements and deliver on the Annual Environmental Plan.

The accountabilities and responsibilities for this role include:

Assist the Environmental team to deliver targets safely, optimally, and in accordance with the Annual Mine Plan.
Participating in the monitoring, analysis, and reporting on programs for land, vegetation, cultural heritage, water, and waste.
Support the development and implementation of Environmental Management plans and systems to improve site environmental performance such as land, vegetation, cultural heritage, water and waste.
Assist the Environmental Team regarding environmental concerns and actions in order to address them in a timely and effective manner.
Inform and educate management, supervisors and employees about the EMS and provide coaching to ensure a high level of awareness, commitment and compliance with EMS processes and guidelines.
Managing onsite routine monitoring and compliance with license conditions.
Review of the site environmental management systems (EMS).
Provide compliance-related advice to operations personnel where required.
Produce timely and accurate reports and plans, including statutory documentation, as required.
Support environmental corporate and regulatory reporting and assurance activities.
Land disturbance advice and permitting.
Monitoring of site disturbance activities to ensure compliance to legislative requirements.
Support in the management of contractors and projects on-site related to the Environmental works.

Qualifications

Tertiary qualifications in an environmental discipline or related degree are required with knowledge of environmental issues relevant to the coal mining industry highly regarded.
Experience using ArcGIS (Pro) or similar mapping software.
Familiarity with Risk Management Processes and Controls.
Experience in understanding, interpreting and analysing relevant environmental data.
Experience with the Microsoft Office suite (Word, Intermediate excel skills, PowerPoint, etc.)

Additional Information

Full-time permanent position based at Grosvenor Mine, Moranbah QLD
Monday to Friday staff roster (9-day fortnight available)
Competitive Salary + Annual Bonus + 12% Superannuation
Residential, FIFO (company funded) & DIDO options
Several conveniently timed, daily bus transfers from the airport to camp and onto site
Subsidised Anglo accommodation and company funded camp with meals provided
Domestic Relocation assistance to Moranbah township

What We Offer

When you join Anglo American, you can expect to enjoy a competitive salary and benefits package and a range of flexible work arrangements that support the balance of work, family and individual circumstances. But more than this, you’ll find yourself in an environment where the opportunities for learning and growth are second to none. From technical training to leadership programmes, we bring out the best in our people. There are plenty of opportunities to move onwards and upwards too. We’re a large, successful multinational company – and we’re still growing all the time.

Who We Are

We aim to lead the industry by pursuing ever safer and more responsible ways of working, demonstrating integrity, and showing care and respect for people and the planet. That means we are constantly seeking new opportunities to mine and process our products sustainably, using less water, less energy and more precise extraction technologies. As the custodians of coal and other precious natural resources – diamonds (through De Beers), copper, platinum and other precious metals, iron ore and nickel – our extraordinary teams work safely and collaboratively, with the utmost consideration for local communities, our customers and the world at large.

Background checks

Successful candidates will be required to complete background screening which may include a criminal check and validation of qualifications.

Inclusion and Diversity

Anglo American is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to promoting an inclusive and diverse workplace where we value and respect every colleague for who they are and provide equality of opportunity so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

How We Are Committed To Your Safety

Nothing is more important to us than ensuring you return home safely after a day’s work. To make that happen, we have the most rigorous safety standards in the industry. Not only that, we’re also continually investing in new technologies – from drones to data analytics – that are helping to make mining safer.

How To Apply

To apply for this role, please complete our online application form. You will have the opportunity to upload your CV and other relevant documentation as part of this process.

The State of Minnesota is committed to equity and inclusion, and invests in employees by providing benefits, support resources, and training and development opportunities. This position is being re-posted. If you previously applied, you do not need to reapply to be considered. Are you passionate about public health? The Drinking Water Protection Section (DWP) of the Environmental Health Division at MDH is seeking a Geospatial Research Specialist. This position exists to lead informatics research and infrastructure around geospatial data collection and analysis to support statewide collection and use of geospatial data. The purpose of this position is to provide an advanced level of geospatial, analytical, data science, and organizational skills to develop and implement business processes that support the geospatial expertise and coordination in the DWP Section. The person in this position serves as the DWP GIS data management expert. Primary Responsibilities Include Maintain and enhance DWP's data infrastructure to support GIS, reporting, and operational needs. Lead efforts to acquire, standardize, and improve the exchange of data with external agencies while serving as the primary coordinator for data integrations initiatives. Support GIS operations by expanding available datasets, improving access to spatial information, and providing technical expertise and training to staff. Provide geospatial related data analysis, data availability, and data management expertise for the DWP Section to support standardization of data pulls, modernization of scripts, and advances in geospatial data analytics. In accordance with HR/LR Policy #1422 Telework , this position is eligible for up to 50% telework for applicants who live in Minnesota or in a bordering state within 50 miles of the assigned work location. Candidates residing outside of Minnesota or in a bordering statewithin50 miles of the assigned work location at the time of application must be able to relocate to Minnesota within 30 days of their start date. MDH does not participate in the federal E-Verify program and is unable to sponsor applicants for work visas, including F-1STEM OPT extensions, and cannot complete Form I-9 or any other documentation requiring employer participation in E-Verify. All applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application. Minimum Qualifications To facilitate proper years of service crediting, please ensure that your resume clearly describes your experience in the areas listed and indicates the beginning and ending month and year for each job held . Only applicants with resumes that clearly demonstrate fulfillment of each of the minimum qualifications will be considered for this position. Four (4) years of experience performing research activities to support programmatic objectives. Experience must include all of the following: Performing GIS activities to enhance data infrastructure, reporting, and business processes. Performing geospatial-related data analysis and evaluation, including executing geoprocessing workflows using Python (ArcPy). Providing data expertise and technical assistance and training to various stakeholder groups. Minimum Qualifications To Be Assessed During The Interview Process Written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical information to diverse audiences and collaborate with internal and external stakeholders. Knowledge of data informatics trends and research using GIS applications and advanced analytics. Knowledge of public health concepts and related data management best practices. Degree Equivalences A related associate degree may be substituted for six (6) months of experience. A related bachelor's degree may be substituted for one (1) year of experience. A related master's degree may be substituted for eighteen (18) months of experience. A related doctorate degree may be substituted for two (2) years of experience. Preferred Qualifications Degree in environmental science, health informatics, statistics, epidemiology, public health, or closely related field. Experience conducting advanced geospatial related research and analytics. Experience leading cross-functional project teams. Experience performing data infrastructure analysis, evaluation, and documentation, and developing and implementing business processes. Additional Requirements This position requires successful completion of a reference check. This employment does not require a valid driver's license, but it does demand occasional travel which the candidate will be responsible for meeting. jobs.description:
Description And Requirements

Who We Are

Enel North America is a proven renewables leader delivering clean, flexible and sustainable energy solutions.

As part of the Enel Group, we develop, build, own and operate renewable power plants and demand response solutions, with over 11 gigawatts (GW) of installed wind and solar capacity, over 1 GW of energy storage and nearly 5 GW of demand response in the US and Canada.

For nearly 25 years, we've reliably powered modern life and driven climate action with our people, partners and communities by putting sustainability at the center of everything we do. Enel is a top-five industry leader for clean power capacity in the US, demand response in North America and utility-scale battery storage in Texas.

We are a smart and passionate team working together to build the Enel North America that we want for the long-term – one that is founded on strong financial, social and environmental values. Being on our team means being part of lasting progress to create a thriving and more sustainable world for our climate and communities. It means valuing safety, trust, innovation, proactivity, flexibility and respect in all we do. Our vision is ambitious, and we'll get there together.

The Opportunity:

The position, in cooperation with other Units and while also supporting other members will ensure the execution of the activities related to:

The preparation of environmental documents needed to obtain the environmental authorization of projects), both directly and/or by external services, required for the assessment of the impacts on the environmental and social matrices;
To identify the environmental constraints of the site. To contribute to the preparation of the Feasibility Studies and Due Diligence Analysis;
The environmental constraints check, in relation to new power plants, in order to comply with the environmental authorizations obtained and to define the related Capex or Opex;
To design and perform environmental monitoring on site.

The Lead Environmental Engineer will address and solve technical issues related to own field of expertise and by means of own knowledge in order to meet project/authorization requirements.. Those activities could be performed also managing external resources.

What You'll Do at Enel North America:

Responsibilities, include, but not limited to:

Address the relevant environmental specialized topics for all project development stages (development, permitting and construction phases) in order to ensure the compliance with company environmental best practices, technical specifications, guidelines and general objectives.
Ensure high level competence on authorization issues of renewable power plants, defining and updating the technical specifications needed for the execution of documents for environmental authorization, supporting and assisting any other involved unit within the Organization.
Provide technical support to E&C colleagues in relation to the activities needed to ensure the compliance of the project/power plant to environmental constraints and requirements, to BD colleagues for the "authorization path" definition, to HSEQ colleagues for the on-site surveillance and environmental reporting.
Management/control of external contractors for the execution, for renewable energy power plants, of:
environmental assessment (and eventual integrative documents)
environmental monitoring on site (permitting/construction/operation phases)

In relation to own field of expertise, execution and/or validation of Environmental Due Diligences, Feasibility Studies, Documents and Studies required for Permitting and Monitoring Plans for renewable power plants (wind, solar, geo, Hydro and storage).
Support the other units within the Organization for assuring the authorization compliance of the construction (supplies and works) of the renewable power plants (wind, solar, geo, Hydro and storage) - related to own field of expertise.
Support the other units within the Organization for the overall planning of the project's activities - related to own field of expertise.
Work and cooperate with the Business Development Unit (BD), Project Engineers, Project Managers and the other specialists from the Engineering Unit for all the environmental aspects of the projects.
Take part to the meetings with the Authorities and the stakeholders, about the technical topics in support of the BD colleagues.
Lead, perform and support the other units estimating the costs for the environmental activities to be executed during construction of renewable power plants (wind, solar, geo, Hydro and storage), in relation to own field of expertise.
Lead perform and support the other units the risk assessment related to the construction of renewable power plants (wind, solar, geo, hydro and storage) - related to own field of expertise.
Develop, create and update on a regular basis the technical specifications to be used for any RFPs to be issued by the Organization - related to own field of expertise.
Lead, perform and support the other units for the preparation of the technical evaluation of the offers submitted by the Vendors for any RFPs sent out by the Organization - related to own field of expertise.
Manage, with the support of other units within the Organization, the environmental engineering service contracts.
Support other units within the Organization for the management and supply contracts entered into with external service providers related to own field of expertise.
Support the younger members of the organization.

Who You Are:

Ability to work within a Global Framework
Ability to work within a Matrix Organization
Ability in working within multidisciplinary and multicultural teams

The purpose of this position is to supervise, schedule, and develop EVS staff to meet the needs of patients, visitors, and staff. . Partners with other OHSU departments to improve patient care and throughput

1 year of lead or supervisory experience with a Bachelor’s degree.

Proficient skills in English language: reading, writing, verbal

Experience in union environment

jobs.title: Director Environmental, Health, and Safety
jobs.description:
Director Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS)

Company Overview

Moffitt Services is a leading Texas-based bulk fuel and lubricants distributor headquartered in Cypress, Texas, with a legacy dating back to 1947. We specialize in providing high-quality fuels, lubricants, and superior service to a diverse range of industries, including construction, agriculture, transportation, energy, and emergency response sectors. Our commitment to reliability extends nationwide, offering same-day delivery, 24/7 emergency fueling, disaster relief support, bulk tank rentals, heavy haul services, on-site fueling, and business continuity solutions. As a privately held company focused on trust, innovation, and customer-centric growth, we are poised for expansion in a dynamic energy and logistics landscape.

Mission Statement

Moffitt Companies are built on generations of family values that stand for superior service. We deliver the right products and services on time, every time, no matter the conditions. Our goal is to serve as a “One Call Does It All” partner dedicated to helping our customers succeed while continuing to grow our legacy of service nationwide.

Position Overview

Moffitt Services is seeking a Director of Environmental, Health, and Safety who will lead the company's comprehensive EHS program. This hands-on leadership role combines strategic direction with active field presence to drive safety culture, ensure regulatory compliance, minimize risks, and foster continuous improvement across operations, fleets, terminals, and facilities.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Lead and manage the Environmental, Health, and Safety department, including building, organizing, and developing a high-performing team; define roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
Serve as a proactive self-starter who identifies opportunities, pushes forward EHS initiatives, and drives implementation of programs to achieve zero-incident goals, regulatory excellence, and operational efficiency.
Develop, implement, and continuously improve company-wide EHS policies, programs, and procedures aligned with federal (OSHA, EPA, DOT, USCG), state (TCEQ), and local regulations, particularly for hazardous materials transportation, fuel storage, emissions, spill prevention, and waste management.
Conduct and oversee regular site inspections, facility audits, vehicle inspections, environmental compliance checks, and safety assessments at terminals, field locations, and fleet operations.
Provide hands-on training, coaching, and leadership to drivers, terminal staff, operations teams, and leadership on EHS procedures, regulatory compliance, hazard recognition, safe handling of fuels/lubricants/hazmat, and emergency response.
Lead incident investigations, root cause analyses, corrective/preventive actions, and follow-up to prevent recurrence; manage reporting and documentation for internal and regulatory purposes.
Track and analyze EHS metrics, inspection results, audit findings, training completion, incident trends, and environmental performance to drive accountability, reporting, and strategic decision-making.
Ensure daily operational compliance with DOT regulations for hazardous materials transportation, OSHA standards for workplace safety, TCEQ requirements (e.g., petroleum storage tanks, air permitting, spill prevention/control, emissions from fuel handling), and other applicable environmental/health/safety rules.
Develop and maintain emergency response plans, spill prevention/countermeasure plans (SPCC), and preparedness programs; coordinate drills and response activities.
Manage environmental programs including hazardous waste handling, storage tank compliance, air/water permitting, emissions monitoring, and sustainability initiatives to reduce environmental impact.
Assist with insurance claims, regulatory audits/inspections, and interactions with legal teams by providing thorough documentation and support.
Foster a strong, visible culture of safety, environmental stewardship, and health awareness through daily engagement, leadership presence in the field, monthly safety meetings, toolbox talks, and cross-functional collaboration.
Identify and champion EHS improvement initiatives, including process enhancements, risk reduction strategies, and best practices adoption to support company growth and compliance.

Qualifications

Proven experience in environmental, health, and safety leadership, particularly in fleet operations, hazmat transportation, fuel/petroleum distribution, or related industries.
Strong working knowledge of DOT regulations for hazardous materials transportation (required), OSHA standards, and TCEQ environmental regulations (preferred, including experience with petroleum storage tanks, air permits, spill prevention, and fuel-related compliance in Texas).
Demonstrated ability to lead and develop teams, manage groups of people, push initiatives forward, and drive cultural/operational change.
Self-starter with a proactive, "boots on the ground" management style; comfortable with field work, independent decision-making, and hands-on execution.
Experience conducting field inspections, incident reviews, root cause analysis, training delivery, and regulatory interactions.
Strong communication, documentation, and organizational skills for managing training, inspections, audits, incidents, and compliance records.
Background working with insurance providers, legal teams, and regulatory agencies on claims, audits, and compliance matters.
Experience managing EHS for fleets and operations of various sizes.

Preferred Qualifications

Certified Director of Safety (CDS) or equivalent certification preferred.
Formal education (Bachelor’s degree preferred) in Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, or a related field.
Additional certifications such as CSP, ASP, CHMM, or TCEQ-related credentials are a plus.

Relocation
This position is not eligible for relocation.

Travel Requirements
Monthly travel (3-5 days) is required to provide EHS support, conduct inspections, lead training, and engage with regional locations and field teams.

Work Schedule/Benefits
This position is on-site Monday through Friday. Moffitt Services offers competitive insurance rates through medical, dental, and vision plans; and a 401(k) match program.

Experience with feature extraction from LiDAR data. Strong attention to detail and ability to identify data-quality issues. Basic/intermediate GIS knowledge. Nice to Have Experience with utility, power transmission, or distribution data. Experience with aerial LiDAR. Experience working with conductors, poles/towers, vegetation, and ground classes. Understanding of conductor/catenary modeling and clearance analysis. Experience with PLS-CADD, TerraSolid/TerraScan, or MicroStation. Experience with utility asset modeling or powerline mapping.

About The Role

At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future. Department Summary: MITRE’s Model-Based Analytics Department (L144) is looking for qualified applicants to bring their geospatial, machine learning, advanced analytics, and applied research skills to bear on solving problems of critical national importance. MITRE’s diverse work program provides opportunities to apply your expertise and creative thinking in challenging domains such as healthcare, transportation, and national security. Employees may also participate in MITRE’s internal research and development program, which provides funding for innovative applied research that addresses our sponsors’ hardest problems. Our department is an interdisciplinary department that thrives on having a large toolbox to support data- and model-driven decision making. We value people who can bring diverse and inclusive perspectives. Our department works to solve modeling and analytic problems in the public interest, in partnership with the government. We also actively conduct independent research in areas of interest to our government partners. If you are passionate about being a Data Scientist that specializes in Geospatial Information Sciences, your skill sets align with our capabilities, and you like working in a collaborative, team-oriented environment, we want to hear from you! Roles & Responsibilities: The successful candidate for this position is a geospatial data scientist who combines a solid theoretical and technical background with the ability to formulate problems, develop and evaluate solutions, and communicate results. Familiarity with advanced geospatial data science, modeling, and analysis techniques and methods (e.g., supervised and unsupervised machine learning, GeoAI, Geosimulation, patiotemporal graphs) is a plus. Hands-on software development skills are a must. Candidates should have a strong understanding of how to engineer spatial solutions for geospatial systems and architecture in both traditional and cloud computing environments. Lifelong learning and keeping up with the latest research and technologies is an essential part of working in this field. Roles and responsibilities include: Support the development of geospatial data science, modeling, analysis, visualization, and engineering deliverables for sponsor projects and programs, internal research and development, and corporate strategic initiatives. Remain current on open-source, industry, academia, and US Government techniques and tools for geospatial data science, modeling, analysis, visualization, and engineering. Apply a variety of spatial data science techniques to tackle customer challenges to include geospatial statistics, spatial optimization, spatial pattern analysis, geospatial artificial intelligence, spatial autocorrelation, activity-based intelligence, imagery analysis, remote sensing, and geospatial data visualization approaches. Build and test geospatial prototypes in MITRE, government, and commercial cloud environments. Basic Qualifications: Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 3 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with relevant experience who can immediately contribute at this job step; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience. Bachelor’s degree in Geospatial Data Science, Geospatial Intelligence, Geographic Information Systems, GeoInformatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or related degree. Applied experience with common GIS tools, developing geospatial workflows, and visualizations using Python. Applied experience in spatial analysis and modeling, and ETL of spatiotemporal datasets and managing spatial databases. Applied experience in the configuration of web-mapping, dashboard applications, and remotely sensed data. Familiarity with geostatistics, spatial machine learning, geosimulation, or GeoAI, and multispectral and hyperspectral imagery or synthetic aperture radar. Familiarity working with spatiotemporal data in graph databases, such as ArcGIS Knowledge, Neo4j, or ArangoDB. Familiarity developing web applications with common libraries, e.g. OpenLayers, Leaflet, ArcGIS JS API. Familiarity with geospatial data architectures and spatial database design and management, as well as containerization concepts. Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance. This position requires a minimum of 3 days on-site. Preferred Qualifications: Active TS/SCI with polygraph. Advanced degree in Geospatial Data Science, Geospatial Intelligence, Geographic Information Systems, GeoInformatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or related technical discipline. Experience leading technical development across multi-disciplinary teams. Applied experience with other software development languages, e.g., C++, Java, C#, JavaScript. jobs.description:
About the role:

The Environmental and Social (E&S) Manager is responsible for ensuring that ACWA and assets in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia comply with applicable Saudi environmental, labor, occupational health and safety, and social requirements, as well as international lender standards. The role focuses on minimizing environmental impacts, managing social risks, maintaining regulatory compliance, and supporting sustainable project delivery in alignment with Saudi Vision 2030.

This is a project-critical role, particularly because ACWA projects may be subject to the requirements of Saudi authorities, including (NCEC), the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA), the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD), and other relevant regulators, in addition to international financing institutions such as IFC, EBRD, ECAs, and Equator Principles financial institutions.

Ensure compliance with Saudi environmental regulations and applicable international lender standards, including IFC Performance Standards, EBRD requirements, and Equator Principles expectations
Implement, maintain, and continuously improve the project Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS)
Manage environmental permits, approvals, renewals, and regulatory submissions with relevant Saudi authorities, including NCEC and other competent agencies as applicable
Monitor environmental impacts (air, water, waste, noise, biodiversity)
Oversee contractor E&S performance (EPC and O&M)
Conduct site inspections, audits, and walkovers
Stop non‑compliant or unsafe activities and ensure corrective actions
Lead stakeholder engagement activities with local communities, authorities, contractors, and project stakeholders in accordance with the project Stakeholder Engagement Plan
Operate and manage the grievance mechanism (communities & workers)
Prepare clear and timely E&S reports for lenders, Saudi regulators, project leadership, and external audits
Advise project leadership on E&S risks and improvements

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Sustainability, Social Sciences, or related field
10+ years experience in environmental & social management
4+ years site‑based experience on energy, infrastructure, or construction projects
Strong knowledge of:

Saudi environmental, labor, occupational health and safety, permitting, and social compliance requirements
Experience implementing and managing Environmental & Social Management Systems (ESMS)

Ability to manage contractors (EPC/O&M) and site compliance
Experience with stakeholder engagement and grievance mechanisms
Strong reporting, documentation, and risk‑management skills

Company Description
Prism Specialty Restoration provides residential and commercial specialty contents restoration, supporting homeowners, businesses, contractors, and insurance professionals. The company focuses on restoring electronics, art, documents, and textiles using safety-focused, proven processes. Prism delivers consistent quality, cost-effective outcomes, and turnaround times that align with claims and broader restoration timelines. The team prioritizes transparency, clear communication, and documented restoration from pickup through delivery. Every item is treated with care and urgency to reduce downtime and help customers return to normal as quickly as possible.
Role Description
The Document Restoration Management role is a full-time, on-site position based in Indianapolis, IN. This role oversees the end-to-end restoration process for damaged or at-risk documents, including intake, assessment, cataloging, and tracking throughout restoration. Day-to-day responsibilities include coordinating document handling and storage, supervising restoration techniques such as drying, cleaning, and digitization, and ensuring accurate documentation of all work performed. The individual in this role will collaborate with field teams, clients, and insurance partners to provide updates, manage timelines, and help resolve questions about scope and status. The role also involves monitoring quality standards, enforcing safety and confidentiality protocols, and identifying process improvements to enhance efficiency and client experience.
Qualifications

Document restoration and preservation skills, including handling sensitive records, applying appropriate drying and cleaning techniques, and understanding basic archival or records management principles.
Operational and project coordination skills, such as workflow planning, task prioritization, inventory tracking, and schedule management in a fast-paced restoration environment.
Attention to detail and quality control skills, including accurate data entry, meticulous recordkeeping, and the ability to review work for completeness and compliance with company standards.
Customer service and communication skills, with the ability to provide clear updates to clients and insurance partners, explain processes, and address inquiries in a professional, empathetic manner.
Safety, confidentiality, and compliance awareness, including adherence to company safety protocols, secure handling of confidential or sensitive documents, and respect for regulatory and privacy requirements.
Basic technical skills, such as using office software, scanners, and other equipment related to document restoration and digitization.
Ability to work on-site in a physical environment, including standing, lifting, and moving boxes or equipment as needed, with a focus on safe work practices.
Previous experience in restoration, records management, or a related field is beneficial; a high school diploma or equivalent is required, and further education or certifications in restoration or archival work are an advantage.

jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Central Region Community Outreach and Environmental Education Specialist 3
within the Water Quality Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Assignment Pay

This bilingual-designated role requires successful completion of a Spanish language proficiency assessment (verbal and written) as part of the hiring process.
The salary listed includes 5% bilingual assignment pay.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
A minimum of one day per week is required in the office.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by August 25, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

You will be the community’s bridge to water quality awareness and action. As the Community Outreach Environmental Education Specialist, you will lead creative, hands-on learning experiences that inspire residents of all ages to become active stewards of their local environment. Through dynamic public engagement, innovative educational programming, and strong partnerships with schools, community groups, and regional partners, you will transform environmental challenges into opportunities for collective impact.

You will design and deliver outreach initiatives that make complex environmental topics accessible, relatable, and locally relevant—whether through interactive workshops, youth programs, public events, or multilingual communications. You will also help build long-term community relationships that support equitable participation and ensure every voice is heard in environmental decision-making.

What You Will Do

Partner with technical experts to craft community-centered engagement strategies that bring water quality science to life and connect residents directly to the mission of protecting the region’s waters.
Serve as a cultural and linguistic bridge by providing Spanish interpretation during workshops, public meetings, school events, and neighborhood canvassing—ensuring every community member can participate fully and confidently.
Spark public learning through accessible outreach—sharing information via presentations, email, web content, and educational materials that help people understand and act on water quality issues.
Translate key outreach materials into Spanish to support inclusive communication and make environmental information easier for more families to access.
Guide thoughtful, on-the-ground engagement efforts—planning, implementing, and evaluating community outreach while elevating community insights and identifying emerging environmental justice needs in the Lower Yakima Valley.
Remove barriers to participation by identifying gaps in access, developing best practices, and creating tailored outreach tools for underserved communities, local interests, governments, industry, and the general public.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Seven (7) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Communication Skills – Ability to share information clearly with diverse audiences to support understanding and informed participation.
Community Engagement – Ability to plan and carry out engagement activities to involve communities in program decisions and actions.
Cultural Humility and Inclusion – Ability to work respectfully with people from diverse cultures and backgrounds to build trust and improve access to agency services.
Outreach and Education Delivery – Ability to develop and deliver accessible outreach materials and learning opportunities to help the public understand program issues and resources.
Bilingual Communication (English/Spanish) – Ability to translate and interpret information accurately to ensure Spanish-speaking communities can fully participate in outreach and engagement activities. This includes: verbal (speaking/listening) and written (reading/writing).
Program and Environmental Knowledge – Ability to understand environmental issues, program activities, and regulatory requirements to share accurate information and support informed public engagement.

Education
involving a major study in environmental, physical, or natural science, education, health sciences, social services, communications or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

Examples Of How To Qualify

7 years of experience.
6 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
4 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
3 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
2 years of experience AND a Master’s degree or above.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license or provide alternate reliable transportation for travel within the state of Washington.
Must pass the verbal (speaking/listening) and written (reading/writing) Spanish language proficiency tests.

Desired Qualifications

Lived or professional experience with underrepresented communities.
An understanding of environmental justice research, demographic data, and equity focused assessments.
Knowledge and practice of collaborative problem solving, conflict resolution, and participatory planning.
Experience with website and social media content development.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are nice to have but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.

Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR)
are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.

Diversity:
We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.

Equity:
We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.

Inclusion:
We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.

Respect:
We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.

We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Duties

As the Industrial Wastewater Permit Manager, you will support Ecology’s mission and represent the Water Quality Program as an Environmental Engineer. Under the supervision of the Industrial Wastewater Permits Unit (IWPU) Supervisor, you will be responsible for developing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits, State Waste Discharge (SWD) permits, and accompanying fact sheets for industrial facilities in the Northwest region of Washington state. This work directly supports clean water protections and helps ensure industrial practices are safe, sustainable, and compliant.

In this role, you will review permit reports, conduct facility inspections, provide technical assistance, investigate complaints, conduct compliance reviews, and provide technical support for enforcement recommendations. Under the guidance of a licensed engineer, you will also review engineering reports submitted by the industrial facilities.

You will frequently collaborate with internal staff to offer technical assistance to industrial facilities and to support the development of compliance or enforcement actions. This position provides opportunities to grow your technical expertise, strengthen your engineering judgment, and contribute meaningfully to environmental outcomes across the state.

What You Will Do

Develop wastewater discharge permits.
Review water quality monitoring data to determine facility compliance.
Conduct facility inspections, provide technical assistance, and write inspection reports.
Conduct water quality sampling and analyze monitoring data to evaluate compliance.
Assist with the development of enforcement actions.
Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, and clearly explain complex technical issues in plain language.
Work with the Ecology Communications team to respond to media inquiries.
Learn to review engineering reports submitted for ISGP and individual NPDES permits.

Learn more about what it is like to be an Engineer at the Department of Ecology

Engineering Review – Ability to assess engineering reports, treatment system information, and monitoring data to identify issues and recommend technically sound solutions.
Engineering Tools & Methods – Ability to use engineering tools, models, and methods to support evaluations of treatment systems, discharge conditions, and environmental impacts.

Technical Collaboration – Ability to work constructively with facilities, Tribal nations, local governments, and colleagues to resolve technical questions, support compliance efforts, and ensure consistent understanding of engineering and environmental requirements.
Communication & Documentation – Ability to communicate technical concepts and prepare clear permits, reports, and correspondence to support regulatory decisions and partner understanding.

jobs.description:
Australia is increasingly affected by climate change, creating a growing need for climate analysis and forecasting services to support community safety and resilience.

To meet this need, the Community Services Group (CSG) delivers customer-focused, integrated and resilient operational services across Australia. jobs.title: Environmental Geoscientist | Energy
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Good environmental and geoscience work starts in the field. The quality of what gets recorded on site, how samples are handled, how monitoring is carried out and how findings are documented lays the foundation for everything that follows. At Stantec, we know that, and we look for people who take that foundation seriously.

We are looking for an Environmental Geoscientist to join our Energy and Resources Group, working across contaminated land, hydrogeology and ground investigation projects from our Warrington, Manchester or Shrewsbury offices. If you are practical, organised and ready to build your career in environmental geoscience within a strong, supportive team, we would love to hear from you.

About The Role

You will play a hands-on role in planning, coordinating and delivering environmental and geoscience siteworks across a varied portfolio of projects. Day to day, this will include supporting ground investigation supervision, undertaking groundwater, surface water and gas monitoring, coordinating samples, maintaining field records and upholding health, safety, security and environmental requirements on site.

Away from the field, you will contribute to the preparation of work plans, fieldwork specifications, HSSE documentation, desk studies and investigation reports. You will work closely with project managers, technical specialists, field teams, laboratories, subcontractors and wider multidisciplinary project teams, developing a broad understanding of how complex environmental projects come together from the ground up. A full clean UK driving licence and willingness to travel to project sites, including extended periods on site where required, are essential for this role.

Your Impact

The data you collect, the samples you coordinate and the records you maintain will feed directly into technical assessments and reports that shape how contaminated and complex sites are understood and managed. That is work with real consequences for the environments and communities around those sites, and your contribution at the field stage makes all the difference to the quality of what follows.

This is also a role with strong career growth potential. The breadth of project experience you will gain across contaminated land, hydrogeology and ground investigation will give you a platform to develop in whichever technical direction suits you best.

About You

You hold a BSc Hons or equivalent in Geoscience, Geology, Environmental Science, Environmental Geoscience, Earth Sciences or a related discipline. You bring a practical understanding of ground investigation, environmental monitoring and site-based data collection, and you are comfortable supporting the supervision of ground investigation works and coordinating site activities safely and efficiently.

You have experience in or a strong interest in groundwater, surface water and ground gas monitoring. You are thorough in managing sample handling, labelling, chain of custody documentation and laboratory coordination, and you prepare clear, accurate field records and factual reporting inputs as a matter of course.

You are well-organised, collaborative and HSSE-aware, with the kind of practical, grounded approach that makes fieldwork run smoothly and projects stay on track.

Why Join Us

We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies in 2025. Named 'Best Place to Work' and 'International Consulting Firm of the Year' at the NCE Awards 2024.
We do what is right: Industry-leading training and development, as well as paid professional subscriptions. A professional progression plan to support you in becoming chartered.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment and Early Careers peer group, and a wider ERG network (see more on our ERGs here: Stantec Employee Resource Groups)
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the UK - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, bonus schemes, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard, as well as discounted gym membership and lots more.
Hybrid/Flexible working: Enjoy a healthy work-life balance with our hybrid approach to flexible work.

#UKEnergy

About Stantec

The Stantec community unites more than 34,000 employees working in over 450 locations across 6 continents. We have been working with our clients and communities in the UK for over 150 years. We plan, design, deliver and manage the development and infrastructure needed to support the creation of sustainable, healthy and prosperous communities.

Our teams provide effective and relevant solutions, translating our clients’ vision into valued consents, deliverable plans for projects and programmes, and efficient designs for delivery, based on technical excellence and deep market insights. We deal with today’s challenges, but also keep a fairer, better tomorrow in sight, looking at how we deliver clean growth, support radical changes in our economy and meet the needs of future communities.

GENERAL PURPOSE

Performs a variety of **working level professional and technical duties** as needed to monitor wildlife populations, plan, organize, direct, and coordinate the planning for preservation of wildlife, obtain and preserve a wildlife migration corridor, and review development plans for impacts to/from steep slopes, natural washes, and other environmental impacts.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED

Works under direct supervision of the Community Development Director.

SUPERVISION EXERCISED

None.

Essential Functions

Conducts field inspections related to development projects' effects on wildlife habitat and the natural environment and ensure compliance with environmental laws and City approvals. Inform manager, administration, and City decision makers of field inspection findings.

Proposes and/or draft zoning codes designed to balance development rights with wildlife habitat protection. Participates in and perform studies related to land use policy development.

Performs wildlife and open space preservation planning, and coordinate with other planners and other departments during various long-range planning efforts to appropriately plan for open space preservation, wildlife preservation, and accommodates wildlife crossings (bridges, tunnels, at-grade). Assists City grants coordinator to provide information and obtain partnerships for various grants related to open space and wildlife.

Recommends wildlife and riparian protection area locations. Uses GIS to depict appropriate open space and wildlife areas.

Communicates effectively in writing and verbally with the public, with industry professionals, with colleagues, and with City decision makers (Planning Commission, Mayor, and City Council).

Develops relationships with regional partners (Camp Williams, Mule Deer Foundation, State Department of Natural Resources and the Division of Wildlife Resources, UDOT, SITLA, and the local Eagle Mountain Nature and Wildlife Alliance. Coordinates meetings, educates, and meets with these partners on a regular basis.

Coordinates with the local high school(s) to teach about wildlife and open space preservation.

Reviews various planning and development applications for impacts to/from steep slopes, natural washes, wildlife habitat, the wildlife corridor overlay zone, wildfire protection, flood protection, etc. Coordinates with City Attorney, landowners, and conservation groups to draft and complete conservation easements and public use easements.

Performs field work to enhance and maintain the wildlife migration corridor, such as erection of fencing, noxious weed control, trail and access management, revegetation seeding, etc.

Assists in the preparation, solicitation, review and administration of contracts for various services funded by the City related to open space, wildlife, etc.

Attends and participates in professional functions, meetings and classes; researches and stays abreast of Federal, State and local

laws, legislation, codes, regulations, environmental matters, wildlife, and zoning and land-use issues; Researches best practices and planning strategies.

Performs related duties as required.

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience:
Graduation from college with a bachelor's degree in wildlife studies, wildlife biology, conservation, environmental science, or a closely related field;

AND

At least four (4) years of progressively responsible experience in, and exposure to, environmental planning, site planning, development application review, land development codes, report preparation, and public speaking;

OR

An equivalent combination of education and experience.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
Considerable knowledge of** mule deer and their migration patterns, habitat, food sources (vegetation), and behavioral patterns; various birds native to the Eagle Mountain area and their esting and migration patterns, habitat, food sources, and behavioral patterns; the Federal Bird Treaty Migration Act; principles and practices of urban and rural planning and design, local government operation and structures; map reading; principles of public relations; personal computers and applications; experience using GIS to collect, maintain, manage, and analyze wildlife, habitat, natural-resource, or other spatial data.; current and long range planning and site plan compliance; site development, zoning ordinances, environmental protection; the relationship between land-use planning, environmental stewardship, wildlife and habitat conservation, and related ecological, economic, political, sociological, legal, and physical considerations; research and statistical methods typically used in the analysis and the evaluation of research data; land use, zoning, federal, state, and local laws.

The Department of Public and Environmental Wellness in the School of Health Sciences at Oakland University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor in Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ). The successful candidate will join a dynamic and multidisciplinary department committed to excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement.

We seek a candidate who will initiate and maintain a successful program of research, scholarship, and service. The ideal candidate will contribute to both undergraduate and graduate instruction in Environmental Health and Safety, support the department’s mission, and actively engage in curriculum development and program growth.

Responsibilities Include

Developing and sustaining an active scholarship agenda in Environmental Health and Safety or a related field
Teaching undergraduate and/or graduate courses in EHS and related topics
Engaging in service to the department, college, university, and professional communities
Advising and mentoring students
Contributing to program development, improvement, and accreditation activities
Participating in community engagement initiatives and, where appropriate, program leadership

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

A doctoral degree (PhD, DrPH, or equivalent) in Environmental Health, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Public Health, or a closely related field by the time of appointment
Evidence of teaching effectiveness and scholarly activity appropriate to rank

Preferred Qualifications

Attainment of the Certified Safety Professional ( CSP ) credential or other relevant professional designations (e.g., Certified Industrial Hygienist [ CIH ], Certified Hazardous Materials Manager [ CHMM ])
Experience with ABET accreditation processes and standards
Interest and experience in continuous program improvement, curriculum innovation, and academic leadership
Evidence of successful community engagement or interdisciplinary academic collaboration
Leadership roles or active participation in professional organizations related to Environmental Health and Safety (e.g., American Society of Safety Professionals [ ASSP ], National Safety Council [ NSC ], etc.), with a demonstrated commitment to advancing the field through these organizations

Special Instructions to Applicants

Applications must include a CV, cover letter, unofficial transcripts, names and contact information of 3 professional references, a teaching statement, and a research statement.

Contact information for references will be requested in the Professional References section of the application and a link provided through which references can submit letters.

School/College & Department/Program Summary

The Environmental Health and Safety faculty offer: a Bachelor of Science (BS), Master of Science (MS), a dual BS/MS program, and four graduate certificate programs within the Department of Public and Environmental Wellness ( PEW ). Guided by the mission of “Pursuing society’s big health challenges,” the department is dedicated to transforming students into leaders, connecting theory to best practices, and addressing the health needs of diverse communities.

Our EHS program focuses on translating knowledge and theory into best practices for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating hazards that pose risks to people, property, and the environment. While our degree and certificate programs are fully available online, we also provide access to well-equipped physical laboratories that enhance hands-on learning and research.

Faculty in the EHS program bring expertise in areas including:

Environmental standards and controls
Industrial hygiene
Industrial and robotics safety
Electrical systems safety
Construction safety
Safety systems management
Fire safety
Biomechanics and ergonomics
EHS program leadership and development

All within the broader context of public health and wellness.

More About Oakland University

The University is located on 1,443 acres of scenic land in the cities of Rochester Hills and Auburn Hills in Oakland County, Michigan. The University offers 142 bachelor’s degree programs and 138 graduate degree and certificate programs. Academics include programs in the College of Arts and Sciences, School of Business Administration, School of Education and Human Services, School of Engineering and Computer Science, School of Health Sciences, School of Medicine and School of Nursing. As an anchor institution in southeastern Michigan that is dedicated to building ongoing, collaborative relationships, Oakland University embraces community and civic engagement to enhance the lives of its students and positively impact the broader community. jobs.description:
