Community Infrastructure
Location:
Remote- USA

Description

Waggoner Engineering, Inc. is seeking an Environmental Services Market Sector Leader
to join our team. The Environmental Services Market Sector Leader is a senior strategic-operations leader responsible for growing the firm in the environmental services market sector across all business units - growing talent, building high-performing teams, expanding the client base, and increasing profitable revenue and backlog in the water market. The role will elevate Waggoner’s brand and thought leadership, lead major client pursuits, and ensure excellent, consistent project delivery. Because the role has limited to no direct reports, success depends on leading through leadership influence - aligning Business Unit Leaders, Area Managers, Discipline Leaders, and Client/Project Teams around clear market priorities, development pathways, and quality outcomes for clients.

Sector Summary

Responsible for the strategy, growth, and delivery excellence of Waggoner’s Environmental Services Market across all Business Units, serving public- and private-sector clients with environmental planning, permitting, compliance, site investigation, remediation, natural resource services, and related sustainability/resilience needs. The leader serves as the primary market-facing champion for environmental services, helping clients navigate regulatory complexity, reduce risk, advance development and infrastructure programs, restore or redevelop impacted sites, and strengthen environmental stewardship and community outcomes. This framing aligns with how major engineering and environmental consultancies currently position environmental services: a multidisciplinary platform spanning permitting, remediation, compliance, natural resources, and climate/sustainability solutions.

Market Sector Scope
Primary clients: Federal, state, and local government agencies; transportation and utility agencies; port, aviation, and energy entities; industrial and commercial owners/operators; developers; and institutional clients with environmental permitting, compliance, remediation, restoration, or redevelopment needs.
Primary services: Environmental planning and permitting; NEPA/environmental documentation and agency coordination; environmental compliance and EHS support; site assessment and due diligence; contaminated site investigation and remediation; brownfields/restoration/redevelopment support; PFAS and other emerging-contaminant services; air quality and waste/resource management; natural and cultural resources support; sustainability, resilience, and climate-related environmental advisory services. These service areas closely reflect current market positioning across leading firms in the sector.
Boundary (clarity of leadership): The Environmental Services Market Sector Leader leads environmental work where environmental risk management, permitting, compliance, remediation, restoration, or environmental approvals are the primary driver of the client need or project scope. Environmental work that is integral to industrial facilities and operations - including plant-specific permitting/compliance or environmental services embedded within industrial capital programs - is led in coordination with the Industrial Market Sector Leader.
Environmental work embedded within public water, wastewater, stormwater, or watershed utility programs is coordinated with the Water Market Sector Leader.
Environmental services supporting transportation approvals, corridor studies, or transportation program delivery are coordinated with the Transportation Market Sector Leader.
In all overlap situations, the Environmental Services Market Sector Leader works with the applicable Market Sector Leader and Business Unit leadership to define clear lead/support roles for client management, pursuit leadership, and delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Market Strategy, Growth, and Thought Leadership
Develop and execute a multi-year market strategy and annual plan (targets, priority clients, services, staffing, investments).
Serve as a visible thought leader: publish, present, and represent Waggoner in industry forums to increase sector brand and market credibility.
Lead or oversee major pursuits, capture plans, teaming strategies, and client messaging; partner with marketing and business development on campaigns and collateral.

Client Development and Winning Work
Develop and maintain trusted advisor relationships with priority clients; lead account planning in coordination with Business Unit Leaders and Area Managers.
Lead capture planning and pursuit strategy for major programs, including go/no-go, teaming, pricing strategy inputs, and interview preparation.
Identify emerging client needs, regulatory/funding drivers, and competitive positioning; evolve service offerings accordingly.
Expand Waggoner's role with clients by connecting environmental services to broader infrastructure, industrial, redevelopment, resilience, and community objectives.

Delivery Excellence, Standards, Quality, and Risk
Ensure project delivery aligns with market strategy, client expectations, technical standards, and risk posture.
Partner with Business Unit Leaders and Area Managers to forecast workload and coordinate resources to meet commitments.
Promote consistent delivery methodologies, lessons learned, and knowledge-sharing across offices and disciplines.
Champion consistent project delivery standards and quality systems across the sector, including use of standard agreements and templates where client requirements allow (e.g., EJCDC-based agreements and front-end documents).
Support the development and use of firmwide templates and standards (e.g., supplemental conditions, spec/plan covers, standard details, report templates).
Lead or participate in QA/QC and risk reviews on key pursuits and high-risk projects; promote ‘do it right the first time’ delivery.
Advance safety in design practices, risk management, and a consistent project closeout process.
Contribute to proposal reviews and continuous improvement of win themes, deliverables, and client communications (including letter proposals where appropriate).

People Leadership and Talent Development (Matrix Organization)
Lead through influence in a matrix environment; align Business Unit Leaders, Area Managers, Discipline Leaders, and project teams to sector priorities.
Establish clear target markets, clients, and services; translate strategy into actionable plans, account plans, and pursuit roadmaps.
Coach, mentor, and develop staff across business units through project engagement, QA/QC reviews, and pursuit leadership—regardless of reporting lines.
Build and sustain high-performing teams by mentoring, recruiting, and aligning talent to the best and highest use in service of clients.
Develop communities of practice and technical development opportunities; encourage cross-office collaboration and staff visibility to sector work.
Support succession planning and development of future leaders.

Financial and Performance Management
Own sector performance and accountability (revenue, backlog, win rate, profitability, utilization, client satisfaction) in partnership with Business Unit Leaders and finance/operations.
Maintain a pipeline and forecast; communicate risks and opportunities to Strategic Operations leadership.
Help prioritize investment in capabilities, hires, teaming relationships, and target clients that strengthen long-term market position.

Cross-Sector Collaboration
Coordinate with other Market Sector Leaders when markets, clients, or services overlap; define clear lead/support roles for pursuits and client management.
Develop integrated solutions and cross-sector teams to deliver greater client value and expand relationships.
Use regular cross-sector planning, shared CRM/account plans, and joint pursuit reviews to prevent duplication and ensure a One Firm client experience.
Escalate and resolve priority or resourcing conflicts through the EVP of Strategic Operations as needed.

Measures of Success
Growth: achievement of annual net service revenue targets, healthy pipeline, improved win rate, and diversified client portfolio.
Brand: increased visibility through speaking, publishing, associations, and client references aligned to the sector strategy.
Delivery: strong client satisfaction, consistent QA/QC outcomes, reduced rework/risk events, and successful closeout on key projects.
People: improved engagement and retention, effective mentoring, and a developing bench of sector leaders and technical experts.
One Firm: effective collaboration across market sectors and business units with clear lead/support roles and integrated wins.

What you'll need

Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Civil, Environmental, or Chemical Engineering. Geology, Environmental Science or related field (Master’s preferred).
Registered Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG), or other relevant environmental professional credential preferred; equivalent environmental consulting leadership experience required.
Typically, 15+ years of progressive water experience, including 7+ years of client leadership and demonstrated pursuit leadership.

Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated success growing environmental client portfolios and leading multidisciplinary delivery teams across multiple service lines.
Experience leading complex environmental programs involving site investigation/remediation, permitting, due diligence, natural resources, PFAS/emerging contaminants, restoration, or redevelopment.
Experience integrating environmental services with water, transportation, industrial, energy, or community development programs. These are all service intersections commonly emphasized by major firms in the sector.

Core Competencies
Strategic thinking and market insight
Client relationship leadership and executive presence
Pursuit leadership and persuasive communication
Technical leadership and commitment to quality
Ability to influence without direct authority; collaborative leadership
Financial acumen and performance accountability
People development, mentoring, and team building
Risk management and regulatory awareness

Travel and Work Environment
Primarily office-based in any WEI location with flexibility; travel to client sites, Waggoner offices, and industry events as required.
Occasional evening and weekend work may be needed during pursuits or critical project milestones.

Why Join Our Team

About Waggoner

Waggoner is a multidisciplinary infrastructure and advisory firm focused on transforming communities and advancing the systems that support them. Our team brings together engineering, science, business, environmental expertise, digital innovation, program delivery, and strategic insight to solve complex challenges facing communities, industries, and governments.

We believe infrastructure is more than projects - it is the foundation of resilient communities, economic opportunity, and a stronger future. By integrating technical excellence with environmental stewardship, data-driven insights, and collaboration problem solving, Waggoner helps our clients realize what's possible and delivers solutions that create lasting impact for the people and places we serve.

Our culture is built on integrity, accountability, collaboration, and excellence. We empower talented professionals to lead, innovate, and work across disciplines to deliver meaningful outcomes for our clients and communities.

Our Vision

To be the trusted partner organizations turn to for integrated solutions that strengthen communities, advance infrastructure, and solve complex challenges.

Our Mission

Transforming communities. To improve the quality of life for our clients, communities, and employees by delivering innovative, resilient, and sustainable solutions that make a lasting difference.

We know work isn't only about what you do, it's also about who you work for and with! Waggo

jobs.title: Associate Director - Environmental Planning
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

We are looking for an experienced Associate Director - Environmental Planning
to join our growing team in London or Reading.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering environmental planning and assessment services across a diverse portfolio of energy transition, water resilience, development and critical infrastructure projects. You’ll work at the intersection of planning, environmental assessment and sustainable development, helping clients understand and navigate environmental considerations throughout the project lifecycle.

You’ll work alongside planners, environmental specialists, engineers and other technical experts, contributing to multidisciplinary projects and developing practical, sustainable solutions for our clients.

As an Associate Director
, you’ll have the opportunity to take ownership of project workstreams, build strong client relationships, contribute to business development and support the development of colleagues within the team.

About The Role

As an Associate Director, you will:

Lead and contribute to environmental planning and assessment projects across a range of development and infrastructure sectors.
Provide environmental planning and consenting advice to clients and multidisciplinary project teams.
Support and coordinate the preparation of Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA), Environmental Statements and associated environmental planning documentation.
Manage individual project workstreams, coordinating inputs from technical specialists and ensuring deliverables are completed to a high standard.
Provide advice on environmental constraints, opportunities and consenting requirements from project inception through to delivery.
Coordinate and contribute to stakeholder engagement, consultation exercises, workshops and project meetings.
Liaise with clients, local authorities, statutory consultees, regulators and other stakeholders.
Undertake environmental and planning research, including reviewing relevant legislation, policy and guidance.
Review technical information and reports, ensuring environmental considerations are appropriately reflected in project outputs.
Support project management, including programmes, budgets, resources and delivery against agreed timescales.
Build and maintain effective relationships with clients and contribute to the development of new opportunities.
Contribute to bids, tenders, proposals and business development activities.
Support and mentor junior colleagues, sharing technical knowledge and helping to develop the wider team.
Work collaboratively with colleagues across our wider planning, environmental and engineering teams to deliver integrated solutions.

Your Impact

You’ll play an important role in helping our clients deliver projects that are environmentally responsible, technically robust and capable of securing the necessary consents.

You’ll have the opportunity to work on a variety of complex projects across sectors including infrastructure, energy, development, transport and the built environment.

As an Associate Director, you’ll take increasing responsibility for project delivery and client relationships while developing your technical and commercial expertise. You’ll also have the opportunity to contribute to the continued growth of our environmental planning capability across the UK.

Working within a multidisciplinary organisation, you’ll have access to specialists across a wide range of environmental and engineering disciplines, enabling you to develop solutions that consider the wider environmental, social and technical context of each project.

About You

We’re looking for an experienced environmental planning professional who is confident working within a consultancy environment and is ready to take the next step in their career.

You Have

Experience in environmental planning, environmental consultancy, planning or a closely related discipline.
Good knowledge of the UK planning and environmental assessment framework.
Experience delivering or coordinating EIA and environmental consenting projects.
Experience managing project workstreams and coordinating multidisciplinary technical inputs.
A good understanding of environmental legislation, planning policy and relevant guidance.
Experience engaging with clients, stakeholders, local authorities, statutory consultees or regulators.
Good project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex environmental matters clearly and effectively.
An interest in developing client relationships and contributing to business development.
A collaborative approach and an enthusiasm for supporting and developing less experienced colleagues.

Qualifications

A relevant degree in environmental planning, environmental science, geography, planning or a related discipline is desirable.
Membership of a relevant professional body, such as the Royal Town Planning Institute (RTPI), or another relevant professional accreditation, would be advantageous.
Most importantly, we’re looking for someone who is collaborative, motivated and passionate about delivering high-quality environmental solutions that make a positive difference.

Why Join Us

We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. Named ‘Best Place to Work’ and ‘International Consulting Firm of the Year’ at the NCE Awards 2024.
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A p rofessional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered with ICE.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment and Early Careers peer group and wider ERG network (see more on our ERGs here: Stantec Employee Resource Groups )
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the UK & Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, bonus schemes, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard as well as discounted gym membership and lots more.
Flexible working: Enjoy a healthy work-life balance with our hybrid approach to flexible working.

#EnvironmentalPlanning

About Stantec

The Stantec community unites more than 34,000 employees working in over 450 locations across 6 continents. We have been working with our clients and communities in the UK for over 150 years. We plan, design, deliver and manage the development and infrastructure needed to support the creation of sustainable, healthy and prosperous communities.

Our teams provide effective and relevant solutions, translating our clients’ vision into valued consents, deliverable plans for projects and programmes, and efficient designs for delivery, based on technical excellence and deep market insights. We deal with today’s challenges, but also keep a fairer, better tomorrow in sight, looking at how we deliver clean growth, support radical changes in our economy and meet the needs of future communities.

Routinely visit company-wide locations to provide support to field associates

jobs.title: Regional Environmental Manager (REM), Environmental Assurance and Protection (EAP)
jobs.description:
Description

This Regional Environmental Manager (REM) is responsible for owning the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across Southern California Amazon Last Mile Delivery Stations.

The REM shapes and evolves the regional environmental compliance strategy by identifying emerging risks, analyzing systemic defect patterns, and designing programmatic solutions that close compliance gaps at scale. The REM translates senior leadership vision into executable program frameworks, defines success criteria, and owns the roadmap for implementation across the region.

The REM works with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, designers, construction, operations, and other key stakeholders. This REM will own environmental compliance across up to 15+ Amazon Delivery Stations in the region, with oversight of Multi-Site Environmental Managers (MSEMs) and Environmental Specialists.

This is a hands-on leadership position that includes time in the yard and on the floor of busy delivery stations conducting inspections and audits, mentoring MSEMs, ensuring program quality, leading regulatory interactions, and driving accountability across multiple departments and all levels of employees throughout the operation.

Key job responsibilities

Own the lifecycle of complex environmental compliance programs across the region — from strategy through execution and continuous improvement.
Shape regional environmental compliance strategy by identifying emerging risks, analyzing systemic defect patterns, and proposing scalable programmatic solutions before they require escalation.
Design and sustain program controllership mechanisms (business reviews, metric dashboards, escalation triggers) that operate independently without requiring manager intervention.
Independently proxy for the Sr Mgr in weekly and monthly forums (WBRs, MBRs) with full ownership of environmental sections — able to answer, defend, and commit.
Force multiply by designing scalable systems, processes, and training that enable MSEMs and operational stakeholders to execute at higher quality with less intervention over time.
Mentor MSEMs and Environmental Specialists; set the quality bar for root cause analysis and corrective action.
Lead COE/A3 investigations independently to closure with leadership, ensuring root causes explain systemic "why" rather than describing "what."
Own procedures and change management for the region, driving adoption end-to-end.
Lead regulatory agency interactions — including inspections, enforcement responses, and agency negotiations — and drive follow-up requirements to closure.
Manage and oversee local, state, and federal environmental regulations and Amazon policy.
Develop strategic programs by integrating with engineering, construction, and operations. Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization.
Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards. Provide comprehensive oversight to 3P environmental vendors and consultants.
Drive environmental metrics — build tools and dashboards that give stakeholders the information they need to make good decisions at scale.
Assess emerging regulations and proactively design mitigation plans before regulatory deadlines create urgency.
Own or coordinate construction and launch activities for new sites within the region to ensure environmental compliance at or before operational readiness.
Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company.
Navigate ambiguity effectively — find paths forward where solutions are not pre-defined and coordinate cross-functionally without deferring decisions upward.
Manage resource trade-offs and competing priorities across the region, escalating only when decisions genuinely exceed authority.
Submit time-critical reports to various governmental agencies.
Up to 50% travel.

A day in the life

Own regional execution of environmental procedures and ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, regional, and local regulations.
Design and implement scalable compliance mechanisms across the region — covering air emissions, surface water, wastewater, waste, and other environmental media.
Manage and prepare site-specific and regional environmental reporting to regulators and within Amazon.
Analyze systemic defect patterns and environmental metrics; review weekly and monthly trends to determine where programmatic improvements are needed.
Drive corrective action where targets are not met — negotiate resources and priorities across organizations to ensure programs are delivered on time and at the required quality standard.
Lead root cause analyses for environmental incidents; ensure corrective actions prevent recurrence at a systemic level, not just site-level fixes.
Conduct and oversee environmental audits and inspections for continuous improvement; set the quality bar for inspection rigor.
Monitor and provide strategic guidance on multi-site performance against applicable environmental regulations, programs, and Amazon global standards.
Design and sustain business review cadences and escalation triggers that surface risk in real time.

About The Team

The mission of the Environmental Assurance and Protection organization (EAP) is to transform environmental regulatory compliance into a zero-defect process through simple, scalable, and sustainable solutions.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project Management experience
8+ years of compliance, audit or risk management experience
Knowledge of Microsoft Office products and applications at an advanced level
- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, or related field of study
- Experience working with and managing third party consultants and vendors

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification
Experience leveraging technology and implementing lean principles / Six Sigma methodologies to drive process improvements or equivalent
Master's degree or equivalent
Experience communicating across technical and non-technical audiences, including executive level stakeholders or clients
Experience in project management, delivery and/or program management

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

jobs.description:
Need help with applying? Visit our Talent Acquisition page here for application guidance and resources.

VISION

El Paso County will be a trusted regional leader known for excellence in county service delivery.

PURPOSE

We provide essential public services to the Pikes Peak Region in support of our residents, businesses, and communities, enhancing the freedom for all to thrive.

VALUES

Service Focused

Collaborative
Accountable
Trustworthy
Transparent

Job Summary

Associate Geospatial Analyst / Geospatial Analyst / Senior Geospatial Analyst

Map Data. Drive Decisions. Shape the Future.

Are you someone who sees the world in layers—of data, design, and discovery? Do you enjoy transforming information into robust planning, infrastructure, and public service tools? El Paso County is seeking a talented Geospatial Professional to join our Department of Public Works team and help build smarter, more connected communities through innovative GIS and asset management.

This is a career progression opportunity, with openings at the Associate, Analyst, and Senior Analyst levels.
Whether you're just starting your geospatial journey or are a seasoned GIS pro, there’s a place for you here to grow and make an impact.

What You’ll Do

As part of the Geospatial Analyst team, you’ll be key in maintaining and analyzing asset data for transportation systems, public infrastructure, and County resources. You’ll support everything from road maintenance planning and crash data analysis to field data collection and custom map development.
Your work will support day-to-day operations, long-term infrastructure planning, and innovative solutions that make our county run more efficiently. From scripting and database development to GIS app creation and stakeholder collaboration, your expertise will help power decisions that matter.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You have strong technical skills in GIS, asset management systems, and data analysis.
You’re fluent in tools like ArcGIS, SQL, Python, ModelBuilder, and GIS dashboards.
You can turn raw spatial data into actionable insights, maps, and visuals.
You’re a collaborative problem-solver who enjoys working with cross-functional teams.
You have a passion for public service and building tools that improve communities.
You're adaptable, self-motivated, and thrive in a fast-paced, detail-driven environment.

Why Join El Paso County?

Your Work Has Meaning – Help plan and maintain the infrastructure that residents rely on every day.
Room to Grow – Our career progression path means your role grows as your skills do.
Use the Latest Tools – Get hands-on experience with cutting-edge GIS, programming, and asset management systems.
Collaborate Across Departments – Work closely with engineers, planners, field staff, and local agencies.
Be Part of a Mission-Driven Team – We’re passionate about service, innovation, and supporting each other.

We want to hear from you if you’re ready to map your career forward and contribute to impactful projects that shape El Paso County’s future.

Apply today to be part of a geospatial team where your skills and ideas truly make a difference!

Assists in the management and maintenance of various Geographical Information System (GIS) related asset datasets stored in a variety of enterprise-level asset databases. Participates in the development of strategic and tactical plans and programs in maximizing El Paso County’s transportation infrastructure. Conducts data analysis and provides various deliverables such as reports, maps, and other related documents. This position is part of the Geospatial Analyst career progression series, which includes Associate Geospatial Analyst, Geospatial Analyst, and Senior Geospatial Analyst. An employee is eligible to advance to the next position within the series when the employee has met the criteria for advancement as notated within the job description and has received a recommendation from the Hiring Authority. Employment is subject to the terms, conditions, and policies detailed in the Personnel Policies Manual (PPM). This position requires regular in-person presence as an essential job function.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities

Assists in maintaining Department of Public Works (DPW) asset data dictionary standards.
Creates, maintains, and modifies asset data inventories in various enterprise-level and siloed asset management systems (AMS).
Prepares geospatial datasets through digitization, data conversion, and manual data entry of electronic and paper-based records into GIS.
Conducts continuous refinement and quality control of Asset Management data; generates reports and conducts data analysis as needed to arrive at results.
Utilizes geospatial analysis techniques to provide a better understanding of certain variables in given geographic locations.
Provides digital and hard copy maps, tabular datasets, reports, graphics, and other asset data products in support of daily operations, planning, engineering, and maintenance operations,
Creates GIS asset data from coordinate geometry (COGO) legal descriptions.
Organizes, documents, and provides backup material for a variety of design projects and engineering studies.
Researches County documents and plans across various County databases and archives.
Provides review and interpretation of subdivision plats and land surveys for County assets.
Prepares DPW asset acceptance submittals for public infrastructure.
Provides research for public right-of-way in support of daily operations and customer service.
Prepares, coordinates, and manages County road name change petitions to the BOCC.
Interacts with County staff to develop custom map project requirements.
Facilitates the implementation efforts for transportation GIS and asset management applications.
Independently evaluates, develops, and programs GIS applications to automate and convert data using approved software and protocols.
Gathers geographic data through field observations, maps, photographs, satellite imagery, censuses, and other sources; analyzes the geographic distribution of physical and cultural characteristics and occurrences.
Maintains and analyzes crash data as required.
Reviews, evaluates, and verifies GIS data provided by other government agencies or private sector contractors for accuracy.
Develops graphical models and provides data of analysis results for committees and the public.
Coordinates with governmental agencies for data collection and transfer.
Assists DPW employees in the use of GIS applications.
Performs other duties as required.

Position Title

Onsite Resource Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist / Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill)

Job Description

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality strives to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable environment that embraces and values diversity. Employees at all levels of the agency work together to foster fairness, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We strive to be a workplace where we share our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals, and while collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations. We celebrate and appreciate diversity, champion equity, and treat each other with respect and dignity.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status , gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, age, or physical or mental disability in the administration of our programs and activities. Visit DEQ’s Civil Rights and Environmental Justice page .

Are you passionate about preserving, enhancing, and protecting Oregon’s environment?
If so, please consider a career with the State of Oregon at the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ). At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full-time opportunity available for an Onsite Resource Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist / Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Underfill)
in Medford, Oregon.

Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

About DEQ!

The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources.

The Water Quality Division’s mission is to protect and improve Oregon's water quality. Protecting Oregon's rivers, lakes, streams, and groundwater quality keeps these waters safe for a multitude of beneficial uses such as drinking water, fish habitat, recreation, and irrigation. This is accomplished by developing and implementing water quality standards and clean water plans; regulating sewage treatment systems, industrial dischargers, and individual onsite septic systems; collecting and evaluating water quality data; providing grants and technical assistance to reduce non-point pollution sources; and providing loans to communities to build treatment facilities.

Over 30% of Oregonians dispose of wastewater from their homes and businesses through the use of septic systems. The siting, design, installation, and ongoing operation and maintenance of septic systems, as well as sewage disposal service licensing, are regulated through the Onsite Wastewater Management Program. Without this oversight, septic systems can fail or malfunction and sewage may be disposed of improperly, thus polluting Oregon’s land and waterways with raw sewage and creating public health hazards.

The Onsite Wastewater Management Program (septic systems) is administered through intergovernmental agreements for 33 counties and is directly administered by DEQ in 3 counties. This position will support Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties.

For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

What you will do!

You will serve as an Onsite Wastewater Management Program technical expert in the evaluation, inspection, and permitting of onsite septic systems in Jackson, Josephine, and Curry Counties. Hundreds of onsite applications are submitted to the Medford office each year from individual homeowners, small businesses, and licensed installers. In addition to these applications, the Medford office receives technical questions from the public regarding the program’s requirements and the care and maintenance of septic systems. The office also receives complaints regarding potential septic system violations, some of which can lead to enforcement actions. In addition, local interested parties occasionally request the assistance of the local onsite technical expert to attend meetings and present information.

What’s in it for you!

The opportunity to work in a productive and creative environment where no two days are ever the same! DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. We offer a competitive benefits package that offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for the employee and their qualified family members, as well as paid sick leave, vacation leave, personal leave, and 11 paid holidays a year. In addition, we offer membership in the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), and you have the opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). If you are passionate about Oregon's environment, apply today!

This is a full-time, AFSCME represented position.

This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.

What are we looking for?

Minimum Qualifications for Natural Resource Specialist 3 – Environmental Health Specialist:

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field
At least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities

6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field

Continued employment in this position will be contingent upon the successful applicant maintaining the required registration. Demonstrated understanding of environmental justice and the historical impacts for marginalized and underrepresented communities; ability to take personal responsibility for increasing their knowledge of environmental justice and diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.

Experience investigating environmental complaints.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to provide clear, concise, and compelling communication of policy and technical information tailored to the needs of diverse audiences; skill in writing and presenting clear and concise reports that include qualitative and quantitative analyses, recommendations, and conclusions to diverse audiences.
Demonstrated experience building and fostering relationships with a diverse group of partners including colleagues, interested parties, communities, organizations, and businesses.

Working Conditions

DEQ believes in a diverse and inclusive work environment. All employees are expected to contribute to a work environment that collectively values and benefits from respecting its diversity and promotes a culture of inclusiveness.

DEQ will provide necessary hardware (laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and cell phone) for an employee to successfully work from home. At DEQ sites, you will have access to a workspace, however, it may be shared with other employees.

This position requires frequent travel by car statewide for meetings, trainings, public hearings, conferences, workshops, seminars, and field visits (such as wastewater treatment facilities, land application sites, and spill or complaint sites). During field visits, there is the potential for exposure to pollutants, pathogens or hazardous materials, chemicals, contaminated soil and water, fumes, airborne contaminants, challenging field conditions (steep slopes, heavy vegetation, and uneven terrain), and inclement weather. Evening and weekend work, as well as overnight stays, will occur.

Because this work requires the incumbent to operate a motor vehicle, personal or state-owned, the incumbent must have a valid driver’s license and complete the defensive driving safety class every two (2) years.

jobs.title: Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW)
jobs.description:
United Infrastructure is a dynamic and rapidly expanding business, focused on delivering critical infrastructure projects, across the utility and social infrastructure sectors.

Our team of highly skilled and hardworking specialists deliver innovative solutions to the complex challenges our clients face.

Our company is split into two business areas:

Utility Infrastructure
–

Our team of Utility Infrastructure specialists design, build and maintain critical water, energy (gas), power and telecoms infrastructure, for the UK’s largest network owners and operators.

Social Infrastructure
-

Our team of Social Infrastructure specialists revitalise homes and communities by carrying out a wide range of work, from retrofit to refurbishment, and maintenance.

Equal Opportunities Statement - At United Infrastructure, we are committed to making every interaction a positive and inclusive experience. If there is anything we can do to support you, remove barriers, or make the process more accessible, please let us know — we want this to be the best possible experience for you.

Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) – Scotland

Reporting To:
SHEQ Manager

Location:
Scotland – project based with regular travel to live construction sites

Function:
SHEQ / Environment

Role Purpose

The Ecologist / Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) will provide specialist ecological advice, assurance and site-based support across major infrastructure and construction projects throughout Scotland.

Reporting to the SHEQ Manager, the role will ensure construction activities are undertaken in accordance with Scottish environmental legislation, planning requirements, protected species licences, client requirements and project environmental commitments.

The role will have a strong field-based component, working alongside project management, construction and environmental teams to identify ecological constraints, develop practical mitigation and provide ECoW supervision of activities in environmentally sensitive locations.

The position will be particularly important on linear power infrastructure projects where construction activities may interact with protected species, designated sites, peatland, watercourses, forestry and sensitive habitats.

Key Responsibilities

Ecological Clerk of Works

Act as ECoW for construction activities requiring ecological supervision.
Undertake pre-construction ecological checks and surveys.
Provide watching briefs during sensitive construction activities.
Monitor compliance with ecological mitigation requirements.
Identify emerging ecological risks and advise project teams on appropriate controls.
Establish and monitor ecological exclusion zones and buffers.
Stop, pause or escalate activities where there is an immediate risk of ecological harm or legal non-compliance.
Maintain accurate records of ecological inspections, observations and interventions.

Protected Species

Provide specialist advice and support relating to protected and notable species including, where relevant:

Otters.
Badgers.
Bats.
Red squirrels.
Pine martens.
Water voles.
Great crested newts.
Reptiles and amphibians.
Breeding birds.
Schedule 1 birds.
Raptors.
Freshwater pearl mussels.
Fish and aquatic ecology.
Invasive non-native species.
Other protected or priority species relevant to project locations.

Ensure works are undertaken in accordance with relevant licences and Species Protection Plans.

Surveys & Assessments

Undertake or coordinate Preliminary Ecological Appraisals.
Undertake habitat and protected species surveys within the individual's competence.
Support UKHab and other appropriate habitat classification and condition assessments.
Review ecological survey information provided by consultants.
Identify requirements for additional surveys or specialist ecological support.
Support ecological inputs into Environmental Impact Assessments and project environmental documentation.

Construction Support

Review RAMS and construction methodologies for ecological risks.
Provide ecological input into Construction Environmental Management Plans.
Develop and implement Species Protection Plans and ecological mitigation measures.
Undertake pre-start ecological briefings and toolbox talks.
Provide practical ecological advice to Site Managers, Engineers, Supervisors and subcontractors.
Attend planning and construction meetings where ecological constraints could affect delivery.

Sensitive Habitats & Peatland

Support the protection and management of sensitive Scottish habitats including:

Peatland and deep peat.
Blanket bog.
Wet heath.
Ancient woodland.
Native woodland.
Riparian habitats.
Freshwater environments.
Protected and designated sites.

Support implementation and monitoring of habitat and peatland restoration and reinstatement requirements.

Designated Sites

Provide ecological support for projects potentially affecting:

Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs).
Special Areas of Conservation (SACs).
Special Protection Areas (SPAs).
Ramsar sites.
National Nature Reserves.
Ancient Woodland.
Local Nature Conservation Sites.

Ensure project teams understand and implement controls associated with designated sites.

Biodiversity & Habitat Enhancement

Support delivery of project biodiversity objectives.
Identify opportunities for habitat enhancement and restoration.
Monitor habitat reinstatement following construction.
Support biodiversity monitoring programmes.
Assist with development and implementation of Biodiversity Enhancement Plans and client commitments.
Maintain evidence demonstrating delivery of ecological mitigation and enhancement measures.

Environmental Compliance

Provide ecological advice relating to applicable Scottish requirements including:

Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
Nature Conservation (Scotland) Act 2004.
Wildlife and Natural Environment (Scotland) Act 2011.
Conservation (Natural Habitats, &c.) Regulations 1994, as amended.
Protection of Badgers Act 1992.
Environmental Authorisation (Scotland) Regulations 2018, where relevant.
Applicable planning conditions, licences, consents and client requirements.

Maintain awareness of legislative changes and guidance affecting ecological management in Scotland.

Ecological Incidents

Respond to ecological incidents and unexpected discoveries.
Immediately advise project teams where protected species or previously unidentified ecological constraints are encountered.
Support environmental incident investigations.
Escalate significant issues to the SHEQ Manager and Environmental Manager.
Support liaison with statutory bodies where required.
Capture and communicate lessons learned.

Stakeholder Engagement

Develop effective relationships with clients, project teams, landowners, ecological consultants, local authorities and statutory bodies including NatureScot, SEPA and relevant planning authorities.

Represent the project at ecological and environmental meetings as required.

Reporting & Assurance

Produce ecological inspection and monitoring reports.
Maintain ecological constraints registers.
Maintain records of licences, mitigation and monitoring requirements.
Track ecological actions through to closure.
Provide ecological information for project SHEQ reports.
Support environmental audits and client assurance visits.
Maintain auditable evidence demonstrating compliance with ecological commitments.

Key Accountabilities

The role is accountable for:

Effective management of ecological risks across project activities.
Competent delivery of the ECoW function.
Compliance with protected species legislation and licences.
Protection of sensitive habitats and designated sites.
Implementation of Species Protection Plans.
Accurate and timely ecological records.
Effective escalation of significant ecological risks.
Supporting habitat restoration and biodiversity commitments.
Prevention of avoidable ecological harm.

Essential Qualifications

Degree or equivalent qualification in Ecology, Environmental Science, Conservation Biology or a related discipline.
Appropriate membership of CIEEM or equivalent professional body.
Strong working knowledge of Scottish ecological legislation and protected species requirements.
Full UK Driving Licence.

Desirable Qualifications

Associate or Full Membership of CIEEM.
Protected species licences relevant to Scottish infrastructure projects.
CSCS/ECS or equivalent construction site competence.
ECoW training or demonstrable equivalent experience.
UKHab training.
Peatland assessment/restoration experience.
Environmental auditing qualification.

Essential Experience

Practical ecological experience within construction, utilities, infrastructure or a similar sector.
Experience undertaking ecological surveys and site inspections.
Experience working as an ECoW or providing equivalent construction-phase ecological support.
Strong knowledge of protected species and habitat management.
Ability to interpret ecological reports, Species Protection Plans and licence conditions.
Experience communicating ecological requirements to construction teams.

Desirable Experience

Power Transmission & Distribution projects.
Overhead line, underground cable and substation construction.
Major infrastructure projects in the Scottish Highlands and remote environments.
SSEN Transmission or SP Energy Networks projects.
Experience working around peatland, forestry and watercourses.
Experience working within or adjacent to internationally and nationally designated sites.
Experience managing ecological interfaces across geographically dispersed construction work fronts.

Skills & Competencies

Strong field ecology capability.
Excellent understanding of Scottish protected species requirements.
Ability to translate ecological requirements into practical construction controls.
Strong communication and influencing skills.
Confidence to challenge or stop activities where ecological harm may occur.
Strong technical reporting and record keeping.
Ability to work independently in remote and challenging environments.
Collaborative and solutions-focused approach.

Values & Behaviours

The Ecologist / ECoW will demonstrate professional integrity, sound ecological judgement and visible environmental leadership. They will work collaboratively with project teams to enable successful infrastructure delivery while ensuring Scotland's habitats, species and natural environment are appropriately protected.

The role holder will be fully empowered and expected to challenge, pause or stop activities where there is a foreseeable risk of significant ecological harm, breach of licence conditions or environmental non-compliance

jobs.title: Research Scientist and Project Director - College of Engineering - Environmental and Public Policy
jobs.description:
Carnegie Mellon University is a private, global research university that stands among the world’s most renowned education institutions. With ground-breaking brain science, path-breaking performances, creative start-ups, big data, big ambitions, hands-on learning, and a whole lot of robots, CMU doesn’t imagine the future, we invent it. If you’re passionate about joining a community that challenges the curious to deliver work that matters, your journey starts here!

The Department of Engineering and Public Policy (EPP) is a unique department in the College of Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University which addresses important problems in technology and policy. We educate technically skilled students to be leaders in policy-focused research; we work on policy problems in which the technology matters.

Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) seeks a Research Scientist to serve as Project Director for Industrial Futures within the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation. The position will lead research and programmatic activities at the intersection of industrial transformation, energy and climate, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, and regional economic development. The Research Scientist will lead the Industrial Futures focus area within the Scott Institute, working with faculty, researchers, students, and external partners across Carnegie Mellon and a network of domestic and international collaborators. The position

combines applied and scholarly research with project leadership, external engagement, policy communication, and mentorship. The Research Scientist will report to the Associate Director of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.

A central objective of the Industrial Futures initiative is to understand how technological change and the energy transition reshaping industry, firms, workers, and regions are — and how policy, innovation, and entrepreneurship can contribute to competitive, resilient, and sustainable industrial transitions. The portfolio connects research and engagement in Southwestern Pennsylvania and the United States with international

research and partnerships addressing similar challenges around the world.

The Research Scientist will have substantial responsibility for two major components of this portfolio: CMU’s leadership of the INDABA Partnership, an international research collaboration focused on industrial transformation and decarbonization, and its links to CMU’s engagement in the Regional Technology and Infrastructure Consortium (RETI), which focuses on industrial innovation, hardtech entrepreneurship, and supporting policies. As Project Director, the Research Scientist will help shape the intellectual agenda of these initiatives while managing research programs, coordinating partners, developing new projects, and translating research findings for policy and practitioner audiences.

Core Responsibilities

Research Leadership:

Develop, lead, and contribute to applied research on industrial transformation, energy and industrial policy, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, workforce development, and regional economic change.
Help define and advance the research agenda for the Industrial Futures focus area and lead or co-lead projects from research design through analysis, publication, and dissemination.
Conduct rigorous quantitative and qualitative research using methods appropriate to the research question, including quantitative empirical analysis, operations research, econometrics, labor-market and regional economic analysis, qualitative and interview-based research, and techno-economic or energy-systems analysis.
Maintain and develop datasets, analytical tools, and methodological frameworks that support research across multiple projects.
Develop and contribute to peer-reviewed publications, policy reports, working papers, and other scholarly outputs.
Collaborate with researchers across Carnegie Mellon and partner institutions, connecting research on industrial transformation in Southwestern Pennsylvania and the United States with related international research and identifying opportunities for new interdisciplinary work.

Program And Project Leadership

Serve as Project Director for the Industrial Futures portfolio, providing intellectual and programmatic leadership across its research and engagement activities.
Coordinate complex, multi-institution research projects, including developing and reviewing deliverables, maintaining timelines, leading project meetings, monitoring progress, and addressing barriers to project success.
Serve as a primary point of contact for research partners, subcontractors, funding organizations, and other collaborators.
Support CMU’s leadership of the INDABA Partnership, including coordinating research across partner institutions, managing a collaborative seed-grant program, and leading knowledge-sharing activities such as newsletters, workshops, and study tours.
Coordinate project reporting and communications with research sponsors and contribute to new grant proposals, including research design, technical narratives, work plans, and partnership development.
Connect researchers across the Scott Institute and broader university who are working on related topics or methodologies and facilitate opportunities for collaboration.

External Engagement And Policy Impact

Build and maintain relationships with industry, government, nonprofit and community organizations, research institutions, funding partners, and other stakeholders.
Engage with firms, policymakers, entrepreneurs, workforce organizations, and regional stakeholders to understand the opportunities and challenges associated with industrial and technological transformation.
Represent Carnegie Mellon and the Scott Institute in external meetings, workshops, conferences, study tours, working groups, and other convenings.
Translate research into accessible and decision-relevant formats, including policy briefs, reports, presentations, data visualizations, and other communications for policymakers and practitioners.
Work with Scott Institute communications and policy staff to disseminate research findings and contribute to policy-informing activities such as briefings, testimony, public comments, and workshops.

Advising And Mentorship

Advise or co-advise student and researcher projects associated with the Industrial Futures portfolio.
Mentor students and junior researchers on research design, quantitative and qualitative methods, data analysis and visualization, and research writing.
Provide feedback on research products, manuscripts, presentations, and policy communications.
Contribute to a collaborative, intellectually engaged, productive, and supportive research culture within the Scott Institute and collaborating research groups.

Adaptability, excellence, and passion are vital qualities within Carnegie Mellon University. We are in search of a team member who can effectively interact with a varied population of internal and external partners at a high level of integrity. We are looking for someone who shares our values and who will support the mission of the university through their work

Qualifications

Ph.D. in engineering, public policy, economics, management, or a related field.
Approximately 3–5 years of relevant research or professional experience. Significant and directly relevant research, project leadership, or stakeholder- engagement experience obtained during doctoral training may count toward this requirement.
Demonstrated research experience in one or more of the following areas: energy, industrial transformation, technological innovation, entrepreneurship, workforce development, or regional economic development.
Demonstrated ability to design and conduct rigorous applied research using multiple quantitative and/or qualitative approaches. Relevant methods may include quantitative empirical research, operations research, econometrics, labor-market or regional economic analysis, qualitative and interview-based methods, and techno-economic or energy-systems analysis.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex datasets using R, Python, Stata, or comparable analytical software.
Experience developing scholarly research products, including peer-reviewed publications, working papers, or major research reports.
Strong project-management and organizational skills and the ability to coordinate activities and collaborators across complex projects.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical research to academic and nonacademic audiences.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across disciplines and institutions.
A combination of education and relevant experience from which comparable knowledge is demonstrated may be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

Research or professional experience related to industrial decarbonization, industrial or energy policy, hardtech innovation and entrepreneurship, or regional industrial transformation.
Experience working at the intersection of academic research and policy or practice and engaging directly with industry, government, community organizations, or other external stakeholders.
Experience managing multi-institutional or interdisciplinary research collaborations.
Experience developing research proposals or contributing to externally funded research programs.
Experience translating academic research into policy-relevant communications for nonacademic audiences.
Experience mentoring students or junior researchers.
Experience working in international research collaborations or comparative research settings.

Requirements

Successful background check

Position Characteristics

This position is designed for a researcher who enjoys moving between rigorous research and real-world engagement. The successful candidate will be comfortable leading research while also building partnerships, managing collaborative projects, mentoring students, communicating findings to policymakers and practitioners, and developing new research opportunities.

The role requires intellectual curiosity, independence, initiative, strong organizational skills, and a collaborative approach. Because the Industrial Futures portfolio connects local, national, and international research and engagement, the position may involve periodic domestic and international travel.

The Research Scientist will be based at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and will report to the Associate Director of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation.

Work arrangement:
In-person expected

Benefits eligible employees enjoy a wide array of benefits including comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision insurance as well as a generous retirement savings program with employer contributions. Unlock your potential with tuition benefits, take well-deserved breaks with ample paid time off and observed holidays, and rest easy with life and accidental death and disability insurance.

Additional perks include a free Pittsburgh Regional Transit bus pass, access to our Family Concierge Team to help navigate childcare needs, fitness center access, and much more!

For a comprehensive overview of the benefits available, explore our Benefits page.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding an Environmental Compliance Specialist
to our team based in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are  Leading with Science  to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For 60 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving  a lasting legacy .

Position Summary

We’re currently seeking an Environmental Compliance Specialist
to join our team based in Albuquerque, NM. This role offers the opportunity to lead environmental compliance for complex water resources and restoration projects across the Southwest and nationally. You will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, clients, and regulatory agencies while leading technical work, mentoring staff, and shaping innovative solutions.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are essential to this role. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

Prepare and coordinate National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) documentation and supporting environmental analyses.
Prepare Biological Assessments and related documentation to support Endangered Species Act (ESA) compliance.
Prepare and oversee environmental permits, including Clean Water Act (CWA) Sections 404 and 401.
Support stream and river restoration planning and related environmental evaluations.
Conduct desktop research and field surveys of vegetation, wildlife, and wildlife habitat.
Evaluate potential project impacts to natural resources and recommend compliance measures.
Perform wetland delineations in accordance with applicable regulatory standards.
Conduct GIS-based mapping, spatial analysis, and preparation of project exhibits.
Manage projects, including leading technical components, tracking budgets, and coordinating with clients.
Lead, mentor, and coordinate project teams and technical staff.
Support business development for biological and environmental services.

Requirements Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Biology , Natural Resources, or a related field, with at least 10+ years of professional experience in environmental science, including resource evaluation, compliance and permitting documentation, regulatory agency coordination, and work as part of an integrated team; or
Master’s degree in Biology , Natural Resources, or a related field, with at least 8+ years of professional experience in environmental science, including resource evaluation, compliance and permitting documentation, regulatory agency coordination, and work as part of an integrated team.
Experience preparing reports and documentation to support NEPA, CWA, and ESA compliance.
Knowledge of regional plant , fish, and/or wildlife species and their habitat requirements.
Experience developing habitat assessments, mitigation plans, and/or monitoring plans.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Experience using GIS for environmental mapping and analysis.
Experience using field data collection equipment, including GPS units.

Physical Requirements

Ability to travel to project sites throughout the Southwestern United States. Travel is estimated to be up to 25% annually.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions, including heat, rain, wind, and cold.
Ability to perform extended fieldwork in rugged terrain, including walking, standing, bending, and kneeling.
Ability to lift and carry equipment and materials weighing up to 50 pounds.
Ability to sit at a workstation and use a computer for extended periods.
Manual dexterity to use a computer, keyboard, mouse, and other tools.
Strong communication skills, both in person and electronically.

Additional Information

This position is based in our Albuquerque, NM office on a hybrid schedule.
This is a full-time position, typically 40 hours per week, with standard hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Additional hours may be required based on project needs.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.    

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 25,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by  Leading with Science ®  to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, marital or familial status, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Environmental Chemist/Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

About You

You are an experienced environmental chemist or scientist with experience reviewing and validating environmental data and supporting field programs. You are a strategic thinker who thrives on the challenges of these complex, interdisciplinary environment matters. A lifelong learner, you want to keep growing intellectually and professionally. Collaborating with colleagues with diverse expertise is exciting for you, and you are also comfortable working independently. Quality management and integrity are among your strongest principles.

About Integral

Integral Consulting Inc. is a science and engineering firm delivering sound technical solutions to meet today’s challenges in the health, environmental, and natural resource arenas. We are a values-driven collaborative team that is as passionate about company culture as we are about the work we do for our clients. Since our founding in 2002, we have operated with a demonstrated commitment to the well-being, diversity, and professional development of our staff and an equal commitment to strong partnerships with our clients and teaming partners. We are a company where people come to solve today’s toughest environmental challenges through innovative ideas, exceptional teamwork, and dedication to accuracy and technical quality.

About The Job

We are currently seeking a chemist with 3 to 5 years of experience who has the desire to also do some field work with our Sediment and Water Investigations and Monitoring practice in our Santa Cruz, California office. The position supports multiple clients and projects, with day-to-day responsibilities that primarily include reviewing and validating of laboratory data, managing a small wet laboratory, supporting field efforts, and on occasion performing some fieldwork. The selected candidate will work closely with project team members on water quality monitoring, stormwater planning and monitoring, and sediment sampling efforts across the Bay Area and Northern California.

This position is primarily in-office, but opportunities for hybrid work may be available.

Requirements

Responsibilities

As a Scientist, your job functions will include, but not be limited to:

Assisting with sample control procedures for multiple projects
Tracking submission of samples to chemistry laboratories and receipt of associated data for multiple projects
Adhering quality control and quality assurance procedures to ensure data integrity
Communicating with laboratories regarding data quality questions or corrections that may be needed.
Performing quality assurance reviews of technical analyses and results
Managing laboratory and data validation subcontractors
Reviewing CEDEN EDDs and applying the Quality Assurance codes associated with chemistry excursions
Performing Stage 2B and Stage 3 data validation and reporting following EPA’s National Functional Guidelines
Assisting in writing formal QAQC reports
Executing laboratory bottle cleaning procedures and maintaining facility organization
Managing and maintaining a small wet laboratory
Collecting river, stream, creek, ocean, and stormwater samples
Collecting sediment and surface water samples both on land and from boats
Maintaining accurate field and laboratory logs
Adhering to company, project, state, and federal safety policies

Fieldwork will occasionally be required; those responsibilities may include long days in the field, extended exposure to the elements (sun, rain, wind), prolonged standing, and other physically demanding tasks such as lifting equipment or materials. You must have the ability and willingness to work outdoors in a wide range of weather conditions. Your work schedule at times will be defined by storm forecasts and may include working nights and/or weekends.

Qualifications

Candidates should hold at a minimum, a B.A. or B.S. in chemistry or a related science and have at least 3 years of experience in a related technical field.

The Ideal Candidate Will Have

Familiarity with environmental analytical methods for water and sediments
Demonstrated strong personal initiative towards projects, critical thinking, and problem solving
Solid attention to detail
Ability to oversee a small wet laboratory, cleaning glassware and field equipment
Flexibility with work hours as required to meet project needs
Affinity for working outdoors in all weather conditions, with some nights and weekends
A valid U.S. driver's license (or ability to obtain one upon hire) and a clean driving record. If a driver’s license cannot be obtained, reliable transportation to project and field sites is required
Ability to lift and carry items of varying weights as required by the job, occasionally up to 40 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation
Proficiency with Microsoft® Office products Word and Excel
Excellent written and oral communication skills
A desire to grow both intellectually and professionally
Strong organizational abilities
Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers

Compensation is commensurate with experience and internal equity, within the listed range. An employee’s total compensation package includes annual salary, company-subsidized (employee and family) medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) participation with a company match of 1% to 4% of annual compensation, company-paid life and short- and long-term disability insurance, paid sick leave (10 days), paid vacation (12 days;), and paid holidays (9 days) per year, and the potential for an annual discretionary bonus based on company performance. Paid time off will be prorated to reflect part-time scheduled hours, if applicable.

Integral Consulting Inc. is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer who provides equal opportunity in all of our employment practices to all qualified employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, pregnancy (including childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin or ancestry, age, sexual orientation, disability, marital status, military, veteran, or Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act protected veteran status, gender identity or gender expression, genetic information (including testing or characteristics), or any other category protected by federal, state, and local laws. We believe that a diverse and inclusive environment drives innovation and excellence, and we are dedicated to building a team that reflects the diverse communities we live in and serve. If you require reasonable accommodations during the application or interview process, please contact us at integraljobs@integral-corp.com.

We are excited to connect with individuals who share our mission and values, and those who bring diverse contributions to our team. We value unique perspectives and skills, and encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every requirement.

All offers of employment are contingent on candidates successfully passing an employment history screening, degree verification, and a federal, state, and county criminal background and Watch List screening. Candidates will receive a written notice of this requirement. All screenings will be done in accordance with all local, state, and federal laws.
