jobs.title: Senior Environmental Planner
jobs.description:
Overview

ABOUT THE POSITION

Senior Environmental Planner | Hybrid

VHB is actively seeking a Senior Environmental Planner to enrich our New England team. This role will be leading and supporting the preparation of federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and Massachusetts Environmental Policy Act (MEPA) documentation, as well as permitting applications, for a diverse set of clients.

At VHB, we specialize in delivering comprehensive environmental services to an array of clients, including municipalities, transportation agencies, airports, energy firms, private developers, and more. The Senior Environmental Engineer serves as a strategic technical leader responsible for the oversight and execution of environmental compliance, permitting, and sustainability programs. Location: Toronto-661 University

Department: Data Science and Analytics

This posting is to fill a current vacancy.

The Role

To provide geospatial analytics expertise that transforms data into actionable intelligence, supporting surveillance, population health assessment, public health planning, research, and evidence-informed decision-making across Public Health Ontario and the broader public health system.

To advance PHO's capacity in geospatial analysis, spatial data management, and geographic information systems by developing innovative analytical approaches, visualizations, and decision-support products that address public health priorities, population health issues, and emerging health threats.

Key Responsibilities-

Develops, maintains, and enhances integrated geospatial data assets from internal and external sources, applying data quality, metadata, and governance practices to support public health analytics and decision-making.
Develops geospatial analyses, visualizations, and spatial intelligence products that support surveillance, epidemiology, population and health system assessment, research, planning, and data science initiatives.
Collaborates with multidisciplinary teams to apply spatial modelling, hotspot detection, population characterization, accessibility analysis, and risk factor analysis to public health priorities, population health issues, health equity considerations, and emerging health threats.
Promotes the adoption of innovative geospatial methods and technologies that advance PHO strategic priorities and strengthen evidence-informed public health practice.
Acquires, integrates, analyzes, interprets, and assesses the quality of administrative, demographic, socioeconomic, environmental, remote sensing, health, and other relevant data.
Identifies and manages spatial reference data, including geographic boundaries, service locations, points of interest, and environmental features of public health relevance.
Serves as a subject matter expert in geospatial analytics, advising PHO and collaborating with external organizations on data standards, data-sharing practices, analytical methods, and geospatial capabilities.
Evaluates emerging geospatial trends, technologies, standards, and practices for appropriate application within PHO.
Communicates geospatial findings through maps, dashboards, interactive applications, reports, presentations, and scientific forums, and represents PHO in relevant collaborations.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge And Skills-

Proficiency in cartographic design, geospatial visualization, geostatistics, spatial modelling, and spatial data analysis, including communicating complex information through maps, dashboards, interactive applications, and other decision-support products.
Knowledge of geospatial data platforms, cloud and web mapping technologies, spatial databases, data integration tools, and practices used to develop, share, and sustain geospatial products.
Knowledge of geospatial theories, methods, and geographic concepts and their application to public health analysis and decision-making.
Knowledge of geospatial data management and governance, including raster and vector data models, spatial databases, metadata standards, data quality, privacy, security, and information management principles.
Knowledge of public health, epidemiology, population health, health equity, environmental determinants of health, and health system concepts relevant to geospatial analysis.
Knowledge of applicable privacy, security, ethical, and data stewardship requirements for collecting, using, linking, visualizing, and sharing health and geospatial data, including Indigenous data governance considerations.
Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning in geospatial analytics, data science, public health intelligence, and related technologies.

Education And Experience-

Bachelor’s degree in geography, geomatics, geographic information systems (GIS), spatial data science, epidemiology, public health, environmental science, data science, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
A minimum of five years’ work experience with GIS and geospatial analysis.
Advanced knowledge of enterprise and open-source GIS and geospatial analytics platforms, with experience in spatial analysis, web mapping, scripting, automation, application development, APIs, and relevant programming and query languages.
Experience with PHO-supported technologies such as ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online, Python, SQL, and R is an asset.

Attributes and Competencies-

Oral, written, visual, and interpersonal communication skills to translate complex geospatial findings into clear, accessible insights for technical, non-technical, and executive audiences.
Consultation, facilitation, and presentation skills to gather requirements, explain analytical methods and limitations, and communicate findings and recommendations through reports, maps, dashboards, interactive products, and presentations.
Develops collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders to understand needs and deliver responsive geospatial analytics and decision-support services for public health priorities, population health issues, and emerging health threats.
Responds to requests for geospatial analysis, visualization, data, metadata, and related documentation, clarifying the intended use and appropriate analytical approach.
Defines client needs, requirements, deliverables, success criteria, and application requirements for geospatial initiatives.
Coordinates assigned geospatial initiatives through planning, delivery, and evaluation to support timely, fit-for purpose results and stakeholder satisfaction.
Advises on the application of geospatial analytics to surveillance, population health and health system assessment, health equity, program and service planning, resource allocation, and response to emerging health threats.
Assesses stakeholder information and analytical requirements and selects appropriate methods for analyzing, visualizing, and communicating spatial information to support public health planning, surveillance, resource allocation, service access, and response activities.
Evaluates available data sources, analytical methods, assumptions, and limitations to determine their suitability for public health use.
Determines how spatial and non-spatial data can be linked, analyzed, and presented to generate actionable insights on public health priorities, population health issues, and emerging health threats.
Delivers accurate, timely, and fit-for-purpose geospatial analyses and decision-support products that inform surveillance, population and health system assessment, health equity, climate and environmental health, service planning, resource allocation, and response to emerging health threats.
Generates spatial insights on patterns, trends, access, inequities, populations, and environmental and social determinants to support evidence-informed public health planning and action.
Provides geospatial subject matter expertise and project leadership within cross-functional teams and initiatives.
Builds team capability through coaching, mentoring, and knowledge exchange on geospatial methods, tools, and interpretation.

jobs.description:
About The Role

Balfour Beatty are looking for a Senior Geo-Environmental Engineer to join thier Power T&D Division in Derby.

Role Purpose

Providing technical support, advice, strategy and direction to the geotechnical and geo-environmental team leader and wider team.

You will deliver integrated site assessments that inform planning, design and remediation strategies.

You will work with the project team, designers and subcontractors through the design phase to deliver safe and suitable scope of works in line with the project objectives and then deliver these to a high standard.

The role includes leading Phase 1 and 2 site and ground investigations and ensuring the production of high-quality technical reporting deliverables, and the development of practical, cost-effective remediation approaches to all projects secured by Balfour Beatty Power Transmission and Distribution (BB PT&D).

Balfour Beatty welcomes applications from both full-time and part-time candidates, including those interested in job-sharing arrangements. Additionally, the company offers a flexible working policy to support a healthy work-life balance.

What you'll be doing

Key Accountabilities

To undertake Phase 1 and Phase 2 geotechnical and geo-environmental assessment as required for OHL, Cabling and Substation projects, from the initial feasibility assessment, through desk study phase and design development to detailed design & delivery / construction phase and scheme closure ensuring completion in accordance with programme, cost and quality requirements.
Ensure the timely and quality delivery of designs to meet budget, programme and pre-determined objectives. Preparation of reports, calculations and drawings to a high technical level which are compliant with the required Client and national technical standards (BS/Eurocodes/ENA).
Checking of other work packages

Key Responsibilities

Design appropriate investigation works to allow for a detailed land contamination assessment and plan for remedial works to suitably remediate contaminated land where proven to exist. Including:

Lead start-to-end delivery of Phase 1 Feasibility and Desktop Studies, Phase 2 Ground Investigations, and follow on remediation strategy and verification works.
Manage multi-disciplinary ground investigations, integrating geotechnical and geo-environmental in-situ and laboratory based test results and other data provision, management and assessments.
Produce GI specifications and schedules and where required contract documents, manage GI contractors and support with exploratory hole termination advice and decisions, installation design and details, sampling, backfill and scheduling of geotechnical and chemical laboratory testing schedules.
Produce high quality and comprehensive geotechnical and geo-environmental factual and interpretative reports, undertake contamination risk assessments with evaluation of ground conditions and design parameters where necessary.
Provide technical input into foundation and infrastructure assessment and design, ground improvement strategies, and remediation schemes
Build and maintain close and strong working relationships with clients, consultants and regulatory bodies.
Schedule chemical testing , analyse and present findings of contamination assessments clearly and support clients to satisfying planning and other regulatory conditions and achieve environmental compliance
Provide on site assessment of geological conditions resulting in design decisions for applicable engineering solutions.
Undertake assessment on the condition and nature of materials and advise on their acceptability for re-use.
Prepare accurate costings, monitor budgets, and drive efficient and timely project delivery in the team.
Appoint, liaise with and manage subcontractors to support delivery of their reports and deliverables.
Devise training plans to upskill and support junior engineers in the team and staff across to be competent in areas of environmental and land contamination assessment including line management responsibilities?
Working closely with Project Teams to determine and maintain common objectives and to ensure work undertaken is appropriate and in accordance with project priorities.
Embed “Safety by Design” principles in all activities, including managing safety through appropriate life cycle designs that minimise risks to personnel and property, by ensuring that Health & Safety Regulations and Balfour Beatty procedures and requirements are followed in the design substation, cabling and OHL projects.

Who we're looking for

Skills Required

Degree level education or equivalent with formal training in geology, civil engineering and/or geotechnical engineering.
Professional membership of either the ICE or Geol Soc & working towards Chartered Engineer status with the aim of achieving this within the next year to two years maximum period of time.
Experience of coordinating with government agencies and local authorities such as SEPA, EA etc
Strong, proven post-graduate track record and level of experience in the civil engineering industry
Proven experience in both geotechnical and geo-environmental project delivery.
Strong technical report writing skills, including Phase 1 & 2 desk study and GIR assessments
Working knowledge of remediation processes and environmental modelling
Practical understanding of ground conditions and foundation types and behaviour
Experience of the supervision and/or monitoring of sub-contractors
Proven experience of the design of large scale civil engineering works
Strong, proven experience of the management of design of civil or geotechnical engineering works
IT Literate (Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel)
Extensive experience of geotechnical design software including slope and retention design packages

Why work for us

Day in, day out, our teams deliver some of the UK’s most ambitious, exciting and meaningful projects; developing, building and maintaining the vital infrastructure that supports national economies and strengthens communities.

Benefits

As if contributing to and supporting work that makes life better for millions wasn’t rewarding enough, we offer a full range of benefits too. You’ll have the freedom to shape the package that’s right for you and your life. Here are some of our key benefits:

Smart working, giving you more flexibility such as staggered start and finish times, with up to 40% remote working, where roles allow.
25 days paid annual leave (pro rata)
Family friendly policies which include 28 weeks full pay for maternity/adoption leave and four weeks full pay for paternity/partners leave
Pension, share incentive plan, volunteering leave, recognition schemes and much more…

About Us

Balfour Beatty’s Power Transmission & Distribution teams work with regional, national and international electricity network owners and operators to provide technical engineering solutions across the full spectrum of the electricity grid, including overhead lines, cabling, substations and distribution networks.

From scoping and feasibility, to design, construction and on-going maintenance, our in-house experts, flexible resources and industry-leading innovations support customers in the development of some of the UK’s most ambitious power transmission and distribution projects.

Diversity and inclusion

At Balfour Beatty we believe that diversity and inclusion are essential components of any successful, happy workplace. Through our Value Everyone Diversity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan, we are growing our diverse workforce and developing our inclusive culture where everyone is able to thrive and reach their full potential, regardless of their identity or background. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer – Drone Development, Design & Test
jobs.description:
About Us

Havoc is a leader in all-domain collaborative autonomy. Its software-defined hardware approach powers military and commercial-grade autonomous systems across sea, air, and land to sense, decide, and act together in complex and contested environments. Havoc connects assets, enabling them to share information, adapt in real time, and continue operating even when communications are disrupted or denied. Havoc optimizes mission performance and minimizes human risk.

Havoc was founded in 2024 and headquartered in Providence, Rhode Island. Learn more at Havoc: All-Domain Collaborative Autonomy .

About The Role

HavocAI is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer to lead the technical maturation of Locust, our advanced unmanned aircraft system (UAS), as it transitions from a demonstrated prototype to a Department of Defense (DoD) fieldable, Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) platform.

This is a hands-on engineering leadership role where you'll drive airframe design for manufacture, structural analysis, and system-level integration while providing the program leadership necessary to keep the production effort on schedule and within budget.

You will serve as the primary technical authority for Locust's production readiness, working closely with manufacturing partners, government customers, and cross-functional engineering teams. Success in this role means delivering a robust, mission-ready aircraft that can withstand the demands of operational use while being reliably manufactured at production scale.

We are looking for an engineer who is equally comfortable designing parts in CAD, working with vendors and machinists, assembling prototypes, and getting into the field or test environment to understand why something failed.

This is not a purely analytical or desk-based engineering position. The ideal candidate has experience developing drones, UAVs, robotics, autonomous systems, or other lightweight electromechanical platforms and enjoys moving quickly between design and hardware.

Key Responsibilities

Design mechanical components, assemblies, structures, enclosures, mounts, and mechanisms for unmanned aerial systems
Develop concepts and detailed designs using 3D CAD
Own mechanical designs from initial requirements through prototype, test, iteration, and production release
Build and assemble prototype vehicles and subsystems
Work directly with machine shops, fabrication vendors, and suppliers to rapidly produce prototype hardware
Develop engineering drawings, tolerances, interfaces, and manufacturing documentation
Perform engineering calculations including structural, load, thermal, vibration, tolerance, and basic mechanical analysis
Design lightweight structures while balancing strength, stiffness, manufacturability, cost, and weight
Develop and execute mechanical test plans Conduct structural, vibration, environmental, durability, and system-level testing
Diagnose mechanical failures and rapidly implement design improvements
Support flight testing and vehicle-level integration
Work closely with electrical, embedded, autonomy, controls, manufacturing, and test engineers
Design for manufacturability, assembly, serviceability, and field repair
Participate directly in vehicle builds, troubleshooting, test campaigns, and engineering validation

Required Qualifications

BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline
3+ years of mechanical product development experience
Strong 3D CAD and mechanical design experience
Demonstrated experience taking hardware from concept through prototype and testing
Hands-on experience assembling, modifying, troubleshooting, and testing electromechanical systems
Strong understanding of mechanical design fundamentals including materials, fasteners, tolerancing, structures, and manufacturing processes
Experience designing parts for CNC machining, sheet metal, composites, additive manufacturing, or similar fabrication processes
Experience developing test fixtures and executing mechanical validation testing
Ability to independently troubleshoot hardware failures and drive design changes

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience designing or developing UAVs, drones, UAS, aircraft, robotics, or autonomous vehicles
Experience with small or Group 1–3 unmanned aircraft
Experience with airframes, propulsion integration, payload integration, landing systems, or flight-control hardware
Experience with composite structures
Experience transitioning prototype designs into low-rate or production manufacturing

Why HavocAI

At HavocAI, you'll help build autonomous systems that solve real-world challenges in some of the most demanding environments imaginable. You'll work alongside exceptional engineers, move quickly, and see your work transition from prototype to production and ultimately into the hands of operators.

If you're excited about solving difficult engineering problems, owning critical technical decisions, and helping shape the future of autonomous systems, we'd love to hear from you.

Benefits

100% Employer paid Health, Dental and Vision Insurance for you and your families
Life Insurance (Employer Paid)
Ability to participate in the companies 401k program (Matching)
Unlimited PTO policy with an enforced 2 week minimum
Equity Package
Work / Home Office Stipend
Global Entry
16 Week Paid Parental Leave
Monthly Health and Wellness Stipend

Our Values

Innovation: We are driven to break new ground. Every day presents an opportunity to challenge the status quo, think boldly, and deliver advanced solutions that transform the future of defense technology.
Integrity: We hold ourselves to the highest ethical standards, ensuring transparency, accountability, and trust in all our actions and partnerships.
Mission-Driven: We are focused on achieving impactful outcomes that align with our core mission—protecting lives through innovation.
Forward-Leaning: We continuously seek out new opportunities and remain at the forefront of technological advancements. We embrace change and anticipate the challenges of tomorrow with confidence and creativity.
Ownership of All Tasks: At HavocAI, no problem is too complex or too trivial. We believe that greatness comes from tackling the hardest challenges, but also in handling the smallest, sometimes thankless, tasks with the same level of commitment and care.
Servant Leadership: We lead by serving others, whether it’s supporting our employees, partners, or the broader community. Empowering those around us is key to achieving long-term success and making a lasting impact.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

SeamonWhiteside is seeking an experienced, entrepreneurial, and technically strong professional to serve as the North Carolina Regional Natural Resources Team Leader. About Us

Since the company’s beginning in 1985, we’ve blended the disciplines of civil engineering and landscape architecture from concept to completion to create places of legacy and inspiration for our clients, community, and family. There is a big difference in how engineers and landscape architects visualize a project. At SW+ we approach every plan from both points of view, working together to create a successfully integrated venture. In our world, that’s a good thing.

With the goal of being the best design firm in the region, the SW+ leadership team continues to attract the brightest talent, each with a unique expertise in one of the many facets of land design. SW+ has a diverse portfolio at a variety of scales in both the public and private sector including mixed-use commercial developments, urban and suburban multifamily, healthcare, office, high end resort and parks and recreation projects.

In addition, company sponsored events, such as golf tournaments, sports teams, and happy hours, along with philanthropic endeavors provide opportunities throughout the year to lift morale and strengthen bonds between coworkers.

Essential Job Functions

Lead and grow SW+ stormwater, stream restoration, floodplain management, and green infrastructure services across North Carolina, with emphasis on client service, technical excellence, quality control, team development, and profitable project delivery.
Develop and maintain relationships with municipal, county, state, institutional, and private sector clients, as well as strategic partners, regulatory agencies, and teaming firms.
Identify, pursue, and support new business opportunities, including proposals, scopes, fee development, interviews, and client presentations.

Promote consistent use of SW+ standards, tools, workflows, quality processes, and project management practices.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, Environmental Engineering, Biosystems Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, Biological and Agricultural Engineering, or a closely related field.
Professional Engineer (PE) license, preferably in North Carolina, or ability to obtain North Carolina licensure within an agreed timeframe.
10 or more years of progressively responsible stormwater, water resources, stream restoration, floodplain management, or green infrastructure experience, preferably with a consulting engineering, municipal stormwater, or infrastructure design firm.
Demonstrated experience leading projects, managing clients, developing scopes and budgets, and delivering quality technical work.
Strong understanding of North Carolina stormwater regulations, erosion and sediment control, post-construction stormwater management, riparian buffers, floodplain management, environmental permitting, and applicable state and federal requirements.
Experience with stormwater control measures, hydrologic and hydraulic modeling, watershed studies, flood mitigation, stream stabilization, stream restoration, or green infrastructure design.

Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

The Business Class Lead (BCL) will work with the Business Class Director (BCD) and HDR peers on monitoring and improvement of technical competencies, staff development, and execution of work associated with water resource planning that meets federal planning standards and expectations. The overall goal of the role is to promote a quality culture, drive or support BC initiatives that drive growth and project delivery, and work with areas to hire, train and support career progression of staff within this technical service area.

The successful candidate will bring a vision for delivery, mentoring, and market growth; and have a proven ability to work broadly with teams to deliver positive outcomes for projects. The BCL will collaborate on business class efforts with market sector directors, business group regional directors, other business class leaders, local business group leaders, local market sector (marketing) leaders, cross sector leadership, and area staff.

The BCL responsibilities include the following:

Fostering a quality culture though project delivery excellence and staff coaching. Serve as a Quality Control lead, technical advisor, and technical lead (i.e., Project Manager or Task Manager) for specific projects. Work with project teams to field needs and align staff to meet delivery expectations and develop strategy to promote knowledge transfer and staff development within water resource plan formulation.
Leading or supporting Business Class sponsored standards and guidelines (i.e., best practices) technical tools, checklists, workflows, and techniques to enhance service quality and efficiency. Promoting forward thinking delivery and strategy approaches as well as technology use and adoption.
Participating in tactical planning including engagement others within HDR to align initiatives with market drivers and client needs. Maintain awareness related to industry trends and drivers. Implementing actions associated with annual planning including leading or supporting recruiting key positions in partnership with others.
Working with others within HDR including client facing and marketing staff to track, develop and share qualifications and project approaches. Engage on specific pursuits as a lead or team member. Drive industry facing strategies associated with technical service area (e.g., professional association engagement, webinars, workshops, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading plan formulation for Federal clients. Specific experience with the USACE’s Principles, Requirements and Guidelines (PR&G) ideal.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams to successful project outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
A minimum of 10 years experience
Professional registration, license or certification may be required based on role
Strong communication and listening skills
Ability to handle multiple assignments
Good leadership and organizational skills
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee ownership, employee health, performance, and success, which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time away, parental leave, paid holidays, a retirement savings plan with employer match, employee referral bonus and tuition reimbursement. jobs.description:
Location: Livermore, CA

Title: Environmental Engineer (NWS 00927)

North Wind Services (NWS) is a high performing, low risk company with a successful history of contributing to their client’s missions. NWS executes and manages a wide range of technical services such as environmental investigation and restoration, construction, demolition, radioactive and hazardous waste management, public communication/involvement, information management, health and safety, industrial hygiene, and emergency response/HAZMAT services.

North Wind Services is actively seeking individuals who can contribute to national security within the science, technology, and engineering fields as part of our supplemental labor team at vital federal research and development installations supporting the Department of Energy. Qualified applicants must be a US citizen, at least 18 years of age, and able to meet pre-employment requirements including any required physicals, drug screen, and/or background investigation to satisfy clearance requirements from the Department of Energy.

Successful candidates will be employees of NWS supporting the missions of their federal client, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in Livermore, CA. Pay, benefits, Human Resources, and employment management functions are all provided by NWS. As an NWS employee working at LLNL, within the client’s environment, you will complete day-to-day tasks, with direction from technical personnel directly employed by LLNL.

The Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) Program of the Environmental Restoration Department has an opening for an Environmental Engineer. The successful candidate will provide engineering support for the planning, design, testing, compliance monitoring, and operation and maintenance of groundwater and soil vapor remediation systems at the LLNL Livermore Site 200 and Site 300 located in Tracy, California.

Essential Duties

Provide advanced environmental engineering knowledge and support for environmental remediation activities at LLNL.
Perform advanced research, development, design, and testing of cost effective and engineering solutions for groundwater and soil vapor remediation systems; ensuring all system designs comply with DOE, federal and state agency regulations and safety requirements.
Monitor treatment system operations and identify opportunities to optimize and improve systems, including opportunities for improved technologies, increased efficiencies, cost savings, and reduced lifecycle costs.
Plan and conduct field experiments to develop, adapt, demonstrate, and validate new environmental remediation technologies.
Oversee existing remediation system operations as well as the design and construction of new remediation systems.
Prepare and review technical and regulatory documents and ensure compliance with all federal and state regulatory requirements and LLNL environmental policies.
Keep informed of new environmental policies and environmental technologies and maintain knowledge of the scientific and technical aspects of various regulatory requirements and how they impact cleanup operations.
Collaborate with colleagues, mid-level managers, and other team members on matters requiring coordination across organizational lines.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Essential Skills, Knowledge, And Abilities

Bachelor’s degree in civil or environmental engineering or related field, or equivalent combination of education and significant related experience.
Advanced knowledge and significant experience in environmental remediation and the design, installation, operation, and maintenance of environmental remediation systems and system components, such as extraction and injection wellhead design, pump specifications, treatment media and vessels, pipelines, associated instrumentation, and control systems.
Significant knowledge and significant experience with technical aspects of environmental restoration, including groundwater and soil remediation systems; pressure and flow calculations; environmental chemistry; and treatability tests.
Advanced knowledge and significant experience with engineering standards, practices and processes; generation of requirements and design documents, configuration control, preparation of test plans and user documentation, and formal and informal design review processes.
Ability to apply advanced engineering principles and innovations to solve complex technical problems with ingenuity and creativity.
Advanced knowledge of State of California and Federal regulations and requirements related to remediation activities.
Knowledge of standard software applications (such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and ability to work on multiple computing platforms (PC and Mac).
Ability to direct own research working effectively in a collaborative team environment and independently.
Advanced verbal and written communication skills to interact effectively with the scientific community, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders; collaborate in a multi-disciplinary team environment; present and explain technical information and provide advice to management.

Desired Skills, Knowledge, And Abilities

Master’s degree in Environmental Engineering or related technical field.
Advanced knowledge and significant experience with compliance sampling, innovative remedial technologies such as in-situ remediation techniques, operation of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, Human Machine Interfaces (HMI), preventative facility maintenance programs, and trend analysis using operational data.
Experience designing, operating, and maintaining groundwater and soil vapor remediation systems for multiple, co-mingled contaminants, including volatile organic compounds, high-explosive compounds, perchlorate, nitrate, and uranium.

Special Requirements

Pre-Placement Medical Exam
: A job-related pre-placement medical examination may be required.

Pre-employment drug test:
External applicants selected for this position will be required to pass a post offer, pre-employment drug test.

Anticipated Government Clearance Level: P
(position will be cleared to this level). Applicants who are selected will be subject to a federal background investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information or matters. In addition, all L or Q cleared employees are subject to random drug testing. Q-level clearance requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold multiple citizenships (U.S. and another country), you may be required to renounce your non-U.S. citizenship before a DOE L or Q clearance will be processed/granted.

Requisition ID:
96019

Florida Power & Light Company is the largest electric utility in the U.S., providing reliable energy to nearly 12 million Floridians. With one of the nation’s most fuel-efficient, cost-effective power generation fleets and industry-leading reliability, we’re redefining what’s possible in energy. Want to be part of something powerful? Join our outstanding team and help shape the future of energy.

Position Specific Description

The role involves ensuring the implementation and management of the PGD Environmental Management System, overseeing site water, wastewater, wildlife, and vegetation in accordance with environmental permits. This position is responsible for managing all regional aspects of environmental compliance, while supporting the execution of site processes and procedures to achieve safety, environmental, compliance, reliability, availability, and cost management goals for the west FL region for solar & BESS. Travel and overnight stays are required.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Maintenance & Performance Optimization

Optimize site environmental maintenance and performance.
Conduct and submit required inspection and maintenance activities on time per site environmental permits.
Prepare and submit environmental reporting to local, state, and federal agencies promptly.

Compliance Management

Oversee adherence to site SPCC (Spill Prevention Control & Countermeasure) and FRP (Facility Response Plan) requirements.
Develop and maintain relationships with local, state, and federal agencies.
Apply process and project management skills to deliver results effectively.
Address site environmental deficiencies proactively.

Process Standardization & Leadership

Standardize processes, procedures, and techniques for repeatability.
Demonstrate leadership for internal employee development and performance management.

Transition From Construction To Operations

Conduct Pre-COD Site Walkdowns to document ongoing civil issues and ensure compliance.
Identify and resolve operational environmental issues before COD and ensure completion of lingering items before turnover.
Collect site information and initiate permitting for all office buildings or operational structures.
Review and ensure compliance with site-specific county, state, and federal permits.
Coordinate contractors and set up contracts for ongoing compliance-related maintenance and monitoring.
Create procedures for any site-specific compliance requirements.
Ensure proper close-out and sign-off on all construction-related permits, supporting final agency walkdowns and transitioning active permits to the operations phase.
Train new and existing operations crew on compliance requirements.

Operational Support

Oversee and support the Regional Environmental Program.
Continuously verify that Wind Environmental Management System (EMS) processes and procedures are executed in the field
Manage Compliance Management tracker tasks and deadlines.
Prepare for and support internal and external environmental audits.
Serve as the local point of contact for agency inquiries and site visits.
Provide field support and management of environmental events.
Proactively identify and resolve site-specific compliance issues.
Perform internal and external reporting on environmental events.
Support root cause analysis for environmental events.
Maintain site compliance with permit conditions and agency requirements.
Ensure sites perform routine inspections and maintenance events ahead of due dates.
Manage contractor oversight and environmental compliance programs, including stormwater management, conservation lands maintenance, vegetation management, wildlife trapping response, oil spill prevention, and response.
Conduct regional annual staff environmental awareness and compliance training.
Handle civil/stormwater/wildlife management and contractor coordination, hazardous material management, tracking, and disposal.
Track water use permitting, reporting, and well management.
Manage environmental record retention and document management.

Desired Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science or a related field.
Knowledge of state and federal environmental regulations.
Familiarity with local flora, fauna, and habitats.
Strong oral and written communication skills.
Proficiency in analysis, problem-solving, compliance, leadership, and process/project management.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite.

Job Overview

Employees in this role are responsible for assuring the execution of the PGD Environmental Management System and ensuring regional environmental compliance in accordance with federal, state and county permits. Employees in this role have responsibility for interpreting, organizing, executing, and coordinating assignments. This involves exploration of subject area, definition of scope, selection of areas for investigation, and developmentof novel concepts.

Compliance Assurance – Continuous verification Solar and Storage Environmental Management System (EMS) processes and procedures are executed in the field
Environmental agency interface - Local point of contact for agency inquiries and site visits
Environmental Event Response - Field support and management of environmental issues, proactively identify and resolve site specific compliance issues to prevent or minimize environmental impacts during events
Quarterly site-specific operational environmental compliance assessments and inspections ahead of EMS due date
Environmental Compliance Program – Maintain site compliance with permit conditions and agency requirements
Environmental contractor management and oversight for Stormwater management system maintenance, conservation lands vegetation management, wildlife trapping, oil spill response
Perform regional staff environmental awareness and compliance training
Transition to Operations support: Incorporate new site into Solar and Storage Environmental Management System (EMS)
Identify and resolve operations related environmental issues prior to COD
Environmental record retention / management
Performs other job-related duties as assigned

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's or Equivalent Experience
Experience: 5+ years

None

This is not a State of Delaware merit position. It is a one-year contractual position with the opportunity to work long term.

The Kent Conservation District (KCD), a governmental subdivision of the State of Delaware, is seeking applicants for the contractual services position of Restoration Coordinator with the Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC), Division of Climate, Coastal and Energy.

JOB SUMMARY

The selected candidate will coordinate habitat restoration projects funded by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) within DNREC, as well as with key external stakeholders representing National Estuary Programs, nonprofits, local governments, and academia.

The Restoration Coordinator will manage the IIJA grants for the Coastal Program.  The selected candidate will develop project selection criteria, project proposals, and project performance measures for IIJA funding that support the goals of the various state habitat and wildlife conversation plans and strategies as applicable. Collectively, these plans collate stakeholder-driven restoration and conservation goals for the state of Delaware to help protect wetland and estuarine habitat to support healthy coastal ecosystems, as well as preserve recreational opportunities.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Essential functions are fundamental, core functions and are not intended
to be an exhaustive list of all job duties.

•       Develop restoration project prioritization and selection criteria.
•       Update existing prioritization criteria and restoration plans.
•       Manage contracts and projects associated with IIJA funds and IIJA grant deliverables.
•       Develop performance measures for IIJA-funded restoration projects.
•       Monitor and track the results of IIJA-funded restoration projects, specifically those projects where the Restoration Coordinator, research reserve, or coastal management staff have provided significant technical assistance during the project development or implementation phases.
•       Coordinate with underserved communities through regular meetings and community outreach.
•       Work with stakeholder groups.
•       Write grant reports and manage grant funds.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Applicants must have the following:
At least three years’ experience as a planner OR at least three years’ experience in a planning function.
Experience in having responsibility for a most complex planning project (complexity is to be determined based on variables such as discipline, population, fiscal impact, geographic area, social impact, planning horizon, public involvement, research and analysis, and the nature of the project team).
Experience in serving as a subject matter expert in habitat restoration and/or resilience-based projects.
Experience in managing grants.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT

1.     Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. The Conservation District participates in the Federal E-Verify system to confirm you are authorized to work in the U.S. The Conservation District shall require verification of identity, validating you are lawfully permitted to work in the United States beyond a temporary period without employment-based sponsorship .
2.     The Conservation District does not provide sponsorship for holders of H-1B Visas.
3.     Direct Deposit of paychecks is required of all new employees.
4.     Possession of a valid Driver’s License is required (not suspended, revoked, cancelled, or disqualified from driving.)
5.     Criminal Background Check: A satisfactory criminal background check is required as a condition of hire. The applicant may be required to pay for the criminal background check as part of the conditional offer of hire.

BENEFITS

The Kent Conservation District offers a comprehensive benefits package, including: 37.5-hour work week with flexible scheduling options, 9.5 hours per month of accrued vacation leave and 9.5 hours per month of accrued sick leave (prorated the first month of employment), and 12 paid holidays per year (holidays and floating holidays follow the State of Delaware schedule.) Health insurance and pension are also included in the benefits package.

ACCOMMODATIONS

Accommodations are available for applicants with disabilities in all phases of the application and employment process.  TDD users should call the Delaware Relay Service at (800) 232-5460 for assistance. Call (302) 739-5458 if you need assistance with an accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) or general applicant support.

The Kent Conservation District is an equal opportunity employer and values a diverse workforce.

TO APPLY

Please email 1) Cover Letter, 2) Resume, and 3) Kent Conservation District Employment Application to:
Jamie L. Willey, MBA
DNREC District HR Manager
Jamie.L.Willey@delaware.gov
(302) 608-5478

About The Company

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world.

In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.

Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.

Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.

Our Company Values Guide Our Daily Actions

Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.

STRATEGY

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.

Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.

Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.

Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.

The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.

Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring two Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialists (Environmental Specialist 4)(Two Positions)
within the Shorelands & Environmental Assistance
(SEA) program.

Note:
This is a temporary position that will end on June 30, 2027. T here is potential to extend based on funding availability.

Location Options:

These positions can be based at any of the following duty stations:

Headquarters Office (HQ) in Lacey, WA .
Central Region Office (CRO) in Union Gap, WA .
Northwest Region Office (NWRO) in Shoreline, WA .

One position will be based in NWRO. The other position will be based in either in HQ or CRO. Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the selected duty station.

Note
: If the selected duty station is the Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, the salary will include an additional 5% premium pay due to its location in King County. Salary range: $6068-$8163 per month.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires reporting to the office one day every two weeks.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by September 15th, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

These Regional Shoreline Compliance/Enforcement Specialist positions provide an opportunity for two senior technical experts to advance Ecology’s mission to protect Washington’s shorelines, wetlands, and riparian areas. In these roles, you will assist with regional implementation of the Shoreline Master Program (SMP) audit and technical assistance effort, support the development of a proactive compliance program, and strengthen state–local partnerships that ensure shoreline development achieves no net loss of ecological functions. You will work directly with local governments to evaluate shoreline permits, assess compliance with SMP requirements, improve monitoring systems, and resolve unauthorized activities affecting priority shorelines and riparian environments.

You will serve as regional enforcement specialists, independently developing cases, conducting investigations, preparing formal enforcement documents, and representing Ecology in complex proceedings involving violations of the Shoreline Management Act. Through collaboration with the Shoreline Policy Lead, SMA Compliance Lead, regional counterparts, and the Attorney General’s Office, you will help implement an adaptive feedback loop that improves statewide consistency, reinforces local permitting systems, and strengthens environmental protections.

What You Will Do

Implement the regional SMP audit and technical assistance program, evaluating shoreline permits, monitoring reports, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection measures to ensure consistency with the SMA and local SMPs.
Provide targeted compliance support to local governments, helping develop monitoring processes, evaluation methods, and systematic approaches to track permit effectiveness and ecological performance.
Conduct field verification for priority shoreline projects, confirming as-built conditions, validating monitoring findings, documenting ecological outcomes, and providing follow-up direction to permittees and local partners.
Lead regional shoreline enforcement activities by identifying unauthorized activities, developing defensible case documentation, conducting site investigations, preparing notices of violation and administrative orders, and coordinating enforcement actions with the SEA Program Enforcement Coordinator and the Attorney General’s Office.
Represent Ecology as senior technical experts in enforcement hearings, settlement discussions, and legal proceedings involving complex shoreline violations and high-priority environmental resources.
Serve as project officers for compliance-related grants and agreements, negotiating work elements, tracking deliverables, and ensuring alignment with shoreline protection and SMP improvement goals.
Collaborate closely with regional shoreline planners, headquarters staff, local governments, and tribal, state, and federal partners to ensure consistent implementation of shoreline management requirements and improve overall SMP compliance statewide.
Contribute to development and refinement of statewide shoreline compliance tools, guidance, training, and best practices that support adaptive management and improve long-term ecological outcomes across Washington.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Nine (9) years of experience and/or education related to the duties of this position, which includes the following:

Shoreline and Environmental Permit Review: Ability to interpret and evaluate shoreline authorizations, permit conditions, mitigation obligations, and riparian protection requirements for consistency with the Shoreline Management Act (SMA) and local Shoreline Master Programs (SMPs).
Compliance Evaluation and Field Verification: Skill in assessing compliance with SMP provisions through document review and site inspections, including verifying as-built conditions, monitoring reports, and ecological performance standards.
Enforcement Case Development: Experience gathering defensible environmental data, documenting violations, preparing enforcement documents (e.g., notices of violation, administrative orders), and coordinating with enforcement leads and legal partners.
Grant and Agreement Administration: Ability to serve as a project officer—developing, negotiating, and monitoring grant or agreement terms, reviewing deliverables, and ensuring alignment with program objectives.
Intergovernmental Coordination: Skill in working effectively with local governments, state and federal partners, tribal entities, and internal regional staff to support consistent and effective implementation of shoreline compliance activities.
Clear and Professional Communication: Ability to communicate technical, regulatory, or enforcement-related information clearly in writing and verbally to varied audiences, including permittees, local partners, and legal representatives.

Education:
Involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; environmental or natural science interdisciplinary studies; environmental planning, or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

Examples Of How To Qualify

9 years of experience.
8 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
7 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
6 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
5 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
3 years of experience AND a Master’s degree.

Desired Qualifications

Knowledge of regulatory programs and Ecology’s statutory authority under the SMA.
Knowledge of local government roles and responsibilities under the SMA.
Demonstrated understanding of environmental legislation and regulations at the federal, state, and local level.
Demonstrated understanding of complex environmental permitting processes.

Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit www.uscis.gov .

Application Process

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

How To Apply

Click “Apply” at the top of this page. Complete the entire application, including full work history and responses to all supplemental questions, and attach:

Cover letter, describing your interest in and qualifications for this position
Resume

Because we base our selection on the information you provide, it is in your best interest to complete the application thoroughly. A resume will not substitute for the “work experience” section of the application or vice versa. Applications with blank fields or supplemental question responses with comments such as “see resume” may be considered incomplete.

For detailed application information, please visit our Recruitment website.

Application Attestation: By submitting an application, you are affirming that the information contained in your application and on all attachments is complete and truthful. join us in serving our communities advancing Colorado's health and protecting the places we live, work, learn, and play, to create a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations thrive.

Mission -
To advance Colorado's health and protect the places we live, work, learn, and play.

Vision -
To create a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations thrive.

Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program. For more information, go to: https://studentloans.gov/myDirectLoan/pslfFlow.action#!/pslf/launch

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Institutions Unit is under the direction of the Deputy Division Director and is responsible for assuring compliance with the requirements of the food laws and sanitation regulations of the State for assisted living residences, swimming pools, child care facilities, and schools. These duties are accomplished through inspections, recall coordination, outbreak investigations, compliance assistance, and compliance assurance; by reviewing registration information, plan review submissions, and other field-generated information for assisted living residences (for retail food regulation compliance), swimming pools, child care facilities, and schools within the State. The school and child care programs are delegated through contracts to Local Public Health Agencies (LPHA). LPHAs conduct inspections and day-to-day program functions at the local level. This unit provides direct service for schools and child care facilities in the absence of a local program. The Division performs program audits and inspection standardization exercises with the delegated LPHAs. The unit, in cooperation with LPHAs, is responsible for assuring compliance with the requirements of the institutional environmental health laws and regulations of the State. The Unit determines the appropriate response, which may include informal or formal inquiries, such as embargo, condemnation, seizure, injunctive relief, and recalls, requesting additional field investigations, recommending and subsequently researching and recommending administrative or judicial enforcement actions, and developing and negotiating assessments. The Unit is also responsible for drafting new regulations, completing State Board of Health documents, and coordinating stakeholder meetings.

What You Will Do

The purpose of this position is to serve as an environmental protection specialist within the school and childcare programs. This position conducts regulatory inspections; prepares inspection reports, compliance advisories, LPHA assessments, and orders or recommendations for enforcement. Additionally, this position serves as a trainer in school and childcare programs. The position conducts training and joint inspections for LPHA staff and develops guidance materials for the programs. In addition to direct facility inspection oversight, this position provides compliance assistance, guidance, and training to the regulated community and local public health agencies. This position is expected to be a junior-level inspector with the goal of being fully operational as a senior-level inspector. This position requires wide-ranging oversight from the supervisor.

Key Responsibilities

Writes technical reports, creates and maintains accurate records, and initiates appropriate enforcement actions such as follow-up inspections, voluntary condemnations, and voluntary closures as necessary when non-compliance is identified within school or childcare operations.
Works collaboratively with epidemiologists to investigate illness and outbreak investigations.
Through research of technical reports, governing regulations, statutory requirements, and other resource materials, creates and drafts responses to questions and inquiries presented by local public health agencies' staff, school administrators, childcare providers, and the public.
Actively monitors progress and reviews reports submitted by LPHAs for completeness and contract requirements.

Residency Requirement

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

Class Code & Classification Description

I3A2T* Environmental Protection Specialist I

Minimum Qualifications

Experience Only:

Five (5) years of professional experience working in a field related to the work assigned to the position, such as environmental health inspections or in an occupation directly related to the work assigned in this position.

Or

Education And Experience

A combination of related education from an accredited college or university in Biology, Environmental Science for a field of study closely related to the work assignment and One (1) year of experience in a field related to the work assigned to the position, such as environmental health inspections or in an occupation directly related to the work assigned in this position to equal five (5) years.

NOTE: An applicant may meet the minimum qualifications for this job in one of two ways: They may qualify through their work experience alone or through a combination of education and work experience.

**This experience must be substantiated within the Work Experience section of your application. "See Resume" will not be accepted. In addition, part-time work will be prorated.**

Preferred Qualifications

In addition to the minimum requirements, the successful candidate in this position will have the following highly desirable experience and competencies:

Experience conducting regulatory inspections in child care facilities, schools, retail food establishments or a related industry.
Ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders including state and local governments, non-profits, community groups, private regulated entities and federal agencies such as EPA.
Advanced Interpersonal and conflict management skills e.g. displays understanding, courtesy, tact, empathy and concern.
Develops and maintains effective relationships, deals skillfully with people who are difficult, hostile or distressed,effectively manages and resolves conflicts, confrontations and disagreements in a positive and constructive way. Computer literate.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Bilingual in Spanish and English preferred.
Ability to analyze facts, data and evidence to arrive at a logical conclusion.
Experience with investigating complaints and outbreak investigations that are received regarding regulated facilities.
Experience with assisting in developing classroom training materials to support learning needs of regulated communities, stakeholders and LPHA staff.
Ability to make recommendations on reporting improvements and / or program improvements based on submitted information.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT:
Must match approved PD

A pre-employment background check will be conducted as part of the selection process.
TRAVEL: Traveling 80% of the time, with up to 30% of that travel being overnights, required to accomplish job duties; it may also require out-of-state travel for training courses/meetings up to two times per year.
Operation of a fleet vehicle on a regular basis.

Appeal Rights

An applicant who has been removed from an employment list or removed from consideration during the selection process may request a review by the State Personnel Director.

jobs.description:
At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.

For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.

At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.

Bloom Energy
is the leading force in transforming the way energy is generated and delivered. We are driving toward the parallel goals of growing a dynamic and forward-thinking company while creating a positive impact on our environment. Our mission is to make clean, reliable energy affordable globally. Our company is filled with smart and innovative thinkers and doers, and we never stop striving to improve our technology, to expand and improve our company performance, and to develop and support the many talented employees that serve our mission!

We are looking for a Director/Senior Director, Environmental Law
to join our team in San Jose, California
in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This is a fully on-site, in office role
.

Reporting to the Vice President, Environmental and Regulatory Law,
this role will serve as a strategic legal advisor for environmental, land use, health and safety, sustainability, and regulatory matters that are critical to Bloom’s continued growth. The Director/Senior Director will provide practical, business-oriented counsel across project development, operations, manufacturing, service, policy, commercial, and compliance functions. This position will be expected to lead in complex and ambiguous regulatory environments, develop creative and compliant paths forward, manage outside counsel where appropriate, and interface with federal, state, and local agencies to advance Bloom projects and support scalable business execution. The ideal candidate will have deep environmental law experience, strong judgment, excellent leadership and communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to partner cross-functionally with business teams to solve complex problems.

Role and Responsibilities:

Provide strategic legal advice and practical business counseling on environmental, land use, health and safety, sustainability, and regulatory matters impacting Bloom’s operations, projects, products, and services.
Support project development strategy and execution, including environmental review, permitting, due diligence, entitlement, and dispute-resolution matters.
Advise internal stakeholders on compliance obligations under federal, state, local, and international environmental and related regulatory programs, including air, water, waste, hazardous materials, occupational safety, climate, and sustainability requirements.
Interface with and advocate before regulatory agencies, including environmental, energy, public utility, occupational safety, and local land use authorities, to advance company objectives and resolve compliance or permitting issues.
Partner closely with Sales, Finance, Engineering, Service, Operations, Quality, Policy, Commercial, and Legal teams to identify risk, develop practical mitigation strategies, and deliver compliant, workable business solutions.
Provide legal support for environmental and land use disputes, administrative proceedings, negotiations, and litigation strategy, including matters involving CEQA, NEPA, air quality, water quality, waste, hazardous substances, and related state law analogs.
Review, draft, and negotiate environmental, sustainability, compliance, and risk-allocation language in commercial agreements, customer contracts, project documents, real estate documents, and transaction materials.
Monitor and assess emerging environmental, climate, energy, ESG, and sustainability laws and regulations; translate developments into business risks, opportunities, and recommended actions for senior leadership.
Manage outside counsel and consultants efficiently, including developing matter strategy, budgets, workplans, and internal alignment.
Advise on corporate sustainability, environmental justice, ESG due diligence, climate strategy, disclosures, reporting, and customer-facing sustainability commitments.
Other duties as assigned.

Skills and Experience:

Juris Doctor from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing with at least one state bar; California bar admission preferred.
10+ years of relevant environmental, land use, regulatory, compliance, permitting, litigation, and/or project development experience; in-house experience preferred.
Deep knowledge of environmental and land use laws and regulatory programs, including CAA, CWA, RCRA, CERCLA, CEQA, NEPA, OSHA-related requirements, climate and air programs, hazardous materials, and state and local analogs.
Demonstrated experience counseling business teams in highly regulated operating environments, preferably involving manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, transportation, industrial facilities, service operations, or emerging technologies.
Experience interfacing with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies and developing successful permitting, compliance, enforcement-resolution, and advocacy strategies.
Ability to lead in ambiguity, exercise sound judgment, learn quickly, and design practical, compliant solutions in a dynamic and evolving regulatory environment.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to coordinate cross-functional teams, outside counsel, consultants, agency stakeholders, and business leaders to drive matters to resolution.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex legal and technical issues into clear business risks and recommendations for senior management.
Experience supporting sustainability, ESG, environmental justice, climate, corporate disclosure, and emerging environmental policy matters is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build credibility and effective working relationships across Legal, Operations, Service, Engineering, Sales, Finance, Policy, Quality, and executive leadership.
Adheres to and promotes an appropriate set of core values and ethical conduct consistent with all laws and regulations.
Maintains confidentiality of work-related information and materials.
Some domestic and international travel required.

Bloom Energy’s mission is to make clean, reliable energy affordable for everyone in the world. jobs.description:
Organization

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)

Reference Code

EPA-OCSPP-2026-0008

How To Apply

To submit your application, scroll to the bottom of this opportunity and click APPLY.

A Complete Application Consists Of
